jobs.title: Mission France - Référent.e projet pluridisciplinaire migration F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Référent.e projet pluridisciplinaire migration pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Au sein du projet Migration de MSF sur le Littoral Nord, vous contribuez à définir, planifier, mettre en œuvre et suivre les activités médico-psycho-sociales et de protection. En lien étroit avec la coordination du projet et les référent·es techniques, vous veillez à la qualité des soins, à la bonne articulation des différentes disciplines et à une réponse cohérente, adaptée aux besoins des personnes accompagnées.

Vous supervisez les responsables des pôles santé somatique, santé mentale, travail social, ainsi que promotion et médiation en santé. Votre rôle est de faire vivre une approche pluridisciplinaire, qui prend en compte à la fois les situations individuelles et les besoins de santé des communautés.

**Principales responsabilités :**

**Piloter et suivre les activités du projet**

- Planifier, mettre en œuvre et suivre les activités sur le Littoral Nord : soins de santé primaires, santé mentale, protection, maraudes et activités post-traversée.
- Contribuer à l’évolution de la stratégie du projet selon le contexte et les besoins du terrain, et participer aux évaluations et missi Eons exploratoires si nécessaire.
- Suivre les indicateurs et les données d’activité, analyser les tendances et proposer des actions correctives pour renforcer la pertinence, la qualité et l’efficience des opérations.
- Participer à l’élaboration du plan annuel, des propositions de projet, des budgets et des rapports opérationnels et narratifs.
- Garantir une prise en charge pluridisciplinaire et centrée sur la personne
- Favoriser la collaboration entre les équipes médicales, de santé mentale et de protection, notamment par des échanges professionnels adaptés et le respect du secret médical partagé.
- Organiser la gestion des situations complexes médico-psycho-sociales et de protection, en priorisant les besoins, en clarifiant les limites de prise en charge et en assurant des parcours de référencement et de suivi lisibles.
- Veiller au consentement des personnes avant tout partage d’informations, à la confidentialité et à la protection des données.
- S’assurer de parcours adaptés pour les personnes victimes de violences sexuelles et pour l’accès aux soins d’avortement sécurisé, avec des procédures opérationnelles claires.
- Intégrer les retours des personnes accompagnées et les besoins exprimés par les communautés dans l’amélioration des activités.

 **Encadrer, soutenir et développer les équipes**

- Superviser les responsables de pôles, clarifier les rôles et responsabilités et assurer un suivi régulier des performances.
- Identifier les besoins de formation et accompagner le développement des compétences, notamment en matière d’intégration de la protection dans la prise en charge médicale.
- Contribuer au recrutement, à l’intégration et à la formation des nouveaux membres de l’équipe, en coordination avec les ressources humaines.
- Promouvoir un environnement de travail collaboratif et respectueux, faciliter la coopération pluridisciplinaire et traiter les difficultés d’équipe.
- Gérer les ressources et veiller à la qualité et à la sécurité
- Veiller à la disponibilité et à la bonne gestion des médicaments, dispositifs, consommables et matériels médicaux, en coordination avec la logistique et le service approvisionnement.
- Suivre les consommations et préparer les commandes médicales, dans le respect des protocoles et des procédures applicables.
- Contribuer à l’application des mesures d’hygiène, de sécurité et de prévention des risques sanitaires pour le personnel, ainsi qu’au suivi des événements indésirables.
- Veiller à la sécurité des personnes accompagnées, au fonctionnement des mécanismes de plaintes et de retours, et au signalement des situations d’abus.

**Représenter MSF et travailler en réseau**

- Entretenir des relations de travail constructives avec les partenaires associatifs, les autorités sanitaires et les acteurs locaux, notamment l’ARS et les structures de santé pertinentes.
- Représenter MSF dans les réunions externes liées aux activités et contribuer aux actions de plaidoyer en coordination avec le·la coordinateur·rice de projet.
- Participer à l’analyse du contexte et à la mise en place des protocoles de sécurité adaptés aux opérations.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Diplôme de médecine ou diplôme paramédical obligatoire.
- Au moins 3 ans d’expérience en lien avec le diplôme et expérience antérieure sur le terrain avec MSF indispensables.
- Expérience de projets Migration indispensable.
- Expérience confirmée de gestion d’équipe et de management pluridisciplinaire, notamment dans les domaines de la santé mentale, des soins de santé primaires et de l’accès aux droits.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Leadership, vision stratégique, sens de l’organisation, capacité à développer les équipes, esprit de coopération, flexibilité et gestion du stress dans des environnements changeants et parfois difficiles, y compris la nuit.
- Permis B souhaitable.

**Langues et outils :**

- Français courant obligatoire et anglais maîtrisé à l’oral souhaité.
- La connaissance d’autres langues est fortement désirée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

 Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 598.40 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an.
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

**Poste à pourvoir : 4 janvier 2026**

jobs.title: Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
PATHWAYS INTERNATIONAL · UK NAMED COMMUNITY SPONSORSHIP PROGRAMME

**Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom**

*London area based (hybrid) · Full-time*

**About us – what do we do?**

At a time of unprecedented forced displacement and system disruption, we are reforming the global system of safe and legal routes to protection. Our world-class team works closely with leaders and innovators from across sectors in over 20 countries. Together we design, launch, and expand safe and legal routes for displaced people. Together we pilot bold new ideas aimed at making the entire global system of safe and legal routes stronger and more sustainable.

**How we do it**

- We build and lead powerful partnerships and networks.
- We provide trusted advice.
- We accelerate operational delivery.
- We generate and share insights.
- We inspire change.

**About the role – what will you do?**

We are seeking a Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom to join Pathways International’s powerful global team at a formative moment for the UK’s new named community sponsorship programme.

This is a broad, versatile role spanning programme and partnership delivery and policy. You will plan and deliver the projects and partnerships that build the named community sponsorship ecosystem, while also helping shape policy development and implementation and keeping the programme informed by wider migration developments. The balance between policy and delivery will flex with the needs of the programme and the shape of the UK team.

Reporting to Hannah Gregory, Global Director Knowledge and Sponsorship, and working closely with Pathways International’s UK and global teams, you will help shape and sustain the development of named community sponsorship in the UK.

**Responsibilities**

- Contributing to the development of the UK named community sponsorship policy framework, supporting the design and development of the framework post-launch, including sponsored labour and education routes, in coordination with colleagues and partners.
- Planning, delivering and coordinating projects across the UK named community sponsorship portfolio, including organising events and meetings, developing resources, materials and tools and supporting monitoring, reporting and learning.
- Building and maintaining relationships across government, civil society, local partners and funders, and communities across the UK, and connecting delivery partners to training, mentoring and resources, including via Pathways International’s global networks and UK partners.
- Supporting the multi-stakeholder working group, engaging government and other policy stakeholders (including preparing for and following up on meetings and events), and representing the programme externally.
- Building and maintaining an understanding of the national, devolved, regional and local landscape relevant to sponsorship, and drawing out its implications for the programme.
- Maintaining an overview of wider migration developments in the UK and globally, and advising on their relevance for named community sponsorship.
- Researching, analysing and drafting high-quality briefings, policy documents and other written materials for senior stakeholders.

**About you – who are we looking for?**

We are looking for a versatile person who can move comfortably between programme and partnership delivery and policy thinking, and who thrives on a varied portfolio in a fast-paced environment. You combine professionalism and maturity with the warmth and versatility to build rapport quickly across very different audiences.

- A proven understanding of one or more relevant fields, which may include forced displacement, refugee protection, community sponsorship, global migration or migration policy.
- At least eight (8) years of relevant work experience, spanning programme or project delivery and policy, research or analysis, including experience of working in or closely with government.
- Experience working with and convening NGOs, civil society and/or other delivery partners.
- A confident representative with an easy, approachable manner, who builds lasting relationships with a wide range of UK stakeholders — government, civil society and others — and brings the judgement to handle senior meetings and the readiness to get stuck into the practical details of running an event.
- Strong policy capability, able to research, analyse and draft high-quality briefings and materials for senior stakeholders with keen attention to detail.
- Excellent project-management and organisational skills, able to coordinate meetings, events and projects and to prioritise effectively across competing demands.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
- Able to work on a varied and constantly evolving portfolio, while consistently displaying professionalism, discretion, tact and responsibility.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and experience collaborating with people from different backgrounds, countries, cultures and languages.
- A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field (e.g. public policy, public affairs, political science, international development). Education and work experience equivalencies will be considered.
- Comfortable preparing well-presented PowerPoint and Word documents and using AI tools, Excel, Zoom, MS Teams and SharePoint.
- We particularly encourage applications from qualified candidates with lived experience of forced displacement or migration, or with close personal and cultural connections to refugee communities.

**Location**

This is a London area based hybrid-working role with the ability to travel within the UK on a regular basis as needed and access available to shared office space. Applicants contacted for evaluation will be asked to provide proof that they have the legal right to work in the UK. Maintaining such legal right to work is a condition of employment.

**Salary**

Competitive, commensurate with experience.

**Contract**

Full-time. \[One-year term (renewable), or permanent — confirm.\]

**How to apply**

Please submit a cover letter, a CV, and a short, unedited writing sample of no more than five pages (in English) through Pathways International’s BambooHR portal at [https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/61](https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/61) by Friday, November 20th at 11:59 pm EST to be considered for this position.

**Equal opportunity employer**

Pathways International is an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage applications from qualified candidates of all genders and from all national, religious, and ethnic backgrounds, including persons with disabilities and those with lived experience of forced displacement. We will provide accommodation upon request during the recruitment, selection, and assessment process.

jobs.title: Grants officer (F/M) - Afghanistan
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

In 2025 and 2026, the mission significantly expanded its operations through new funding secured from ECHO, CDCS, and GFFO. The current funding strategy focuses on diversifying the donor portfolio and securing additional funding sources to further expand programmatic coverage. To support this objective, a donor mapping tool has been developed and is regularly updated by the grants officer, in coordination with the deputy general coordinator, to ensure systematic monitoring and follow-up of potential funding opportunities.

## About the role

You will be responsible for coordinating and overseeing grants management, donor compliance, resource mobilization, and partnership and donor engagement for MdM in Afghanistan. In addition, you will be responsible for the mission's communication and will promote visibility on MdM works, particularly when it comes to ensuring implementation of donors’ communication requirements.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator, your main responsibilities are the following:

**Proposal management:**

- Lead and coordinate concept notes and proposals
- Write the non-technical sections (context, needs analysis, cross-cutting)
- Ensure coherence between narrative, logframe and budget as well as alignment with MdM strategy and donor requirements

**Reporting:**

- Track all active grants and deadlines
- Coordinate donor and internal reports (including the monthly situation report)
- Ensure quality and consistency between programmatic and financial information

**Donor engagement:**

- Maintain donor mapping and a database of calls for proposals
- Train teams on donor rules, prepare meetings and briefing materials for the general coordinator
- Support audits and evaluations

**Partnerships:**

- Support the development of MoUs and partnership agreements
- Coordinate due diligence
- Manage collaboration with partners, including in a consortium

**Communication:**

- Develop communication products (factsheets, country profiles, success stories)
- Contribute to the visibility strategy, train staff on guidelines
- Collect field content, and manage social media in line with MdM and donor guidelines

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the program officer at HQ, the Institutional Funding Unit, the technical coordinators, the support coordinators, the MEAL team, and the communication teams at HQ and in the field, among others.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree in the following or related field: Development, International Relations, Humanitarian Management
- Have at least two years of experience in a similar role
- Have demonstrated experience in coordinating and preparing strong narrative and financial reports for a variety of donors
- Have a strong understanding of donor compliance, especially for ECHO/INTPA, FCDO, BHA, GFFO
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (MdM) (strong asset)
- Speak English fluently

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in multi-donors’ budgets
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in insecure and fast-changing contexts, with sound judgment, diplomacy and adaptability
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 069 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility.

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Program Development and Awards Advisor, WACAR
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***The IRC is seeking two (2) Program Development & Award Advisors. These positions are open to candidates in the West and Central Africa Region (WACAR), or other IRC locations in GMT and EAT time zones, who have significant experience working in West and Central Africa countries. Candidates based in these countries are encouraged to apply.***

**BACKGROUND**

Over the past 80 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The International Rescue Committee is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient. The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD)**

The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) have a growing portfolio of humanitarian relief, post-crisis recovery, and development programs under their remit. This work focuses support in five key areas: ensuring safety from harm, improving health, increasing access to education, improving economic well-being and ensuring people have the power to influence decisions that affect their lives. In all these programs, there is a drive to address the unique needs of women and girls (who represent the majority of those displaced) – and the universal barriers they face.

**The Awards Management Unit (AMU)** is one of four pillars within CRRD**.** The unit is responsible for identifying, securing, and supporting the management of all funding from statutory/government donors. The AMU is a bridge between donors and country programs: providing expert technical advice to the country teams, while maintaining portfolio-level visibility to ensure consistency and compliance and manage risk. This pillar ensures that donor compliance policies and procedures are implemented consistently and supports all staff working across the award management cycle for all restricted funding from global government sources.

**West and Central Africa Regional Overview**

The West and Central Africa Region (WACAR) supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges—conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation—through integrated, impactful approaches.

WACAR prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration.

The regional team responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. WACAR focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs.

WACAR comprises Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon and CAR, Chad, Cote d’Ivoire, DRC, Mali, Niger, Nigeria.

**The Purpose of the Role**

As part of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) team, the PDAAs oversee a diverse portfolio of awards across the humanitarian, recovery, and development sectors. PDAAs liaise with country programs, HQ departments and donor contacts to ensure high-quality guidance and support to country offices throughout the award lifecycle.

These roles will support country programs in the West and Central Africa region (WACAR) with donor compliance, award management, and producing high-quality donor deliverables. They will advise on IRC’s partnership system (PEERS), manage donor relationships including with HQ counterparts.

In addition, these roles will support WACAR country programs in securing funding for their programmes, through supporting and leading pursuit of new funding opportunities, in line with IRC’s Business Development Strategy. Support includes all phases of the business development process, from opportunity identification to contract signature, including pre-positioning, partnerships building, proposal development, and due diligence phases.

Successful candidates will have a strong track record of contributing to new humanitarian and development funding opportunities, deep knowledge of donor rules and regulations, and experience collaborating with local partner organizations.

**Scope and Authority**

These roles have no line management responsibilities.

**Key Working Relationships**

These positions will report jointly to the Senior Program and Awards Advisor (SPAA) and the Head of Business Development (HBD) for the WACAR region and work closely with RPAS team members, country program grants and partnership teams, and across all teams within the Awards Management Unit, Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department, Global Supply Chain, Finance, Office of General Counsel, Technical Excellence, and other key departments within IRC. PDAAs also serve as donor and partner points of contact as applicable per region.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

***Awards Management and Compliance***

- Manage a portfolio of awards for the WACAR region as assigned.
- Provide timely support on narrative reporting and post-award deliverables, guiding country offices on amendments, modifications, and submissions while collaborating with technical and financial staff.
- Provide support on budget realignments, changes in scope, NCEs, and other amendments for project elements not captured at proposal stage or emerging needs.
- Serve as first point of contact for country program-based awards staff to problem solve, guide and advise them on compliance post-award issues within the mentioned portfolio and to act as a connecting point between country program and other AMU teams to facilitate the timely flow of key information between them.
- Manage donor relationships by maintaining communication on contractual issues, updates on program implementation and following up on compliance queries and securing changes and approvals as needed.
- With support from the Program & Awards Officer (PAO), guide and coach country offices on partner management policies and PEER system compliance, and review and process sub-grants/partnership agreements. Coordinate with the Sub-awards and Partnerships (S&P) team as needed.
- Provide support to and monitor projects to ensure compliance with donor guidelines and IRC internal requirements. Monitoring awards can take the shape of monitoring visits, project implementation meetings and targeted calls following specific donor internal guidelines and IRC established processes.
- In collaboration with other regional team members, monitor award spending and help problem-solve for under-/over-spending. Partner with country programs and regional team as needed, to address implementations challenges.
- Provide technical advice to country offices on ad-hoc queries on donor compliance issues in coordination with AMU’s Compliance and Policy team on non-routine and high-level compliance matters and escalate to leadership for support as needed.
- Take part in meetings and calls with country teams where required to provide support and collaborate closely on specific issues related to donor compliance, submissions and/or monitoring/award management.
- Ensure lessons learned from finalized projects are fed back into new Business Development.
- Advise and support country programs appropriately to enable them to successfully follow internal IRC policies and procedures and maintain the integrity of awards-related data (e.g. OTIS, PEERS).
- Stay informed about programmatic issues and security and political developments affecting implementation.
- Coordinate with other members of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) Team and other AMU members for information sharing and establishing a coherent awards support.
- Ensure proper donor-related and contractual documentation to support compliance and audit readiness (including maintaining up-to-date, organized award files).
- Participate in the recruitment of and the onboarding of new CP Grants Coordinators/Heads of Grants teams.
- Contribute to the development of training materials, and deliver training to in-country staff, as required and in coordination with the Director, Awards Management (DAM) and Program and Award Support (PAS) team leaders. In coordination with the DAM and PAS leaders, develop and maintain work-processes and checklists for award implementation and report review, as well as record lessons learned.
- Onboard new country office Grants and Partnerships staff and new PAS team members to assigned donors, policies and/or IRC processes, as requested.
- Mentor and coach Grants and Partnerships staff on IRC systems and processes to ensure capacity is built at country level.
- Contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities and initiatives.
- Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

***Business Development***

- undefined
- Help drive business development in the region by providing effective proposal support, ranging from direct proposal management to light quality assurance.
- Support country offices with donor engagement, intel sharing and positioning with prioritized donors in the PDAA portfolio; prepare for and participate in donor calls as needed.
- Represent IRC externally at country-specific meetings, with donors and stakeholder networks in donor capitals as needed.
- Coordinate proposal development, including sharing initial assessments of new opportunities, preparing timelines, ensuring the proposal team adheres to deadlines, supporting recruitment, assisting in budget development, ensuring document completion, organizing meetings and compiling notes, and drafting and proofreading proposal sections.
- Collaborate with regional technical leads and technical advisors, country offices, and other colleagues to support conceptualization of winning proposals and designs for new project activities and/or amendments to current projects.
- Provide quality assurance and quality compliance support on proposals. Ensure responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements, including the PEER system.
- Lead or support coordination, communication, and inputs from consortium partners in accordance with donor and IRC processes.
- Coordinate and support regional reviews and approvals of proposal packages depending on country and regional needs. This includes partners’ packages if applicable.
- Review agreements to ensure accurateness and highlight key compliance requirements, in coordination with compliance and country grants teams and support in award negotiation and hand-over as required.
- Work with RPAS to incorporate lessons learned from implementation at the proposal stage.
- Maintain complete and accurate electronic files, including final submission packages and internal trackers.
- Deploying offices to lead proposal development as available and needed.
- Facilitate internal post-submission debrief sessions with country teams, technical units, regional team and other relevant stakeholders to collect lessons learned.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Essential**

Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications:

- Degree, preferably in a subject related to IRC’s work (International Relations, Refugee or Migration Studies, Development Studies, Public Policy) or equivalent experience
- \*\*Fluency in English and French, both spoken and written
- \*\*Good understanding of humanitarian aid and development programming
- Ability to work collaboratively as part of a diverse team and handle a multifaceted workload
- Good financial management and budgeting skills
- Ability to analyze and synthesize information
- Proven organizational skills, detail-oriented, ability to prioritize tasks, and to learn quickly
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to successfully and effectively liaise with people within and across departments in a multi-cultural environment.
- Ability to work independently in a very fast paced environment
- A flexible and calm work attitude
- International work experience in the Global South is a plus
- Excellent IT skills (Word, Outlook, Excel)
- Ability to travel internationally, sometimes on short notice and to insecure areas (15%)

Experience:

- Experience with and a strong understanding of institutional donors’ compliance requirements, e.g. UN, World Bank, US government, and/or European government donors (experience with all is not required, but a good mix would be a strong asset)
- Working at a distance and supporting country-based staff
- Writing, reviewing and editing narrative and financial reports and excellent attention to detail
- Working on new funding opportunities in the humanitarian and international development sectors with a range of multilateral and bilateral donors (FCDO, EU and ECHO, GFFO, BMZ, Sida, SDC, World Bank, US Department of State, etc.), as well as experience collaborating with local partner organizations.
- Experience with strategies and proposal processes of key government/statutory donors – US, UK, EU, German, Scandinavian, etc.

**Compensation (UK):** (GBP 52,210 -GBP 58,000). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: 23852 Project Officer (Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion) (P)
jobs.body:
Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Cameroon and the direct supervision of the Head of Programmes, and in close coordination with relevant units, Government counterparts, and partners, the Project Officer (Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion) will support the implementation of activities under the Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion Unit within the IOM Cameroon Country Office.

The Project Officer (Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion) will provide technical and operational support for project-funded interventions in the areas of labour migration, migration and trade, skills development and training, skills mobility partnerships, business and human rights, migrant inclusion, access to decent work and social protection, and other migration and sustainable development-related areas in line with IOM mandates.

The Project Officer (Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion) supports project implementation and coordination activities at national and regional levels and contributes to the delivery of project outputs in line with IOM global frameworks, regional priorities, and national development objectives.

1. Support, under the guidance of the Head of Programmes, the implementation of donor-funded projects under the Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion Unit, including programmes on labour mobility, diaspora engagement, skills development, cross-border trade, and socio-economic inclusion, in line with IOM and donor requirements.
2. Support the full project cycle (planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and closure), ensuring timely delivery of outputs, outcomes, and indicators as defined in approved project documents.
3. Assist in the day-to-day implementation and administrative coordination of assigned project tasks, including preparation and regular update of work plans, implementation schedules, procurement plans, risk matrices, and monitoring tools.
4. Provide technical support for the implementation of labour mobility and skills-based interventions, including ethical recruitment, skills partnerships, labour–trade–mobility initiatives, private sector engagement, and diaspora contributions to development.
5. Support the implementation of diaspora engagement activities, including skills transfer, investment mobilisation, entrepreneurship support, and contributions to resilience and regional cooperation initiatives.
6. Work closely with Government counterparts at national, regional, and local levels to support implementation of migration, employment, trade, and social inclusion activities.
7. Support in the implementation of socio-economic inclusion activities, including entrepreneurship support, financial inclusion, business formalization, and capacity building for women, youth, migrants, and small cross-border traders.
8. Support the integration of cross-cutting priorities in assigned tasks, including gender equality, youth empowerment, protection mainstreaming, disability inclusion, conflict sensitivity, and environmental sustainability.
9. Provide day-to-day supervision and guidance to assigned project staff, and support coordination with consultants and implementing partners, including performance monitoring and review of technical deliverables.
10. Support coordination with Resource Management, HR, Procurement, and Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) units to facilitate budget monitoring, compliance, timely procurement, and effective use of project resources.
11. Prepare and consolidate, in coordination with the Head of Programmes, donor deliverables, including narrative and financial reports, technical inputs, concept notes, and funding proposals, and contribute information and documentation as required.
12. Support monitoring, evaluation, and reporting activities, including data collection, results analysis, documentation of lessons learned, and dissemination of good practices.
13. Maintain working relationships with partners and relevant stakeholders, including with UN agencies, development partners, regional organisations, civil society, workers’ and employers’ organisations, and private sector actors.
14. Identify operational risks and implementation constraints and report issues to the supervisor and support the implementation of corrective actions, undertake duty travel as required.
15. Perform other duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Labour Economics, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Law, International Relations, Political Science, Human Rights, Social Sciences, or a related field from an accredited academic institution, with two years of relevant professional experience; or
- University degree in the above-mentioned fields from an accredited academic institution, with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Progressive professional experience in labour migration, labour mobility, skills development, employment, social inclusion, or related migration and development fields, with demonstrated application in African contexts;
- Proven experience in project coordination and implementation, including results-based management, donor reporting and compliance, preferably within multi-country or regional programmes;
- Hands-on experience engaging with government authorities, regional institutions, UN agencies, international and national organizations, social partners and private sector actors in Africa;
- Experience supporting initiatives related to skills development, ethical recruitment, migrant worker protection, labour governance, business and human rights, and/or socio-economic inclusion;
- Demonstrated experience working in Central Africa, and/or supporting regional or sub‑regional initiatives (e.g. CEMAC, ECCAS), with understanding of regional integration, mobility and labour dynamics; and,
- Prior exposure to complex operational or border contexts in Africa, is an asset.

**Skills**

- Solid technical knowledge of labour mobility, migration governance, skills development and employment systems, including understanding of African and Central African contexts;
- Solid familiarity with UN system policies, rules and procedures, including implementation of donor-funded programmes;
- Good analytical and drafting skills, including preparation of reports and programme documentation;
- Good coordination and stakeholder engagement skills, including experience working across ministries, regional stakeholders and implementing partners; and,
- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, supervise teams, and deliver quality results in deadline-driven environments.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Portuguese and other official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23673 Project Development and Donor Liaison Officer (P)
jobs.body:
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Ghana (resident), Togo, and Benin, and in close collaboration with the relevant units at the Regional Office (RO) and Headquarters (HQ), the Project Development and Donor Liaison Officer will be responsible and accountable for supporting the coordination and facilitation of project development, donor and institutional reporting in the fields of migration management, emergency response, as well as assisting with liaison activities with counterparts in the government, UN agencies, and other relevant stakeholders in line with IOM’s regional and country strategies.

**Responsibilities**

Contribute to the development of results-based programmes and projects, concept notes and project proposals, in close coordination with the CoM, Project Managers, United Nations Country Team (UNCT), relevant donors, government counterparts and project partners, by providing technical inputs and support that respond to emerging trends and priorities and that are in compliance with IOM and donor interests and requirements.

- Demonstrated knowledge of monitoring and evaluation concepts, approaches and methodologies;
- Proven analytical and planning skills; capacity to establish working relationships with  
    governmental authorities, national and international institutions and Non-Governmental Organizations;
- Demonstrated capacity to supervise and train support staff; ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and professional backgrounds;
- Demonstrated ability to work with accuracy under constraints and pressure; high sense of confidentiality, initiative and good judgment;
- Demonstrated personal commitment, efficiency, flexibility, drive for results, creative thinking; and,
- Good level of computer literacy, including database applications.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23559 Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer (P)
jobs.body:
Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Afghanistan and the direct supervision of the Head of the Programme Support Unit and in coordination with relevant units at Headquarters (HQ) and the Regional Office (RO), the Monitoring and Evaluation Officer will be responsible for leading the management of the monitoring, evaluation, learning, reporting and communicating functions of the Country Office (CO), supporting the CoM in identifying IOM-relevant project opportunities, developing the country strategy and project proposals and liaising with government counterparts, United Nations Country Team (UNCT), and other development partners, as necessary.

**Responsibilities**

**Institutional and Operational Set-Up**

1. Supervise and guide the implementation of the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) activities of the CO according to projects/ programmes/strategy result matrices and M&E plans, in close coordination with the Project/Programme Managers and other relevant IOM staff and partners.
2. Ensure adherence to existing Evaluation and Monitoring policies and guidelines and Results-Based Management (RBM) roadmaps, frameworks and guidance, including proper use of Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) for monitoring, reporting and evaluation.
3. Contribute, in collaboration with the Regional M&E and Risk Management Officer, to the development of plans, tools and systems to monitor implementation of projects/programmes and/or strategies within the CO focusing on activities, results, expenditure, budget, risks and assumptions, in line with donor/UNCT requirements, IOM strategies, and institutional M&E and reporting requirements.
4. Ensure that risks are assessed and new ones identified during the regular monitoring of project activities, and where appropriate ensure that associated Project Risk Register Matrix and Risk Treatment plans are monitored and regularly reviewed.
5. Provide substantive inputs to strengthen the capacity of IOM staff and partners to carry out M&E activities in the CO through training, mentoring, and coaching.
6. Regularly update the evaluation and monitoring plans for projects/programmes/strategies at the CO, including identification of key performance questions, indicators, and parameters for monitoring and evaluating performance in line with the Strategic Results Framework (SRF), and share the evaluation plan with the Regional M&E and Risk Management Officer on a regular basis.
7. Actively engage in M&E activities for and with UN Agencies, UNCT, donors, government and external partners at country level, including on possible joint monitoring and evaluations, for instance in the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) Evaluation.
8. Document good practices and lessons learned through analysis of monitoring findings and evaluation reports, identify causes of potential bottlenecks and corrective measures, and facilitate discussion of related M&E and RBM findings and challenges with relevant IOM project staff, management, and partners.
9. Facilitate regular feedback from beneficiaries and stakeholders on activities and services provided through the organization’s support, in close coordination with field units and relevant focal points of CO.

**Reporting and Communication**

1. Support Project/Programme Managers in compiling periodic donor reports in line with the M&E plans and agreed reporting schedules, as well as the CoM/ Head of Office (HoO) in compiling data for UNCT reporting requirements.
2. Provide comprehensive inputs for materials requested by the UNCT/ Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) or individual agencies, Government institutions, Donors, IOM relevant Units at HQs, RO and/or other partners.
3. Monitor the work of Implementing Partners (IPs) by receiving and reviewing progress reports in a timely manner as per agreement with IOM, UN and donors' terms and conditions.
4. Provide technical support to IP to improve the quality of data collection, consolidation, analysis, and reporting through capacity building and regular monitoring visits to the field.
5. Support the CO’s communication strategy through documenting IOM activities such as capturing case studies, life-changing stories for donor/UN reports, updating CO’s social media accounts, and producing quarterly newsletters and local media briefings.
6. Contribute to the preparation of meetings and events, to include donor/UN briefings, donor visits, and conferences.
7. Manage submissions for the IOM global institutional reporting processes, including the Institutional Questionnaire.
8. Conduct M&E activities that can contribute to the management and analysis of migration trends and related data relevant for IOM in the country.

**Project Development Support**

1. Contribute to the identification of new project development opportunities in close coordination with CoM, Project/Programme Managers, and RO’s Thematic Specialists, and in line with IOM global frameworks and CO’s strategy.
2. Provide inputs for the development of project/programme logic, including Results Matrices and Theory of Change, and for the monitoring and evaluation sections of project proposals/strategies.
3. Ensure that adequate monitoring and evaluation costs are budgeted and advocated for as per IOM M&E policies, guidelines, and Project Handbook.
4. Participate in UN, donor, sectoral, working groups, and other meetings aimed at development of new projects, for instance within Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM) regional and national networks.
5. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Business or Public Administration, International Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in project/strategy conceptualisation, development, monitoring, reporting and evaluation;
- Experience in capacity-building activities, including design and delivery of trainings;
- Experience in liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities as well as with national and international institutions;
- Demonstrated experience and familiarity in financial and business administration;
- Proven understanding and experience of internal and international migration issues in the country and in the region;
- Experience in organizing consultations, workshops and seminars with high-level stakeholders;
- In-depth knowledge and experience of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of monitoring and evaluation concepts, approaches and techniques including qualitative and quantitative methods, participatory approaches, and evaluative methodologies; and,
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of UN and bilateral donor programming and institutional requirements.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated writing and research skills;
- Excellent communication and analytical skills;
- High degree of judgment and initiative, ability to work with a high degree of independence within assigned areas;
- Demonstrated interpersonal and teamwork skills; and,
- Proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with people of diverse cultural and national backgrounds.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Request For Proposal - CERIM II Chatbot
jobs.body:
## 1. CERIM

CERIM II Is a project designed to support young people most at risk of irregular migration, as well as their communities, to think critically about irregular migration, reject smuggler narratives, increase confidence in viable alternatives. The project is delivered by Seefar Foundation in partnership with the Women Empowerment Organization (WEO)

## 2. Background

As part of CERIM II, we have built a working two-way WhatsApp chatbot on the Turn.io platform. The chatbot gives people information on irregular migration, covering:

- safe alternatives to irregular migration
- risks, myths and facts
- living in the UK
- dangers of the journey
- real-life stories.

The chatbot is built for multiple journeys and runs in three languages: English, Kurdish Badini and Kurdish Sorani. It also includes infographics and videos, and is powered by AI.

## 3. Purpose of this RFP

We invite qualified suppliers to submit technical and financial proposals for the development, maintenance and capacity building of the CERIM II WhatsApp chatbot, as set out in the scope of work below. We expect to award one contract to a single supplier.

*Important to note:*

We hold a Turn.io subscription until the end of the project on 31 March 2027. The selected supplier will work on our existing Turn.io account; no separate platform licence is needed.

## 4. Scope of work

The selected supplier will deliver the six deliverables below. All work must be carried out on our existing Turn.io account and must work in English, while we provide Kurdish translation where needed unless stated otherwise.

### Deliverable 1: Counselling sign-up journey (priority deliverable)

Design, build, test and launch a new chatbot journey that directs users to our MALTO tool, sign-up form for individual remote counselling. Users who meet the eligibility criteria will be contacted by a Seefar counsellor. The supplier will:

- design the journey flow and share it with us for approval before building
- build the journey in English, While Seefar translate the journey into Kurdish Badini and Sorani
- integrate it with the existing chatbot flow, including entry points from existing menus and journeys
- test the journey end-to-end in all three languages, including the link to the sign-up form
- launch the journey between 15 and 20 November 2026.

This deliverable is time-critical. The launch window is not negotiable.

### Deliverable 2: Monthly capacity-building workshops

Deliver one online workshop per month for Seefar and WEO staff, from contract start to project end (November 2026 to March 2027). The workshops should teach staff how to manage, build and edit journeys independently on Turn.io. Each workshop should include practical exercises on the live account or a test environment, and short follow-up materials.

### Deliverable 3: Handover workshop and documentation for WEO

WEO will take full ownership of the chatbot at the end of the project. Before the project ends, deliver a comprehensive handover workshop and handover documentation so WEO can own and run the chatbot independently. Documentation should include, at minimum:

- journey maps for all live journeys
- an admin guide for managing the Turn.io account
- user guides for building, editing and publishing journeys and content.

### Deliverable 4: Chatbot review and quality assurance

Carry out an initial review of the full chatbot, covering functionality, broken flows, language consistency and user experience. Submit a written finding report with prioritised recommendations, then fix the issues we agree on.

### Deliverable 5: Feedback mitigation

Respond to staff feedback that we share during the contract, and make the necessary fixes or changes. Response and resolution times will be agreed at contract stage, based on the times bidders propose.

### Deliverable 6: Content integration

Upload and integrate new content that we produce during the project – such as infographics, videos and stories – into the relevant journeys, in all three languages. We will provide content in final form and translated; the supplier is responsible for integrating and testing it.

The supplier should ensure that all new content is correctly displayed, functional, and consistent with the existing design and user experience across all three language versions. This includes checking the formatting, links, media playback, and overall functionality of the relevant user journeys before publication.

## 5. Timeline

**Milestone | Date**

RFP published | Thursday 29 October 2026

Proposal submission deadline | Thursday 5 November 2026, 12 AM Iraq time (UTC+3)

Expected contract start | Tuesday 10 November 2026

Counselling sign-up journey live | Between 18 and 20 November 2026

Monthly capacity-building workshops | November 2026 to March 2027

Handover workshop | During March 2027

Contract end | 31 March 2027

The timing of deliverables other than the counselling sign-up journey can be negotiated with the selected supplier.

The supplier should propose a realistic timeline for the remaining deliverables. The timeline will be agreed upon jointly with the project team and may be adjusted as needed, subject to mutual agreement and without affecting the agreed deadline for the counselling sign-up journey.

## 6. Budget

The maximum budget for this assignment is **GBP 6,800 inclusive of all taxes**. We will not consider proposals above this ceiling.

We assess value for money across quality, cost and the ability to deliver on time. The lowest price will not automatically win.

## 7. Proposal requirements

### 7.1 Technical proposal

The technical proposal must include:

1. Company profile and proof of legal registration.
2. Relevant experience, especially with Turn.io, WhatsApp chatbots and humanitarian or migration contexts.
3. Understanding of the assignment and proposed methodology for each of the six deliverables.
4. A detailed work plan and timeline, including how the counselling sign-up journey will be live by 20 November 2026.
5. Proposed team and CVs.
6. Approach to the monthly capacity-building workshops and the handover workshop, including format, content and materials.
7. Approach to data protection and the confidentiality of user data, given the sensitive subject matter and the vulnerability of users.
8. Proposed response and resolution times for feedback and fixes.

### 7.2 Financial proposal

The financial proposal must include:

1. An itemised quote in GBP, broken down by deliverable, with day rates and number of days where relevant. Please use the template in Annex A.
2. The quotation should clearly identify the costs associated with each deliverable, including any relevant assumptions, additional expenses, or potential costs that may arise during implementation. Any costs not included in the initial quotation should be clearly specified, and the supplier should seek approval from the project team before incurring any additional expenses.

## 8. Eligibility, conflict of interest and anti-fraud

- **Eligibility.** Bidders must be legally registered entities or individuals able to enter into a contract and issue invoices. Bidders must not be subject to sanctions or debarment by the UK Government or any other donor.
- **Conflict of interest.** Bidders must declare any actual or potential conflict of interest, including any personal, family or business relationship with Seefar.
- **Anti-fraud and anti-bribery.** We have zero tolerance for fraud, bribery and corruption. Any attempt to offer gifts, payments or other inducements to Seefa, or to collude with other bidders, will lead to immediate disqualification. Bidders must comply with the UK Bribery Act 2010 and all applicable anti-corruption laws.

## 9. Safeguarding

The chatbot serves people who may be considering irregular migration and who may be vulnerable. The selected supplier and all its personnel must comply with our safeguarding policy and code of conduct, and report any safeguarding concern immediately.

## 10. Intellectual property

All journeys, content, documentation and other materials produced under this contract belong to Seefar. They will be transferred to WEO at the end of the project. The supplier may not reuse or publish these materials without our written consent.

## 11. Seefar's rights

We reserve the right to accept or reject any proposal, in whole or in part, and to cancel this RFP at any time without explanation. We are not obliged to award a contract. We will not cover any costs bidders incur in preparing or submitting a proposal.

jobs.title: Grants and compliance coordinator (F/M) - Yemen
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Yemen**

Yemen remains one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises, after more than a decade of conflict, economic decline, climate shocks, and political instability. In 2026, over two-thirds of the population require humanitarian assistance, including 9.4 million people identified as most in need of life-saving support.

The health system is under extreme strain, with only 59.3% of health facilities fully operational and 19.3 million people requiring healthcare services, including more than 660,000 pregnant women in need of urgent care. Cholera continues to pose a major public health challenge, adding pressure to an already weakened system.

The operational environment remains highly volatile, marked by security incidents, service disruptions, funding cuts, and economic challenges that regularly affect humanitarian activities.

Médecins du Monde operates across northern and southern Yemen, with a coordination office in Sana’a and field offices in Aden and Marib. Its interventions focus on two strategic priorities:

- Supporting 29 health facilities to deliver primary healthcare services, including outpatient care, vaccination, nutrition, and reproductive health.
- Providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through healthcare facilities and community-based networks trained in identification, referral, and awareness-raising activities.

**About the role**

You will be responsible for providing technical expertise on grants and compliance while playing an essential coordination lead role amongst all departments. You are a key in ensuring all departments have a clear understanding of their role and responsibilities as regards to grants and compliance aspects.

You are actively involved in the country strategy and the overall project cycle management, especially through contracts management (including partnerships), reporting, donor communication, fundraising and compliance.

**Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator in charge of programs and the technical management of the HQ program officer, you will work in close collaboration with the general coordinator, the deputy general coordinator in charge of support services, along with other key departments when relevant (MEAL, field coordinators, etc.).

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator in charge of programs, your main responsibilities are the following:

- Support country strategy development through donor mapping, strategic opportunity identification, and donor engagement
- Lead fundraising efforts, identify funding opportunities, and build relationships with donors and key stakeholders
- Coordinate the development of grant proposals, budgets, and project design processes with technical and support teams
- Ensure effective grant management, donor compliance, contract follow-up, and timely donor communications
- Oversee the preparation and submission of high-quality donor reports and visibility materials
- Manage partnerships, including partner identification, due diligence, agreements, and performance monitoring
- Ensure compliance with donor requirements and MdM procedures, while supporting audits and risk management processes
- Facilitate coordination between departments and represent MdM in relevant meetings, forums, and donor engagements

**You are the right match if you...**

- Hold a master’s degree in one of the related fields or project management
- Have 5 years of proven experience in humanitarian and/or development contexts, with at least 2 years in a similar role
- Demonstrate strong knowledge in partnerships, multi-sectoral, regional and/or co-funded programming management
- Are skilled in developing high-quality funding proposals, reports and have experience working with institutional donors
- Experience /knowledge of the region
- Speak English fluently. Arabic is highly appreciated.

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Are uncomfortable working in complex, unstable, or rapidly evolving humanitarian contexts that require flexibility, resilience, and adaptability
- Prefer close supervision and highly structured processes rather than taking initiative, anticipating needs, and working independently
- Do not have strong written English skills or experience producing donor proposals, narrative reports, and other high-quality programme documentation
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

jobs.title: Deputy general coordinator in charge of programs (F/M) - Yemen
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Yemen**

Yemen remains one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises, after more than a decade of conflict, economic decline, climate shocks, and political instability. In 2026, over two-thirds of the population require humanitarian assistance, including 9.4 million people identified as most in need of life-saving support.

The health system is under extreme strain, with only 59.3% of health facilities fully operational and 19.3 million people requiring healthcare services, including more than 660,000 pregnant women in need of urgent care. Cholera continues to pose a major public health challenge, adding pressure to an already weakened system.

The operational environment remains highly volatile, marked by security incidents, service disruptions, funding cuts, and economic challenges that regularly affect humanitarian activities.

Médecins du Monde operates across northern and southern Yemen, with a coordination office in Sana’a and field offices in Aden and Marib. Its interventions focus on two strategic priorities:

- Supporting 29 health facilities to deliver primary healthcare services, including outpatient care, vaccination, nutrition, and reproductive health.
- Providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through healthcare facilities and community-based networks trained in identification, referral, and awareness-raising activities.

**About the role**

You will be responsible for the development and implementation of the country programme strategy, in line with MdM’s mandate and overall strategy. You will also ensure continuous quality improvement and strong technical positioning through the guidance and management of the medical, MHPSS, and WASH coordinators under your supervision.

Under the direct supervision of the general coordinator and the technical management of the HQ program officer, you will work in close collaboration with the deputy general coordinator for support services, as well as with other key departments at coordination level, including but not limited to grants, security, safety and access, and MEAL. You will also collaborate closely with the deputy field coordinators for programs at field-base level.

**What you’ll do**

- Lead overall program strategy, implementation, and quality across the mission

- Promote organizational learning through evaluations, lessons learned, best practices, and adaptive programming
- Manage, coach, and develop program staff while strengthening team performance and collaboration
- Represent the mission internally and externally, fostering coordination with donors, partners, authorities, and other stakeholders

**You are the right match if you...**

- Hold a master’s degree in international relations, public health, social science or any other relevant field
- Have 5 years of proven experience in humanitarian and/or development contexts, with at least 2 years in a similar role
- Demonstrate strong knowledge in partnerships, multi-sectoral, regional and/or co-funded programming management
