jobs.title: PSS and Community Development Unit Manager
jobs.body:
**Job Title:** PSS and Community Development Unit Manager

**Location:** Erbil, Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI), with regular travel to other areas of KRI.

**Type of position:** Employment contract

**Length of Contract:** 12 Months

**Compensation and Benefits:** Competitive salary and benefits commensurate with skills and experience. Expatriate/National Compensation Package: includes local transportation allowances, Medical insurance and Life insurance

**About SEED**: SEED is a women-led, local NGO in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, dedicated to creating a thriving society by advancing social protection and human development. We support individuals, empower communities, and strengthen systems to drive lasting change and equal opportunity. With a focus on collaboration, we promote gender equality, protect children, combat human trafficking, and improve mental health and well-being. SEED’s holistic, locally-driven approach integrates transformational services, community development, training and education, and advocacy to create sustainable impact. SEED is committed to creating a just, equitable society where everyone's rights are protected, with healthy families and strong communities, and a future where everyone can thrive.

**Role of the PSS and Community Development Unit Manager:**

SEED is seeking a dynamic and experienced Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Community Development (CD) Manager to lead the PSS/CD Unit and guide on SEED’s strategic objective of engaging and empowering communities. The PSS/CD Manager will lead and plan for the implementation of community-based programming aimed at engaging and empowering communities towards the development of a strong, healthy, resilient, and cohesive society through community-based initiatives designed to foster social and emotional well-being, prevent violence and discrimination, and promote social and economic empowerment. The PSS/CD Manager will oversee and support the technical/thematic leads and implementation of PSS/CD programming across thematic pillars, various programs, and locations across Kurdistan. The Manager will lead a team to design, manage, adapt, and support implementation of programming that improves MH and psychosocial wellbeing, achieves gender equality and ends GBV, and protects children and empowers their development. The PSS/CD Unit Manager will work in close collaboration with the MEAL Unit to ensure communities are involved from the start until the end of each program and that feedback is collected and the learnings are at the foundation of any future programming and requests for funding. This position requires a leader with both a deep understanding of psychosocial support and the ability to design community-driven interventions that promote positive social behaviors. The role also includes managing PSS resources, managing staff and building their capacity, and planning and guiding the strategic direction and execution of SEED’s community programming. The ideal candidate will bring strong leadership, planning and management skills, along with technical expertise in PSS, community development, promoting equality and combating gender-based violence (GBV), protection, mental health (MH), social behavioral change, and social cohesion programs, and a passion for empowering communities through transformative, locally driven change. The PSS/CD Unit Manager will oversee the 3 Technical Thematic Leads and ensure activities are appropriately tailored to the needs of each community. This position is based in Erbil with frequent travel required to Sulaimani and surrounding areas.

**Specific Tasks:**

**Management, Leadership, and Technical Support (60%):**

- Lead and manage SEED’s PSS/CD Unit and its 3 Technical Thematic Leads, and provide strategic direction to SEED on its cross-cutting strategic objective to engage and empower communities.
- Develop technical strategies, guidelines, and standards for the unit and provide strategic direction and day-to-day management of SEED’s PSS and community development programming.
- Oversee development, adaptation and dissemination of technical resources, including group curricula, training manuals, facilitator guides, and standardized tools for PSS and community development interventions created by the Technical Thematic Leads.
- Support the Technical Thematic Leads with the design, adaptation and delivery of awareness-raising sessions, PSS group activities, and community development interventions.
- Collaborate with Program Managers and Coordinators to align community needs with interventions and ensure technical quality and consistency across projects.
- Ensure the formation of community led initiatives, social cohesion activities, and social behavioral change (SBC) programming.
- Ensure PSS teams have PSS outreach plans for all locations and provide inputs into new partnerships engagement.
- Identify, mitigate and manage risks related to program delivery, partnerships, safeguarding and community dynamics
- Develop policies related to PSS program implementation and community engagement and accountability.
- Ensure the development of partnerships to enhance SEED’s PSS portfolio.
- Ensure that all activities are implemented in accordance with donor requirements, organizational policies, and international standards and practices.
- Set project direction by prioritizing and organizing actions & resources to achieve objectives.
- Provide input into program development pertaining to SEED’s PSS/CD work.
- Support the recruitment, interviewing, and onboarding of Thematic Leads, PSS facilitators and coordinators working on various programs and across locations.

**Reporting, MEAL, and Communications (30%)**

- Work closely with the MEAL unit to ensure communities are actively engaged throughout the whole programming cycle.
- Support with the development and adaptation of MEAL tools that collect information from communities, stakeholders, and other relevant parties to ensure community based ownership.
- Monitor implementation quality and adapt programming based on learning and community feedback.
- Ensure quality assessments are taking place to understand community needs prior to starting programs / interventions, and use data to inform program adjustments and quality improvements.
- Contribute to the development of PSS tools to ensure that M&E systems provide adequate feedback.
- Measure impact of interventions through proper feedback mechanisms and data collection.
- Provide input on safe and ethical data collection and storage.
- Contribute to developing articles, flyers, briefs, and other communication materials as needed.
- Provide input into awareness raising campaigns and advocacy strategies on related topics / thematic areas.

**Coordination and Organizational Representation (10%)**

- Identify, build and manage collaborative partnerships with other partners, coordination bodies, local authorities and other stakeholders.
- Represent SEED in meetings with communities, stakeholders, NGOs, KRG, and with donors.
- Develop strategic partnerships and maintain effective working relationships with key stakeholders including donors, government actors, UN agencies, international and local NGOs.
- Work closely with program partners, consultants, contractors, and sub-grantees.
- Conduct external meetings, presentations, or trainings on PSS related topics as requested.

**Key values:**

- Serve as a positive role model and SEED ambassador at all times.
- Treat all people with respect regardless of age, gender, religion, nationality, sexual orientation, disability status, marital status and ethnicity.
- Working collaboratively with all colleagues, and maintaining a positive, cooperative attitude.

**Essential criteria:**

- Master’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, Gender Studies, International Development, Public Health or related field.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in managing teams and building staff capacity through training, coaching, and supervision.
- Minimum of 7 years of relevant experience in PSS, community engagement, GBV prevention, social behavioral change, MH, and peacebuilding in humanitarian or development settings.
- Strong technical knowledge of gender equality, women and girls empowerment, GBV prevention, and social norm change with experience designing or leading awareness and social behavioral change initiatives.
- Strong knowledge of social change theories and approaches
- Experience in developing culturally sensitive messages and materials.
- Demonstrated leadership, strategic planning, and staff management skills.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including experience with diverse communities.
- Experience in program design and development, program implementation, MEAL, and reporting.
- Experience in resource management and program/activity planning.
- Experience in development and humanitarian settings a must; experience in the Middle East, Iraq, or Kurdistan, a plus.
- Strong belief in human rights and gender equality.
- Ability to work in a stressful setting and adapt quickly to changing environments.
- Strong ability to work independently.
- Experience working with vulnerable populations, especially in the Middle East, is highly desirable.
- Excellent English required; proficiency in Kurdish and/or Arabic a plus.
- Good computer skills, experience with Google Drive
- Committed to SEED’s mission, values, and ethical standards.

jobs.title: Protection Cluster Co-Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Overall purpose of the role**

DRC co-leads the Sudan Protection Cluster in partnership with UNHCR, the Cluster Lead Agency, in line with Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) and Global Protection Cluster (GPC) standards. The Co-Coordinator provides strategic and operational coordination to strengthen a principled, inclusive and evidence-based protection response across Sudan; elevate the voices of NGOs, particularly national and local actors; promote the centrality of protection across the humanitarian response; and translate protection risks, community priorities and response gaps into collective action, advocacy and resource prioritisation.

**Responsibilities**

Working jointly with the UNHCR Protection Cluster Coordinator and in consultation with cluster members, the Strategic Advisory Group (SAG), subnational structures and relevant Thematic group, the Co-Coordinator delivers the cluster’s agreed functions and workplan. The position complements UNHCR’s formal Cluster Lead Agency accountabilities while providing independent and meaningful NGO co-leadership.

***Protection Cluster Meetings, Information Exchange and Representation***

- Co-chair national Protection Cluster and SAG meetings with UNHCR; agree priorities, facilitate participation, document decisions and follow up on collective commitments.
- Connect national and subnational coordination structures through field missions, mentoring, timely information exchange and support to decentralised or area-based coordination arrangements.
- Promote complementarity with Child Protection, Gender-Based Violence and Mine Action Thematic groups and relevant housing, land and property (HLP) mechanisms, respecting their respective technical mandates.
- Represent agreed cluster positions in the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), relevant Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) engagements, donor dialogues, NGO fora and inter-agency initiatives.
- Maintain constructive coordination with OCHA, UN agencies, NGOs, community-based and women-led organisations, relevant authorities and other sectors, upholding neutrality and humanitarian principles.

***Strategic Planning and Reporting***

- Co-develop and regularly review the Sudan Protection Cluster strategy, workplan and contingency plans with UNHCR, the SAG, Thematic groups and partners, based on evolving conflict, displacement and access trends.
- Lead technical inputs to the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP): protection needs, severity and people-in-need analysis, prioritisation, objectives, indicators, targets and financial requirements.
- Identify critical gaps, duplication and underserved locations through field evidence, service mapping, partner reporting and response-monitoring data; support coordinated corrective action.
- Support rapid-onset emergency coordination, field assessments, preparedness and integrated/mobile protection response approaches, with clear referral and operational linkages.
- Liaise with donors to mobilize resources for the joint protection response and update donors on protection cluster priorities and needs
- Contribute to the HCT centrality of protection agenda and to evidence-based inter-cluster priorities, advocacy, periodic situation reporting and response performance reviews.

***Capacity Building, Trainings and Promotion of Protection Mainstreaming***

- Provide technical guidance and capacity strengthening for partners and subnational coordinators on protection standards, risk analysis, safe referrals, protection monitoring and operational guidance/SOPs.
- Advance protection mainstreaming across sectors, including safe and equitable access, dignity, do no harm, GBV risk mitigation, child safeguarding, PSEA, accountability and age, gender and disability inclusion.
- Promote meaningful participation and leadership of national/local NGOs, women-led and community-based organisations; strengthen inclusive decision-making and locally led responses.
- Support harmonised technical guidance on cash for protection, coordinated mobile responses, safe referrals and other agreed protection interventions.

***Protection Tools and Protection Information Analysis***

- Coordinate harmonised protection monitoring, key informant interviews, field assessments and the Protection Analytical Framework; oversee analysis of protection risks, geographic severity, access constraints and emerging threats.
- Produce or coordinate Protection Analysis Updates, protection alerts, advocacy briefs, needs/gap analyses, and other timely, action-oriented information products for humanitarian decision-makers.
- Facilitate evidence-based collective protection advocacy on attacks against civilians, unsafe displacement and return, movement restrictions, violence, discrimination and denial of essential services.
- Work with information-management colleagues and Thematic groups to maintain reliable 5W/service-mapping, referral, response-monitoring and severity-analysis tools, with appropriate validation and disaggregation.
- Apply data responsibility, confidentiality, informed consent and survivor-centred standards; prevent unsafe collection or disclosure of sensitive individual protection data.
- Support the leading of Protection Information Management (PIM) systems to identify and address field-based protection concerns through state-level clusters and partner organisations

***Promote and Support Accountability to Affected Populations***

- Ensure affected people, including IDPs, returnees, host communities and persons at heightened risk, inform protection analysis, priorities, response design and feedback processes.
- Strengthen safe, confidential and accessible referral pathways and community feedback mechanisms, and encourage coordinated action on gaps and barriers to services.
- Promote adherence to humanitarian principles, international humanitarian and human rights law, safeguarding, PSEA and protection-sensitive approaches to movement, return and durable solutions.

***Qualifications, Experience and Technical Competencies***

- Postgraduate degree in international law, social sciences, humanitarian studies or a related field.
- At least three years of relevant humanitarian protection experience in complex emergencies; substantial inter-agency coordination experience, preferably in a Protection Cluster/Sector leadership role.
- Demonstrated expertise in protection risk analysis, monitoring, the humanitarian programme cycle, preparedness, coordination and collective advocacy.
- Strong understanding of IASC/GPC guidance, Thematic group mandates, protection principles, international humanitarian/human rights law and safe information management.
- Sound understanding of humanitarian coordination, funding, and leadership mechanisms, as well as experience in working with protection cluster coordination
- Proven ability to facilitate diverse partnerships, engage senior humanitarian leadership/donors, and draft concise, high-quality strategic and analytical products.
- Excellent understanding of protection issues in emergency and displacement situations, detailed knowledge of humanitarian principles, guidelines for humanitarian assistance, and relevant international legal frameworks
- Experience in Sudan or a comparable conflict-affected context, with field coordination, localisation and capacity strengthening, is strongly desirable.
- Excellent advocacy and representation skills including the ability to develop strong interpersonal relationships to facilitate communication within the cluster

**Languages:**

- Advanced Proficiency in written and spoken English.
- Fluency in Arabic is strongly desireable

**About you**

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:*

- *Striving for excellence:* You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- *Collaborating:* You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- *Taking the lead:* You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- *Communicating:* You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- *Demonstrating integrity*: Upholding and promoting the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Conditions**

*Contract:* One-year contract with possibility of extension, subject to funding and performance. Salary and conditions in accordance with the Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for International staff. This position is graded at Band NM.F

*Start Date:* December 2026

*Duty Station:* Khartoum, Sudan (with regular field travel)

Reports to: Country Director

jobs.title: Senior Officer - Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (Climate, Natural Resources and Peace)
jobs.body:
This is an exciting opportunity to coordinate monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) activities across an impactful, international, multi-partner programme on water, peace and security. In addition, the successful candidate will also contribute to International Alert’s wider programming on climate and peace.

We are looking for an excellent candidate, with at least five years’ experience working in the development, peacebuilding, water or natural resource management sectors and substantive experience designing and delivering effective MEL. With a proven ability to collaborate, communicate and coordinate effectively with partners in different locations and from a range of sectors, you will support partners, including through training, to design and implement MEL data collection and analysis. In addition, the successful candidate will have the skills to help implement Alert’s projects on climate and peace, supporting evidence generation, policy influencing and advisory activities.

In return, you will have the opportunity to work for a dynamic, motivated and friendly team and the chance to contribute to the organisation’s mission, supporting people to build peace in countries affected by conflict.

**Job Purpose**

The Senior Officer - Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer (SOMEL) supports monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) processes across the organisation, helping to ensure that monitoring and evaluation is rigorous, high-quality and fit for purpose, and that learning is embedded in our approach to our work. Reporting to the Head of Peace Integration, the postholder will work with Alert’s network of MEL focal points in our country offices, building a common approach, sharing experiences and developing in-country capacity. They will develop and disseminate tools to enable us to plan for, measure and disseminate the impact of our peacebuilding work. The postholder will oversee annual reflection sessions across the organisation, ensuring we capture the outcomes of our work. The Senior Officer - Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer will coordinate submissions of team annual reports and draft the organisation’s Annual Report.

**Duties & Responsibilities**

**Monitoring and Evaluation**

- Develop and disseminate common Alert M&E tools and resources, including drawing on global best practice to develop new resources when needed.
- Support country and global programmes to design programmes, develop realistic and useable theories of change and establish appropriate monitoring systems at both project and programme level.
- Convene the network of M&E leads across Alert’s programmes, to enable roll out of agreed organisational approaches to M&E, sharing of experiences, learning opportunities and peer support.
- Support capacity building of country programme Alert M&E staff by providing focussed trainings, inductions, and individual advice.
- Coordinate the annual reflection process with partners.

**Impact assessment**

- Oversee the annual reflection process across the organisation, ensuring teams have the necessary resources to undertake reflection sessions, collate and analyse the data.
- Strengthen our Outcome Harvesting (OH) practice, including encouraging facilitation of OH sessions by colleagues from other teams, and enabling partners involvement in OH reflection.
- Support the establishment of an organisational impact reflection and design reflection process
- Support country and global programmes in the design of programme evaluations.

**Learning**

- Establish processes and/or fora for Alert staff to regularly share, learn and challenge one another on peacebuilding practice and policy (in particular on Alert’s priority themes), drawing on internal and external knowledge and experience.
- Monitor developments in MEL practice and apply these to Alert’s approach, ensuring the continuing evolution and improvement of our MEL.

**Organisational contributions**

- Coordinate submissions of team annual reports and draft the organisation’s Annual Report.
- Contribute to internal communications and knowledge management and participate in organisation-wide events and discussions.
- Occasionally supervise volunteers and monitor the work of consultants as required.
- Undertake any other tasks commensurate with the role, as required by the - Head of Peace Integration

**Travel requirements**

Occasional travel to our countries of operation.

**Essential requirements**

- Knowledge of, and experience of applying to development or peacebuilding projects and programmes, monitoring and evaluation approaches and methodologies.
- Experience developing theories of change, indicators and logical frameworks for international development or peacebuilding projects and programmes.
- Understanding of peacebuilding and conflict transformation.
- Experience developing and implementing monitoring and evaluation systems for an organisation.
- Experience undertaking monitoring and evaluation in complex settings (such as fragile states)
- An understanding of current trends in M&E for international development, including using participatory M&E approaches that enable for staff, partners and participants to jointly reflect on the impact of their work.
- Experience working remotely with country teams, supporting and building capacity of others to undertake or plan monitoring and evaluation.
- Experience facilitating workshops, trainings and events, including remotely and with people with diverse first languages.
- Fluent written and spoken English; excellent analytic and report writing skills, including ability to simplify and explain technical issues.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to engage with a wide spectrum of actors, including staff at all levels, partners, peers and donors.
- IT literate, including experience using Excel for budgeting, and using databases.
- Existing permanent right to work in the country in which you wish to be based, in which Alert has a registered office.

**Desirable Requirements**

- Fluent written and spoken French or Russian.
- Experience facilitating and coordinating Outcome Harvesting for a team or an organisation.
- Experience managing projects.
- Experience of cross-organisational coordination.

jobs.title: Finance Assistant- Accounting & Audit- Damascus
jobs.body:
**Background/Context:**

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs in Idleb, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Hassakeh, and Deir ez-Zor, with new programs expanding into Hama, rural Damascus, and Homs. With a team of over 700 members, the IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery. It plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and adapting to the evolving context.

With the new realities under the new government, as of December 2024, the IRC has deployed a team to Damascus to set up operations and engage in coordination structures for newly accessible areas across Syria—including parts of NES, NWS, and other previously unreachable locations in South and Central Syria, adjusting operations to maximize coverage and efficiency.

**Job overview:**

The Finance assistant is an integral part of Syria finance team. This position supports Damascus office and program centers in Homs and any future program’s centers which fall under Damascus D4, in implementing the Finance policies & procedures of IRC and our donors. Besides, this position is mainly responsible about all cash related activities (i.e. receive cash from Bank or Hawala and make deposits in Damascus safe and related banks, issue cash payments, contribute in preparation of cash requests/cash forecasts, checking the supporting documents of the payments requests before release payments , ensure that all needed approvals are available based on the authorization matrix, monitor the cash flow, arrange with Hawala agents and banks for cash distributions to (vendors, staff, Incentive workers, …) , ensure timely payments for all payees, ensure that complete and accurate supporting documents are uploaded to the system and to the related files for all released payments, invoices). In addition, this position is responsible for liaising with the contracted banks and Hawala inside and outside Syrai for any deposit, withdrawal including the quiches. Will make sure all cash and bank entries booked in system on time and cash and bank reconciliation are performed on monthly bases on time with accurate performance, also support Finance Officer for data entry into Integra System and audit requirements and daily operations of accounting side in Damascus related work.

**Responsibilities:**

- Closely work with Finance Officer to ensure the best understanding and implementation of IRC Finance Policies and Procedures, as well as IRC Donors rules and regulations.
- Support the finance officer in initial reviewing all kinds of financial documents to ensure that all the supporting documents and approvals needed are available. Support in record and submit PO & Non-PO invoices, JEs, Cash receipts, PMNTs to Integra daily. Besides, ensure saving all the supporting documents in the related files & uploading them to the system per transaction references.
- Prepare the cash request for Damascus office in coordination with the line supervisor, and under direction from FM and per cash management SOP guidance.
- Receive cash from Hawala agencies and bank, make sure all cash pieces of dollar/ SYP and any other Currency have been received properly (no scratch, tidy, etc.). Besides, maintain the cash in office in a safe in a proper way and ensure all information about cash/ cheques are confidential.
- The finance assistant should contact all suppliers and ask them to collect their dues on the determined distribution dates. Besides, for other types of payees such as IWS, beneficiaries .... etc. the finance assistant should ask all payments requestors to contact the payees and ask them to collect their dues on the determined distribution dates and follow up with requestors regarding any uncollected amounts to mitigate cash risk.
- Represent finance in the distribution sites if needed, sign & reconcile any related documents. Besides, verify the payees’ identities before disbursing as well as the letter of delegations from staff, suppliers or beneficiaries.
- Pay out all suppliers, incentive workers, vendors, advances, salary of staff when needed and deal with them in high performance of respect and integrity and in line with cash management SOP. Besides, before releasing the payments the finance assistant should make sure that all required approvals/ documents are available (make sure PO match invoice match payment in terms of amount and payee name), and he/she should take quick action and inform the head of finance department and line Supervisor in case of any findings.
- Ensure all documents are labeled as “PAID” once payment is cleared with vendors and in line with Cash management SOP.
- Conduct a cash count daily in a proper and secure way. Verify any discrepancies and report that immediately to the Finance & line managers if not resolved. Maintain cash tracking sheet on daily basis and keep the signed versions of cash count in the cash count file and keep scan copies on BOX, share the final cash count /bank statements after reconciliation with system with FM for action.
- Receive cash refunds from staff/contractors and charge them back to proper account codes, make sure that the receipt Voucher is signed by the staff and approved by the Sr. Finance Officer / Finance Officer.
- Support finance officer in providing any documents needed for audit purposes or any other reason. And help with the finance office admin work such as photocopying and scanning if any.
- Plan, organize and manage workload and be resilient in accepting new assignments and extra working hours during competing priorities.
- Contribute in the month & year end closing to ensure high quality of closing & meeting HQ deadlines. Besides, participate in coordination with the finance officer in the monthly review for the following balance sheet accounts: Cash in office, Petty cash, Advances, Accruals, Prepaid, Vendor payable, Miscellaneous Payables, Miscellaneous Receivable, Hawala/ Cash Transfer Agent/ bank statements.
- Support finance officer in preparing cash requested and fees allocation JVs resulted from: incentive workers payments, NES staff salary payments, drivers’ payments, and vendors payments.
- Attend distribution sites for staff salaries and vendors dues in program centers per need.
- Support finance officer in doing Pool cost allocation JVs Damasus office when needed.
- Support in Prepare cash projection on monthly basis, share with Finance Manager on time.
- Support in Conduct inventory check for warehouses and assets and property from time to time and per request from Supply Chain team.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- University or institution Degree in economics (accounting departments, business management or relevant financial studies), or any other college degree alongside one years` experience in accounting position preferably in an INGO.

**Work Experience:**

- Good understanding of accounting processes and procedures.
- Meeting targets and deadlines and being flexible and comfortable in multi-cultural workforce.
- Team player, cooperative and supportive to colleagues from same and different departments.
- Ability to work under pressure and load of work and willingness \\ ability to work for extra hours when and as needed.
- English is a plus.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Computer literate and has strong competencies in MS Office package, especially Excel (e.g common formulas) and outlook
- Any ERP System experience is an advantage.
- Strong ability to work independently, organize work, meet deadlines, maintain composure, prioritize work under pressure, coordinate multiple tasks and maintain attention to details.
- A commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values and IRC Way – Professional Code of Conduct.
- Credible written, presentation and verbal communication skills; ability to convey information effectively and solid experience providing training and staff development.
- Validated sense of professional discretion, integrity, and ability to handle complex situations diplomatically and to effective resolution.
- Excellent management and interpersonal skills and a solid ability to promote harmonious/cohesive teamwork, in a cross-cultural context.
- Validated ability to plan long-term, organize priorities and work under administrative and programmatic pressures with detail orientation and professional patience.
- Highly collaborative and resourceful; ability to establish positive working relationships with senior level management and all other partners to maximize cooperation and productivity.
- Curiosity, a desire to continually learn and develop is a must.
- Analytical ability in creating effective solutions to complex matters while adhering to labor laws and internal policies.

**Language/Travel:**

- Good practical and spoken language skills of Arabic and English, Kurdish is an advantage.
- Travel: 10% to field sites in **NES upon request** as well as attending regional and global workshops and meetings upon request.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to: Finance officer**  
**Position directly supervises: N/A**

**Indirect Reporting:**   
**Key Internal Contacts:** Other Finance team members in all areas, Supply Chain team, Field Director, program colleagues.

**Key External Contacts:** Suppliers, IWs, Beneficiaries**.**

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

jobs.title: Finance Manager – Audit and Accounting-Damascus
jobs.body:
**Background/Context:**

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs in Idleb, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Hassakeh, and Deir ez-Zor, with new programs expanding into Hama, rural Damascus, and Homs. With a team of over 700 members, the IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery. It plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and adapting to the evolving context.

With the new realities under the new government, as of December 2024, the IRC has deployed a team to Damascus to set up operations and engage in coordination structures for newly accessible areas across Syria—including parts of NES, NWS, and other previously unreachable locations in South and Central Syria, adjusting operations to maximize coverage and efficiency.

 **Job overview:**

The **Finance Manager – Accounting & Audit** is responsible for providing strategic and operational leadership across accounting, audit, internal controls, compliance, and financial risk management. The position ensures the accuracy and integrity of financial records maintained in the **Integra system**, oversees month-end and year-end closing processes, and ensures effective management and reconciliation of cash, bank, and Hawala transactions and all balance sheet accounts on timely fission.

The role strengthens financial accountability by ensuring that internal controls and compliance mechanisms are effectively implemented, financial risks are proactively identified and addressed, and organizational assets are adequately safeguarded. It also supports audit preparedness and follow-up, promotes the efficient and transparent use of resources, and ensures adherence to IRC policies, donor requirements, applicable regulations, and accounting standards.

 **Responsibilities:**

1. **Accounting and Financial Management and Internal Control**

- Manage day-to-day operations of the Accounting Department
- Assist with the implementation of finance policies, procedures and systems
- Ensure compliance with IRC procedures and guidelines and donor guidelines
- Review supporting documentation for payments to ensure accuracy and ensure that costs are allocable and allowable.
- Review expenditure worksheets for accuracy and completeness
- Review and approved entries according to the assigned authorization limit from files offices before posting into Integra, including but not limited to: PO, and Non-PO, Journal entries, cash receipts, cash deposits, payments.
- Ensure monthly, quarterly, and annual financial closing processes are completed in accordance with organizational policies and deadlines.
- Monitor financial data quality and ensure proper maintenance of accounting records and supporting documentation.
- Provide oversight of cash management activities to ensure adequate liquidity and effective safeguarding of funds
- Review and approve bank and cash reconciliations, ensuring discrepancies are identified and resolved in a timely manner
- Ensure Hawala transactions are properly authorized, documented, recorded, reconciled, and monitored.
- Strengthen controls over cash transfers, banking activities, and Hawala settlements.
- Maintain monthly Folder for WOS filing and balance sheet analysis, make sure all month/year end closures are properly updated and archived including cash and bank and lease statements.
- Liaise with the budget holders regarding the monthly cash forecast, support in preparation of cash transfer Reports due to regional office and HQ before the end of each month.
- Ensure donor funds are used in accordance with grant agreements and organizational policies.
- Establish, maintain, and continuously strengthen internal control systems to safeguard organizational assets and resources.
- Identify financial and operational risks and develop mitigation measures to address control gaps.

**2. Audit Management**

- Support Finance Coordinator in the planning and coordination of internal, external, donor, and statutory audits.
- Ensure complete, accurate, and timely provision of audit documentation and information requests.
- Monitor audit findings and recommendations, ensuring corrective actions are implemented and tracked to closure.
- Support continuous improvement initiatives arising from audit observations and lessons learned.
- Maintain audit readiness throughout the year through proactive review of financial records and controls.
- Monitor implementation of audit recommendations and report on progress to direct manager.
- Conduct regular audits of timesheets to ensure adherence to policy and approved allocations

**3- Balance Sheet and Reconciliation Management**

- Oversee the preparation, review, and timely clearance of all balance sheet reconciliations.
- Ensure Monthly reconciliation of cash, bank, Hawala, advances, accruals, payables, receivables, and other balance sheet accounts.
- Investigate and resolve unreconciled items and ensure corrective actions are implemented promptly.
- Maintain strong oversight of ageing balances and ensure timely resolution of outstanding items.
- Respond to Regional office for any quarterly and monthly related trail balances

**4- Payrolls:**

- Oversee the monthly payroll review process to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with organizational policies, local labor regulations, and statutory requirements.
- Ensure payroll costs are correctly allocated to projects, cost centers in accordance with donor requirements and approved budgets.
- Forward to the Payroll Administrator every month, outstanding personnel advances and charges related to T7, for recovery.
- Responsible for payroll allocation for Expat staff and reviewing the payroll costs and its allocation for National staff.

***5- INTEGRA System Related processing:***

- Ensure effective utilization of the Integra system and promote best practices in financial data management.
- Performing and supervising the posting of entries ensuring accurate general ledger(accounts payable, receivables, Invoices, payroll, journal entries)and proper controls are enforced and appropriate systems in place to maintain all required supporting documentation for each single transaction.
- Develop expertise in controlling the system, develop new reports and be able to train staff in processing data.
- Support Finance coordinator in monthly and quarterly and yearly reports required to HQ including but not limited to (Cash forecast, lease schedule, Month closure package, Yearend closure package, address HQ notes on closure of month/Year)
- Identify and resolve system errors or discrepancies, escalate to service now when needed.
- Support in Production and address of required monthly and ad hoc financial reports (Analytical Package, Vendor, Financial Exposure Request, accrued expenses, pending PO…. etc.)

**6- Team Leadership and Capacity Building**

Supervise, mentor, and develop accounting and finance staff to ensure high-quality performance and professional growth.

Establish clear objectives, performance expectations, and accountability mechanisms for finance team members.

Build staff capacity on accounting principles, internal controls, financial systems, compliance requirements, and organizational policies.

Foster a collaborative and high-performing work environment that promotes continuous learning and improvement**.**

Establish very collaborative workspace with all other departments stakeholders, to excel the teamwork and fill gaps and address cross departmental related issues in collaborative way and on time**.**

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

Bachelor’s degree in accounting, or Finance or CPA.

Proficient in Microsoft (MS) suite applications; experience in using advanced MS Excel is essential

**Work Experience:**

Minimum of Seven years’ accounting experience.

Minimum of 2 years’ experience in Audit-related performance.

Minimum of one year knowledge of an accounting system package such as Integra system is preferable

Experience with an International NGO preferably.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Validated sense of professional discretion, integrity, and ability to handle complex situations diplomatically and to effective resolution.

jobs.title: Environment & Energy Officer - Nakivale Refugee Settlement
jobs.body:
**About HEKS/EPER:**  
HEKS/EPER (Swiss Church Aid) is a faith-based international development and humanitarian organization committed to justice, human dignity, and sustainable development. In Uganda and South Sudan, our work focuses on supporting marginalized communities and building resilience through a triple nexus approach that integrates humanitarian response, sustainable development, and peacebuilding. We promote a rights-based, participatory, and conflict-sensitive approach that upholds dignity, inclusion, and accountability to affected populations.

**Standard functions:**

The Environment & Energy Officer will lead the environmental restoration, natural resource management and clean energy components of the project Empowering Youth and Women through Inclusive Skills Development (EWISE) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement. The project aims to improve the self-reliance and inclusive economic participation of vulnerable youth and women in refugee and host communities while enhancing environmental restoration and reducing pressure on natural resources.

The Environment & Energy Officer will coordinate, implement and monitor project interventions on natural resources management, especially watershed management inputs, community and institutional woodlot management, and the integration of gender through Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) with focused targeting of youth and women. The Officer will also design community-led plastic waste collection and recycling hubs, and will ensure that environmental safeguards, climate adaptation and sustainable energy considerations are integrated across the project.

In addition, the Officer will provide technical support on environment, climate and energy across other projects of the country programme, dedicating approximately 10% of the position's time to technical guidance and promoting consistent application of environmental safeguards and scale-up of sustainable energy approaches across the country programme.

M**ain responsibilities:**

**1. Programme Strategy and Implementation**

- Ensure effective and efficient planning and implementation according to approved budgets, workplan and HEKS/EPER policies.
- Ensure the project adopts the humanitarian–development–peace nexus approach and aligns with the thematic areas of livelihoods, conflict transformation, climate adaptation, and protection.
- Conduct environmental, climate-risk and energy assessments to inform project targeting, design, and implementation and guide the design of interventions on natural resources management at the community and institutional level.
- Design interventions that promote sustainable energy solutions that complement woodlot restoration, such as fuel-efficient stoves, clean-cooking practices and woodlot-based fuelwood management plans, to reduce pressure on natural resources.
- Develop strategies and promote approaches that strengthen integration and inter-linkages of climate-smart agriculture, agroforestry, reforestation, sustainable land management, water conservation, soil and water protection, and biodiversity-friendly practices.
- Provide technical input to project proposals across the country programme, ensuring environment, climate and energy principles are integrated into context analyses, theories of change and results frameworks.

**2. Project Cycle Management (PCM)**

- Coordinate the targeting, selection and engagement of youth and women as change agents, using vulnerability, capacity and gender-inclusion criteria.
- Support the establishment and strengthening of woodlot management committees, including management plans, bylaws, benefit-sharing and conflict-resolution arrangements and gender-balanced leadership.
- Design and deliver specialized training for community members and institutions on woodlot restoration, including nursery management, planting, maintenance, protection, and sustainable harvesting, with integrated modules on gender equality, safeguarding, and conflict sensitivity.
- Conduct sensitization and awareness sessions in institutions on environmental protection, climate change and energy efficiency and strengthen the capacity of school Eco-clubs to mainstream environmental protection in schools.
- Support plastic waste collection and recycling, including establishing community-led recycling hubs and working with the MSD Officer to link collection groups to recyclers and green business opportunities.
- Conduct environmental and social safeguard screening of project sites and activities (including woodlots, nurseries and recycling hubs), develop and monitor mitigation measures, including safe waste handling.
- Work with the MEAL team to track log frame indicators (including tree survival, area restored and waste collected), conduct assessments, and document success stories, case studies and lessons learned; contribute to the internal mid-term and end-term reviews.
- Provide technical assistance and capacity building to schools and community structures on woodlot restoration, watershed management, environmental safeguards and sustainable energy.

**3. Donor Compliance, Reporting and Representation**

- Ensure compliance with donor contract, HEKS/EPER's Field Financial and Administrative Guidelines (FFAG), and national environmental regulations as applicable.
- Prepare high-quality narrative inputs for donor reports, programme briefs and case studies on woodlot restoration, tree survival, sustainable energy and plastic waste recycling, in consultation with the MEAL Officer and Grants and Acquisition Coordinator, ensuring donor visibility requirements are met.
- Represent HEKS/EPER in environment and energy coordination platforms at settlement and district level (OPM, UNHCR, Isingiro District Local Government, CRRF structures) and build partnerships with environment partners and institutions, especially schools and community structures.

**4. Budget Oversight and Financial Accountability**

- Develop project workplans, procurement plans and budget follow-ups (BFUs) to contribute to monthly forecasts and variance analysis. Review and approve procurement requests and expenditure plans within delegated thresholds.

**5. MEAL and Learning**

- Contribute to organisational learning on climate resilience, environmental restoration and energy access.

**6. Team Management and Capacity/Building**

- Ensure age, gender, disability, conflict sensitivity (Do No Harm) and environmental considerations are mainstreamed in all activities.
- Promote team cohesion and ensure staff, partners and trainers adhere to Do No Harm, Protection and HRBA principles and to HEKS/EPER's Gender and Diversity, PSEAH and child safeguarding policies.

**Any other task relevant to this role, assigned by the Supervisor.**

**Minimum requirements**

- Bachelor's degree in environmental science, Natural Resource Management, Forestry, Agroforestry, Climate Change, Renewable Energy, Environmental Engineering, Agriculture or a related field (a master's degree is an added advantage).
- Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in environmental management, woodlot restoration/agroforestry, watershed management, climate adaptation, sustainable energy or natural resource management in humanitarian and/or development settings.
- Demonstrated experience in environmental and social safeguards, environmental risk assessment, community mobilisation, training and field monitoring.
- Knowledge of tree nursery and woodlot management, fuel-efficient stoves and clean-cooking technologies, solar energy, waste management, plastic recycling or circular-economy approaches.
- Experience working in refugee-hosting contexts and with refugee and host communities, women, youth and persons with disabilities.
- Strong report-writing, data collection and analysis skills; proficiency in MS Office and data tools (Excel, KoboToolbox, PowerPoint; GIS or Power BI preferred).
- Fluency in English; knowledge of Runyankole/Rukiga, Kinyarwanda, Kinyabwisha, Swahili or French is an added advantage.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.body:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organisation that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** Project Manager

**Code**: SR-60-10330

**Duty station:** Mykolaiv with regular field visits to Kharkiv

**Starting date:** 01/12/2026

**Contract duration:** until 14/07/2028

**Reporting to:** Head of Programme

**Functional supervisor:**

**Supervision of:** CW/PSS Team Leaders, MAMs and GFFO staff

**Type of duty station:** Non-family duty station

## **General context of the project**

The war in Ukraine, which started on the 24th of February 2022, shows no signs of abating, and continues to drive increasing humanitarian needs across the country. Access concerns and humanitarian needs are particularly high in eastern Kharkivska, Sumska oblasts and southern Khersonska oblast, where the conflict is intensifying and critical infrastructure damage prevents civilians from accessing basic services.

Today INTERSOS is present in Odeska, Mykolaivska, Khersonska and Kharkivska Oblasts with bases of operations in Kharkiv, Kherson, Mykolaiv, Odesa, and Kyiv, allowing a wide geographical coverage. Moreover, INTERSOS is currently implementing Health, Protection, and NFIs interventions, funded by OCHA, AICS, GFFO and ECHO, encompassing several components: distribution of medicines to Regional Health Departments and shelters and equipment for clinics, Cash for Health, mobilisation of Protection mobile teams, establishment of community-based protection mechanisms, case management for CP/PWSN cases, psychosocial support (PSS), Protection Monitoring (PM), and distribution of material assistance to vulnerable individuals and households.

## **General purpose of the position**

The Project Manager ensures constant engagement by/with different support departments to ensure timely support to the project team.

The Project Manager is the budget holder for the whole GFFO-funded project grant/budget and supervises/monitors closely the financial planning, liquidity planning and budget utilisation/burn rate monitoring.

The financial/budget management is the final responsibility of the project manager for the specific project, and he/she must ensure that this goes together with a close log frame and work plan monitoring.

## **Main responsibilities and tasks**

**General:**

- Ensures the planning, implementation and monitoring/evaluation and sets targets as included in the project description. Flag significant deviations from the programme implementation plan and estimated expenditures; alert relevant staff.
- Guarantee efficient financial management as the main budget holder for the project in compliance with INTERSOS’ model and donor regulations.
- Team/HR management (staff and volunteers)
- Deliver quality project activity reporting, including findings in terms of impact/changes at the level of beneficiaries achieved through the project, compliant and consistent reporting per INTERSOS and donor requirements, in collaboration with the HQ Grants Unit
- Develop a clear understanding of the INTERSOS programme and country strategy among the project team – ensure also timely input/feedback by the team on strategic issues.
- Support the head of the programme in programme/project development.
- Ensure that programme delivery matches INTERSOS and donor technical minimum standards and seek technical section and MEAL department guidance and tools.
- Ensure a clear overview of actors and services in the area of intervention, permitting development and implementation of partnerships and referral pathways.
- Administrative and office support activities (agreements, amendments, signed reports, communications, etc.), ensuring the documentation cycle is up-to-date and that all departments’ requirements are aligned and addressed.

**Detailed responsibilities and tasks:**

- Ensure the full and timely implementation of the project proposal as approved, proactively respecting deadlines for reporting:
- Project kick-off and presentation/sharing of the project with teams
- Review and prepare a detailed activity plan with the team
- Verification of the targeting of beneficiaries

**Financial management and procurement:**

- Prepare, monitor and implement the financial and procurement plan.
- Prepare financial plan
- Approval of all purchases/contracting and budget line allocations
- Verify the bookkeeping entries in the INTERSOS accounting spreadsheets (JOURNAL): verify budget line allocations, budget expenditure status against actual delivery and the financial plan for the remainder of the project implementation period
- Ensure, for all purchases/contracting of goods/services/supplies, the correct INTERSOS procurement guidelines are applied and properly documented, in coordination with the Finance and Logistics departments.
- Verify the list of expenditures before finalising the interim and final financial reports
- Holds final responsibility for verification of all support documents’ completeness and correctness.

**People management:**

- Agree on and establish clear reporting and communication lines
- Team recruitment: liaises with the HR Department to secure up-to-date HR files.
- Permanent on-the-job coaching of teams to work on quality in delivery.
- Manage and evaluate the performance of the project staff.
- Conduct weekly and monthly meetings with the team to review the planning and discuss the main concerns to focus on for the upcoming period.
- Continuous/fast verification of data quality collected and received from field staff.
- Ensure teams respect INTERSOS rules and guidelines for the mission and adhere to INTERSOS’s Code of Conduct and Charter of Values.

**Monitoring & evaluation:**

- Ensure monitoring and verification for the targeting of beneficiaries.
- Applying a results-based management approach, monitor the project outcomes, in addition to the outputs and activities, including changes at the household and community level achieved through the project.
- Undertake (if the security situation allows) field visits to provide technical guidance and supervision to the team and to monitor the progress and quality of the different project activities.

**Reporting:**

- Ensure quality reporting on achievements through daily short briefings, monthly and weekly planning presented against weekly and monthly performance reports containing clear quantitative and qualitative information related to the activities.
- Secure regular reporting per team and compile, review and analyse reports on a monthly basis, to be reflected in INTERSOS’s Project Appraisal Tool.
- Prepare ad hoc progress reporting for the donor and official required interim and final project reports; prepare interim and final narrative reports for the donor in a timely and qualitative manner, looking into achievements against outcomes and outputs; and reflect lessons learnt clearly into recommendations for future programming.
- Holds final responsibility for all support documents (means of verification) and general project documents.
- Delivers regular communication products (including pictures) on the project to be used by the INTERSOS communication department in different outlets.

**Coordination and representation:**

- Support the Programme/Technical Coordinator(s) in attending cluster meetings and ensure timely reporting of highlights and relevant information for the intervention area.
- Participate in regular meetings with the donor representatives and partners and facilitate field visits by donor missions (when security allows), in coordination with the Programme Coordinator.
- Ensure systematic information and update sharing with the head of Programme
- Perform any other related duties as required.

## **Required profile and experience**

**Education**

- Advanced university degree in Social Sciences, Political Sciences, International Relations, Humanitarian and International Cooperation or a related field

**Professional Experience**

- Minimum 3 years of professional experience in the management of a humanitarian project/programme, including financial management and logistics responsibilities
- Minimum 1 year of experience in the implementation of multi-sector humanitarian programming

**Professional Requirements**

- Experience in complex emergency settings and insecure countries
- Administration, finance and budget management skills
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)
- Analytical thinking, analysis capacity and strategic program development skills
- Experience in establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with donors and government counterparts, and with donors compliance and reporting

**Languages**

- Fluent knowledge of English (written and spoken)

**Personal requirements**

- Strong representation and negotiation skills
- Ability to ensure quick quality delivery in stressful environment
- Ability to adhere to deadlines and respect line management
- Strong interpersonal skills: communication, diplomatic skills and problem-solver
- Leadership, people management and development
- Organization and problem solving
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles

## **General conditions and benefits:**

- **Salary grid:** 11 - 3.430€ - 3.868€ monthly gross
- **Accommodation:** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R:** INTERSOS staff required to work for extended periods at duty stations under hazardous, stressful and difficult conditions are granted a regular and mandatory period of Rest and Recuperation (R&R). This is due to protecting their health and well-being and ensuring optimal work performance upon the resumption of their duties, while, at the same time, preserving the operational readiness of the Organisation. R&R benefits are not financial compensation for the degree of hardship and insecurity of a duty station. Eligibility: staff members recruited as international field staff whose contract states one R&R Duty Station as the main Duty Station and whose contract duration is equal to or longer than 4 calendar months. R&R: 7 days of psycho-physical recovery every 8 weeks + 1000€ allowance.
- **Remuneration:** The monthly remuneration is defined, for each position, according to the standard salary grid and function grid, taking into account the experience of the selected candidate. It is communicated during the HR interview, or at any rate during the first stage of the selection process.
- **Transportation:** Round-trip flights for the humanitarian. For any mission lasting at least 9 months, an additional flight ticket to the Country of residence and return to the mission is covered by the Organisation for the humanitarian worker.
- **Medical insurance:** Injuries and death insurance; civil liability insurance, reimbursement for vaccines, medical certificate and PCR test for deployment; psychosocial support on request for the humanitarian worker.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS covers the costs and visa support for the humanitarian worker.
- **Annual Leave:** 2.5 days per month
- **Induction:** Online orientation course: each new staff member receives preparatory training before departure, adequate to provide the necessary information related to the structure of INTERSOS and the main decision-making processes and working tools, in order to facilitate entry into the Organisation.
- **Note 1:** INTERSOS applies a “Learning & Development Policy” which includes the possibility to receive capacitation and participate in internal and external training. Priority will be given to the staff working for INTERSOS for over two years.
- **Note 2:** The categorisation of Accompanied, RnR, and Unaccompanied Duty stations is subject to security criteria, access to health and education services, and is non-negotiable.

jobs.title: Market Systems Development Officer (MSD) - Nakivale Refugee Settlement
jobs.body:
**About HEKS/EPER:**  
HEKS/EPER (Swiss Church Aid) is a faith-based international development and humanitarian organization committed to justice, human dignity, and sustainable development. In Uganda and South Sudan, our work focuses on supporting marginalized communities and building resilience through a triple nexus approach that integrates humanitarian response, sustainable development, and peacebuilding. We promote a rights-based, participatory, and conflict-sensitive approach that upholds dignity, inclusion, and accountability to affected populations.

**Standard functions:**

The Market Systems Development (MSD) Officer will lead the implementation of the skilling, enterprise development, private sector engagement and market linkage components of the project Empowering Youth and Women through Inclusive Skills Development (EWISE) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement. The project aims to improve the self-reliance and inclusive economic participation of vulnerable youth and women in refugee and host communities while enhancing environmental restoration. The MSD Officer will be responsible for the delivery of market-driven vocational and business skills training, apprenticeships and job placements with the private sector, business development services (BDS), market linkages, and financial inclusion. The MSD Officer works closely with the co-implementing partner, Department of Possibility (DoP), the Office of the Prime Minister (OPM), Refugee Welfare Councils, Isingiro District Local Government, UNHCR, the Directorate of Industrial Training (DIT) and private sector actors, and coordinates with the MEAL, Grants, Finance, and Procurement & Logistics teams to ensure quality, safeguarding, accountability, donor compliance and learning are integrated in the project management cycle. In addition, the MSD officer will provide technical support Market Systems Development (MSD) across other projects, dedicating approximately 10% of the position’s time to technical guidance, and promoting consistent application of the MSD approach across the country programme.

**Main responsibilities:**

**1. Programme Strategy and Implementation**

- Ensure effective and efficient planning and implementation according to approved budgets, workplan and HEKS/EPER policies
- Ensure that the project adopts the humanitarian-development Nexus approach and is aligned to the thematic areas of livelihoods, conflict transformation, climate adaptation, and protection
- Lead the labour market and skills demand assessment to ensure its integration into the project implementation cycle.
- Conduct private sector mapping and analysis of the systemic barriers to transition to work and dignified employment in Nakivale, Isingiro and Mbarara markets, including assessment of facilities and potential private sector actors.
- Ensure development of gender inclusive and appropriate Assessment and Training Packages (ATPs) and integration of a market systems approach to ensure interventions respond to market skill needs.
- Provide technical input to the development of project proposals across the country programme, ensuring that Market Systems Development (MSD) principles are appropriately integrated into context analyses, market assessments, theories of change, intervention strategies, and results frameworks.

**2. Project Cycle Management (PCM)**

- Coordinate beneficiary profiling and gender-inclusive selection of women and youth using vulnerability capacity assessment and market-alignment criteria.
- Oversee the development of inclusive training materials and curricula, with the private sector engaged in the design of the ATPs and support the profiling and engagement of trainers, instructors and facilitators.
- Ensure decentralized zonal-based technical, vocational and business skills training in the three zones of Nakivale through engagement of local artisans, including life skills, financial literacy, entrepreneurship and soft skills (FLESS), digital literacy and workplace readiness, with gender equality, safeguarding and conflict-sensitivity modules integrated.
- Coordinate beneficiary capacity and competency assessments, and certification of trainees with the Directorate of Industrial Training (DIT) to ensure work readiness.
- Support specialized training and market linkages of youth and women in community-based plastic-waste collection as a green business.
- Identify, verify and engage artisans, SMEs, cooperatives, employers and service providers in private sector for work-placements, apprenticeships and on-the-job training.
- In consultation with the Head of Programs, Head of Finance and Administration and Grants and Acquisition Coordinator, develop and ensure safe apprenticeships, job placements and private sector linkages through formal agreements and Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs).
- Conduct structured risk assessments of host enterprises (employer policies, feedback and response mechanisms, labour law compliance, safe pathways to self-reliance) to ensure the safeguarding of trainees in line with the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS).
- Support the establishment and strengthening of micro and small businesses and green enterprises by managing the selection and distribution of toolkits, start-up kits and start-up capital.
- Design and deliver tailored Business Development Services, business incubation and mentorship to trainees.
- Develop a gender inclusive business tracker to track trainee graduation and enterprise growth and use it to tailor BDS to each business's stage and support a graduation pathway from aid dependency to dignified employment or self-employment.
- Facilitate contracts between groups and buyers, traders and local markets, trade fairs and exhibitions; link plastic-waste collection groups with recycling companies and aggregators to secure reliable market access and fair prices.
- Work with the MEAL team to track logframe indicators, conduct tracer studies, and document success stories, case studies and impact stories; contribute to the internal mid-term and end-term reviews.

**3. Donor Compliance, Reporting and Representation**

- Ensure compliance with donor contracts, HEKS/EPER’s Field Financial and Administrative Guidelines (FFAG), and national regulations as applicable to each thematic area.
- In consultation with the MEAL Officer and Grants and Acquisition Coordinator, ensure communications, visibility and advocacy efforts are aligned with programme goals.
- Prepare high-quality narrative inputs for donor reports, programme briefs and case studies on skilling, placements and enterprise development.
- Liaise with the MEAL Officer and lead the preparation of programme briefs, success stories, and case studies in compliance with HEKS/EPER and donor guidelines and requirements.
- Represent HEKS/EPER in livelihoods and economic inclusion of working groups and coordination platforms at settlement and district level (OPM, UNHCR, Isingiro District Local Government, CRRF structures) and build partnerships with the private sector.

**4. Budget Oversight and Financial Accountability**

- Develop project workplans, procurement plans and budget follow-ups (BFUs) to contribute to monthly forecasts and variance analysis.
- Review and approve procurement requests and expenditure plans within delegated thresholds.

**5. Partner Capacity Strengthening, MEAL and Learning**

- Provide technical assistance and capacity building to DoP on BDS, market systems approach, digitalisation, MEAL and safeguarding.

**6. Team Management and Capacity/Building**

- Provide day-to-day technical guidance to the project team and to DoP field staff working on skilling, business support and VSLAs; support performance appraisals of staff as delegated.
- Support HR processes such as the recruitment and onboarding of project staff and trainers.
- Ensure age, gender, disability, conflict sensitivity (Do No Harm) and environmental considerations are mainstreamed in all activities.
- Promote team cohesion and ensure staff, partners, trainers and private sector partners adhere to Do No Harm, Protection and HRBA principles and to HEKS/EPER's Gender and Adversity, PSEAH and child safeguarding policies.

**Any other task relevant to this role, assigned by the Supervisor.**

**Minimum requirements**

- Bachelor's degree in business administration, Economics, Agribusiness, Entrepreneurship, Development Studies, Vocational Education or a related field (a master's degree is an added advantage).
- Minimum 4 years of relevant experience in market systems development, skills development/TVET, youth and women economic empowerment, enterprise development or private sector engagement in humanitarian and/or development settings.
- Strong knowledge of project cycle management, budget control, donor reporting and community engagement.
- Demonstrated experience in business development services (BDS), business incubation, coaching and mentorship/apprenticeships, job placement and building partnerships or MoUs with private sector actors, artisans and SMEs.
- Experience working in refugee-hosting contexts and with refugee and host communities, women, youth and persons with disabilities.
- Good knowledge and understanding of DO NO HARM principles, safeguarding and the Human Rights Based Approach in development.
- Proficiency in MS Office and data tools (Excel, Power BI, KoboToolbox, etc.).
- Fluency in English; knowledge of Runyankole/Rukiga, Kinyarwanda, Kinyabwisha, Swahili or French is an added advantage.

jobs.title: Child Rights Situation Analysis Methodology and Reporting Consultancy Service Providers
jobs.body:
- **Duration**: Estimated level of effort: 30 working days
- **Expected starting date**: ASAP
- **Location**: Ukraine

**Background on Save the Children**

Save the Children is the leading global independent organisation for children. Save the Children believes every child deserves a future. Around the world, we work every day to give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm. When crisis strikes, and children are most vulnerable, we are always among the first to respond and the last to leave. We ensure children’s unique needs are met and their voices are heard. We deliver lasting results for millions of children, including those hardest to reach.

**Objective of the Methodology and Reporting Consultancy Service Provider**

This consultancy has two objectives:

1. To develop a comprehensive CRSA Plan and Research Methodology Guide that will guide the implementation of Save the Children Ukraine's first Child Rights Situation Analysis.
2. To synthesize all collected evidence (secondary desk review, primary data collected by a Research Company, and partner/child contributions) into the final CRSA Report.

The consultancy service provider will ensure that the methodology and final CRSA report:

- are grounded in a Child Rights-Based Approach;
- integrates gender equality through an intersectional lens, alongside disability inclusion, climate and conflict sensitivity throughout the analysis;
- enables meaningful participation of children and local civil society organisations throughout the process; and
- provides practical guidance for conducting safe, ethical and high-quality research.

**Scope of Work**

The Methodology and Reporting Consultancy service provider will lead the design of the research framework and tools, as well as the final data synthesis and reporting for Save the Children Ukraine's Child Rights Situation Analysis (CRSA). Secondary data review, primary data collection and fieldwork will be undertaken by a separately selected research company (under existing FWA) under the methodological guidance of the consultancy service provider.

**Phase 1: Conduct desk review of secondary sources**

Review relevant Save the Children guidance, programme documents, country reports and external evidence to identify existing knowledge, evidence gaps and priorities for the CRSA.

Review and integrate findings and documentation from internal consultations (facilitated and conducted by the Save the Children team) with Save the Children staff, civil society partners, children, and other relevant stakeholders to inform the CRSA design.

**Phase 2: Develop the CRSA Methodology Guide**

Based on the contextual review and consultations, develop a detailed CRSA Methodology Guide, setting out the governance arrangements, participation approach and implementation framework for the analysis. The plan should include:

- analytical framework
- governance structure, roles and responsibilities
- stakeholder engagement approach
- participation strategy for children, civil society partners and other stakeholders
- indicative implementation timeline
- draft table of contents for the final CRSA report.
- sampling strategy
- mixed-methods research design
- data collection tools and protocols
- guidance for desk review, surveys, focus group discussions (FGDs) and key informant interviews (KIIs)
- ethical protocols, safeguarding measures and referral procedures
- integration of gender equality, disability inclusion, climate and conflict sensitivity throughout the methodology
- quality assurance and data validation approach.

**Phase 4: Revision and validation**

Present the draft CRSA Methodology Guide for review by Save the Children technical teams. Revise the document based on consolidated feedback before final approval.

**Phase 5: Handover**

Provide a structured oral handover of the approved CRSA Plan and Research Methodology Guide to the selected research company, including a briefing on the methodological framework, research tools, quality standards, safeguarding requirements and key implementation considerations. Maintain ad-hoc methodological guidance during the fieldwork phase to address critical queries and ensure data quality.

**Phase 6: Data synthesis and drafting of the report**

Receive and validate cleaned primary data and the desk review report from the research company. Triangulate internal SCI contextual evidence, desk review, primary field data, and co-authored contributions from children. Produce and submit the first draft of the CRSA Report and Executive Summary for internal review and feedback by the CRSA Steering Team (Annex 1).

**Phase 7: Partners’ validation, revisions, and report finalization**

Integrate all consolidated feedback and recommendations from Save the Children and civil society following the SC-led validation process, finalize the reporting package (second draft of the CRSA Report and Executive Summary), and submit it for formal approval and sign-off by Save the Children.

All Save the Children employees and consultancy service provider are expected to work in accordance with the organization’s safeguarding policies, code of conduct, and core values: creativity, accountability, integrity, collaboration, and ambition. These attitudes and beliefs guide our actions and relationships. The consultancy service provider must uphold these principles in all interactions, deliverables, and engagements with children and adults.

**Qualifications and experience**

- At least five years of professional experience in social research, child rights, child protection, or other relevant social science fields.
- In-depth understanding and practical application of the child rights-based approach, international child rights standards, and the child protection context.
- Proven track record in leading and coordinating Child Rights Situation Analyses (CRSA), with demonstrated expertise in synthesizing findings into comprehensive final reports.
- Proven experience in designing CRSA-specific research methodologies, analytical framework matrices, and data collection toolkits (both qualitative and quantitative).
