- Based on the approved RWP, our client is supporting MNCAH and EPI services in the country and working to improve coordination, develop policies, strategies, and guidelines, support implementation and monitoring of activities. extenders are tasked to facilitate and support our client programme activities implementation and monitoring tasks that cannot be done by our client staff due to accessibility, security, and scale. Which make extenders modality the most reliable and efficient way to support those tasks.
- Extender will be based at their area of responsibility, and usually selected from communities in same area for easy mobility and to reduce security risks, and transportation time and cost. These extenders are not given task that is supposed to be done normally by our client staff.

Role objectives

TASK TO BE PERFORMED

- Conduct regular situation monitoring in specific areas based on requests by the programme or Zonal Office, to assess the overall humanitarian situation and document the needs of affected populations, in particular women and children health needs.
- Provide technical services to our client projects primarily in hard-to-reach areas, through ensuring regular and systematic technical advice, quality assurance and technical guidance to implementing partners and counterparts, for the efficient implementation of our client programmes and effective achievement of results for the benefit of Afghani children and women.
- Identify capacity and technical gaps of implementing partners and counterparts and provide technical support to ensure capacity building and on job training as needed.
- Support the implementation of Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNT) supported by our client through technical support and capacity building, and monitor the service implementation and quality. and work with partners at the provincial level to improve MHNT programme results.
- Monitor the work of health facilities supported through our client CERF and other funds using the common checklists and tools.
- Support EPI programme routine immunization activities including -but not limited to- service delivery, cold chain system, vaccine and non-vaccine supplies, information system.
- Support emergency preparedness and response activities implementation and monitoring.
- Report any suspected PSEA case directly to the responsible our client focal point and inform the programme specialist.
- Report any suspected fraud case to the Zonal programme specialist or relevant our client staff.
- Coordinate the monthly working\\monitoring plan with the regional extender, and share the progress and visits repots on timely manner.
- Participating in PHCC, Staff meeting with SP, EPI sub comettee and relvent meetings.

Conduct regular visits to monitor Health programme activities supported by our client, and facilitate our client staff programmatic visits, with a focus on:

- Assessing programme implementation by Implementing Partners through PCAs (Programme Cooperation Agreements) and SSFAs (Small-Scale Funding Agreements) as well as programme implementation by partners and agencies according to the our client Afghanistan Country Office Work Plans.
- Checking EPI supplies chain systems and equipment in place and their functionality status, including following SOPs in vaccine storage and utilization.
- Supporting Health information system and data registration reviews and assessments, and the implementation of Data Quality Improvement plans and microplanning activities.
- Verifying health supplies are delivered to target beneficiaries in line with relevant programme documents and flag any delays and bottlenecks.
- Conducting post-distribution monitoring (PDM) of supplies to assess beneficiaries’ feedback in terms of the quality, timeliness and relevance of supplies delivered. Other end-user monitoring of specific programmes will be conducted as required by the Zonal Office.
- Collecting direct feedback form beneficiaries and affected population about the situation and needs, and the suitability of the services provided and how to improve.

DELIVERABLE(s)

- Provincial need assessment for implementation of mobile health teams completed
- Monthly monitoring of mobile health and nutrition teams service delivery points conducted.
- Monthly report of availability of ORS/Zinc stock with CHWs submitted
- Coordination, and monitoring of community mobilization/engagement activities facilitated
- Need assessment of CHWs training for target provinces completed
- Training of CHWs supported by our client monitored
- Routine EPI monitoring checklists completed and reported (this checklist includes all components of Routine EPI).
- Oriented on new RI activities e.g., accelerated immunization, Measles interventions, awareness raising activities (IEC, media broadcast, etc.).
- Percentage of HFs equipped with SDDs reported.
- Emergency need assessment of emergency affected areas completed
- Our client supported emergency activities monitored including HF under the Sahatmandi CERF support.
- Field visits implemented and reported timely with the required quality.
- Situation monitoring reports and needs assessment data is provided.
- Programme monitoring reports are developed and shared with zonal office programme officers\\specialists and reginal health extender including progress information, gaps and challenges, supplies monitoring, and beneficiaries’ feedback.
- Partner’s capacity in area of extender technical expertise is built.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Minimum Qualification and Experience:

- Having certificate in health, medicine, public health, nursing, midwife or related field.
- Minimum of 2 years of experience in in health, medicine, public health, nurse, midwife or related field.
- Proficiency in data analysis and interpretation.
- Excellent communication skills for effective collaboration with healthcare professionals and stakeholders.
- Proven ability to contribute to the enhancement of health programs through data-driven insights.
- Reporting skills

Team management

 This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.

jobs.title: Sudan - Head of Programmes
HEAD Of Middle East Durable Solutions Platform
jobs.body:
The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunity for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfilment of the wish to return home.

The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956, and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced.

All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation.

DRC hosts the Middle East Durable Solutions Platform (ME DSP), a membership-based NGO platform established by DRC, NRC and IRC and later joined by Oxfam, ACF and Save the Children to strengthen evidence, programming and advocacy on solutions to displacement in and from Syria. In 2022 its scope was widened to Iraq and Yemen. Following a period of hibernation since 2023, ME DSP has secured core donor funding and is in the process of re-establishing its membership, reviewing its governance and operating model, and diversify its partnerships. ME DSP is one of three DRC-hosted solutions platforms, alongside ReDSS (East Africa and Great Lakes) and ADSP (Asia), and sits within the DRC Middle East, Asia and Europe Hub under the leadership of the Hub’s Executive Director.

The **Head of ME DSP** provides overall leadership, strategic direction and management of the Platform, a membership-based, consensus-driven platform of NGOs working on solutions to displacement across the Middle East. As the Platform’s principal convener, s/he leads engagement with members and governance structures, builds consensus around shared priorities and ensures delivery of agreed commitments; leads the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy agenda so that research is translated into programming and policy guidance; represents the Platform at senior level with members, governments and donors, UN agencies and policy makers at country regional and global levels; manages ME DSP grants, staff and consultants; and works in close collaboration with DRC’s sister platforms, ReDSS and ADSP.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Leadership, Governance and Management**

- Facilitate the implementation of the ME DSP Strategy 2026-2028, lead the regular review of the Platform’s work plans, and ensure ME DSP maintains a strategic, neutral and member-driven role that complements existing coordination mechanisms
- Lead the re-establishment of the Platform’s membership and the review of its governance and operating model, in line with Steering Committee decisions
- Lead annual planning and budgeting and report to the Steering Committee and members on progress, risks and results; maintain the risk matrix, commission periodic evaluation of ME DSP and integrate lessons learned
- Work in close collaboration with ReDSS and ADSP to share learning, align approaches and tools, and contribute to joint NGO engagement in global solutions fora
- Accountable for people management of direct reports, including recruitment, objective setting, performance management and staff development, and for the management of ME DSP consultants

**Membership Convening and Coordination**

- Act as the Platform’s principal convener. Design and facilitate member meetings, technical working groups and consultations in an inclusive and transparent manner that builds collective ownership of the Platform’s agenda and outputs
- Facilitate consensus-building among members, managing differing priorities and resolving issues that may affect Platform decisions and delivery
- Ensure effective coordination and information sharing among members and the Steering Committee, and support members’ engagement with the Platform at country, regional and global levels
- Lead a membership engagement strategy, including the onboarding of new members and clarity on members’ roles and contributions.

**Research, Evidence and Learning**

- Define and oversee the Platform’s research and knowledge management agenda with members, initiating and commissioning studies, managing researchers and research institutions, and ensuring methodologically rigorous, research ethics and relevance to programming and policy
- Lead the analysis of regional displacement and solutions data, strategies, policies and legislation; translate evidence into programming and policy guidance, briefing papers and policy briefs; and ensure quality control of all ME DSP publications and monitoring of their uptake
- Facilitate regular technical workshops and learning events and the roll-out of learning tools and training packages, ensuring cross-learning across countries and with global developments in solutions policy and practice
- Promote the meaningful engagement of displacement-affected communities and local civil society in the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy work

**Policy Engagement and External Representation**

- Represent the Platform at senior level with governments and national authorities, donors, UN agencies, international financial institutions, regional bodies and policy makers, building trusted relationships and navigating politically sensitive contexts with discretion and in line with humanitarian principles
- Oversee the development and implementation of the Platform’s policy and advocacy strategy with members, ensuring positions are evidence-based, agreed by members and coordinated with NGO fora and durable solutions working groups in the region
- Support members’ advocacy with governmental and inter-governmental actors and engage proactively in regional and global policy processes on solutions for displacement-affected populations
- Engage research institutions, think tanks and academia, and oversee high-quality external communications reflecting members’ agreed positions

**Business Development and Project Management**

- Manage existing and future grants, including budgets, work plans, monitoring and donor reporting, ensuring timely delivery and compliance with DRC and donor policies, including safeguarding
- Develop and implement a fundraising strategy to ensure financial sustainability, including donor engagement and partnerships, in coordination with the Steering Committee

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have **Experience and technical competencies** :

- Advanced university degree or equivalent in political science, international relations, humanitarian law, migration, Middle East studies, or related field
- Understanding of the regional displacement dynamics. Excellent understanding of
- At least 8 years' relevant experience, including 5 in people management and substantial experience leading, facilitating or coordinating a membership-based, consensus-driven consortium, network, NGO forum or inter-agency platform
- Expert knowledge of durable solutions to displacement and the relevant international frameworks, with demonstrated experience in complex and contested return and reintegration contexts
- In-depth knowledge of the displacement context of the Middle East, displacement in and from Syria, Iraq and Yemen, and of the political complexities, policy landscape and coordination architecture of the region
- Demonstrated strategic leadership, ability to manage competing priorities, and ensure accountability for results
- Proven experience in grant management, budget oversight and resource mobilization
- Proven experience in leading, conducting or commissioning research, or in working in close collaboration with researchers, and in translating evidence into programming and policy guidance
- Excellent convening, facilitation and networking skills, with the ability to build trust and broker consensus among diverse organizations; outstanding interpersonal and diplomatic skills, political and cultural sensitivity, tact and impartiality
- Excellent analytical and writing skills, with proven experience producing high quality research and policy briefs and presenting complex information in an accessible manner
- Demonstrated commitment to collaborative working across organizations and with sister platforms, ability to work in a multicultural environment, and flexibility, proactive engagement and high tolerance for change, complexity and unpredictability

**In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:**

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with DRC’s vision and values.

**Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. **Applications sent by email will not be considered.**

*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised deadline if a suitable candidate is identified.* “

**Location:** Jordan/Amman with potential travel in the region

**Contract length**: 1 year contract

**Start date;** 1 Jan 2027

**Closing date for applications:** 16-11-2026.

If you have questions or are facing problems with the online application process, please visit [drc.ngo/jobsupport](https://forms-hr.drc.dk/view.php?id=348161).

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://drc.ngo/).

jobs.title: Climate, Environment & Health Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Join MSF OCG as a Climate, Environment & Health Coordinator !**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

We are looking for a Climate, Environment & Health (CEH) Coordinator to join MSF OCG.

Reporting to the Deputy General Director, the CEH Coordinator is responsible for leading and coordinating OCG’s strategic approach to reducing the environmental impact of its activities, while strengthening the integration of the health and humanitarian consequences of climate change into operational planning.The position works closely with the Logistics, Medical, Communication and Operations departments, supporting field missions and contributing to more relevant, responsible and effective humanitarian operations.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

- Develop and implement OCG’s strategy to address climate change and environmental issues across its activities.
- Support the integration of climate risks and evolving patterns of climate-sensitive diseases into operational planning to strengthen the relevance of operational responses.
- Promote the reduction of environmental impacts across OCG’s activities to enhance the environmental responsibility of MSF operations.
- Coordinate cross-functional initiatives on climate and environmental issues to ensure alignment and consistency across OCG.
- Develop frameworks, guidelines, and tools to support teams in effectively addressing climate risks and environmental impacts.
- Monitor progress towards climate and environmental objectives to ensure accountability and continuous improvement, including overseeing the organisation’s annual carbon accounting process.
- Represent OCG in intersectional and external meetings on climate, environment, and health.

## Your profile

*Education*

- Essential: Advanced university degree in environmental health, climate change, sustainability, environmental engineering, or a related field.
- Desired: Certification in carbon accounting.

*Experience*

- Essential: Experience in a similar role or in leading cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders without direct hierarchical authority.
- Field experience with MSF or another humanitarian organization is an asset.

*Languages*

- English and French are mandatory.
- Additional languages are an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Carbon accounting.
- Environmental sustainability and climate change.
- Health and humanitarian impacts of climate change.
- Strategic planning and change management.
- Data analytics, monitoring, reporting, and performance tracking.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Strategic thinking.
- Influencing and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Coordination and facilitation skills.
- Communication and presentation skills.
- Project and change management skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment to diversity, gender-responsive, inclusive, and non-discriminatory behaviours and attitudes.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Geneva
- Ideal start date: 1st of December 2026
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 119’964.- to CHF 137’640.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

jobs.title: Project Evaluation Consultant
jobs.body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23684**  
Position Title: **Project Evaluation Consultant (Type B)**  
Duty Station City: **Port Vila**  
Duty Station Country: **Vanuatu**  
Contract Type: **Consultant B**  
*Recruiting Type:* **Consultancy**  
*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**  
Initial duration: **2 months**  
Closing date: **03 November 2026**

**Context:**

Since 2015, more than 30 per cent of Ni-Vanuatu citizens have experienced temporary or protracted displacement due to disasters. Vanuatu's approximately 300,000 people (Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics, 2020) spread across 83 islands are exposed to cyclones, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, ashfalls, earthquakes, mudslides, flooding and drought. As the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events increases due to climate change, disasters pose a primary threat to Vanuatu's national security and human development.

Tropical Cyclones (TC) Judy and Kevin (both of Category 4 intensity) made landfall over Vanuatu on 1 and 3 March 2023. TC Judy and Kevin affected an estimated 24,657 households (123,288 people) with 90 per cent of houses in Shefa and Tafea provinces destroyed or severely damaged. The cumulative impact of compounding events such as previous cyclones (TC Harold), high La Nina rainfall and COVID-19, has had a devastating impact on basic living conditions, access to basic services, livelihoods, and coping capacities. While traditional resilience in Vanuatu is strong, emergency preparedness needs strengthening at all levels - national, provincial, area council and community – particularly in light of intensifying climate change impacts in the Pacific.

In response, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is implementing a project to support the Vanuatu National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) in strengthening the capacity of national and provincial government institutions, Community Disaster and Climate Change Committees (CDCCCs), Area Councils, faith-based organizations, and community leaders — particularly women leaders — to develop and maintain safe and dignified evacuation arrangements during emergencies.

This builds on the existing work being undertaken by the Displacement and Evacuation Centre Management (DECM) Cluster which brings together key partners to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities. It will strengthen and extend the work of the DECM Cluster to provincial and community level, moving towards improved localization of emergency response measures in Vanuatu.

Specifically, the Sef Ples Blong Yumi Phase 2 project funded by the Government of Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), implemented by the National Disaster Management Office, Vanuatu in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration, supports the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness, coordination, and evacuation centre management across multiple hazards. The project focuses on strengthening the DECM Cluster’s coordination capacity, updating and rolling out the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and Evacuation Toolbox / Training Materials, improving information management systems, and supporting preparedness at national, provincial, and Area Council levels.

**The Objective of the project is:**

To contribute to the protection and resilience of people at risk of displacement in Vanuatu by supporting the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness and evacuation procedures.

The project will update and finalize the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and developing the Evacuations Toolbox / Training Materials for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to strengthen:

1. National, provincial and area council-level coordination of evacuations.
2. Capacity of communities, CDCCCs, faith-based groups to manage and lead their own community-based evacuations in ways that both draws on traditional knowledge about evacuations and increases protections for vulnerable groups, especially women, children, older people and people with disability.

The Outcomes and Outputs of this project are the following:

Outcome 1: Government, faith-based groups and communities have enhanced capacity to coordinate, develop, maintain and monitor safe, dignified evacuation accommodation in emergencies.

Output 1.1: Improved information management at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in sudden-onset emergencies.

Output 1.2: Improved coordination at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in emergencies.

Output 1.3: Updated National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines and Evacuations Toolbox for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

Output 1.4: Roll out of Evacuations Toolbox training for national trainers, Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Disaster Risk Reduction - Humanitarian

Project code: CC0083

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**The Final Evaluation Report shall include the following sections:**

- Executive Summary
- Introduction, objectives, methodology, and limitations
- Findings (relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, sustainability and cross-cutting issues)
- Discussions of outcomes and results
- Lessons learned and good practices (success factors and/or those which challenged performance)
- Conclusions
- Recommendations
- Annexes (i.e. TOR, Data Sources, Evaluation Matrix, etc.)
- Further details of the deliverables are:
    
    **Other general tasks to be undertaken as part of this assignment will include**
- Providing advice and input to project direction and methods.
- Reporting to and keeping up good communication with National Programme Officer and Project Manager.
- Attendance at project meetings online or in person.
- Meetings, where requested, with IOM Chief of Mission, IOM Project Staff, or Government of Vanuatu representatives.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Performance should be assessed according to the tangible and measurable deliverables of the work assignment as stated in Section 7 above.
- Payment instalments to be made upon the satisfactory completion of each of the deliverables and approval by the project manager.
- Performance will be assessed against the outputs as provided above.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- The evaluator should preferably have a master's degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 2 years of relevant professional experience.
- Or the evaluator should have a bachelors degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 4 years of relevant professional experience.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in carrying out similar evaluation assignments for projects related to humanitarian preparedness, response, recovery, disaster resilience, climate change, evacuation center management, or displacement and evacuation center management coordination.
- Demonstrated capacity to coordinate with and secure key informants (including government actors, community networks, other key stakeholders, and community participants) is required.
- Minimum 4 years of experience working with research, policy development, analysis, monitoring and evaluation, and program evaluation preferably in the field of climate change, disaster risk reduction, emergency response, and / or environment.
- Understanding of Vanuatu displacement, emergency response, evacuation centres, and climate change context are an advantage
- Experience of working in the Pacific region is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Good communication and coordination skills.
- Computer skills required (MS Word and basic MS Excel) for reporting.
- Strong facilitation, mentoring, and stakeholder coordination skills.

**Languages**

- For this consultancy, Fluency in Bislama and English language is required. Working knowledge of French is an advantage.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

One trip to Port Vila will be required as part of this ToR:  
Trip 1: Approximately 10 days (estimated early - December 2026 or early January 2027) – this travel is required to coordinate evaluation activities, attend meetings, and conduct key informant interviews. Exact dates of the trip to be coordinated between IOM Project Management Team and the selected evaluator(s).  
If budget allows a second trip can be considered in mid or late January 2027.  
IOM will cover costs relating to round trip airfares, accommodation, and a consultant / evaluator daily subsistence allowance. Travel and health insurance will not be covered by IOM and is the responsibility of the consultant / selected evaluator(s).

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at [this link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

- Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 1)

- Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

- Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.
- This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.
- This post is subject to only those holding a valid residence and work permit for the country where this position is based will be eligible for consideration.
- Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, verification of residency, visa, and authorizations by the concerned Government, where applicable.
- IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.
- IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.
- IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM online recruitment system. The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.
- For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: [IOM Careers and Job Vacancies](https://www.iom.int/careers)

jobs.title: Helios+ Center Assistant
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children. Since 2019, IRC Hellas implements an alternative care project for unaccompanied children and will now pilot this project to Greek born children and adults.

**SCOPE OF WORK:** Helios+ - Comprehensive Actions for the integration of Third Country Nationals in the Labor Market - (MIS 6016874) is a portfolio of regional Integration Projects, dedicated to fostering the integration of third-country nationals into Greece's labor market and society. Designed by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) with the support of the Government of Greece (GoG), co-financed by the European Union under the Regional Programs (RP) for 2021–2027 and aligns fully with Greece's National Strategy for Integration. HELIOS+ is committed to empowering Beneficiaries of International and Temporary Protection residing in Greece by providing them with the tools and resources needed to achieve socio-economic independence and actively participate in the Greek community, while promoting self-reliance and inclusion through a comprehensive set of services tailored to the needs of the target group.

In the Attica Region, International Rescue Committee Hellas participates as a partner of IOM Greece, together with Solidarity Now, in the consortium led by Caritas Hellas.

The IRC supports access to job counseling and job matching, life skills, education and psychosocial support – directly and in collaboration with partners. The IRC is recruiting a HELIOS+ Center assistant for the reception and registration of beneficiaries, providing first-level information, and guiding beneficiaries to the specialized services of the center. The HELIOS+ Center assistant will also be responsible for preparing the necessary documents for their registration, monitoring the security of the center, and ensuring the smooth operation of the center’s overall spaces and equipment.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Welcome and receive beneficiaries and visitors to the Center warmly and friendly**;**
- Provide information about the Center and its services to the beneficiaries of the subproject, as required**;**
- Provide administrative support to ensure the smooth daily operation of the Center**;**
- Manage the Center’s calendar and scheduling of sessions, appointments, etc., in coordination with the Center’s Manager**;**
- Manage the Center’s correspondence and communications (phone/email/mail)**;**
- Update and maintain a contact list**;**
- Effectively maintain filing systems, both electronic and paper-based**;**
- Collect and organize the data required for each beneficiary;
- Monitor the Center’s spaces and their security, maintain cleanliness and order, aim to ensure smooth and efficient operation, in close cooperation with the Center’s Manager;
- Other related duties as assigned by the subproject Coordinator;
- Participate in regular team meetings and external meetings as requested;

**REQUIREMENTS:**

- BA/BS Degree in Pedagogical Studies, Administrative Studies, and/or other related fields;
- At least three (3) years of experience in a corresponding position of responsibility, preferably in the field of humanitarian organizations;
- Excellent knowledge of Greek and English, spoken and written (level C1/C2).
- Computer skills, in particular word processing, excel spreadsheets and internet services;
- Excellent interpersonal, team and communication skills;
- Ability to organize and prioritize workload using initiative;
- Ability to work under pressure;

**PREFERRED EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS:**

- Experience in customer service.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks.
- Intercultural awareness and flexibility.
- Ability to work on own initiative and at the same time as part of a multicultural and interdisciplinary team.
- Knowledge of French, or Arabic, or Farsi, or Pashto, or Urdu is an advantage.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

Working hours: 9:00-17:00

Travel and other requirements: Occasionally to other areas of IRC programs within Athens

**This position is expected to end on May 30, 2027.**

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: £1,300 - £1,590/month). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Administrative Assistant, Global Board Engagement
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background/IRC Summary**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is a leading global humanitarian organization in roughly 40 countries and in 25 cities in the United States. The IRC responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to recover and regain control of their futures.

As the IRC approaches its 100th year of service in 2033, we remain passionate about ensuring that the impact of our programs and the influence of our ideas empower people caught in crisis to make lasting change in their lives. The President’s Office supports the IRC to deliver on its mission through strategic and focused organization-wide priority setting and delivery. The External Relations (ER) department raises revenue and the profile of the IRC, enabling the organization to respond to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and help people to survive and rebuild their lives. Within ER, the Global Board Engagement team is directly responsible for all Board practices, engagement, and strategy for the Board of Directors and Advisors (B&A) for IRC, Inc.

**Job Overview**

The Global Board Engagement team supports IRC's Global Board of Directors and Board of Advisors. We are looking for an assistant who is exceptionally detail-oriented and highly organized, with a proven track record of managing complex logistics and information accurately. Board work depends on materials, schedules, records, and communications being accurate, timely, and handled with discretion. You will work closely with the President's Office and with internal and external leadership, and you will see how your work contributes to IRC's broader operations and programs. The right person will be deeply committed to IRC's mission of helping people whose lives are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future.

**Responsibilities**

- Committee support: Attend and take minutes for four to six Board committees, each meeting three to four times a year. Prepare minutes for external sharing and condense them into two-page summaries for the Board of Directors.
- Scheduling and meeting logistics: Coordinate annual committee and Board meeting schedules, orientation sessions, and ad hoc meetings with internal and external leadership. Provide day-of logistical support at quarterly in-person Board meetings, and arrange rooms and IT for internal and external meetings.
- Communications: Produce the monthly internal Bulletin for fundraising staff who partner with Board and Advisors members and the external monthly newsletter for Board and Advisors, and coordinate related internal updates as needed.
- Candidate tracking: Track candidates for the Nominating & Governance Committee as they move through the pipeline, maintaining accurate, confidential records.
- Data and records: Keep Board and Advisors contact information, activity records, and campaigns current in Salesforce, and maintain email distribution lists and team materials in RescueNet and Box.
- Finance administration: Handle purchase requests, the team credit card, expense reports, and invoices.
- Additional Duties: Support ad hoc Board related projects and perform other administrative and job-related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships**

- Position reports to: Director of Global Board Engagement.
- Internal: Works closely with departments across the organization. Key stakeholders include the President/CEO; Executive Board Assistants; the Vice President, Philanthropy; and other Leadership staff across the organization.
- External: various members of the Board of Directors and Advisors; others as relevant.

**Work / Educational Experience**

- Bachelor's degree preferred, but not required.
- 3 years of relevant work experience in a fast-paced environment, with gradually increasing responsibilities and a track record of high performance.
- Prior experience working as an administrative assistant.
- Experience working in a non-profit business development department a plus.
- Experience working with high net-worth individuals and/or senior partners a plus.
- Experience working with database platforms, such as Salesforce, a plus.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Bring a can-do attitude, flexibility, and resilience to navigate ambiguity, shifting priorities, and setbacks with positivity and enthusiasm
- Ability to pivot and adapt to rapidly changing circumstances
- Thrives in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. Calm under pressure.
- Outstanding attention to detail and problem-solving skills
- Strong organizational and time-management skills to deliver on tight deadlines and make progress against multiple demands
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, interacting with a variety of internal and external contacts with confidence and poise
- Strong listening skills and the ability to accurately follow guidance
- Maintains the highest standards of discretion and confidentiality in handling sensitive information
- Ability and interest to work both independently and in a complex, cross-functional team structure
- Proactive, takes initiative and anticipates needs
- Cordial and kind demeanor in all interactions, fostering a welcoming and collaborative environment
- Experience with Outlook email and calendar and familiarity with complex scheduling
- Highly proficient in Microsoft Office suite; strong in database management and Adobe Acrobat Pro experience
- Familiarity with AI tools such as Claude, and interest in using them to improve existing systems and workflows (preferred)

**Working Environment**

- Hybrid work with a minimum of 2 days per week in our NYC headquarters.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.  
  
**Compensation:** ($28-36/hour). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

jobs.title: P&C Operations Training Specialist
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The P&C Training & Learning Delivery Specialist ensures employees and managers have the knowledge and skills to work effectively as P&C transformation initiatives roll out. This role owns end-to-end training design and delivery for Workday enhancements, process changes, and digital capability rollouts.

Working closely with the Change Management Specialist, Business Analysts, and P&C Partners, this role builds training on a real understanding of stakeholder needs and readiness — turning the Change Management Specialist's impact assessments into practical, audience-appropriate learning experiences, and applying the reusable frameworks, tools, and methodology to deliver consistently at scale.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training Design & Delivery**

- Lead the end-to-end design and delivery of training programs for Workday enhancements, process changes, and digital capability rollouts — developing and executing training in line with the approach and standards set out in the Global Workday Learning Strategy and Rollout Training Methodology.
- Design and conduct training needs assessments ahead of every major rollout, building on the Change Management Specialist's stakeholder impact assessments, with a consistent methodology identifying what each user group needs, in what format, and by when
- Create a range of training assets appropriate to audience and context — job aids, quick reference guides, process guides, facilitator guides, and e-learning content — establishing reusable templates and standards
- Facilitate live and virtual training sessions for P&C and non-P&C users across the organization, adapting delivery style for different audiences and contexts
- Build an evaluation framework to measure training effectiveness through feedback, assessment, and post-training adoption data, iterating on content and delivery based on findings
- Establish and maintain a centralized training library, creating the structure and governance to keep materials current as systems and processes evolve

**Partnership & Knowledge Management**

- Partner closely with the Change Management Specialist to ensure training design is grounded in real stakeholder readiness and impact findings, and coordinate on rollout timing and sequencing
- Track training completion and content-effectiveness metrics, feeding into the team's broader adoption reporting
- Build the team's training capability through reusable templates, toolkits, and standards applied across all P&C transformation projects
- Conduct post-implementation reviews on training effectiveness, using findings to improve future delivery
- Stay current on Workday training approaches and adult learning principles

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience**

- 3–5 years of experience in training/learning & development, ideally including system rollouts or process change contexts
- Experience building training tools, templates, or frameworks
- Solid working knowledge of Workday from an end-user or training perspective is a strong advantage
- Instructional design background or certification is an advantage
- Experience in a complex, matrixed organization preferred
- Experience creating microlearning content for adult learners and/or working with tools like Articulate 360, Adobe Suite, Moodle, or equivalent

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Instructional design capability: able to assess needs, build practical learning materials, and adapt content for different roles, formats, and audiences
- Confident facilitator of live and virtual sessions for diverse groups
- Clear and adaptable communicator across audiences
- Data-aware: able to define training effectiveness metrics, interpret findings, and recommend action
- Well-organized and able to manage multiple concurrent workstreams without losing detail

**Working Environment:**

Standard office working environment with the ability to work remote 2-3 days per week.

This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Lebanon, and Colombia.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: MOZAMBIQUE - DEPUTY COUNTRY DIRECTOR FOR PROGRAMS (M/F) - CABO DELGADO
jobs.body:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date: ASAP**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**  
**Location: CABO DELGADO**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Solidarités International (SI) has been providing life-saving assistance in northern Mozambique since March 2019, initially responding to Cyclone Idai. As the crisis in Cabo Delgado escalated, SI began operations in Mueda in July 2021 and progressively expanded to other northern districts including Nangade, Muidumbe, Palma and, more recently, Mocímboa da Praia. By 2022, SI had established a coordination office in Pemba and operational bases in Mueda and Palma.

Following the closure of the Palma base, SI opened a new base in Mocímboa da Praia in July 2023 to support urgent returnee needs. Today, SI operates from Pemba, Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia, covering not only the northern districts (Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Palma) but also additional districts further south, such as Metuge, Chiúre, Mecúfi and Ancuabe.

At the beginning of 2025, major BHA funding cuts forced a significant restructuring, reducing the mission from approximately 140 to around 50 staff and prompting a reorganisation of operations to maintain essential activities. This restructuring coincided with a deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with renewed attacks, increased displacement and unpredictable access since mid-2024.

In early 2026, the mission entered a new phase with the confirmation of significant short-term emergency funding, alongside the launch of a major 3-year development-oriented WASH/FSL/Education project in Consortium. This shift requires strengthened programmatic oversight to manage simultaneous emergency and longer-term interventions within a rapidly evolving operational context.

Despite these challenges, SI continues to deliver principled, needs-based assistance across Cabo Delgado with the support of key donors such as ECHO, SDC, CDCS, IFSAN, UNICEF and WFP.

Projects and activities include:

\- Rapid Response Mechanism to shocks (conflict, natural disasters, epidemics): multisectoral WASH / Food / Shelter-NFI assistance through CVA or in-kind distributions

\- WASH: rehabilitation of large water networks, water points construction/rehabilitation, WASH in schools and health facilities, rainwater harvesting systems, sanitation and hygiene promotion

\- FSL: seeds and equipment distributions, support to cooperatives, cash-for-work and income-generating activities

\- Shelter/NFI: mainly emergency shelter and NFI through RRM

Around 50 staff in total across the mission in April 2026, but it will increase in May/June with the new funding.

SI operates 3 bases:

• Pemba (Coordination / Operational Base): 27 staff

• Mueda (Operational Base): 19 staff

• Mocímboa da Praia (Operational Sub-base): 4 staff

• Chiure (Operational Sub-base) to be opened: 6 staff

The DCDP is based in Pemba and covers operations in all bases of SI in Mozambique.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**GENERAL OBJECTIVE:**

The Deputy CD for Programs (DCDP) is responsible for the overall supervision, quality and strategic orientation of Solidarités International programmatic operations and MEAL systems in Cabo Delgado. S/he ensures effective, high-quality and compliant implementation of programmes in line with SI strategy and donor requirements. S/he supervises Program Managers and the MEAL Manager, supports adaptive programming, and works closely with the Area Coordinator and field teams to strengthen coordination, accountability and operational continuity.

**THE MAIN CHALLENGES:**

1- Major mission restructuring following BHA funding cuts in early 2025, with reduced staffing and evolving organisational set-up, followed by a rapid increase of funding in 2026, including short-term emergency grants and a multi-year development project  
2- Short implementation timelines for emergency projects (6 months) requiring strong planning, monitoring and adaptive management  
3- Volatile and unpredictable security context requiring continuous analysis and flexible programming  
4- Multi-base programme (Pemba, Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Chiure) with limited resources and high coordination needs  
5- High workload linked to simultaneous project closures, scale-up of emergency response and launch of new projects  
6- Strengthening and maintaining relationships with local authorities and coordination bodies in a sensitive operational environment

**PRIORITIES FOR THE 2/3 FIRST MONTHS:**

1- Ensure structured supervision of ongoing programmes across all bases and also the suppervision of the technicall departments (WASH, FSL, RRM Co, and MEAL)  
2- Strengthen MEAL systems and ensure effective use of monitoring data and accountability mechanisms for programmatic decision-making  
3- Ensure quality closure of ending projects and structured launch of new projects (Apri-May 2026)  
4- Reinforce program compliance with donor requirements and internal procedures  
5- Clarify roles, workflows and coordination mechanisms between Program, MEAL and Support departments  
6- Lead and coordinate proposal development with Project Managers, Technical Coordinators and the Grants Department  
7- Strengthen representation and collaboration with provincial and district authorities, clusters and key partners

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS:**

Security level 2 in Pemba with limited constraints.

Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia are security level 3, with more restrictions. Movements and activities depend on local conditions and Security Department guidance.

The security situation remains volatile, with unpredictable insurgent attacks and evolving dynamics involving armed actors. Close monitoring of the context is required for daily movement validation. Travel to field bases is mainly via UNHAS flights.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMA AND EXPERIENCE:**

Diploma : Master in humanitarian action, development, international law or any other technical area related to the humanitarian sector

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS:**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Strong Project Cycle Management skills
2. Solid background or experience in at least one technical
3. Strong understanding of MEAL systems and accountability mechanisms, with ability to ensure effective use of monitoring data for programmatic decision-making
4. Good knowledge of donor compliance and reporting requirements

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Strong information management capacity and ability to coordinate multiple activities across bases
2. Strong planning, prioritisation and organisational skills
3. Ability to represent SI with authorities, partners and coordination bodies
4. Strong analytical capacity and ability to adapt programming to evolving contexts
5. Capacity to supervise and structure teams in a complex operational environment

**LANGUAGE:**

1. English (mandatory)
2. Portuguese (strong asset)
3. Spanish or Italian (asset)

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3300 gross per month (3000 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Pemba is a coastal city with good living conditions for expatriates, including stable water and electricity and reliable 4G internet. There is no curfew, and walking is allowed during the day. SI provides comfortable office and guesthouse facilities close to amenities.

The position is based in Pemba, with frequent visits to the bases. Field bases are reachable by UNHAS flight in less than one hour. Living conditions in field locations are basic but functional.

jobs.title: Project Development Consultant (Fiji Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23660**  
Position Title: **Project Development Consultant (Fiji Nationals Only)**  
Duty Station City: **Suva**  
Duty Station Country: **Fiji**  
Contract Type: **Consultant A**  
*Recruiting Type:* **Consultancy**  
*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**  
Initial duration: **6 months**  
Closing date: **02 November 2026**

**Context:**

The IOM Coordination Office for the South Pacific in Suva, Fiji supports programme development, resource mobilization, donor relations, and programme oversight across multiple Pacific Island Countries. As the Pacific portfolio continues to expand in areas including climate mobility, disaster risk reduction, labour mobility, border governance, protection, and humanitarian preparedness and response, additional surge support is required to strengthen project development and donor engagement efforts.

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Programme Support Unit and direct supervision of the Programme Development Officer, the consultant will support the Programme Support Unit in the development of concept notes, project proposals, resource mobilization, partnership engagement activities and programme information products. The consultant will work closely with programme teams and relevant IOM offices to ensure timely and high-quality project development processes. This consultancy will contribute to strengthening the Mission's project pipeline, resource mobilization, and programme quality assurance mechanisms across the South Pacific region.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:**

Programme Support Unit (PSU)

IOM Coordination Office for the South Pacific, Suva, Fiji.

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

- Assist in the development of results-based concept notes, project proposals, budgets and supporting documentation in accordance with IOM, donor and UN requirements.
- Compile, summaries, analyze, and present information/data on specific project topics, highlighting noteworthy issues on donor priorities, funding opportunities, regional trends and emerging programme needs to support resource mobilization efforts.
- Support coordination with programme managers, technical specialists, regional offices and external partners during project development and donor reporting processes.
- Maintain project development tracking systems and programme support unit information share points.
- Assist in organizing donor meetings, consultations, workshops, missions, and partnership engagement activities, including preparation of background materials and meeting summaries, when required.
- Contribute to the preparation of visibility materials, success stories, factsheets, programme summaries and external communication products.
- Provide support to programme reviews and information requests from donors, governments, regional organizations, headquarters and regional offices.
- Perform such other related duties as may be assigned.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Timely completion of assigned project development and coordination tasks.
- Quality and accuracy of concept notes, proposals and briefing materials produced.
- Compliance with IOM project development and donor standards.
- Number of contributions to proposal development and resource mobilization processes.
- Timely response to information requests and programme support requirements.
- Maintenance of accurate project development and resource mobilization records.
- Demonstrated professionalism, accountability and adherence to IOM policies and procedures.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Social Science, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or a related field from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience; or,
- High School diploma with six years of relevant professional experience.

**Experience**

- Experience in project development and proposal writing for bilateral and multilateral donors.
- Experience working with international organizations, development agencies, government institutions or non-governmental organizations.
- Experience coordinating with multiple stakeholders and working in multicultural environments.
- Experience in the other Pacific countries is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of drafting, proposal writing, editing and analytical skills.
- Knowledge of UN and bilateral donor programming.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
- Knowledge of Results-Based Management and monitoring frameworks.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

**Languages**

- Language: Excellent command of English
- For this consultancy, Fluency in English language is required.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

- NO

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at [this link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

- Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 1)

- Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

- Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.
- This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.
- This post is subject to only those holding a valid residence and work permit for the country where this position is based will be eligible for consideration.
- Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, verification of residency, visa, and authorizations by the concerned Government, where applicable.
- IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.
- IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.
- IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM online recruitment system. The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.
- For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: [IOM Careers and Job Vacancies](https://www.iom.int/careers)

jobs.title: Project Finance Officer
jobs.body:
Sightsavers implements projects in over 30 countries in Africa and South Asia working to eliminate avoidable blindness and promote the rights of people with disabilities.

**Title**: Project Finance Officer

**Location**: Monrovia, Liberia

**Contract**: Two-year fixed term contract

**Salary**: Local Terms and Conditions apply

**About the role**

Working closely with our programme and finance teams, project partners and Liberia’s Ministry of Health, you will manage project budgets, monitor expenditure, prepare financial reports and support partners to strengthen their financial processes. You will also contribute to audits, procurement and effective financial planning across the project.

This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional who enjoys working closely with programmes and partners to ensure funding is used effectively and delivers maximum impact.

**Responsibilities**

- Preparing, maintaining and monitoring project budgets and spending plans.
- Producing monthly Budget versus Actual reports, including commentary on significant financial matters.
- Preparing accurate and timely quarterly donor financial reports.
- Monitoring project cash flow and preparing monthly cash-flow forecasts.
- Reviewing project transactions to ensure they are accurately recorded and correctly coded.
- Preparing invoice and expense projections and analysing differences against actual expenditure.
- Reviewing and consolidating financial reports submitted by project partners.
- Undertaking financial monitoring visits and supporting partners to improve their financial controls, procurement, reporting and compliance.
- Supporting audit preparation and providing the required financial documentation.
- Coordinating project procurement requirements and supporting compliance with donor rules, Sightsavers policies and value-for-money commitments.

This is a highly varied and involved role and the above is not an exhaustive list of duties or required professional skills. Please see the [Job Description](https://sightsavershh.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/HRExternal/IQD-3ZdJRH-IRb_MeChH5AeDAR2ePk8ie01YLL_B_Fw7_Sg?e=u4ghny) for full details.

**Jobholder Requirements**

**Essential:**

- A bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration or a relevant experience.
- A completed or well-advanced professional accounting qualification, such as ACCA, CPA, CIMA or an equivalent.
- At least three years’ progressive experience in project finance, ideally within an international INGO.
- Experience managing donor-funded grants and meeting donor financial reporting requirements.
- Auditing experience.
- Experience working with government organisations.
- Experience in financial management, project management and administration.
- Strong project financial management, budgeting and data analysis skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to work with limited supervision

**Desirable:**

- Experience managing donor-funded projects.
- Experience supporting health or neglected tropical disease programmes.
- Experience working with Ministry of Health partnerships.
- Experience financially monitoring implementing partners and field-based activity costs.
