jobs.title: Head of support services (F/M) - Lebanon
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## **MdM in Lebanon**

MdM has been working in Lebanon for 30 years and actively contributed to respond to needs of the most vulnerable communities as the context unfolded (2011 Syrian crisis, 2019 severe economic crisis, 2020 Beirut Blast) and the current period since October 7th, 2023 – especially as the war resumed in Lebanon since March 2nd, 2026.

MdM’s intervention in Lebanon aims to strengthen the national health system and increase access to quality healthcare.

MdM is recognized in Lebanon as a major actor in the areas of mental health (MHPSS) and sexual and reproductive health (SRH). MdM supports several health centers and mobile clinics in the South, Beirut Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and Baalbek Hermel; and works with other partners.

Despite the June 2026 ceasefire, the situation remains highly volatile and high needs remain, particularly in the South of the country. MdM continues to closely monitor the situation to ensure an appropriate, timely and flexible intervention, always in line with the needs of the various conflict-affected populations.

## **About the role**

You are responsible for the overall strategy and compliance, through the management of logistics, human resources and finance departments in the MdM Lebanon mission.

You ensure support services are fully compliant with MdM policies, donor requirements, national authorities' regulations, and applicable legislation.

## **Who you’ll work with**

Under the line management of the General coordinator, and the technical management of the Desk manager, you work in close collaboration with the other departments: Program, Medical/MHPSS, Grants, Security-Safety-Access, MEAL.

## **What you’ll do**

**Support services leadership & strategic planning**

- Provide strategic leadership and guidance to the General Coordinator and Country Management Team on all support-related matters
- Contribute to country strategy development, annual planning and financial planning processes
- Lead support services planning and ensure alignment between operational and programme priorities
- Anticipate operational challenges and oversee contingency planning to ensure humanitarian response continuity

**Development & reporting**

- Ensure support functions contribute effectively to proposal development, reporting and donor-related processes
- Coordinate the timely provision of analyses and support inputs required for programme development and decision-making

**Support services management & quality**

- Oversee the quality, compliance and performance of all support functions in accordance with organizational policies, donor requirements and local regulations
- Ensure sound resource management, accountability and legal compliance across the mission
- Monitor support systems, identify risks and corrective actions, and strengthen tools and procedures to support informed decision-making
- Promote effective integration and collaboration between Finance, HR, Logistics and programme teams

**Risk management, compliance & internal control**

- Strengthen internal control systems and ensure appropriate management of mission resources
- Identify and mitigate financial, operational, compliance, safeguarding, fraud and corruption risks
- Lead or coordinate audits, investigations and follow up on recommendations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders
- Promote adherence to anti-fraud, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies across the mission

**Team management & capacity building**

- Recruit, manage and develop the support services team through coaching, performance management and capacity-building initiatives
- Foster effective coordination, communication and information sharing across teams
- Identify learning and development needs and ensure access to appropriate technical support and resources

**Coordination & representation**

- Ensure strong coordination between support, programme, field and headquarters teams
- Facilitate effective information sharing and contribute to organizational reporting
- Represent the organization with authorities, partners and donors, alongside the General Coordinator, when required.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you...**

- Have significant experience in humanitarian operations, including in complex contexts, and have held a senior support coordination role within an international NGO
- Have strong expertise across HR, Finance, Logistics and Administration, ideally supporting health programmes and donor-funded projects
- Are a strategic and analytical leader, able to drive operational performance, manage risks and support decision-making
- Have a proven ability to lead, coach and develop teams while fostering collaboration across departments
- Are organized, adaptable and solution-oriented, with the confidence to make decisions and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Are an excellent communicator and relationship builder, comfortable engaging with partners, authorities, donors and diverse teams
- Are comfortable using Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel
- Are fluent in English; knowledge of French and/or Arabic and experience in the Middle East are strong assets.

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Prefer a specialist role rather than overseeing multiple support functions and leading cross-department coordination
- Are uncomfortable working in complex, evolving humanitarian environments where priorities can shift rapidly
- Are not motivated by team leadership, capacity building and stakeholder engagement responsibilities

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info:  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3392€
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Beirut, Lebanon
- Field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable.  
  
The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices.

## About the Role

The Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer supports the Ethiopia Trees Program's expansion through desk research, primary data gathering, field verification scoutings, and evidence generation to identify and assess potential expansion opportunities across Ethiopia.

The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights.

## Responsibilities

Data Collection & Research

- Conduct desk research to identify and assess potential program expansion areas across regions, zones, and woredas.
- Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning.
- Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights.
- Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion.
- Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness.
- Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability.
- Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes.

Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data

- Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information.
- Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings.
- Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks.
- Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information.
- Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations.

Reporting & Collaboration

- Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions.
- Present research findings and recommendations to relevant teams and stakeholders and contribute to expansion planning discussions.
- Collaborate with the expansion team and relevant technical and operational teams to translate research findings into actionable expansion plans.
- Maintain clear documentation of research findings, field validation results, assumptions, and recommendations to support decision-making and future reference

Reporting, Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration

- Support engagement with government institutions, community representatives, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders during expansion assessments and field scouting activities.
- Coordinate information gathering, stakeholder consultations, and validation activities to support expansion planning and decision-making.
- Identify collaboration opportunities that strengthen expansion planning, field implementation, and operational readiness.
- Prepare high-quality assessment reports, presentations, briefing materials, and regular progress updates for internal and external stakeholders.
- Document research findings, field observations, lessons learned, stakeholder feedback, and key decisions to support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research findings and stakeholder insights into actionable recommendations and expansion plans.
- Track assigned activities and maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to expansion research, assessments, and planning.
- Perform other research and operational support tasks as assigned to advance the Tree Program’s expansion objectives.
- Support the recruitment of field staff

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Education

- Bachelor's degree required.
- Candidates with academic backgrounds in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Rural Development, Watershed Management, or related fields are preferred.

Experience

- 2 years or more of relevant professional experience in forestry, agroforestry, agriculture, natural resource management, landscape restoration, rural development, field innovation, government relations, or related fields.
- Experience conducting research, data collection, expansion assessments, market assessments, or strategic planning.
- Experience working with government institutions, development partners, or community stakeholders.

Skills

- Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills.

- Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
- Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

jobs.body:
**Background:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive, recover, and gain control of their future.

We aim to make our programs a model for the highest global standards and to cultivate power and lasting change not just for our clients but for all people affected by humanitarian crises. To achieve that vision, the IRC’s Technical Excellence (TE) group, located within the Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department, provides technical assistance to IRC’s country program staff and shares what we learn to influence policy and practice.

IRC’s Technical Excellence team is comprised of seven teams which have deep expertise in their respective fields: Education, Economic Wellbeing, Governance, Health, Violence Prevention and Response, MEAL, and Grants & Operations.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Technology, Accountability, and Learning at the IRC**

The METAL Unit is responsible for supporting CRRD to have a culture of strong data and evidence use through stewardship of the Data & Performance Ecosystem, and for coordinating successful piloting and uptake of innovative technology solutions. The METAL Unit provides specialized support across four pillars to strengthen program effectiveness, improve decision-making, and enhance organizational learning: Global MEAL Practice, Technology for Programs, Regional MEAL Support, and CRRD Data & Analytics.

**Job Overview**

The Software Developer will be part of the METAL team which is responsible for delivering products that support the collection, management and visualization of KPIs relevant to higher-level decision-making for CRRD Programs.

The Software Developer will build and support data tools that drive decision-making across IRC, working with platforms like PowerApps, Power BI, Databricks, and Azure SQL. They will be a skilled contributor to the CRRD Data & Analytics team with strong experience in Microsoft PowerApps and Power Automate.

Specific tasks include data platform development, support, configuration, technical assistance and routing of technical issues, 2nd line help desk support, and participation in setting standards for processes, data quality, data security, and systems configuration.

The Software Developer will report to the Technology Development Lead. They will work closely with other developers, QA, Project Manager and the Program Data Systems Product Manager.

**Major Responsibilities**

- Design, develop, and maintain PowerApps and Power Automate solutions
- Support development and rollout of organization-wide data products in collaboration with METAL and sector experts
- Create technical documentation including system diagrams and implementation manuals
- Implement and maintain data quality processes and development standards
- Ensure compliance with IRC’s data protection, confidentiality, and security policies
- Provide Tier-2 and Tier-3 technical support, including issue routing and resolution
- Collaborate with IT and data engineering teams on systems integration
- Review software requirements and translate them into development tasks
- Contribute to setting and enforcing standards for processes, data quality, and system configurations
- Provide hyper-support during pilot phases of technology rollouts
- Perform other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships**

- Position Reports to: Technology Development Lead
- Direct Reports: None
- Management in Partnership: None

**Key Internal Relationships:**

- METAL Product Managers
- METAL QA Analyst
- METAL Project Manager
- IT Data Team

**Desired Experience and Skills**

- At least five years of experience working in technology domain to develop and rollout data platforms for programs – out of which, at least three years of experience developing, implementing, and supporting PowerApps applications for large and complex programs.
- Experience in source code and version control platforms, for example, GitHub, Azure DevOps, or similar.
- Strong in team development processes including pair programming, shadow sessions, code reviews and other strategies to ensure high quality programing.
- Strong code quality assurance practices including unit testing, integration testing, as well as regression testing to ensure quality of the code getting shipped into production.
- Ability to effectively communicate in English both in verbal (i.e., day-to-day discussions, team meetings) and written (requirements and design specifications) form, as well as an overall ability to be clear and concise in all communications.
- Strong analytic curiosity and innovative problem-solving skills using a system thinking approach.
- Demonstrable ability to work both independently and in a dynamic, cross-functional team structure.
- Demonstrable ability to establish and maintain working relationships across all departments and levels of the organization.

**Education:**

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology, or related discipline
- Experience with Databricks, Dataverse connectors, APIs, and Microsoft Azure
- Certifications such Microsoft Power Platform Developer are an added advantage

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $85,000 - $95,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: £46,780 - £55,552/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

Our Burundi program, founded in 2011, operates under the local brand Tubura. 1662 staff serve close to 400,000 hard-working farmers. Our Burundi headquarters in Muramvya is supported by two regional offices in Gitega and Ngozi, and a small support office in Bujumbura. One Acre Fund works in the center and north of Burundi, in the provinces of Muramvya, Gitega, Ngozi, Kayanza, and Mwaro.

## **About the Role**

As a Program Associate, you will have the opportunity to learn from field operations and to help improve our program. Your proposed initial role will focus on execution of our core program as well as general program innovation, but the exact makeup of your work will depend on staffing and program needs, as well as your own interests.

## **Responsibilities**

**Operations management**

The FOP Associate will focus on delivering services to farmers. He/She begins as generalists, with overall responsibility for executing our program within a given region of operation in Burundi. Over time, He/she can continue to grow as a general leader, potentially managing Field Operations for an entire country. He/She may also choose to specialize, for example in designing and rolling out training programs.

Program associates also build the infrastructure necessary to sustain and scale the program. These teams proactively remove barriers to scale across a wide range of areas, processing millions of payments made by farmers, communicating with farmers through tens of millions of SMS messages, recruiting hundreds of new staff each year, and physically transporting more than 20,000 tons of agricultural inputs to various delivery sites. Program Associates also drive continuous improvements to accelerate growth, for example by implementing mobile money system integration at the country level.

**Core program execution and operations management**

- Own end-to-end execution of the core program across an assigned region and functional area (exemple of core activities can be farmers training, enrollment, distribution, repayment, expansion…), ensuring services reach farmers on time and at quality.
- Ensure seasonal objectives and KPIs are communicated and in line with country and department priorities, monitor performance against them, and intervene where results deviate.
- Ensure operational processes are documented, standardized and cost-efficient, and that spend stays within budget.

**Project and portfolio management**

- Lead a portfolio of 1–3 medium-to-large projects from design through field execution, defining objectives, work plans, timelines and success measures with limited manager support.
- Coordinate delivery across departments (Impact, Systems, Logistics, Business Operations, People) and with external partners, keeping stakeholders aligned and decisions timely.
- Produce analysis, post-mortems and reporting that inform leadership decisions on whether to continue, scale or discontinue an approach.

**Team management and development**

- Manage and mentor a team of direct reports (Senior Field Directors, Specialists, Coordinators) and the wider structure beneath them, driving both performance and professional growth.
- Recruit, onboard and develop staff using One Acre Fund's experiential recruitment approach, and progressively delegate as the team strengthens.
- Maintain performance follow-up systems and remove day-to-day barriers so field teams can consistently deliver quality service to farmers.

**Innovation and continuous improvement**

- Identify opportunities to improve farmer impact, program quality or cost efficiency, and translate them into structured trials or pilots.
- Design and run trials with field teams and farmers, analyze results, and recommend refinements to products, training or the operating model.
- Champion adoption of improved systems, tools and ways of working across the department, ensuring changes are embedded and sustained.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Project management: Able to design and lead medium-to-large projects with a high degree of independence, navigating ambiguity with limited manager support.
- Planning and prioritization: Creates and executes work plans independently. Work is characterized by a high degree of collaboration, higher visibility, and longer-term impact on the team and department.
- People management and coaching: Able to recruit, develop and manage a multi-level team, set clear performance expectations, give effective feedback, and progressively delegate as deputies grow.
- Data analysis: Strong analytical ability, using data to drive decisions and monitor performance against KPIs.
- Communication and stakeholder management: Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence without authority and coordinate across country teams, global departments and external partners.
- Innovation and process improvement: Leads innovation and process improvement within the department, from identifying opportunities through to embedding change.
- Budget and resource management: Able to build an annual budget, monitor budget versus actuals, and identify cost-efficiency opportunities without compromising program quality.
- Judgment and execution: Able to make interpretive decisions with incomplete information in a fast-moving field environment, and to keep detail-heavy operations on track.

jobs.body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**JOB SUMMARY**  
Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) is seeking a motivated Credit & Portfolio Analyst to join Habitat Capital (HCap), a nationally certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI), certified in 2017. Habitat Capital is a wholly-owned entity of HFHI and was created to serve our more than 900 US-based Habitat for Humanity affiliates. HCap provides an array of financial services and products to Habitat affiliates to support their work as affordable mortgage originators, real estate developers, home-builders, sellers, and partners for housing and community solutions. To date, HFHI and HCap has provided over $400MM in capital to its US domestic affiliate network via enterprise-level, secured project-level, bridge and structured financing for affordable housing and community development projects as well NMTC allocation for homeownership initiatives. Additionally, HCap seeks to develop and provide permanent mortgage financing products. HCap values creativity and flexibility in developing financial products for our customers and working with capital partners who share our mission.

**About the Program and Role**  
The HCap Analyst Program ("the Program") is a new intentional effort between HFHI and HCap to recruit and train early-stage professionals to succeed in mission-driven financial services roles. In this two-year program, participants will support HCap's efforts to attract and deploy capital to create and increase the production of affordable housing and greater community development across the US. The Analyst will possess and develop strong financial, entrepreneurial, program management and analytical skills while providing communications and research to advance housing and community development initiatives and support broader strategic initiatives and operations.

The HCap Analyst Program is a new intentional effort between HFHI and HCap to recruit and train early-stage professionals to succeed in mission-driven financial services roles. In this two-year program, participants will support HCap's efforts to attract and deploy capital to create and increase the production of affordable housing and greater community development across the US. The Analyst will possess and develop strong financial, entrepreneurial, program management and analytical skills while providing communications and research to advance housing and community development initiatives and support broader strategic initiatives and operations.

Supporting HCap Directors, the Analyst's primary responsibilities will include financial analysis and modelling, transaction underwriting, portfolio management, investor relations, marketing and communications, and supporting new programmatic initiatives. While the analyst will have broad responsibilities, there will be a primary focus on credit and underwriting.

Participants will receive training designed to foster mission-alignment, understanding of the housing and community development finance sectors, development of technical skills, and other ongoing enrichment. This 2-year program with the potential for a 3rd year to be evaluated at the end of year 2. The Program is committed to diversity and inclusion and encourages diverse candidates to apply.

These positions are strongly preferred to be based at our headquarters office in downtown Atlanta (Remote considered) and involves up to 10% travel within the US.

**Loan Origination and Underwriting (50%)**

- Conduct credit analysis, due diligence and structuring for investment and real estate transaction
    - Financial statement analysis
    - Project-level analysis and diligence
    - Impact analysis
    - Term sheet creation
- Support the creation of written investment memo for internal investment committee
- Interface with multiple internal and external to support all aspects of deal lifecycle from prospecting through closing
- Conduct financial modelling of new financial products that are innovative, socially responsible, fiscally responsible and attractive to the investing community.
- Provide technical assistance, as needed, to potential or current applicants

**Portfolio Management (20%)**

- Provide support to Portfolio Management Associate to monitor and provide analysis on the existing loan portfolio
- Support monthly, quarterly and semi-annual reporting requirements, collateral substitutions and loan prepayments
- Support investor financial and impact reporting requirements
- Interface with trustees, paying agents and internal finance to ensure timely and accurate satisfaction of debt service obligations

**Research & Analysis (20%)**

- Provide reliable borrower, property, and market-level data by using available third-party and internal resources to conduct research.
- Support the creation and analysis of models, charts, tables, templates, maps and other resources related to lending and programmatic initiatives
- Conduct market research, portfolio and impact data analysis related to historical and future lending work in advancing affordable homeownership, racial equity and climate resiliency

**General Operations (10%)**

- Develop investor and management presentations and reports as well as support training and educational materials for HFHI affiliates
- Prospecting and research in support of broader strategic initiatives and new products and programs
- Financial modelling and budgeting support
- Assist in the preparation and submission of funding proposals for federal and private programs
- Other special projects/task as assigned

**Cross Functional Capabilities**

Employees in multiple divisions with different skillsets work together to achieve Habitat for Humanity International’s mission and common strategic goals.

Key aspects of cross-functional responsibilities in a global non-profit include: Strategic planning, program design and implementation, communication and branding, monitoring and evaluation, and compliance and risk management.

**Education**

• Undergraduate (required) in a related field

**Years of Related Experience**

• 2+ years of relevant experience (including internships)

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

• Product Knowledge: Familiarity or interest in CDFI lending, tax credits, impact investing.

• Technical Experience: Experience building models and data analysis; Fluency with Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word and PowerPoint)

Preferred Requirements

• Preferably with experience in affordable housing, community development, finance, real estate development, nonprofit management or similar.

• Credit training and commercial underwriting experience strongly desired

Location: Remote U.S. - work from anywhere

Employees located near Atlanta, Americus, GA, or Washington, DC offices who are hired in a hybrid capacity report to the office on Tuesdays.

## Our Values

At Habitat, our work is guided by three core values:

- Accountability — We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission.
- Courage — We do what’s right, even when it’s difficult.
- Humility — We recognize we are part of something bigger than ourselves.

***Safeguarding: HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work. Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct.***

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the annual hiring range for this position is:

$73,500.00

$109,350 USD

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

**Habitat for Humanity International is an E-Verify employer.**

[E-Verify information (English/Spanish)](https://url.us.m.mimecastprotect.com/s/vGsOC1wv1YfPl5pVT1u4iVZdtz?domain=e-verify.gov)

[Right to work (English/Spanish)](https://url.us.m.mimecastprotect.com/s/06wyC2kw4gtBgOkMCXCZi5YAFm?domain=e-verify.gov)

jobs.title: Tupande Procurement Contracts Management Senior Coordinator
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications

## About the Role

The job holder is responsible for the contracting processes for the procurement department and the management of Long Term Agreements.

## Responsibilities

Forecasting and Tender Management

- Run tenders and establish contracts for all frequently needed goods/services, high-value purchases, and identified strategic purchases that require long-term agreements.
- Identify opportunities for cost savings through upstream supplier relationships and advise the relevant teams. Set a 0-6 month target for strategic procurement activities
- Improve existing contracting and tendering processes in order to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and customer service.
- Set target prices for all items before contracting, align with the relevant stakeholders, and negotiate prices to achieve the target or below.

Odoo contracting support to the Tupande Procurement Team

- Be recognized and consulted as an Odoo tender master user.
- Deliver ad-hoc training and provide training when requested.
- Run tenders through Odoo & provide support to the suppliers.

Contract Planning & management

- Prepare an annual tender calendar for different categories and review on a quarterly basis.
- Monitor contract expiry and renewal dates and execute their timely renewal
- Review market trends and advise management of potential contracting risks or significant anticipated price changes. Review price changes over the allowable tolerance and advise management on proposed next steps e.g. re-tendering
- Support direct reports to ensure the team takes the lead on all key contracting initiatives. Regularly measure and report cost-savings achieved through contracts.
- Provide cross-country support on global procurement projects and manage assigned global contracts.

Supplier management and performance evaluation

- Organize and manage supplier meeting calendars to minimize supply challenges by meeting with at least 2 top suppliers on Long Term Agreements per month.
- Manage the bi-annual supplier evaluation and categorize suppliers based on performance and bargaining power.
- Create supplier performance reports, rank by performance and create performance improvement plans for poor performing suppliers.
- Ensure supplier contractual commitments are respected, in particular, coordinating timely payments.

People Management

- Manage up to 2 direct reports and provide the required support for them to meet set objectives
- Conduct regular performance reviews with direct reports to measure performance, identify areas of growth, and provide tailored support to enhance their performance.
- Lead weekly check in meetings with the direct reports and use the session to provide needed guidance for the execution of tasks.
- Provide or assign necessary training to equip them with the skills/knowledge required for the proper execution of their duties

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor’s degree in Law, Procurement & Supply Chain, or a related field.
- 3+ years of relevant work experience in contracts or legal operations.
- Comfortable working cross-functionally with legal, finance, and operational teams.
- Able to support contract drafting and reviews, flagging legal or commercial risks where relevant.
- Experienced in managing contract trackers, monitoring expiry timelines, and supporting renewals.
- Strong data analysis skills
- Capable of organizing supplier meetings, tracking follow-ups, and supporting performance reviews.
- Clear communicator able to liaise with suppliers and stakeholders, and escalate risks when needed.
- Solid understanding of basic contract law and its application in procurement (e.g., liabilities, SLAs, renewals).
- Familiar with the contract lifecycle including drafting, negotiation support, and renewal tracking.
- Awareness of commercial risks (e.g., inflation, pricing volatility, vendor

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Kakamega, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

02 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator - BU Support
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications

## About the Role

Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring smooth and efficient execution of procurement projects by closely aligning with business units (BUs) needs, controlling spend, and improving procurement processes. This role involves managing the full procurement lifecycle for assigned BU procurement projects, supporting supplier and stakeholder relationships, driving process improvements, and maintaining strict contract management and compliance. The coordinator also provides performance tracking and reporting to facilitate strategic decision-making and continuous enhancement of procurement activities.

## Responsibilities

Targeted process and performance improvement

- Support cross-functional improvement initiatives by helping develop templates, SOPs, and training materials.
- Coordinate periodic reviews with assigned Business Units to clear aged Procurement Requests (PRs) and Purchase Orders (POs).
- Perform root cause analysis to identify bottlenecks and improve PR to PO turnaround time.
- Identify capability gaps and propose practical, incremental improvements to strengthen processes and team performance.
- Facilitate effective collaboration between BU and PRO teams to ensure alignment on priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
- Promote proactive communication between BU units and PRO to support timely planning, coordination, and issue resolution.

Strategic sourcing responsibilities

- Define the scope and profile of assigned procurement categories.
- Conduct comprehensive spend analysis, market analysis, and profile demand/supply markets to identify opportunities.
- Develop strategic sourcing strategies, setting clear objectives for cost savings, quality improvement, risk mitigation, and determining appropriate tactics.
- Identify, evaluate, and pre-qualify potential suppliers based on strategic needs.
- Lead RFx processes, including negotiation of pricing, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), payment terms, delivery windows, and change management processes, while integrating selected suppliers into planning systems.
- Finalize and execute contracts, ensuring all terms and conditions are clearly defined and favorable.
- Monitor supplier performance against contract terms, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and hold regular business review meetings to ensure costs are consistently driven down.

Reporting and documentation

- Prepare routine reports and dashboards on procurement project progress, highlighting status updates, risks, and key actions for timely decision-making.
- Support data collection and analysis, including responding to ad-hoc market research requests that inform sourcing decisions and category strategies.
- Capture and document supplier performance data to help drive improvements in service levels, quality, and on-time delivery.
- Analyse cost drivers by Business Unit, identifying short-, medium-, and long-term trends to support planning and spend management.
- Work with other BU coordinators to promote standardization and consolidation of requirements, helping reduce duplication and improve sourcing efficiency across BUs.
- Monitor KPI performance for assigned procurement projects and follow up on corrective actions when targets are not met.
- Maintain clear, organized, and audit-ready documentation for all procurement transactions to support compliance and transparency.
- The Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator will also perform any other duties as assigned by the manager.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Strong communication skills.
- Analytical Skills: Ability to apply logical thinking and problem-solving techniques to break down complex issues and reach sound conclusions.
- Data Analysis Skills: Proven ability to collect, analyze, and interpret large datasets to inform decision-making. Advanced proficiency in data manipulation and visualization tools, including expertise in Excel (Pivot Tables, Lookups, and Array formulas).
- Solid stakeholder management skills
- Strong working knowledge of process improvement tools and methodologies, DMAIC, 5Whys
- Supply chain risk management skills
- Commercial contracting skills
- Strategic sourcing skills
- Supplier relationship management skills
- Commercial negotiation skills
- Minimum 3 years of work experience in a demanding professional environment.
- Bachelor's degree in procurement, project management, business strategy, or related discipline. Candidates with higher diploma and extensive relevant experience may also qualify.
- Professional qualification e.g CIPS, CILT preferred
- Familiarity with procurement models, sourcing frameworks, and PR-PO systems such as Odoo or Power BI
- Language: Fluent in English and Kiswahili preferred.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Kakamega, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

02 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

jobs.title: Supply Chain Coordinator
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the world's leading crisis response agencies, providing life-saving assistance and supporting recovery and reconstruction for people affected by war and natural disasters. Active in public health, education, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, IRC assists people from harm to home.

The IRC was registered in Uganda in mid-1998 and implements rehabilitation activities in the sectors of Child and Youth Protection and development, Health, Economic recovery and Development and women protection and empowerment as well as contributing to the response to the Southern Sudanese Refugee situation. IRC Uganda has a head office in Kampala, field offices in Lamwo, Kiryandongo, Moroto, Kyaka and West Nile.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

Supply Chain Coordinator is a key position to the success and delivery of quality programs. Supply Chain entails all the systems and functions necessary to implement programs effectively, inclusive of planning, procurement, inventory management, constructions property and asset management as well as vehicle and fleet management. The Supply Chain Coordinator is accountable for the design, planning, execution, and monitoring of supply chain activities at the country level.

**The Supply Chain Coordinator will:**

- Collaborate and coordinate with Programs and Finance to ensure integrated and harmonized operational systems.
- Collaborate with the Deputy Director Finance to ensure that internal controls are met with minimum bureaucracy.
- Work with Field Office Supply Chain Staff and Field Managers/Senior Field Coordinator to ensure effectiveness, countrywide uniformity of Supply Chain structure and implementation of the IRC’s standard operating policies and procedures.
- Implement job and site-specific trainings to ensure that Supply Chain staff possess the knowledge and skills commensurate with their responsibilities.

**SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is an integral member of the country management team and reports directly to the Senior Field Management Coordinator. This position is responsible for the management and delivery of effective Supply Chain support throughout the country program in compliance with IRC and donor regulations. Key responsibilities include procurement, inventory, construction management.

**Supply Chain Planning**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for supply chain activities planning. The role holder coordinates closely with internal and external stakeholders to develop supply chain plans to support program implementation. Supply chain plans include procurement plans, warehousing plans, transport plans, staffing plans, distribution plans and training plans.

- Prepare consolidated annual procurement plans and develop country program sourcing strategy for all active and pipeline grants in collaboration with program Coordinators and Managers,
- Ensure that the program team develops distribution plan for supplies and assets of closed grants in the warehouses.
- Proactively Participate in the Project Cycle Meetings, including Project design, project planning, Project opening, project review, project close-out and project learning meetings to ensure that supply chain related issues are well articulated to all stakeholders and resolved for successful project delivery. Coordinate with supply chain field staff to ensure that there is sufficient space in the warehouses before sending program supplies to the field sites.
- Ensure supply chain staff training and capacity building plans are developed as the PMEs and incorporated into the budgets.
- Ensure that supply chain department has sufficient staff and roles and responsibilities of each have clear job description.

**Procurement Management**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is accountable for developing country procurement strategies. The Supply Chain Coordinator owns, manages, and drives IRC in country procurement strategies, policies, and procedures. The position holder ensures all country program procurement needs are met on time in accordance with Global Supply Chain and donor standards

- Ensure compliance to IRC and donor policies in the procurement of program supplies and assets.
- Ensure review and execution of procurement contracts in a timely way.
- Lead market surveys and analyses by collecting, organizing, and analyzing market data, share results with program team, Field Coordinators and Managers on a regular basis.
- Ensure the bidding process by developing and implementing the office sourcing strategy, managing the Master Agreements and RFQ/RFP Processes, and completing a purchase request process
- Develop negotiation strategies and manage negotiations for high spent categories
- Proactively engage with Programs, Suppliers, Partners, NGOs, logistics clusters and other stakeholders to ensure good coordination and adequate information sharing to address common concerns or risks affecting the market
- Organize procurement trainings sessions for procurement / tender committees in the field offices and non - supply chain staff if deemed necessary.
- Identifying fraud and corruption red flags and address them in a timely manner.
- Establish reasonable and appropriate lead-time for all procurement of program supplies and delivery of goods to the program sites.
- Make sure the supply chain monthly and quarterly reports are analyzed and communicated to stakeholders, including key actions to be taken and submitted on time to the leadership team.
- Review of SC Key performance indicators (KPIs) and set improvement plans.
- Ensure all vendors’ history and performance Information, is properly documented and procurement transaction files and supplier files maintained in accordance with applicable Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Work with Field Offices Supply Chain staff and Field Managers/SFC and Managers to ensure effectiveness, countrywide uniformity of supply chain structure and implementation of the IRC’s standard operating policies and procedures

**Inventory Management**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for managing and controlling all inventory and warehouses operation in the country program and to ensure excellent record keeping, in accordance with inventory standard operating procedures and controls as provided by Global Supply Chain. The Supply Chain Coordinator will:

- Ensure appropriate warehouse site selection, and Implementation of warehouse safety/security requirements
- Ensure effective handling of inventory, including drug storage, cold chain, buffer stock, contributions in kind (CIK) and food commodities
- Set up stock reorder levels as per the IRC standard operating procedures and donor requirements
- Implement the IRC inventory policies for all project Items including cycle count, investigate discrepancies and develop action plan to address them.
- Produce grants ending and year ending inventory report during each grant closing and end of fiscal year in timely manner.
- Coordinate inventory disposal procedures as per host government, IRC and donor rules and regulations

**Assets Management**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for the procurement, maintenance, safekeeping and record on all IRC country program assets and equipment. The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for all aspects of the administrative, financial, capital and operations of asset management in accordance with IRC and donors’ rules and regulations.

- Conduct Asset needs assessment
- Develop Assets maintenance plans as per IRC policies, including repairs tracking and insurance coverage process.
- Ensure spot-checks are done systematically on a quarterly basis, any discrepancies documented and reported; and action to address the root causes developed for all IRC assets, inventory, and equipment.
- Handle asset and property disposal, including auction management as per the IRC asset disposal process
- Ensure that the grant inventory and asset report is accurate, regularly produced, reviewed, and approved before the Grant closing date.

**Logistics and Fleet Management**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for overseeing and coordinating all IRC country fleet transportation and Logistics activities to ensure that all IRC fleet operations are conducted with adherence to IRC Fleet management policies and procedures including vehicles procurement, vehicles movement, maintenance, and reporting accuracy. The Supply Chain Coordinator:

- Implements IRC global Fleet Management policies and procedures and/or develops country specific fleet management policies and procedures needed to comply with local regulations and ensure that they are implemented and followed in all IRC in country offices.
- Ensure that legal status (customs clearance, registration, licenses, insurance) are up to date.
- Conduct transport needs assessments
- Develop and monitor fleet movement plans, vehicle maintenance, driver assignment, vehicle safety, and fuel consumption.
- Analyzes fleet spent, including fuel consumption and maintenance costs and produces reports on a periodic basis to facilitate strategic decisions and ensure fleet optimization
- Regular issuance, review, and usage of vehicle monthly reports to inform strategic decision-making process.

**Compliance and Ethics**

The supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for identifying and analyzing compliance risk in supply chain process, developing, and implementing strong procurement controls. The Supply Chain Coordinator:

- Identifies and sets mitigation plans to manage Supply Chain risks, including identification of red flags, and implementing internal and external audit corrective action plans to ensure all supply chain activities are conducted in an ethical manner.
- Ensures compliance to IRC and donor policies in the procurement and distribution of program supplies and assets.
- Ensure that assessments of supply chain policies, procedures, controls, and performance are conducted, and any deviations addressed in the country program where designated
- Implement and sustain segregation of duties in procurement and other related functions.
- Develop and support implementation of post-audit corrective action plans and other improvement plans.
- Familiarize with various donor regulations.
- Maintain and update donor guidelines related to Supply Chain field (procurement, asset, etc).
- Update as required of the IRC standards in terms of assets/equipment to be purchased.
- Finalize Procurement Plans for all grants.
- Ensure all donor reports for assets are completed and submitted to the Grants Department on time.

**Staff Management and Development:**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible and accountable for overseeing all supply chain learning and development initiatives in the country by:

- Leading the recruitment of new staff through effective utilization of the IRC supply chain competency matrix.
- Ensuring that the supply chain department is well staffed and the roles and responsibilities of each have a clear job description.
- Ensuring each team members' objectives are set following the organizational unit vision as well as operations context(s).
- Identify staffing and/or skill gaps and see that these gaps/needs are filled and support the recruitment of all Supply Chain staff and provide day-to-day supervision of department.
- Provide feedback through regular performance evaluations.
- Ensure that any staff discipline follows a progressive methodology which provides for clear and structured improvement.
- Ensuring assessment of supply chain staff competency and training gaps and develop appropriate intervention programs
- Coordinating training and maintaining training records
- Develop long term plans for continued quality leadership by providing staff development and succession plans

**Pharmaceutical Supply Chain**

- In collaboration with the health team, ensure forecasts and supply planning for pharmaceutical supply are created for all health projects by project start date.
- With the guidance and support from global pharma leadership, develop a supply strategy for the supply of pharmaceuticals (global, regional, national) including freight.
- Ensure the IRC standard pharmaceutical inventory tracking tool is in place and accurately maintained in each location
- Ensure implementation of the IRC pharmaceutical quality assurance policy, associated SOPs, and procedures for Cold Chain best practice in the warehouse and in local transport.
- Ensure adequate drugs management and transportation tool and materials are available for the effective management of drugs.

**Construction Management**

- Supervise construction consultant & construction engineers
- Map construction works for all grants and making sure the procurement process is started and completed on time
- Ensure all due processes like technical drawings and Bills of Quantities (BOQ) approval are done by relevant Authorities before commencement of the procurement process.
- Work with the supervising engineer to ensure timely, cost effective and quality delivery of the works standard as per the specification, requirement, and standard of IRC & its funding agency.
- Ensure compliance with IRC Safety policies and procedures in construction.
- Develop construction tracker and regular update as work progresses

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to**: Senior Field Management Coordinator

**Position directly supervises**: Supply Chain Manager, Construction Consultant, Construction Engineer, Transport Manager, Supply Chain Officer, Supply Chain Systems Officer.

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

**Internal:** Regular relationships with HQ, regional and country Supply Chain staff at all levels, Senior Field Management Coordinator, Country Director, and interacts with IRC Program departments

**External**: May Serve as IRC Supply Chain representative in outside meetings, logistics clusters, other non-governmental organizations, inter-agency groups and foundations.

**REQUIREMENTS:**

**Education:**

- Master’s Degree in Procurement and Logistics or relevant field required.
- Advanced professional certification in supply chain management and/or emergency response management are strongly preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- 8 years of progressive Supply Chain professional experience, with 3 years at a similar level of responsibility
- Experience working in an ERP environment
- Experience with Data Analysis
- Demonstrated ability to develop and roll-out supply chain policy and SOPs.
- Clear training and mentoring ability.
- Experience working with a diverse portfolio of Donors and knowledge of specific donor guidelines.

**Leadership and management skills:**

- Minimum of 5 years of progressive people management/leadership experience, including direct supervision of multi-disciplinary and/or geographically dispersed teams and demonstrated experience leading and managing teams in a complex, matrixed, or emergency response environment, including staff recruitment, performance management, and capacity building.
- Strong leadership and people management skills, with a proven ability to lead, motivate, and hold accountable multi-disciplinary teams across multiple field locations, and Proven change management skills, including the ability to build staff capacity and support succession planning within the Supply Chain function.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- A high degree of flexibility and ability to work under sometimes acute hardship conditions against tight deadlines.
- Strong computer and communication equipment skills, including in Microsoft Office applications.
- Strong collaborator and influencer with effective interpersonal and analytical skills who can work seamlessly across countries, cultures, and organizational units
- Able to work effectively in a highly matrixed structure.
- Strong financial management and budgeting skills.
- Excellent training and coaching ability.
- Ability to travel to remote field offices.

**Language Skills:**

Fluency in English is required.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

**Security:** Kampala is Security Level 2 - yellow.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. jobs.title: EOD Diver Technical Advisor & Senior Mentor (Reserve Pool)
jobs.body:
- **Organization:** HAMAP-Humanitaire (HH)
- **Duty Station:** Primarily based in Kyiv, Ukraine (with frequent travel within Kharkiv Oblast and potentially Sumy/Mykolaiv Oblasts)
- **National Partner:** Ukrainian Deminers Association (UDA)
- **Reporting Line:** Country Coordinator (Ukraine) / Head of Mine Action (HQ)
- **Contract Type:** 9-to 12-month international contract (renewable) – Reserve Pool
- **Security Level:** Volatile, high-risk environment (National Level D) – Strict safety protocols in place

## **Program Context**

In Ukraine, HAMAP-Humanitaire operates under a strict, partner-driven capacity-strengthening framework, respecting a "red line" of non-substitution. Rather than deploying as a direct operator, HAMAP-Humanitaire acts exclusively as a technical mentor, advisor, and quality controller to the **Ukrainian Deminers Association (UDA)**, the country’s premier national civilian mine action operator recently accredited for underwater clearance.

The primary objective of this program is to deploy, consolidate, and scale Ukraine’s first civilian **Land & Water Release** capability. Operations focus on surveying, mapping, and clearing explosive remnants of war (ERW) and submerged munitions from rivers, lakes, agricultural irrigation canals, and water reservoirs heavily affected by active hostilities and hydraulic infrastructure failures.

## **Core Duties & Responsibilities**

### **1. Technical Mentoring, QA/QC & Localization**

- **On-the-Job Mentoring:** Provide daily technical mentoring, coaching, and operational support to UDA EOD team leaders and diving personnel during field deployments.
- **Quality Assurance & Control (QA/QC):** Implement and supervise rigorous QA/QC protocols on UDA subaquatic worksites, ensuring total compliance with International Mine Action Standards (specifically **IMAS 09.60**) and Ukrainian National Mine Action Standards (NMAS).
- **Accreditation Support:** If requested, assist UDA’s leadership in refining and submitting their technical dossiers to secure and maintain national subaquatic demining accreditation with the National Mine Action Centre (NMAC).
- **SOP Development:** Co-evaluate, test on-site, and continuously improve the IMAS-compliant underwater Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) developed jointly by HH and UDA.
- **Technical Representation:** Participate in IMAS review boards and international technical side-event forums to contribute specialized expertise, promote the project’s technical achievements, and actively advance humanitarian and localized approaches to underwater explosive ordnance clearance.

### **2. Subaquatic Operations Supervision & Training**

- **Technical Instruction:** Co-facilitate and supervise advanced theoretical and practical training modules (inland diving operations up to 20 meters depth) for UDA's EOD divers in accordance with HAMAP-Humanitaire's training curriculum.
- **Advanced Technology Deployment:** Oversee the operational use and data analysis of advanced subaquatic detection hardware, including side-scan sonars, marine magnetometers, handheld subaquatic metal detectors, and underwater Remote Operated Vehicles (ROVs).
- **Decompression Safety Innovation:** Implement human-centric safety controls, specifically monitoring post-dive nitrogen desaturation using ultrasonic venous microbubble detection.

### **3. Security, Emergency Management & Ethical Compliance**

- **Hyperbaric Emergency Management:** Validate, update, and run weekly simulated emergency evacuation drills (*Medevac*) and decompression accident management protocols in coordination with designated national hyperbaric medical facilities.
- **HEAT & BTLS Integration:** Actively support the ongoing training and field application of Hostile Environment Awareness Training (HEAT) and Basic Trauma Life Support (BTLS) first aid protocols for all deployed team members.
- **Compliance & Safeguarding:** Ensure absolute adherence to HAMAP-Humanitaire's Code of Conduct, dual-use equipment export regulations, and **PSEAH (Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment)** standards, including the monitoring of internal alert systems for both HH and UDA staff.

## **Job Requirements & Qualifications**

### **Mandatory Certifications**

- **IMAS EOD Level 3**
- **Professional Diving Qualification:** Recognized commercial or military diving certification (equivalent to Ukrainian Class 3 Group 3, *or French **Classe II/III Mention A, B or D** (industrial, technical, or military/rescue diving or or UK **HSE Surface Supplied** (or Royal Navy Clearance Diver equivalent)*.

### **Required Experience & Competencies**

- **HMA Experience:** A minimum of 4 years of operational experience in Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA), with active involvement in Non-Technical Survey (NTS), Technical Survey (TS), and Land Release processes.
- **EOD Diving Expertise:** Proven experience in underwater search, mapping, and EOD recovery in low-visibility, high-current, and high-turbidity inland waterways (rivers, canals, lakes).
- **Pedagogical Skills & Posture:** Proven track record in technical mentoring, training delivery, or capacity building with national personnel (civilian, civil protection, or state deminers). Ability to maintain a highly professional, objective, and standard-compliant posture under pressure.
- **Languages:** Fluent English (essential for project management, donor reporting, and technical documentation). Working knowledge of French, Ukrainian or Russian is considered a significant asset.

### **Working Conditions & Benefits**

- **Contract:** Standard international humanitarian contract
- **Financial Package:** Competitive salary/allowances, monthly per diems, and a dedicated hardship allowance calibrated for active conflict zones in Ukraine.
- **Insurance:** 100% comprehensive medical, life, and repatriation insurance (with specific war-risk coverage).
- **R&R:** Regular Rest and Recuperation cycles provided in line with HAMAP-Humanitaire’s country security guidelines.

jobs.title: Analyst, Office of the CFO (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. jobs.title: Zambia MEL Lead (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

In Zambia, from our hub in Kabwe, we run a specialised climate-smart input and agroforestry program to address challenges such as irregular rainfall and soil degradation. By partnering with local Tree Nursery Operators, we raise and distribute agroforestry trees that enrich soils and build long-term financial resilience. Supported by a structured frontline field team across Central and Southern Provinces, we use rigorous, data-driven frameworks to measure our impact and ensure we drive meaningful improvements in farmer yields, asset accumulation, and food security.

## **About the Role**

We are seeking an exceptional MEL professional with 4+ years of experience to run our day-to-day field data collection operations, and statistical analysis, strengthen data quality, and manage our 13-person field implementation teams. You will coordinate the entire survey lifecycle from questionnaire scripting and data cleaning to field deployment across our operational districts, ensuring our climate-smart agriculture and agroforestry programs are backed by bulletproof evidence to drive impact for smallholder farmers in Zambia. As the team’s direct link to our Global MEL team, you'll be based in Kabwe and report to our Research and Data Lead.

**Survey Design & Data Management**

- Design statistically sound data collection instruments and survey methodologies tailored to rural agricultural interventions.
- Establish rigorous data management workflows, cleaning protocols, and automated quality assurance checks to minimise data errors.

**Survey Analysis**

- Analyse survey data using statistical software (R, Python, etc.) to produce summary statistics and rigorous impact analysis and other statistical analysis as needed (e.g. regression, multi-level modeling, and difference-in-difference methods).
- Apply appropriate statistical approaches, including parametric and non-parametric methods, based on the nature of the data.

- Knowledge of R, Python, or suitable languages, combined with survey tools (e.g., CommCare, ODK, KoboToolbox), and Google Sheets.

- Prior experience directly supervising field teams, enumerator networks, or data collectors in rural environments.

Kabwe, Zambia
