jobs.title: Education and Child Protection Officer (Training Facilitator)
jobs.body:
The **International Rescue Committee (IRC)** responds to the world’s most pressing humanitarian crises and helps people whose lives and livelihoods have been shattered by conflict and disaster. In Poland, IRC is supporting refugees and host communities with economic recovery, livelihood programs, and social protection initiatives to foster resilience and self-reliance.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

REAL Talk is a two-year, EU-funded project that prevents gender-based violence (GBV) and cyber GBV among adolescents aged 11–16 in Poland, Italy and Estonia. It works with adolescents and with the adults around them: caregivers, especially fathers and male caregivers, and school staff and educators. IRC Poland leads the project’s work with caregivers and delivers all activities in Poland, together with IRC Italia (coordinator), Una Casa per l’Uomo, the University of Tartu and the International Child Development Initiatives (ICDI).

The **Education and Child Protection Officer (Training Facilitator)** is IRC Poland’s facilitator for REAL Talk. Working in tandem with another facilitator, the post holder delivers sessions of the project’s Cross-Cultural Socio-Emotional and Relational Education Model: dedicated sessions for adolescent boys, the “Cycle of Aware Fatherhood” workshops for fathers and male caregivers, and training for teachers and educators. The post holder also takes part in the project’s mandatory transnational training for facilitators, which starts on 12 November 2026.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Facilitation and delivery**

- Facilitate sessions of the Model with adolescents aged 11–16 at the partner school: dedicated sessions for boys, and mixed-gender groups co-facilitated with the female facilitator. Groups have 10–15 adolescents and follow a series of 5–8 sessions of 100–120 minutes, reaching around 40 adolescents in Poland.
- Deliver the “Cycle of Aware Fatherhood”: a series of 4–6 workshops of 60–90 minutes for small groups of 3–8 fathers and male caregivers (around 15 in total), on masculinity, emotional literacy, non-violent role modelling and parenting in the digital age.
- Co-facilitate, with the female facilitator, mixed-gender information sessions for parents and caregivers on adolescent relationship violence, social media and online safety (around 80 caregivers).
- Co-deliver training for school staff (around 30 teachers, in groups of about 10) and online basic training sessions for educators across Poland (around 80 participants).
- Create a safe, trauma-informed and non-judgmental space in every session. Respond to disclosures following IRC procedures and refer participants to support services through the agreed referral pathways.

**2. Preparation and learning**

- Take part in, and prepare for, the mandatory transnational capacity-building sessions for facilitators (online, in English). The first session is on 12 November 2026, and further sessions follow through January 2027.
- Study the Model and adapt session plans and materials to the Polish context and to participants with migrant or refugee backgrounds, together with the female facilitator and the project lead.
- Prepare sessions, materials and logistics, and stay in contact with participants, especially fathers, in line with the project’s engagement and retention strategy for caregivers.
- In November 2026, support colleagues, where needed, in focus group discussions and key informant interviews for the project’s research on online masculinity norms.

**3. Partnerships and coordination**

- Coordinate with the partner school (leadership, teachers and school counsellors) on schedules, venues, consent procedures and the recruitment of participants.
- Plan, deliver and debrief sessions jointly with the female facilitator, and exchange practice with facilitators from the project’s partner organizations in Italy and Estonia.
- When requested, support other REAL Talk activities in Poland, such as consultations with adolescents and caregivers, the Champions workshop, the national webinar and the study visit to Poland.

**4. Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL), safeguarding and compliance**

- Administer pre- and post-session questionnaires and feedback tools, and collect signed attendance lists and consent forms, following MEAL guidance and data protection (GDPR) requirements.
- Record sex-disaggregated session data and write short session reports. Contribute lessons learned to the project’s deliverables and donor reports.
- Apply the IRC Child Safeguarding Policy, the IRC Poland Child Protection Response Procedure and the IRC Way standards at all times. Report any concern immediately to the Protection and Safeguarding Coordinator.
- Make sure session materials carry the EU funding acknowledgement required by the donor.
- Mainstream gender equality, inclusion and a Do No Harm approach in all activities.
- Carry out other duties assigned by the supervisor, within the scope of the project.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

- **Working time:** part-time. The indicative workload is around 230 hours over the assignment; the exact working time is confirmed in the offer.
- **November 2026 – January 2027:** onboarding, five online transnational training sessions of about two hours each (the first on 12 November 2026) and, if needed, support to the research activities. The successful candidate must be able to start in time for the first session.
- **February – May 2027 (dates to be confirmed):** delivery of sessions with adolescents, fathers, parents, teachers and educators, as the partner school is confirmed and the school semester allows. The rest of the assignment covers follow-up and reporting.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree (Master’s preferred) in education, pedagogy, psychology, social work, sociology, gender studies or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Additional training in facilitation, child protection or trauma-informed practice is an asset.

**Experience**

- At least 2 years of experience facilitating group sessions or workshops with adolescents and/or adults (such as parents or teachers) in a school, NGO, youth or community setting.
- Experience addressing sensitive topics, such as relationships, consent, violence, masculinity or online risks, in a participatory and non-judgmental way.
- Experience in gender equality, GBV prevention, engaging men and boys, positive parenting or child protection is strongly preferred.
- Familiarity with approaches such as Engaging Men through Accountable Practice (EMAP), Engaging Adolescent Boys in Accountable Practice (EABAP) or My Safety, My Wellbeing is an asset.
- Experience working with refugee or migrant communities, or in EU- or donor-funded projects, is an asset.

**Skills and competencies**

- Strong facilitation skills: able to build trust quickly with adolescent boys, fathers and teachers, and to manage group dynamics.
- Commitment to gender equality, an anti-racist and Do No Harm approach, and to modelling respectful behaviour. Ability to work in close tandem with a co-facilitator and in an international team.
- Good planning and organizational skills, attention to detail and reliable record keeping.
- Good digital skills: Microsoft Office, Teams, Zoom or Google Meet, confidence delivering online sessions, and an understanding of social media and online safety.
- Languages: Polish (fluent or native) and English (upper-intermediate or higher, as the transnational training is delivered in English). Ukrainian and/or Russian is an asset.
- Willingness to travel within Poland, and to deliver some sessions in the late afternoon or evening.
- Right to work in Poland.

Appointment is subject to the safeguarding screening for work with minors required by Polish law and IRC policy, including a certificate from the National Criminal Register, a check in the Register of Sexual Offenders and, where applicable, certificates from other countries of residence.

*We encourage male candidates to apply as the sessions are to be delivered to adolescent boys.*

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: 100 PLN/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Intensive Case Management Caseworker
jobs.body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Job Overview:**

The Intensive Case Management Caseworker will address barriers to safety and wellness for especially vulnerable refugees, asylees, and other ORR-eligible populations. The ICM caseworker will be expected to provide strengths-based, client-centered case management to single-headed refugee households; survivors of domestic violence and gender-based violence; older refugees; youth and young adults without parents or permanent guardians; refugees experiencing mental health or psychological difficulties; refugees with physical disabilities or medical conditions; unanticipated refugee arrivals and secondary migrants; and refugees who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer (LGBTQ). They work closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:** Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Determine client eligibility for ICM programming and conduct intake assessments, review program expectations, outcomes, and confidentiality with each potential client.
- Develop individualized, SMART Self-sufficiency plans for each client enrolled in the ICM program.
- Evaluate client progress every six months during active program enrollment to determine the client’s progress towards goals and work with the client to identify new needs and actions needed.
- Assist clients in navigating healthcare and social service systems, which may include helping clients apply for benefits and attend and schedule appointments.
- Conduct community outreach and maintain a strong network of service providers that meet client needs. The ICM caseworker may also be expected to maintain a strong relationship with local and state level refugee coordinators and health coordinators to ensure client needs are met.
- Provide clients with extended orientation on a variety of topics such as women’s health, navigating transportation systems, and navigating physical healthcare systems at the local level.
- Respond to client crises, with guidance from supervisor as needed.
- Assist clients with requesting financial assistance when applicable and track the received financial assistance within case files.
- Maintain up-to-date documentation in client’s case file to ensure services are properly documented throughout the client’s service period; document all services provided in IRC’s database, Efforts to Outcomes (ETO).
- Attend relevant trainings and meetings at the local and national level.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Safety and Wellness Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers  
**Other Internal and/or external contacts:** The Intensive Case Management Caseworker (Safety and Wellness Caseworker) will be responsible for developing relationships within the network of external relations with grant partners, social service agencies, and government entities.

***Internal:** IRC RSS, Employment team, Youth program and other IRC programs*

***External:** social service agencies, community education presentations, and community outreach*

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $23.50). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: 23705 Project Officer (Disaster Risk Management (DRM)) (P)
jobs.body:
IOM South Sudan implements a broad portfolio of programmes across humanitarian coordination and response, resilience, peacebuilding, transition and development, working closely with the Government of South Sudan, communities, development partners and other stakeholders. Within its community resilience portfolio, IOM implements programmes aimed at strengthening resilience to climate-related shocks, disaster risk and displacement, including the Regional Climate Resilience Program (RCRP), implemented in partnership with the Government of South Sudan with financing from the World Bank. The programme seeks to strengthen flood resilience and reduce the impacts of flooding in targeted areas of South Sudan through flood risk management, climate-resilient infrastructure and strengthened institutional capacity.

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and the direct supervision of the Project Manager (Community Resilience) in Juba, and in close coordination with relevant IOM units and government counterparts, the Project Officer (Disaster Risk Management (DRM)) will be responsible and accountable for supporting the implementation of DRM and flood resilience activities under Regional Climate Resilience Program (RCRP) and across IOM South Sudan's community resilience portfolio. The Project Officer (DRM) will provide technical support on flood risk assessments, hydrological and hydraulic studies, infrastructure design and implementation of flood mitigation works, including dykes, drainage systems, culverts, embankments and other climate-resilient infrastructure. The Project Officer (DRM) will also support the technical review of designs and specifications, monitoring of construction works and quality assurance activities, and assist with the coordination of DRM governance and institutional capacity-building activities, and support the integration of disaster risk reduction and climate resilience into programme planning and implementation.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical support for the planning, design, and implementation of flood risk management and climate-resilient infrastructure under RCRP, including dykes, drainage systems, culverts, embankments, and related works, to support technically sound, climate-resilient, and sustainable investments.
2. Review and provide technical inputs to flood risk assessments, hydrological and hydraulic modelling, feasibility studies, engineering designs, drawings, technical specifications, bills of quantities and other technical documentation, identifying issues and recommending appropriate technical solutions in accordance with applicable standards and project requirements.
3. Monitor the implementation of flood mitigation infrastructure through regular field visits and technical reviews, assessing construction progress, quality of works and compliance with approved designs, specifications, environmental and social requirements and agreed workplans, and flagging technical or implementation issues and recommending appropriate corrective actions to the Project Manager.
4. Support technical coordination with the Government of South Sudan, engineering consultants, contractors and other relevant stakeholders on infrastructure design and implementation, flood risk management and DRM, including through participation in technical meetings, site inspections and review processes.
5. Support the development and implementation of disaster risk management and institutional capacity-building activities, including DRM training, risk-informed planning, preparedness, operation and maintenance arrangements and strengthening of relevant national, state and local government structures.
6. Support the integration of disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, environmental sustainability, community engagement, protection and inclusion considerations into infrastructure planning, design and implementation, supporting resilient and sustainable programme outcomes.
7. Monitor assigned technical and programme activities and prepare technical inputs for project reporting, including progress updates, technical briefs, presentations and other documentation, identifying implementation constraints, risks and emerging issues and proposing appropriate follow-up actions to the Project Manager.
8. Contribute technical inputs to guidance, lessons learnt and knowledge products on flood risk management, climate-resilient infrastructure and DRM, documenting good practices and supporting their application across IOM South Sudan programming.
9. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, Hydraulic Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change/Climate Governance, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in the planning, design, implementation and/or technical oversight of flood risk management and climate-resilient infrastructure, including dykes, drainage systems, culverts, embankments or similar infrastructure;
- Experience in reviewing engineering designs, drawings, technical specifications, bills of quantities and other technical documentation related to infrastructure works;
- Experience in monitoring construction works, including field inspections, assessment of progress and quality, identification of technical issues and follow-up on corrective actions;
- Experience with flood risk assessments, hydrological and/or hydraulic studies and modelling, including application of technical findings to infrastructure planning and design;
- Experience in disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation and/or resilience programming, preferably including institutional capacity building and risk-informed planning;
- Experience coordinating with government authorities, engineering consultants, contractors, communities and other technical stakeholders in the implementation of infrastructure or DRM programmes;
- Experience working in humanitarian, recovery, stabilisation or development contexts, preferably in fragile or conflict-affected environments; and,
- Experience working in South Sudan or a comparable operational context is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated technical knowledge of flood risk management, climate-resilient infrastructure and disaster risk reduction;
- Ability to review and interpret engineering designs, drawings, technical specifications and bills of quantities;
- Demonstrated knowledge of relevant engineering standards, construction quality assurance and infrastructure operation and maintenance principles;
- Proficiency in relevant engineering and technical software, including AutoCAD and/or GIS applications; knowledge of hydrological/hydraulic modelling software is an advantage;
- Demonstrated analytical, technical writing, reporting and communication skills; and,
- Demonstrated proficiency in standard office software, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Senior Policy Officer – Remote (within the range of ET–CET Time Zones)
jobs.body:
PATHWAYS INTERNATIONAL

**Senior Policy Officer**

**About us – what do we do?**

At a time of unprecedented forced displacement and system disruption, we are reforming the global system of safe and legal routes to protection. Our world-class team works closely with leaders and innovators from across sectors in over 20 countries. Together we design, launch, and expand safe and legal routes for displaced people. Together we pilot bold new ideas aimed at making the entire global system of safe and legal routes stronger and more sustainable.

**How we do it**

- We build and lead powerful partnerships and networks.
- We provide trusted advice.
- We accelerate operational delivery.
- We generate and share insights.
- We inspire change.

**About the role – what will you do?**

We are seeking a **Senior** **Policy Officer** to join the powerful global team at Pathways International (PI).

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to PI’s global strategy on pathways to protection and community sponsorship by working closely with the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and the Executive Chair (EC) as part of the executive office.

The role will include supporting the CEO and the EC in their daily work, which includes high-profile public and private engagements across a wide range of stakeholders, including those at a high political level and within the private sector. We are looking for a strategic thought partner who can proactively project manage multiple high-level strategic mandates in the executive office consistently and on schedule, while supporting the CEO and EC’s time management and achievement of deliverables.

The role will also entail supporting the CEO and the EC in preparing, executing, and following up on key meetings of the organization’s senior executives and the Board.

**Responsibilities**

- **Coordination of strategic initiatives:** Oversee end-to-end coordination of strategic projects, acting as a central point of contact for the CEO and EC to manage and track high-priority  
    timelines, dependencies, and deliverables across the executive office to ensure strategic goals and organizational objectives are met on schedule.
- **Stakeholder management, development and communication support:** Support and coordinate the CEO’s and the EC’s engagements with key PI partners, including with government, the private sector, and other NGOs, in particular to further the organization’s fundraising and development strategy. The candidate must be able to manage high-level stakeholders in a highly professional manner while exercising discretion and good judgment. This role will also entail coordinating PI’s communication on social media channels.
- **Writing and analysis:** Prepare policy and other briefing documents to support the CEO and the EC. Offer executive-level communication support, including drafting and editing of confidential background documents, correspondence and emails.
- **Meeting and event organization**: Collaborate with colleagues to prepare meeting strategy. Prepare agendas; schedule and organize meetings with senior stakeholders, and record and distribute minutes. Communicate with meeting and event participants in a professional and timely manner.
- **Organizational development:** Support the CEO in fostering the organizational development of Pathways International, in particular by integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into PI’s work, with a strong comfort level using AI tools to draft high-quality correspondence and streamline project management processes.

**About you – who are we looking for?**

We are looking for a restless, nimble, and confident team member who can tactfully, strategically and effectively project manage work within the executive office, while contributing to policy analysis and writing at a senior level within a dynamic and fast-paced environment.

- You have a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field—such as public policy, public affairs, political science, or international development; or equivalent professional experience in diplomatic, private sector, political or chief of staff roles.
- You have a proven understanding of one or more relevant fields which may include: forced displacement, refugee protection, global migration, geopolitics and diplomacy.
- You have at least eight years of relevant work experience in a fast-paced work environment, with a preference for direct work with executive offices or similar functions.
- You have strong organizational skills and thrive on project managing executive office projects, meetings and event deliverables and deadlines to enable leadership success critical to the organization.
- You demonstrate strong policy capability, able to research, analyze and draft high-quality briefings and materials for senior stakeholders with keen attention to detail.
- You have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Proficiency in other languages, in particular Spanish and Italian, is an asset. Editorial or copyediting experience is also an asset.
- You have excellent interpersonal skills and experience collaborating with people from different backgrounds, countries, cultures and languages.
- You are able to work on a varied and constantly evolving portfolio, while consistently displaying professionalism, discretion, tact and responsibility. You have a strong understanding of confidentiality and need-to-know principles, ideally having directly handled similar sensitive functions.
- You have a strong comfort level using AI tools to draft high-quality correspondence and to inform and strengthen project management processes.
- You are comfortable preparing well-presented PowerPoint and Word documents and using Excel, Zoom, MS Teams and SharePoint.

We encourage applications from qualified candidates with lived experience of forced displacement, migration, or with close personal and cultural connections to refugee communities.

**Location**

This is a full-time **remote position within the range of Eastern Time (ET) to Central European Time (CET)**. The candidate must be available for flexible working hours, including meetings in CET and ET.

Applicants contacted for evaluation will be asked to provide proof that they have the legal right to work in their country of residence. Maintaining such legal right to work in their country of residence is a condition of employment.

**Salary**

Competitive, commensurate with experience.

**Contract**

- One-year term contract (renewable)

**How to apply**

Please submit in English:

- Cover letter
- CV
- Unedited writing sample of no more than five pages.

Please apply through BambooHR at [https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/60](https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/60) by **November 15th, 2026, at 11:59 pm EST** to be considered for this position.

**Equal opportunity employer**

Pathways International is an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage applications from qualified candidates of all genders and from all national, religious, and ethnic backgrounds, including persons with disabilities and those with lived experience of forced displacement. We will provide accommodation upon request during the recruitment, selection, and assessment process.

jobs.title: Country WASH & Infrastructure Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Overall purpose of the role**

Under the direct supervision of the Head of Programme, the Country WASH & Infrastructure Coordinator provides technical leadership, strategic guidance and quality assurance for DRC Sudan's WASH and WASH infrastructure portfolio, covering emergency, nexus and long-term WASH, water resources, sanitation and hygiene, climate resilience and preparedness, and WASH in institutions. The role also supports programme development and positioning, working with DRC technical and area teams, global advisors, and partners and authorities.

**Responsibilities**

The post holder acts as DRC Sudan's national technical advisor for WASH and WASH infrastructure, working closely with Area Managers and technical teams to ensure timely, high-quality implementation. Area Managers retain operational management and delivery; the Coordinator sets technical standards, provides oversight and quality assurance, and supports planning, proposals and technical documents (e.g. designs, BoQs, tools, SoPs). To achieve the overall and specific position's objectives, the job holder's tasks and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

***Technical Leadership, Strategy and Programme Quality***

- Provide technical leadership on WASH: develop and update the WASH strategy under the Sudan Country Strategy, and produce standards, guidance, tools and SoPs aligned with Sphere, national codes, Cluster guidance and DRC frameworks.
- Ensure coherent approaches across emergency, protracted-displacement and nexus/long-term WASH, moving from emergency response towards sustainable, climate-resilient services with sound O&M and local ownership.
- Integrate WASH with Protection, Shelter/Site Management, and Economic Recovery, including cholera response.
- Support field teams in needs identification and RNAs; conduct field visits (including Darfur) or remote follow-up where access is constrained, to quality-assure design, construction and implementation.

***Water, Sanitation, Hygiene and Community-Led Approaches***

- Water supply and resources: advise on hydrogeological and source assessments, groundwater and surface water options (e.g. boreholes, hafirs), solar systems, water quality and conflict-sensitive access, promoting IWRM.
- Sanitation: guide safe, inclusive sanitation across the service chain (household, communal, camp and institutional), including excreta management, market-based sanitation, solid waste and vector control.
- Hygiene and behaviour change: promote evidence-based hygiene promotion and social and behaviour change approaches, including menstrual health, adapted to context and informed by community feedback.
- Community-led WASH: promote community-led approaches (e.g. CLTS, WASH committees, community management of services, local service providers) for ownership, O&M and sustainability.
- WASH in schools and public institutions (incl. health facilities, IPC): standards, designs and sustainable management.

***Climate, Resilience, AA and Preparedness***

- Integrate climate risk, DRR, nature-based solutions and IWRM into WASH strategy and design, promoting climate-resilient infrastructure (e.g. solar, flood-proofing).
- Lead WASH preparedness and anticipatory action: contingency planning, early warning and trigger-based action for floods, drought and cholera, prepositioning of supplies and surge readiness, with the WASH Cluster and authorities.

***Infrastructure, Engineering Review and Procurement***

- Lead the technical review and clearance of WASH designs, drawings, BoQs, specifications and cost estimates (water, sanitation, schools and public institutions), ensuring feasibility, cost-effectiveness and compliance with standards.
- Guide tendering, contracting, supervision, quality control, handover and O&M, including rehabilitation of damaged systems.
- Support Area WASH Managers and Supply Chain in procurement and pipeline planning, including market-based approaches.

***Proposals, Monitoring, Reporting and Accountability***

- Lead technical WASH and infrastructure inputs to proposals, concept notes, budgets, donor reports and advocacy notes, and to business development including nexus opportunities; apply DRC's Operational Handbook.
- With MEAL teams, ensure projects are designed and monitored to DRC and sector standards and donor requirements (including water quality, infrastructure functionality and remote monitoring), and capture learning and good practice.
- Ensure accountability mechanisms and mainstreaming of protection, gender, disability and PSEA.

***Capacity Building, Partners and Technical HR***

- Design and deliver capacity building for DRC and partner staff (e.g. Sphere, cholera and flood response, water quality, O&M, behaviour change, infrastructure design), strengthening local partners and localisation.
- Advise on technical recruitment and competency frameworks; promote the code of conduct.

***Representation and Coordination***

- Represent DRC in national and sub-national WASH Cluster and coordination forums, feeding 5Ws and insights to teams.
- Build relationships with authorities, donors, UN agencies and partners to maintain trust in DRC's technical standards; with Area WASH Managers, maintain mapping of WASH actors and identify potential partners.

**Qualifications, Experience and Technical Competencies**

- Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering (or Water/Environmental Engineering) required; Master's degree in WASH, water resources management, hydrogeology or a related field desirable.
- Minimum 5 years relevant WASH experience, including at least 3 in a technical advisory or coordination role.
- Proven experience in complex emergency and protracted-displacement contexts (Sudan/Darfur or comparable).
- Solid engineering background: technical design and review of BoQs, specifications and drawings for water supply (groundwater, solar pumping), sanitation and WASH in schools and public institutions.
- Strong knowledge of sanitation, hygiene and behaviour change, community-led approaches (e.g. CLTS), cholera response, water resources management, and climate-resilient WASH and anticipatory action.
- Experience in standards and tool development, proposals, donor reporting and WASH Cluster coordination.
- Proven ability to live and work in an unstable, insecure environment.

**Languages:**

- Proficiency in written and spoken English.
- Fluency in Arabic is desirable

**About you**

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:*

- *Striving for excellence:* You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- *Collaborating:* You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- *Taking the lead:* You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- *Communicating:* You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- *Demonstrating integrity*: Upholding and promoting the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Conditions**

*Contract:* One-year contract with possibility of extension, subject to funding and performance. Salary and conditions in accordance with the Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for International staff. This position is graded at Band NM.F

*Start Date:* December 2026

*Duty Station:* Khartoum, Sudan (with regular field travel)

Reports to: Head of Programme

jobs.title: HR & Administration Manager Nigeria Abuja
jobs.body:
**What we’re looking for:**

Are you an experienced HR professional ready to strengthen people management, build organisational capacity, and drive operational excellence in a humanitarian setting? NRC Nigeria is looking for a results-driven **HR & Administration Manager** to lead and strengthen HR and administrative functions across its country programme.

In this role, you will help shape and implement the HR strategy, strengthen recruitment processes, promote staff development, and drive training and capacity-building initiatives. You will ensure that HR and administration systems remain efficient, effective, and aligned with NRC standards, enabling teams to deliver on their humanitarian mandate. This opportunity is open to **Nigerian nationals only**.

**What you will do:**

***Human Resources:***

- Provide leadership in the implementation of the Global Standards and initiatives at Country and Area Office level (NRC People Management Systems, Talent Management, L&D initiative, Duty of care, PSEA…)
- Plan and feed into country wide strategies and plans, working closely with senior
- Pro-actively work to support the Area Manager, Area Support Manager, HR Team Leads & HR Officers in running an effective HR function in the Area Offices
- Lead efforts in facilitating staff consultations, town halls, and feedback sessions in efforts to build and sustain employee-engagement.
- Lead efforts in monitoring employee wellbeing and champion initiatives to improve employee wellness, ensuring a best-practice staff care programme for all staff is regularly reviewed and that adequate staff care systems are in place and implemented across the country.
- Work with the CMG to facilitate role mapping, position rationalisation and support leadership in communicating organizational changes
- Ensure robust onboarding plans that enable organisational-wide understanding of organizational priorities are in place and implemented across the country offices.
- Strengthen the recruitment processes, ensuring adherence to the minimum standards management and programmes to ensure HR proactively meets the needs of the programme
- Payroll: Ensures accuracy of payroll before transmission to the Finance team/Manager.
- Handling personnel cases according to guidelines and policies
- Focal point for working with the Nigeria staff representatives

***Administration:***

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

jobs.title: International Migration Data Governance Specialist
jobs.body:
## **Job Description**

**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

The consultancy contributes to the the ‘Awda Amina Phase II: Strengthening Miration Governance in Iraq’ project funded by the European Union and to the ‘Strengthening Data Systems to Improve the Managament of Internally Displaced Persons Referral Systems in Iraq’ project funded by the United Nations Internal Displacement Solutions Fund.   
Under the overall guidance of the Head of Sub-Office (Erbil) and the direct supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research), The consultant will provide specialized technical support and policy-development support to IOM staff working on migration and displacement data governance initiatives under the project portfolio. The consultant will draft technical and policy documents under the supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research) and support technical consultations, workshops, framework development, implementation tracking, and reporting activities, identify technical and policy challenges, and provide recommendations for consideration by the Programme Officer (DTM and Research). All managerial, representational, and decision-making functions shall remain the responsibility of IOM staff.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

  
The consultant will work under the direct supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research) and the overall supervision of the Head of Sub-Office (Erbil).

## **Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**Data ownership and access**

  
i. Support the development a structured framework that outlines roles, responsibilities and processes for managing migration and displacement data across government ministries and agencies, in both Federal Iraq and KRI.  
ii. Provide technical support and draft clear guidelines for data ownership, access, sharing and utilisation, complying with national policies and promoting adherence with international best practices in terms of data protection.  
iii. Under the supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research) and in consultation with relevant IOM staff, the consultant will provide technical input and draft documentation for consideration by IOM in relation to:  
 i) Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) between relevant ministries and the Central Statistical Office; and  
 ii) data-sharing protocols between Federal and KRG authorities aimed at enhancing collaboration and access to migration-related data.  
iv. Draft a Data Integration Framework and provide technical recommendations regarding its implementation under the supervision of the Programme Officer (DTM and Research), to establish links with the National Referral Mechanism and enable seamless data flow by connecting the digital infrastructure for migration management.

**Data standards**

  
v. Draft a national framework for migration and displacement-related statistical definitions and concepts aligned with international/UN recommendations and standards, integrating inputs from consultations led by IOM staff with relevant national and international partners.  
vi. Develop technical data guidelines and standardized indicators to ensure consistency and comparability across different governmental agencies in the operationalization of agreed definitions.

**Data analysis and use**

  
vii. Utilize secondary data analysis to inform and enhance policy development and facilitate Iraq's participation in international migration data forums.  
viii. Develop recommendations for improved data analysis and reporting on migration and displacement by relevant Ministries, supporting evidence-based policy formulation.  
ix. Prepare briefing materials and provide technical support to IOM staff for intra- and inter-ministerial workshops led by IOM staff.Draft recommendations, publication schedules, and other technical documents to facilitate the publishing of periodic statistics on government-owned websites to ensure public availability of migration data.

**Other**  
x. Perform any other duties as may be assigned.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

• Agreed outputs set out in the ToRs are delivered in a timely manner and to a satisfactory quality standard.  
• Technical outputs produced by the consultant result in measurable improvements in data governance practices.

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

• Master’s degree in law, economics, political science, public policy, demography/statistics, or a related field with at least five years of relevant professional experience, or Bachelor’s degree with seven years of professional experience.  
• Proven experience in migration data governance through previous work with government bodies, international organizations or think tanks.  
• Familiarity with international statistical standards such as the International Recommendations on IDP Statistics and the Recommendations on Statistics of International Migration and Temporary.  
• Familiarity with IOM’s Data Protection Principles and with othe international data protection frameworks and best practices.  
• Familiarity with the Iraqi context and government institutions.  
• Strong writing and communication skills; experience in facilitating multi-stakeholder workshops and in drafting policy framework, guidelines and technical standards.  
• Fluency in Arabic and English.

**Languages**

For this consultancy, excellent command of English is required.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

Yes

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

jobs.title: Mozambique - Head of Finance and Administrative department (M/F) - PEMBA
jobs.body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 03/01/2027**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**  
**Location: Pemba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

Solidarités International (SI) has been providing life-saving assistance in northern Mozambique since March 2019, initially responding to Cyclone Idai. As the crisis in Cabo Delgado escalated, SI began operations in Mueda in July 2021 and progressively expanded to other northern districts including Nangade, Muidumbe, Palma and, more recently, Mocímboa da Praia. By 2022, SI had established a coordination office in Pemba and operational bases in Mueda and Palma.  
Following the closure of the Palma base, SI opened a new base in Mocímboa da Praia in July 2023 to support urgent returnee needs. Today, SI operates from Pemba, Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia, covering not only the northern districts (Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Palma) but also additional districts further south, such as Metuge, Chiúre, Mecúfi and Ancuabe.  
In 2024–2025, SI Mozambique has prioritized integrated, multisectoral programming focused on the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM), WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), and Shelter/NFI. At the beginning of 2025, however, major BHA funding cuts forced a significant restructuring, reducing the mission from approximately 140 to around 50 staff and prompting a reorganization of operations to maintain essential activities.  
This restructuring coincided with a deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with renewed attacks, increased displacement, and unpredictable access since mid-2024, requiring continuous adaptation of SI’s strategies.  
In 2026, despite these challenges, SI continues to deliver principled, needs-based assistance across Cabo Delgado with the support of key donors such as ECHO, SDC, CDCS, OCHA, IFSAN and UNICEF while exploring emergency and nexus funding opportunities with other donors such as DG INTPA, adapting its WASH strategy and stenghtening its FSL expertise,

## About the job

**GENERAL OBJECTIVE:**

The administrative coordinator will direct and coordinate all administrative, accounting and financial services associated with the mission.  
He/she will take part in defining Solidarités International’s human resources policy and ensure that it is followed.  
As coordinator, he is responsible for the mission’s financial balance.  
He/she will monitor adherence to Solidarités administrative procedures and donor procedures as well as to the laws of the country in which intervention is taking place.  
He/she is the point of reference for the mission, and the link between headquarters and the mission for all administrative matters.

**THE MAIN CHALLENGES:**

• Complex and evolving Mozambican legal and administrative environment   
• Visa and work permit procedures for expatriates remain lengthy and restrictive  
• Young mission with a relatively new team requiring training, coaching, and mentoring  
• In 2025 and 2026, the mission went through rapid decline and growth of its budget which led to signfiicant delays in accounting closure, budget management and reporting.

**PRIORITIES FOR THE 2/3 FIRST MONTHS:**

• Stabilised the implementation of the shared costs policy

• Strengthen and build the capacities of the HR and Finance newly nationalised teams

• Ensure ongoing capacity building and follow-up with the local partner organizations.

• Support the development of new financial proposals, including budget preparation

• Implement SI's new financial software in Mozambique

• Streghten internal control, conduct internal audit and lead on the financial aspects of the external audits

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS:**

Very limited security constraints in Pemba where the position is based ; with regular visits of one to two weeks visits in the different bases.  
Mueda and Chiure – more restrictions; movement and activities depend on local conditions and Security Department guidance.

## Your profile

**DIPLOMA AND EXPERIENCE:**

Diploma : Minimumum Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration,Social sciences , Organization Development or related HR discipline

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS:**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. In-depth technical knowledge of the principles and concepts in HR administration (workforce and organizational planning,recruitment & selection , compensation and benefits , performance management, Training and development, employee relations, staff health and safety, and employee engagement), HR-good-practices, HR information systems and databases; / Knowledgeand experience working with SI HR procedures and tools is a major plus
2. Mastery of budget and accounting management, shared costs requirement, donors' financial requirements, audit management
3. Experience in capacity building and setting frameworks for staff development
4. Experience leading workplace investigation and supporting resolution of employee relations / Knowledge of Mozambique labout law is a plus

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. coordination and management skills
2. training and facilitation skills
3. Diplomacy

**LANGUAGE:**

1. English mandatory
2. Portuguese is desirable
3. Spanish a plus if no portuguese

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Pemba is a peaceful coastal city with beautiful beaches, seafood, and a wide range of restaurants and leisure activities. There is no curfew, and walking is allowed during the day for expatriates. Many international NGOs are present. The guesthouse offers comfortable living conditions for expatriates with stable water and electricity. Internet connectivity is reliable (4G). Both bases are reachable by UNHAS flight in less than one hour.

jobs.title: MEAL Assistant – Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning
jobs.body:
## **1. Background**

Habibi Association was founded in Italy in 2013 to promote social justice and socio-economic inclusion, with a particular focus on refugee protection, humanitarian assistance and support for people experiencing poverty or affected by conflict. The Association is recognised as a Civil Society Organisation by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (*Agenzia Italiana per la Cooperazione allo Sviluppo – AICS*) and operates in several countries across the Middle East.

In 2018, Habibi Association registered with Jordan’s Ministry of Social Development and has since implemented projects supporting refugees and vulnerable members of host communities, with particular attention to women, young people and persons with disabilities.

Habibi Association is seeking a **MEAL Assistant** to support the implementation and development of monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities across its projects in Jordan, ensuring the quality and effective use of project data.

## **2. Key Responsibilities**

Reporting to the MEAL Officer and working closely with Project Managers, the MEAL Assistant will be responsible for the following:

**A. Monitoring, Evaluation and Data Management**

- Support the implementation of projects’ MEAL plans and monitoring tools, including logical frameworks, project monitoring plans, indicator tracking tables and project databases.
- Support the design, adaptation and digitalisation of data collection tools, ensuring that data is systematically disaggregated by sex, age, displacement status, disability and other relevant vulnerability criteria.
- Conduct field visits to project implementation areas, currently including Amman, Zarqa, Maan, Mafraq, Madaba, Ader and Petra, to monitor progress, document challenges and verify reported results.
- Support baseline, midline and endline assessments, post-distribution monitoring and beneficiary satisfaction surveys.
- Contribute to data cleaning, validation and Data Quality Assessments (DQAs), ensuring that collected information is accurate, consistent and reliable.
- Analyse quantitative and qualitative data and contribute to the preparation of monitoring reports, donor reports and other project documentation.
- Support needs assessments and the development of new project proposals through data collection, analysis and the identification of relevant indicators.

**B. Accountability and Learning**

- Support the establishment and management of accessible Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms (CFMs), ensuring the confidential recording, follow-up and analysis of feedback in accordance with established procedures.
- Contribute to the analysis of feedback and monitoring findings to identify trends, challenges and opportunities for improving project implementation.
- Support project reflection sessions and the documentation of lessons learned and success stories, ensuring that findings are evidence-based and contribute to organisational learning.
- Provide technical support to project teams and implementation partners on MEAL tools, data collection procedures and reporting requirements.

**C. Coordination and Organisational Support**

- Participate in internal project meetings and coordination meetings with consortium partners, as required.
- Collaborate closely with Project Managers and teams, implementation partners and relevant external stakeholders.

## **3. Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Degree in Social Sciences, Political Science, International Relations, International Cooperation, Statistics or a related field.

**Professional Experience and Technical Skills**

- At least two years of relevant professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities, preferably within development or humanitarian projects.
- Practical experience with MEAL frameworks, indicator tracking tools, digital data collection and project databases.
- Knowledge of quantitative and qualitative data collection methods, data cleaning and validation, data quality assurance, and the preparation of analytical reports.
- Familiarity with Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms (CFMs) and accountability to affected populations.
- Good command of IT tools and standard office software. Experience with KoboToolbox or other digital data collection and management software will be considered an asset.
- Valid driving licence and ability to drive in Jordan.

**Languages**

- Advanced proficiency in Arabic, both written and spoken.
- Proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

**Personal and Interpersonal Skills**

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to work constructively with people from diverse backgrounds.
- A proactive, solution-oriented approach and the ability to respond effectively to challenges.
- Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and commitment to meeting deadlines.
- Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and maintain confidentiality.
- Commitment to social inclusion, child protection, gender equality and the rights and dignity of vulnerable and marginalised people.
- Willingness and availability to travel regularly to project locations outside Amman.

## **4. Contractual Conditions**

- **Duty station:** Amman, Jordan.
- **Contract duration:** 12 months.
- **Expected starting date:** December 2026 / January 2027.
- **Gross monthly salary:** JOD 850–950, depending on the candidate’s qualifications and relevant experience.

jobs.title: Head of Programmes - CAR
jobs.body:
DanChurchAid (DCA) is looking for an experienced Head of Programmes to lead its Central African Republic (CAR) programme portfolio. Reporting to the Country Director and serving on the Senior Management Team, you will turn country strategy into well-managed projects, strengthen programme quality and partnerships, and support teams delivering assistance in a demanding operating environment.

**Duty station:** Bangui, with regular travel to field locations | International, non-accompanied position

**Contract:** 12 months, with the possibility of extension | Opening date: 22 October 2026 | **Closing date: 20 November 2026**

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply early.

**Our programme in CAR**

DCA has worked in CAR since 2015, implementing humanitarian, development and peacebuilding activities directly and with national civil society partners. Our work responds to the consequences of conflict and displacement while supporting recovery, community resilience and efforts to reduce violence and exclusion.

The portfolio brings together protection, psychosocial support and assistance to victims of conflict; conflict prevention, peacebuilding and social cohesion; and cash assistance and food security. Humanitarian mine action and explosive ordnance risk awareness also form part of DCA’s experience in CAR. We seek practical links between these areas, informed by communities’ priorities and by conflict-sensitive analysis.

Current projects portfolio includes project funded by the Gov. Of CAR (back donor World Bank) alongside interventions supported by ECHO, INTPA, FPI, the CAR Humanitarian Fund, the UN Peacebuilding Fund, the ICC Trust Fund for Victims and Danish strategic partnership funding. These projects combine different delivery models, partnership arrangements and reporting requirements. The Head of Programmes will maintain a coherent portfolio while ensuring that each project meets its commitments to communities and donors.

**Your team and working relationships**

You will work with project managers, area coordinators, MEAL colleagues, technical staff and national partners, supported by DCA headquarters advisers. Based in Bangui, you will maintain close contact with field teams and make regular visits to implementation locations.

DCA CAR is strengthening area-based management and clarifying responsibilities between programme and support functions. The Head of Programmes provides programme, MEAL and quality oversight and technical supervision within the authority delegated by the Country Director. Area coordinators retain line management of staff assigned to them, while multi-area project oversight and management remains under the Head of Programmes. You will make these arrangements work in practice through clear priorities, coaching, joint planning and timely escalation of unresolved issues.

Close collaboration with finance, procurement, logistics and HR is essential. Together, you will ensure that activity plans, procurement schedules, staffing, budgets and donor commitments are realistic and aligned.

**What you will lead**

• **Programme strategy and relevance:** translate the country strategy into operational priorities; use needs assessments, IPC and MSNA findings, response coverage and community feedback to guide geographic and sector choices; identify and secure opportunities that fit DCA’s capacity and added value.

• **Delivery and quality:** steer complex projects through integrated project management frameworks; oversee and support implementation against agreed results, budgets and timelines; support project managers and area coordinators to identify delays early, agree corrective actions and follow them through; ensure technical standards, protection mainstreaming and conflict sensitivity across the portfolio.

• **People and management:** manage staff assigned to you under the country organigram; set clear objectives, delegate effectively and address performance issues; provide technical supervision and coaching to area coordinators and programme colleagues through the agreed management framework.

• **MEAL and accountability:** strengthen practical monitoring systems, data quality and analysis; create and maintain project and portfolio dashboards covering progress, results, expenditure, procurement, deadlines and risks, and use them to guide management reviews and corrective actions; ensure accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms, including safe referral of sensitive complaints; use findings to improve delivery and demonstrate results.

• **Partnerships and localisation:** build equitable relationships with national organisations; agree responsibilities, resources and capacity-strengthening priorities jointly; work with support colleagues on proportionate due diligence, partner monitoring and follow-up.

• **Project development and funding:** lead concept notes, proposals, results frameworks and donor reports with country and HQ colleagues; work with finance and support teams on credible budgets, staffing and procurement plans; maintain a realistic funding pipeline.

• **Grant and risk management:** maintain oversight of reporting deadlines, contractual commitments and programme risks; work with finance colleagues on budget reviews, forecasts and partner expenditure; ensure that changes requiring donor approval are identified and addressed in time.

• **Cash working group Co-lead:** Act as the Cash Working Group co lead; providing support to the WFP / OCHA led structure and ensuring adequate support to the group.

• **Senior management and representation:** contribute to country-level decisions, organisational priorities and risk reviews; represent DCA with donors, clusters, authorities, civil society and peer agencies; promote cooperation across departments and support agreed SMT decisions.

**The challenges you will help us address**

You will join a programme that needs both strategic direction and consistent management follow-through. Priorities include keeping a diverse portfolio on track, strengthening the connection between field delivery and Bangui oversight, and improving the use of monitoring and financial information in decisions. The World Bank-funded NDOYE project adds a substantial implementation and contractual workload alongside humanitarian and peacebuilding grants.

Success will require early procurement and staffing planning, clear ownership of actions, strong programme–support collaboration and constructive engagement with partners. You will balance immediate delivery pressures with team development and sustainable systems, adapting plans to access and security constraints while protecting programme quality and accountability to communities.

**What you bring**

• At least three years of experience managing a multi-project programme portfolio, including responsibility for staff, programme quality, donor engagement and delivery in a complex humanitarian or fragile setting.

• Strong knowledge of CAR or comparable Central African contexts, and the ability to translate political, conflict and humanitarian analysis into practical programme decisions. Previous experience in CAR is a strong asset.

• Previous substantive experience in at least two of the following three areas is required: cash programming; food security; and Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning, including Accountability to Affected Populations. Experience in protection, conflict prevention or peacebuilding is an additional asset.

• Demonstrated people-management skills: setting priorities, coaching managers, delegating, resolving disagreements and holding teams accountable while maintaining respectful working relationships.

• Proven experience developing successful proposals and producing clear donor reports. Familiarity with ECHO, pooled humanitarian funds, UN funding or institutional development financing is an advantage; World Bank-funded project experience is particularly relevant.

• Demonstrated experience steering complex projects involving multiple locations, partners, funding requirements or interdependent workstreams. You can translate contractual commitments into integrated workplans, track milestones and dependencies, and lead corrective action across programme and support teams.

• Hands-on experience designing and using project or portfolio dashboards that bring together activities, results, expenditure, procurement, reporting deadlines and risks. You can establish reliable data flows, assign responsibility for updates, and use dashboards in management reviews to drive decisions and follow-up.

• Experience strengthening community accountability and equitable partnerships with national organisations, including capacity development and management of implementation risks. Strong judgement under pressure, experience working in insecure environments, and a commitment to safeguarding, inclusion and responsible risk management. Recent HEAT or equivalent training is desirable.

• Fluency in written and spoken French and a good working knowledge of English are required. You must be able to lead teams and engage with partners in French, and work effectively with English-language donor documents, reporting and headquarters communications.

**What we offer**

• A 12-month contract with the possibility of extension and a competitive salary package.

• 30 days of paid annual leave and three R&R cycles per year, subject to DCA’s Staff Welfare Policy for Bangui as a duty station.

• Insurance as per industry standards.

• A substantive leadership role with opportunities to shape programme quality, develop colleagues and strengthen national partnerships, with support from country and headquarters teams.

**How to apply**

Please submit your CV and cover letter through DCA’s online recruitment system by **20 November 2026**. Explain how your experience relates to the portfolio, management responsibilities and challenges described above. Only applications submitted through the recruitment system will be considered. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Applications open on 23 October 2026 and will be reviewed on a rolling basis throughout the three-week publication period. Shortlisting and interviews may begin before the closing date, so early applications are encouraged.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, abilities or ethnic affiliation are encouraged to apply. DCA conducts an anti-terror check as part of the recruitment process. It is a prerequisite that you can pass this check and maintain this status throughout your employment. Everyone applying for a job with DCA must be ready to comply with our Staff Policy on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment and our Child Safeguarding Policy.

jobs.title: Grants and Partnership Manager
jobs.body:
**What we are looking for**

We are looking for a strategic, proactive, and collaborative professional who is passionate about strengthening humanitarian response through effective grants management, resource mobilisation, and meaningful partnerships.

The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise with excellent leadership and relationship-building skills, bringing people and organisations together to deliver quality, accountable, and impactful programmes.

Knowledge of the Jordan’s humanitarian context is also important.

***We invite applications from qualified internal candidates in NRC Jordan matching the profile.*** ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Jordan, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***

**What you will do**

NRC Jordan is seeking a dynamic and results-oriented **Grants & Partnerships Manager** to provide strategic leadership in grants management, business development, and partnership development, contributing to high-quality programming and impactful humanitarian interventions in Jordan.

Key responsibilities:

- **Grants Management and Compliance:** Oversee the grants portfolio, ensuring compliance with NRC policies, donor requirements, project cycle management standards, and reporting deadlines.
- **Proposal Development and Fundraising:** Lead the development of high-quality concept notes, funding proposals, and donor reports, while identifying new funding opportunities and supporting donor engagement.
- **Strategic Partnership Management:** Lead the development and implementation of the Country Office partnership strategy, promoting equitable, sustainable partnerships aligned with NRC’s localisation objectives.
- **Partner Assessment and Capacity Building:** Oversee partner identification, due diligence, capacity assessments, risk mitigation, and capacity-strengthening initiatives.
- **Systems and Quality Assurance:** Strengthen grants and partnership management systems, tools, SOPs, and processes to ensure quality, accountability, and continuous learning.
- **Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination:** Build and maintain effective relationships with donors, implementing partners, and internal teams to support quality programming and shared objectives.
- **Team Leadership and Development:** Provide technical and administrative leadership to Grants & Partnerships staff, fostering performance, collaboration, and professional development.

**What you will bring**

- A minimum of **3 years’ relevant experience** in grants and/or partnerships management within a humanitarian or development context.
- Proven experience in donor engagement, fundraising, proposal development, reporting, and compliance with humanitarian donor requirements.
- Demonstrated experience managing implementing partners and consortia, including partner assessments and capacity development.
- Strong knowledge of the humanitarian and development sector in Jordan, including NGO and UN operations.
- Fluency in **written and spoken Arabic**, alongside excellent communication, coordination, planning, and leadership skills.
- A collaborative, trustworthy, and results-oriented professional with strong interpersonal skills, integrity, and the ability to build effective relationships and adapt to change.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQB8V4R-ZMG5QLsMcubOID_AAZceYE8kIGfbslZH3h8UiP4?e=Oo48Yc) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Amman
