jobs.title: Head of Mission Mali (f/m/d)
jobs.body:
arche nova - initiative for people in need (AN) is an independent, non-religious, non-profit and non-governmental organisation (NGO) from Germany working in the fields of humanitarian aid, rehabilitation and development. The primary focus of our activities lies in Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH).

Since 2013, AN has been working in Mali, implementing humanitarian and transitional aid projects in the sectors of WaSH, Food Security & Livelihoods (FSL) and DRR. The activities in Mali are managed through the AN Bamako office in close collaboration with the arche nova’s headquarters in Germany.

We are currently looking for a

**Head of Mission Mali (f/m/d)**

**Position to be filled:** 15thof December 2026

**Duty station:** Bamako, Mali with travels to the project locations in Gao (Mali) and Niamey (Niger)

**Duration:** initial 12 months contract (extension desired) with 6 months’ probation period

**Note: This position is only filled locally with a local contract (Mali). Applicants must hold a valid work permit.**

**Overall Purpose of the Position**

The responsibilities of the **Head of Mission (HoM) Mali** include the overall operational, human resources and financial management of the mission Mali, ensuring programme quality, compliance, staff wellbeing, and the implementation of the country strategy. The responsibility also includes fundraising as well as communication and representation of arche nova e.V. towards relevant authorities and stakeholders.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. General**

- Coordinate the general management of the AN Mali office and, in close coordination with headquarters (HQ), the further adjustment of the organisational structure.
- Ensure the strict application of arche nova's policies and procedures.
- Ensure all relevant and required reporting for authorities in Mali.
- Ensure that all operations are in line with laws of Mali.
- Implementation of AN Mali mission strategy in collaboration with the HQ in Germany and Senior Management Team.
- Ensure AN is represented in technical working groups in relevant sector clusters, ensure meaningful participation in advisory boards, steering committees, NGO consortia and other relevant meetings for Mali.
- Maintain strong relationships with authorities, donors, UN agencies, INGOs, and local partners.
- Ensure quality and timely communication and reporting with all relevant stakeholders.
- Close collaboration with and regular reporting to the different relevant departments at HQ level.
- Identify new funding opportunities and develop donor engagement plans.
- Ensure the promotion and visibility of AN through presentations, reports, and external communication.
- Fostering a positive and accountable work environment, as well as empowering and encouraging staff to take initiative
- Ensure safeguarding of AN’s assets and interests and protect from loss arising from fraud, waste, weak administration and poor value for money.
- Guarantee the correct, efficient, and effective use of logistical, financial and human resources.

**2. Programme & Grants Management**

- Oversee the management and quality assurance of all programmes and grants, ensuring compliance with AN policies and donor regulations in close cooperation with the Head of Programmes.
- Ensure that programme design reflects innovation, community participation, sustainability, and humanitarian principles.
- Supervise project implementation and provide regular support to programme staff and partners.
- Ensure MEAL systems, accountability mechanisms, learning processes, and safeguarding standards are implemented in close collaboration with the MEAL Officer.
- Lead and coordinate proposal development, ensuring strong technical input and alignment with donor priorities.
- Lead and strengthen existing consortia relations in close cooperation with the Desk Manager and the Head of Programmes.
- Approve and oversee external research, evaluations, audits, and rapid assessments of emerging crises.

**3. Human Resources, Administration & Capacity Building**

- Overseeing the HR management: development of programme staff structures, recruitment, performance monitoring, capacity building (including being the lead for any disciplinary procedures of AN staff, e.g. issuing warnings, terminations, suspensions, etc.)
- Promote staff wellbeing and duty of care, ensuring safe and enabling working conditions.
- Identify and support capacity-building needs for staff and partners.
- Ensure compliance with national labour laws, AN HR policies, safeguarding, Code of Conduct, and anti-fraud measures.
- Ensure harmonised and compliant administrative, procurement, and financial procedures.
- Ensure that internal review and exchange meetings are regularly conducted and documented

**4. Finance Management & Compliance**

- Oversee financial planning, budget management, expenditure monitoring, and forecasting.
- Ensure compliance with AN’s authority matrix, procurement rules, and donor financial regulations.
- Signatory of all contracts (i.e. employment, consultancies, contractors, PAs, etc.).
- Ensure compliance with AN, donor and governmental rules and regulations
- Support internal and external audits and ensure follow-up on audit recommendations.
- Monitor financial risks and advise HQ on sustainability and growth.

**5. Security Management**

- In collaboration with the HQ Global Security Advisor and the Security Focal Point, monitor the programme implementation environment, including security, political, development and personnel issues that may affect implementation of the projects, and provide updates to the Desk Manager (DM) and Team Lead Africa in a timely manner
- Ensure all security protocols, SOPs, contingency plans, and risk mitigation measures are up to date.
- Provide regular security briefings to HQ and ensure staff receive security training.
- Ensure appropriate response to political, operational, or natural crisis developments affecting programming.

**6. Operations, Logistics**

- Oversee logistics, procurement, fleet, warehousing, and asset management.
- Ensure transparent and efficient procurement in line with AN and donor standards.
- Oversee office registrations, legal compliance, and adherence to national regulations.
- Manage risk, prevent fraud, and safeguard AN’s assets and reputation.

**7. Partnership Management & Localisation**

- Strengthen partnerships with national NGOs, community-based organisations, and technical institutions.
- Lead due diligence processes, capacity-strengthening plans, and partnership compliance.
- Promote equitable partnerships and localisation principles.
- Where appropriate and feasible visit to project sites for monitoring purposes.

**8. Safeguarding (PSEA & Child Protection)**

- Ensure that safeguarding and PSEA policies are implemented across all offices and programmes.
- Deliver and monitor mandatory staff training on PSEA and child protection.
- Ensure there are confidential, safe, and efficient reporting mechanisms for safeguarding concerns.
- Promote a culture of protection, equality, and accountability among the staff and affected populations.

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

- Master’s degree (or BA with substantial experience): in development and cooperation, humanitarian and international affairs, management of non-profits or other relevant fields.
- Minimum **5 years’ experience** in senior management roles in humanitarian or development settings.
- Strong experience in programme management, strategic leadership, HR oversight, and financial management.
- Firm understanding of donor compliance, reporting and proposal development (especially BMZ, German Federal Foreign Office, Europe Aid, ECHO)
- A broad understanding of the roles and responsibilities of international cooperation and humanitarian architecture including key actors, standards, clusters, donors
- Strong understanding of and experience in security management in complex environments.
- Excellent team leader skills, guidance and support to the team
- Fluency in written and spoken French; Excellent communication skills in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Bambara, is a strong asset.
- Sensitivity to cultural differences and the ability to work in a culturally diverse team
- High degree of intercultural competences and conflict-sensitivity, strong sense of integrity and sensitivity towards the needs of vulnerable groups
- Having the ability to work under pressure and changing project environment.
- Experience in West Africa, particularly Mali.
- Commitment to gender equality, safeguarding, and localisation.

Note: This position is only filled locally with a local contract (Mali). Applicants must hold a valid work permit.

We would like to encourage people with similar CVs, and especially women to apply.

**We offer:**

- Competitive salary
- 30 days of annual leave + public holidays
- Professional development and training
- An inclusive, respectful, and diversity-positive organisational culture

**Attention:** this is not a family duty station

However, arche nova is a family-friendly employer and allows for flexibility regarding children or care work.

AN is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment without attention to race, age, ability, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, or any other factor. At AN we celebrate diversity and appreciate our employees for the people they are and their unique skills, backgrounds, and perspectives. We encourage all interested candidates to apply!

**Deadline for application:** 15.11.2026

jobs.title: Head of Programme
jobs.body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Head of Programme.

Danish Refugee Council is a leading protection agency pursuing our mandate to protect and promote durable solutions to displacement-affected populations based on humanitarian principles. In East Africa and the Great Lakes, DRC has operational presence in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

In the DR Congo, DRC has been involved in humanitarian aid since 2009. Initially working in Province Orientale, DRC gradually extended its reach to North Kivu and Ituri provinces. The sectors of intervention for DRC in the country are provision of Emergency Response, Protection (including GBV and child protection), Economic Recovery, Shelter and WASH. DRC is currently responding to the Ebola outbreak as this is unfolding in Ituri province where DRC has a longstanding presence.

**About the job**

Provide strategic direction, leadership and oversight of DRC’s country programme, ensuring coherent strategy, high programme quality, effective departmental management and sustainable funding. Lead country-level programme development and support accountable implementation through Area Managers and Project Managers. As a member of the Senior Management Team, the HoP oversees a multi-sector portfolio spanning emergency response, early recovery and resilience in eastern DR Congo, including consortia led by DRC, and works closely with the Head of Support Services and the Head of Safety to balance programme excellence, cost efficiency and safety.

**Main Responsibilities**

*Programme Strategy & Development*

- Lead and periodically review the Country Programme Plan, Theory of Change and sector/geographic priorities; translate strategy into clear departmental workplans.
- Coordinate an integrated, multi-sector approach across Protection, Economic Recovery, WASH, Education and other sectors; ensure the centrality of protection, safe programming, access and adherence to humanitarian principles; uphold technical standards and safeguarding.
- Promote cash and market-based programming (including multi-purpose and emergency cash) and link emergency response with early recovery and durable solutions.
- Drive innovative programme design with the SMT, in line with DRC global and regional strategies.

*Programme Coordination*

- Lead the Programme Department; clarify reporting lines, roles, delegation, staffing and cost structure with the Head of Support Services.
- In collaboration with the Area Manager, maintain consolidated priorities, deliverables and follow-up
- Provide strategic oversight to PDQM; ensure Grants and MEAL have clear strategies, workplans, quality controls, donor reporting and learning systems.
- Oversee portfolio quality and delivery; work with Area Managers on operational feasibility, project start-up/closure and timely escalation of implementation risks.
- Lead the Country Office Business Development Plan, donor mapping, opportunity pipeline, strategic partnerships and funding proposals, including ECHO HIP processes.
- Coordinate programme approaches across Protection, Economic Recovery, WASH, Education and other sectors; uphold technical standards and safeguarding.
- Maintain programme risks and mitigation actions in the Country Office Risk Register; analyze options and take timely decisions within delegatedauthority.
- Provide concise, decision-oriented updates to SMT and coordinate priorities with Area Offices, Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Safety, Regional Hub and HQ.
- Ensure effective and transparent planning and use of financial resources (budget follow-up, burn rates) in compliance with DRC and donor rules; keep programme staff updated on donor regulations.

*Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning (MEAL)*

- Provide strategic oversight to PDQM; ensure Grants and MEAL have clear strategies, workplans, quality controls, donor reporting and learning systems.
- Ensure monitoring systems produce quality evidence that is used for programme adjustment and accountability to affect populations; document and share lessons learned and good practices internally and externally.

*Fundraising, Proposal Development & Reporting*

- Lead the Country Office Business Development Plan, donor mapping, opportunity pipeline, strategic partnerships and funding proposals, including ECHO HIP processes.
- Oversee timely, quality concept notes, proposals, budgets and donor reports with Grants, Finance and field teams, in line with DRC and donor requirements.

*Donor Liaison, Partnerships & Representation*

- Represent DRC with donors, consortia, coordination bodies, authorities and local partners; advance localization and coherent programme positioning; ensure effective governance of DRC-led consortia.
- Deputize for the Country Director when delegated.

*Advocacy & Communication*

- With the CD and the Advocacy & Communications function, develop evidence-based advocacy messages grounded in programme data, promoting the protection and rights of displaced and conflict-affected populations.
- Support the development and review of external communication materials (case studies, success stories, donor visibility).

*People management*

- Providing leadership and direction to a team, ensuring clarity of roles, expectations, and performance standards to achieve agreed goals and objectives.
- Exercising team budget oversight and decision-making authority where assigned.
- Leading or contributing to recruitment processes for staff within their team
- Conducting and/or signing off on performance appraisals and ensuring regular, constructive feedback to support continuous improvement.
- Supporting the professional development of team members through coaching, capacity building, and development planning.
- Addressing poor performance and disciplinary issues, including handling Code of Conduct cases referred to management, in line with DRC policies and procedures.

*Technical supervision – Field Offices*

- Providing technical direction, guidance, and where mandated, instructions to ensure compliance with DRC policies, standards, and strategies.
- Supporting managers and technical staff through regular communication, capacity building, and promotion of best practices.
- Support managers with assessing the technical skills and performance of most senior technical staff in the Country/Field offices.
- Escalating and, where authorized, addressing issues of non-compliance or poor performance in line with the technical supervision mandate.
- Participating in the recruitment of most senior technical staff in Country/Field offices.

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to At least 7 years in humanitarian/development programming, including at least 4 years managing staff and senior country-level programme responsibilities. Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- Proven strategic planning, Theory of Change, multi-sector programme management, institutional fundraising, proposal and budget development experience.
- Master’s degree in international development, Humanitarian Affairs, Political Science, Economics, Social Sciences or related discipline.
- Strong management, delegation, prioritisation, decision-making, PCM, grants/MEAL oversight, donor compliance, partnership and communication skills; experience in complex contexts.
- Sound knowledge of displacement issues and related international standards; knowledge of the DR Congo / Great Lakes context is a strong asset.
- Proven experience of external representation with donors, authorities and clusters, and of managing programmes within consortia.
- Experience of leading change processes (scale-up/scale-down) and of working in insecure, rapidly changing environments.
- English – full professional proficiency.
- French – professional proficiency highly desirablefull professional proficiency required

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: *1 Year*

Band: *Management E*

Work location: *Bunia*

Designation of Duty Station: *Non-Accompanied*

Start date: *2nd January 2027*

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of , please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-us/work-with-us/working-at-drc/salary-package-and-benefits/) for more details.

jobs.title: Business and Financial Analysis Lead
jobs.body:
The **Business and Financial Analysis Lead** will provide technical leadership in assessing the viability, effectiveness, sustainability, and scalability of inclusive agricultural business models and financial interventions. The role will lead the analysis of agribusiness performance, smallholder sourcing systems, financial service delivery, investment leverage, and market development outcomes. The specialist will generate robust evidence on commercial performance, financial sustainability, and developmental impact to inform strategic decision-making, learning, and future investment programming. The position will also contribute to evaluating how market actors, financial institutions, and agricultural enterprises create value for smallholder farmers while strengthening resilient and inclusive market systems.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Lead the assessment of the commercial viability, efficiency, and sustainability of smallholder sourcing and aggregation models.
- Analyze business performance indicators, including procurement costs, margins, productivity, quality improvements, supply reliability, and operational efficiency.
- Assess the financial sustainability and profitability of investments made by agribusinesses and other market actors.
- Conduct financial and portfolio analysis of lending mechanisms, risk-sharing facilities, and agricultural finance products supporting farmers, cooperatives, and enterprises.
- Evaluate the accessibility, utilization, and additionality of financial services and their influence on business growth and farmer participation.
- Analyze market system changes, including domestic sourcing, import substitution, market linkages, private sector engagement, value addition, and financial inclusion.
- Lead quantitative and qualitative analyses of business and financial performance data collected throughout the evaluation.
- Contribute to the design of methodologies, analytical frameworks, data collection tools, and performance indicators related to business and financial outcomes.
- Develop analytical reports, technical briefs, presentations, and evidence products that communicate findings to diverse stakeholders.

**Required Qualifications**

- Master's degree in Finance, Economics, Agricultural Economics, Agribusiness, Business Administration, Development Economics, or a related field.
- Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in financial analysis, investment assessment, agribusiness development, market systems, or private sector development.
- Demonstrated experience evaluating business models, value chains, agricultural enterprises, and market-based development interventions.
- Strong expertise in financial modeling, investment analysis, profitability assessment, and business case evaluation.
- Experience assessing agricultural finance programs, blended finance mechanisms, guarantee schemes, credit facilities, or impact investment initiatives.
- Proven experience analyzing financial institutions, lending portfolios, and investment performance.
- Experience working with private sector actors, financial institutions, investors, donor-funded programs, and development partners.
- Fluency in written and spoken English; additional local language skills are an asset.

jobs.title: Finance Manager Mali
jobs.body:
**Contexte**

Depuis 2012, le Mali fait face à une crise humanitaire complexe marquée par une dégradation progressive de l’environnement sécuritaire dans plusieurs régions du pays. Au cours des dernières années, les incidents sécuritaires et les tensions communautaires se sont étendus à de nouvelles zones, y compris dans certaines régions du sud, accentuant les vulnérabilités des populations et compliquant davantage l'accès aux services essentiels. Cette situation continue d'avoir des répercussions significatives sur les conditions de vie des communautés et sur les besoins humanitaires à travers le pays.

Le Conseil norvégien pour les réfugiés travaille au Mali depuis 2013. L'organisation dispose d'un bureau de coordination à Bamako, et de bureaux de terrain situés à Mopti , Ségou, Tombouctou, Gao et Ménaka.

Pour répondre aux besoins des populations affctées par les conflits, les déplacements et les aléas climatiques, le NRC met en œuvre des programmes danes les domaines suivants : éducation, abris/WASH, mécanismes de réponse rapide (MRR), Information, Conseil et Assistance juridique (ICLA), moyens de subsistance et sécurité alimentaire, médiation humanitaire et protection contre la violence.

**Ce que nous cherchons:**

NRC est à la recherche d'un Finance Manager expérimenté et dévoué. Le titulaire du poste contribuera activement à la gestion des financements multiples et diverses pour la mission NRC au Mali. Il/elle sera responsable de la mise en place des systèmes et outils de finance de NRC, ainsi que de la formation rigoureuse et compréhensive du personnel des finances et du programme.

Le/la candidat(e) idéal(e) sera un(e) travailleur(euse) humanitaire passionné(e) et engagé(e) avec 3 ans d'expérience minimum dans un poste de gestionnaire des finances ou directeur financier, dans un contexte humanitaire ou de relèvement (post-crise). NRC est particulièrement à la recherche d’un(e) responsable des finances ayant la force et la vision nécessaires pour soutenir des équipes nouvelles, composées d’un personnel hautement professionnel dans tous les départements /unités du bureau pays. Un penseur stratégique, un connecteur, avec de solides compétences en gestion financière et une personne ayant une solide compréhension du contexte. Les candidats ayant une compréhension approfondie et une expérience de travail avec les systèmes et procédures financiers sont particulièrement encouragés à postuler. Une expérience de l'audit, de la gestion des risques et de la budgétisation est essentielle

**Ce que vous ferez:**

1. Superviser la mise en œuvre de toutes les politiques, procédures, stratégies et initiatives liées aux finances en coordination avec l'équipe des finances des bureaux de pays et de zone pour assurer le succès, la cohérence et la conformité.
2. Responsabilité de la direction hiérarchique pour le personnel hiérarchique direct et responsabilité de la supervision technique pour le personnel des finances dans les bureaux de zone, sur la base de la supervision technique de NRC. Lignes directrices. Cela comprend :
    - Processus de gestion de la performance : fixer des objectifs clairs alignés sur les priorités stratégiques, suivre et soutenir la réalisation du personnel.
    - Planification de la main-d'œuvre, recrutement, intégration et perfectionnement du personnel, et soutien au devoir de diligence.
3. Élaborer et tenir à jour les documents, procédures, directives et outils financiers des pays, y compris la stratégie, en veillant à la cohérence dans l'ensemble du programme national et conformément aux normes organisationnelles.
4. Maintenir le contrôle budgétaire global du pays et surveiller les flux de trésorerie.
5. S'assurer que la budgétisation, la comptabilité, les procédures de fin d'année et les autres processus financiers se déroulent conformément au Manuel financier, aux politiques du NRC et aux exigences des donateurs et des auditeurs.
6. Former et développer les capacités du personnel et des partenaires du NRC en matière de responsabilités financières et budgétaires.
7. Assurer une mise en œuvre correcte de la politique de lutte contre la corruption dans toutes les opérations et activités financières.

**Compétences professionnelles:**

- Minimum de 10 années d’expérience, dont trois années dans un poste de direction financière avec des responsabilités de gestion dans un contexte humanitaire.
- Master dans un domaine pertinent.

***Compétences, connaissances et expérience liées au contexte***

- Une expérience antérieure dans la région et/ou la zone d'opérations est préférable.
- Maîtrise professionnelle du français ET de l'anglais, tant à l'écrit qu'à l'oral.
- Expériences de rapportage et d’audit avec les bailleurs de fonds humanitaires.
- Expérience de la gestion des risques avec les partenaires de mise en œuvre.

**Compétences comportementales**

- Gestion d'un environnement non sécurisé
- Planification et obtention de résultats
- Analyse des risques
- Communiquer avec impact et respect
- Faire face au changement

***Compétences du profil de leadership***

- Établir des relations significatives
- Responsabiliser l’équipe
- Obtenir des résultats
- Agir avec intégrité

Veuillez trouver la [JD \_Finance Manager Mali.pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCn3foZkHf4QZGXoCcL6ESKAWsaCjX-ExOyF33ad5qYin8?e=uRaReB)

**Ce que nous offrons:**

- Contrat: CDD 12Mois Renouvelable
- NRC echelle nationale/international : Grade 9
- Lieu: Mali, Bamako
- Une opportunité d’associer votre carrière à une cause impérieuse
- Une chance de rencontrer et de travailler avec des personnes qui sont les meilleures dans leur domaine

[Apprenez sur les avantages de travailler avec NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

**Informations importantes sur le processus de candidature:**

- Pour postuler en tant que candidat interne, connectez-vous avec votre adresse électronique officielle ou cliquez sur Opportunity MarketPlace.
- Lors de la création de votre profil, indiquez votre nom complet tel qu'indiqué sur votre passeport.
- Remplissez tous les champs requis par le système concernant l’expérience, les antécédents professionnels et l’éducation.
- Déposez votre candidature et votre CV en français ou en anglais, en prenant soin de joindre votre dernier CV.
- Les candidatures ne répondant pas aux normes minimales en termes d’expérience ou de qualifications ne seront généralement pas prises en considération. Les candidatures spontanées non liées à cette offre d'emploi spécifique ne seront pas prises en compte.
- Seuls les candidats sélectionnés seront contactés. Nous recevons de nombreuses candidatures pour chaque poste vacant.
- Si vous avez des questions sur ce rôle, veuillez envoyer un e-mail à cwa.recruitment@nrc.no avec le titre du poste comme objet.

jobs.title: Stagiaire - Support Juridique F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission du/ de la stagiaire Support juridique est d'apporter un soutien aux opérations humanitaires à travers les différentes juridictions où sont mises en œuvre les activités de MSF, spécifiquement associées aux pôles thématiques DIH et Médico-Légal.

Le Département Juridique Intersectionnel de MSF est composé de conseillers et managers juridiques sous une Direction unique qui avise les différents centres opérationnels de MSF de manière harmonisée et mutualisée. Il est constitué de pôles thématiques (1. DIH, 2. Médico-Légal, 3. RH & Duty of care 4. Cadre légal et administratif 5. Gouvernance 6. Innovation, recherche médicale et protection des données).

Le service juridique recherche un·e : Stagiaire Juriste - Droit international humanitaire, Droit pénal national et/ou international, Médico-légal

Le Département Juridique de MSF apporte conseil et support juridique aux équipes de Médecins Sans Frontières aussi bien sur le terrain qu’aux sièges.

Au sein du département juridique vous serez rattaché.e aux pôles thématiques 1 et 2.

**Activités principales**

**En support des opérations humanitaires, et à travers les différentes juridictions où sont mises en œuvre les activités de MSF :**

- Recherches juridiques variées en droit international humanitaire ainsi que sous différentes législations nationales (médico-légales, santé sexuelle et reproductive, droit des patients et l'éthique médical, droit pénal, état d’urgence…) ;
- Rédaction de notes, d’outils et de guidelines ;
- Facilitation de l’organisation de réunions et de leur suivi (CR, suivi des points d’action…) au sein des Unités 1 et 2, ainsi qu’en interaction avec les autres unités du département ;
- Archivage des dossiers médico-légaux confidentiels.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation/Expérience :**

- Stage PPI EFB / Titulaire d’un Master 2 / Ecole de droit de Science Po / Autre profil équivalent.
- Droit international humanitaire, droit pénal national et/ou international, ou droit de la santé.
- Expérience en ONG, contentieux pénal, cabinet d’avocat ou un service juridique couvrant les thématiques des Unités 1 ou 2, serait un atout.

**Compétences et aptitudes :**

- Rigueur rédactionnelle,
- Capacité de problématisation et de synthèse,
- Intérêt pour les activités humanitaires et associatives de MSF,
- Ouverture d’esprit,
- Capacité d’adaptation et travail en équipe.

**Langues :**

- Très bon niveau d’anglais et de français, notamment à l’écrit (50% du travail en anglais).

**Statut et conditions :** Stage de 6 mois, avec **convention de stage obligatoire.**

Basé à Paris 19ème. Le montant de la gratification est compris entre 4,35€ et 7,70€ brut par heure en fonction du niveau d’études.1 ticket restaurant est attribué par jour travaillé, d’une valeur faciale de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF). 2 jours de repos indemnisés par mois. Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

**Poste à pourvoir** : 4 janvier 2027

jobs.title: Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
PATHWAYS INTERNATIONAL · UK NAMED COMMUNITY SPONSORSHIP PROGRAMME

**Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom**

*London area based (hybrid) · Full-time*

**About us – what do we do?**

At a time of unprecedented forced displacement and system disruption, we are reforming the global system of safe and legal routes to protection. Our world-class team works closely with leaders and innovators from across sectors in over 20 countries. Together we design, launch, and expand safe and legal routes for displaced people. Together we pilot bold new ideas aimed at making the entire global system of safe and legal routes stronger and more sustainable.

**How we do it**

- We build and lead powerful partnerships and networks.
- We provide trusted advice.
- We accelerate operational delivery.
- We generate and share insights.
- We inspire change.

**About the role – what will you do?**

We are seeking a Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom to join Pathways International’s powerful global team at a formative moment for the UK’s new named community sponsorship programme.

This is a broad, versatile role spanning programme and partnership delivery and policy. You will plan and deliver the projects and partnerships that build the named community sponsorship ecosystem, while also helping shape policy development and implementation and keeping the programme informed by wider migration developments. The balance between policy and delivery will flex with the needs of the programme and the shape of the UK team.

Reporting to Hannah Gregory, Global Director Knowledge and Sponsorship, and working closely with Pathways International’s UK and global teams, you will help shape and sustain the development of named community sponsorship in the UK.

**Responsibilities**

- Contributing to the development of the UK named community sponsorship policy framework, supporting the design and development of the framework post-launch, including sponsored labour and education routes, in coordination with colleagues and partners.
- Planning, delivering and coordinating projects across the UK named community sponsorship portfolio, including organising events and meetings, developing resources, materials and tools and supporting monitoring, reporting and learning.
- Building and maintaining relationships across government, civil society, local partners and funders, and communities across the UK, and connecting delivery partners to training, mentoring and resources, including via Pathways International’s global networks and UK partners.
- Supporting the multi-stakeholder working group, engaging government and other policy stakeholders (including preparing for and following up on meetings and events), and representing the programme externally.
- Building and maintaining an understanding of the national, devolved, regional and local landscape relevant to sponsorship, and drawing out its implications for the programme.
- Maintaining an overview of wider migration developments in the UK and globally, and advising on their relevance for named community sponsorship.
- Researching, analysing and drafting high-quality briefings, policy documents and other written materials for senior stakeholders.

**About you – who are we looking for?**

We are looking for a versatile person who can move comfortably between programme and partnership delivery and policy thinking, and who thrives on a varied portfolio in a fast-paced environment. You combine professionalism and maturity with the warmth and versatility to build rapport quickly across very different audiences.

- A proven understanding of one or more relevant fields, which may include forced displacement, refugee protection, community sponsorship, global migration or migration policy.
- At least eight (8) years of relevant work experience, spanning programme or project delivery and policy, research or analysis, including experience of working in or closely with government.
- Experience working with and convening NGOs, civil society and/or other delivery partners.
- A confident representative with an easy, approachable manner, who builds lasting relationships with a wide range of UK stakeholders — government, civil society and others — and brings the judgement to handle senior meetings and the readiness to get stuck into the practical details of running an event.
- Strong policy capability, able to research, analyse and draft high-quality briefings and materials for senior stakeholders with keen attention to detail.
- Excellent project-management and organisational skills, able to coordinate meetings, events and projects and to prioritise effectively across competing demands.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
- Able to work on a varied and constantly evolving portfolio, while consistently displaying professionalism, discretion, tact and responsibility.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and experience collaborating with people from different backgrounds, countries, cultures and languages.
- A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field (e.g. public policy, public affairs, political science, international development). Education and work experience equivalencies will be considered.
- Comfortable preparing well-presented PowerPoint and Word documents and using AI tools, Excel, Zoom, MS Teams and SharePoint.
- We particularly encourage applications from qualified candidates with lived experience of forced displacement or migration, or with close personal and cultural connections to refugee communities.

**Location**

This is a London area based hybrid-working role with the ability to travel within the UK on a regular basis as needed and access available to shared office space. Applicants contacted for evaluation will be asked to provide proof that they have the legal right to work in the UK. Maintaining such legal right to work is a condition of employment.

**Salary**

Competitive, commensurate with experience.

**Contract**

Full-time. \[One-year term (renewable), or permanent — confirm.\]

**How to apply**

Please submit a cover letter, a CV, and a short, unedited writing sample of no more than five pages (in English) through Pathways International’s BambooHR portal at [https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/61](https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/61) by Friday, November 20th at 11:59 pm EST to be considered for this position.

**Equal opportunity employer**

Pathways International is an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage applications from qualified candidates of all genders and from all national, religious, and ethnic backgrounds, including persons with disabilities and those with lived experience of forced displacement. We will provide accommodation upon request during the recruitment, selection, and assessment process.

jobs.title: Operational Research Advisor (f/m/x) specialized in Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Preventable Diseases (ID/VPD)
jobs.body:
**Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international humanitarian aid organization that provides assistance in more than 70 countries to populations in distress, to victims of natural or manmade disasters and to victims of armed conflicts, without discrimination and irrespective of origin, religion, creed or political affiliation. Our actions are guided by medical ethics and the principle of impartiality, independence and neutrality.**

**To contribute to this work, MSF-Luxembourg is recruiting an**

## **Operational Research Advisor (f/m/x)** specialized in **Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Preventable Diseases (ID/VPD)**

### **Context**

The Luxembourg Operational Research Unit (LuxOR) is part of the MSF-OCB Medical Department and supports evidence-based improvements to MSF operations through Operational Research. LuxOR is also coordinating Field Epidemiology activities, providing technical support to strengthen data quality, analysis, and operational decision-making across MSF projects.

We are looking for an **Operational Research Advisor** specializing in **Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Preventable Diseases (ID/VPD)** to support research activities ranging from outbreak documentation and epidemiological studies to clinical research and vaccine-related implementation studies.

**The successful candidate will combine strong scientific expertise with a pragmatic understanding of humanitarian operations and will work closely with medical, epidemiological, social science, and operational teams across MSF.**

### **Main responsibilities**

#### **Lead and support operational research activities**

- Guide research projects throughout the full research cycle, from question formulation to dissemination of results.
- Support the development of concept notes, study protocols, and ethical review submissions.
- Ensure methodological rigor, scientific quality, and adherence to ethical standards.
- Provide technical support to research teams and principal investigators.
- Contribute to manuscript writing, scientific publications, reports, policy briefs, and conference presentations.

#### **Research design, data analysis, and scientific support**

- Advise on study design, research methodologies, and data collection strategies.
- Support data management, statistical analysis, interpretation of findings, and evidence synthesis.
- Contribute expertise in infectious diseases, outbreak investigations, vaccination, and clinical research.
- Strengthen the use of research findings to inform operational decision-making and policy development.

#### **Capacity strengthening and collaboration**

- Mentor and support researchers and field teams.
- Contribute to training initiatives in operational research, epidemiology, and data analysis.
- Participate in field visits and provide direct support to projects.
- Promote collaboration across MSF departments and with external academic and public health partners.

#### **Support in advancing clinical research in the areas of ID/VPD in MSF in coordination with public health intelligence:**

- Contribute to advancing evidence synthesis and knowledge gaps in ID/VPD as one of the core activities of MSF activities.
- Information sharing, coordinate with social science teams, especially in areas like surveillance, outbreak response, and data analysis.
- Represent MSF in scientific networks, technical platforms, and international conferences.
- Support the translation of research evidence into operational practice and policy.

### **Profile**

- **Adhere to the MSF principles and to our managerial values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust and Empowerment**
- **Adhere to the MSF Behavioural Commitments**

#### **Education**

- Postgraduate degree (Master's level minimum) in Medicine, Epidemiology, Public Health, Research Methods, Microbiology, or another relevant health-related discipline.
- PhD considered a strong asset.
- Certification in Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
- Additional training in epidemiology, biostatistics, or research methodologies is an advantage.

#### **Experience**

- Significant experience conducting operational, clinical, or biomedical research.
- Proven experience within MSF or another international humanitarian organization.
- Experience designing and implementing studies or clinical trials in low-resource and/or humanitarian settings.
- Experience in scientific writing and dissemination of research findings.

#### **Skills**

- Strong expertise in study design, epidemiology, biostatistics, and data interpretation.
- Excellent scientific writing and communication skills.
- Ability to work autonomously while collaborating effectively across multidisciplinary teams.
- Strong commitment to research ethics, scientific integrity, and humanitarian principles.
- Proficiency with statistical software such as R and/or Stata,
- Knowledge of data management and data collection platforms (e.g., REDCap, Kobo).
- Knowledge of GIS and Health Information softwares are an asset (e.g., ArcGIS, QGIS, HIS, DHIS2, etc)
- Excellent command of English (C1 level or higher).
- French is an asset.

### **What we offer**

- A unique opportunity to contribute to humanitarian medical research with global impact.
- Collaboration with multidisciplinary experts across the MSF movement.
- Exposure to innovative research in infectious diseases, vaccination, and outbreak response.
- Opportunities for field engagement, capacity building, and professional development.

### **Conditions**

- 1-year Full-time contract with possibility of extension
- Based in Luxembourg with frequent travels abroad
- Gross salary over 12 months from 63000 to 76200 € according to MSF experience
- 29 days annual paid leaves
- Possibility of teleworking 2 days per week
- Medical complementary insurance (including hospitalization)
- 18 Lunch vouchers each with a face value of 10,80 € (2/3 covered by MSF).
- Public transport allowance & relocation package (if applicable)
- **Expected starting date: Mid-January 2027**

jobs.title: Associate Philanthropy Advisor – Private Major Donors
jobs.body:
**Join MSF OCG as a Associate Philanthropy Advisor – Private Major Donors!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

MSF Switzerland was created in 1981 and it is headquartered in Geneva. The Philanthropy Unit is one of the eight units at the Communications and Fundraising Department. To ensure a good geographical coverage of the Swiss fundraising market, the Unit is divided into two offices: Geneva and Zurich. The Unit’s mission is to strengthen MSF’s relationship with its private major supporters, including wealthy individuals, foundations, companies, and other philanthropic organisations. It also manages grants and donations from Swiss cantons and communes. Last but not least, it is also in charge of legacy fundraising, including management of heritages as well as contacts with potential legators and confirmed bequestors.

The Associate Philanthropy Advisor for private major donors in German speaking Switzerland is a key member of the Philanthropy Unit, ensuring an efficient and effective cultivation approach for private major donors in German speaking Switzerland and Liechtenstein. The mission is to secure and grow income for MSF from private major donors in German speaking Switzerland.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

*Strategy and action plan*

- Actively contribute to the implementation of the yearly plan

*Cultivation and stewardship*

- Manages a portfolio of Major Donors and potential Top Major Donors and, alongside the Team Coordinator, design and develop the donor journey for donors giving between CHF 10’000 and CHF 20’000 annually.
- Regularly reports to and consults with the Team Coordinator on the strategy for the pool regarding upgrading donors within this segment.
- Determine the best approach and journey for each individual donor depending on their wishes and level of engagement.
- Prepare and facilitate one-to-one meetings, calls, presentations and other meaningful interactions with major donors.
- Interact and collaborate with key spokespersons within MSF (President, General Director, Director of Operations, other management team members), as well as field staff, with the aim of bringing donors closer to the organisation to demonstrate our life-saving mission and work in the projects.
- Define, propose and organise visits to MSF offices and projects, in line with MSF criteria and guidance.
- Ensure that the nature / identity of donors is in line with MSF gifts acceptance policy.
- Ensure that the donor journey runs smoothly, and donors are thanked and stewarded promptly.
- Ensure the database is kept up-to-date.
- Draft engaging communication for the MDs about MSF projects.

*Solicitation/ask*

- In line with the yearly plan and past giving history of main donors, proactively present asks to selected donors for gifts (general and individualized asks) and consult with the Team Coordinator about the solicitation plan
- Ensure that the major donors journey strategy is followed and that major donors are solicited according to their motivations in a personalised way.

*Information and data management*

- Closely work with the System Support Team to ensure most efficient use of Customer Relationship Management Database.
- Support the Team Coordinator in income forecasting and quarterly analysis of results.

*Others*

- Participate in the Community of Practice for Individual Major Donors of MSF in particular with other German-speaking sections.
- Work proactively on projects as needed in the Unit, upon request by her/his supervisor.

## Your profile

*Education*

- University degree in Business Management, Marketing,
- Communications, Political Science, International
- Relations or other relevant areas

*Experience*

- First professional experience in the non-profit sector or in the fields of marketing/sales/communication or client relationship management

*Languages*

- German mother tongue & very good English
- French and Italian an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Proven excellent writing skills (drafting and editing)
- Excellent in oral public presentations
- Strong knowledge of the Windows environment (Word, Excel, Power Point) and tech-savvy
- Strong Analytical skills
- Knowledge of the humanitarian and development sector in Switzerland.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Excellent interpersonal skills
- Service oriented
- Dynamic, proactive and autonomous
- Rigorous and good organizational skills
- Empathic, enthusiastic, optimistic
- Discretion
- Team spirit.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Zurich, Switzerland
- Ideal start date: As soon as possible
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 80’856.- to CHF 97’224.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

jobs.title: Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator - BU Support
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications

## About the Role

Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring smooth and efficient execution of procurement projects by closely aligning with business units (BUs) needs, controlling spend, and improving procurement processes. This role involves managing the full procurement lifecycle for assigned BU procurement projects, supporting supplier and stakeholder relationships, driving process improvements, and maintaining strict contract management and compliance. The coordinator also provides performance tracking and reporting to facilitate strategic decision-making and continuous enhancement of procurement activities.

## Responsibilities

Targeted process and performance improvement

- Support cross-functional improvement initiatives by helping develop templates, SOPs, and training materials.
- Coordinate periodic reviews with assigned Business Units to clear aged Procurement Requests (PRs) and Purchase Orders (POs).
- Perform root cause analysis to identify bottlenecks and improve PR to PO turnaround time.
- Identify capability gaps and propose practical, incremental improvements to strengthen processes and team performance.
- Facilitate effective collaboration between BU and PRO teams to ensure alignment on priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
- Promote proactive communication between BU units and PRO to support timely planning, coordination, and issue resolution.

Strategic sourcing responsibilities

- Define the scope and profile of assigned procurement categories.
- Conduct comprehensive spend analysis, market analysis, and profile demand/supply markets to identify opportunities.
- Develop strategic sourcing strategies, setting clear objectives for cost savings, quality improvement, risk mitigation, and determining appropriate tactics.
- Identify, evaluate, and pre-qualify potential suppliers based on strategic needs.
- Lead RFx processes, including negotiation of pricing, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), payment terms, delivery windows, and change management processes, while integrating selected suppliers into planning systems.
- Finalize and execute contracts, ensuring all terms and conditions are clearly defined and favorable.
- Monitor supplier performance against contract terms, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and hold regular business review meetings to ensure costs are consistently driven down.

Reporting and documentation

- Prepare routine reports and dashboards on procurement project progress, highlighting status updates, risks, and key actions for timely decision-making.
- Support data collection and analysis, including responding to ad-hoc market research requests that inform sourcing decisions and category strategies.
- Capture and document supplier performance data to help drive improvements in service levels, quality, and on-time delivery.
- Analyse cost drivers by Business Unit, identifying short-, medium-, and long-term trends to support planning and spend management.
- Work with other BU coordinators to promote standardization and consolidation of requirements, helping reduce duplication and improve sourcing efficiency across BUs.
- Monitor KPI performance for assigned procurement projects and follow up on corrective actions when targets are not met.
- Maintain clear, organized, and audit-ready documentation for all procurement transactions to support compliance and transparency.
- The Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator will also perform any other duties as assigned by the manager.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Strong communication skills.
- Analytical Skills: Ability to apply logical thinking and problem-solving techniques to break down complex issues and reach sound conclusions.
- Data Analysis Skills: Proven ability to collect, analyze, and interpret large datasets to inform decision-making. Advanced proficiency in data manipulation and visualization tools, including expertise in Excel (Pivot Tables, Lookups, and Array formulas).
- Solid stakeholder management skills
- Strong working knowledge of process improvement tools and methodologies, DMAIC, 5Whys
- Supply chain risk management skills
- Commercial contracting skills
- Strategic sourcing skills
- Supplier relationship management skills
- Commercial negotiation skills
- Minimum 3 years of work experience in a demanding professional environment.
- Bachelor's degree in procurement, project management, business strategy, or related discipline. Candidates with higher diploma and extensive relevant experience may also qualify.
- Professional qualification e.g CIPS, CILT preferred
- Familiarity with procurement models, sourcing frameworks, and PR-PO systems such as Odoo or Power BI
- Language: Fluent in English and Kiswahili preferred.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Kakamega, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

02 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Grants officer (F/M) - Afghanistan
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

In 2025 and 2026, the mission significantly expanded its operations through new funding secured from ECHO, CDCS, and GFFO. The current funding strategy focuses on diversifying the donor portfolio and securing additional funding sources to further expand programmatic coverage. To support this objective, a donor mapping tool has been developed and is regularly updated by the grants officer, in coordination with the deputy general coordinator, to ensure systematic monitoring and follow-up of potential funding opportunities.

## About the role

You will be responsible for coordinating and overseeing grants management, donor compliance, resource mobilization, and partnership and donor engagement for MdM in Afghanistan. In addition, you will be responsible for the mission's communication and will promote visibility on MdM works, particularly when it comes to ensuring implementation of donors’ communication requirements.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator, your main responsibilities are the following:

**Proposal management:**

- Lead and coordinate concept notes and proposals
- Write the non-technical sections (context, needs analysis, cross-cutting)
- Ensure coherence between narrative, logframe and budget as well as alignment with MdM strategy and donor requirements

**Reporting:**

- Track all active grants and deadlines
- Coordinate donor and internal reports (including the monthly situation report)
- Ensure quality and consistency between programmatic and financial information

**Donor engagement:**

- Maintain donor mapping and a database of calls for proposals
- Train teams on donor rules, prepare meetings and briefing materials for the general coordinator
- Support audits and evaluations

**Partnerships:**

- Support the development of MoUs and partnership agreements
- Coordinate due diligence
- Manage collaboration with partners, including in a consortium

**Communication:**

- Develop communication products (factsheets, country profiles, success stories)
- Contribute to the visibility strategy, train staff on guidelines
- Collect field content, and manage social media in line with MdM and donor guidelines

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the program officer at HQ, the Institutional Funding Unit, the technical coordinators, the support coordinators, the MEAL team, and the communication teams at HQ and in the field, among others.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree in the following or related field: Development, International Relations, Humanitarian Management
- Have at least two years of experience in a similar role
- Have demonstrated experience in coordinating and preparing strong narrative and financial reports for a variety of donors
- Have a strong understanding of donor compliance, especially for ECHO/INTPA, FCDO, BHA, GFFO
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (MdM) (strong asset)
- Speak English fluently

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in multi-donors’ budgets
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in insecure and fast-changing contexts, with sound judgment, diplomacy and adaptability
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 069 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility.

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Head of Programme
jobs.body:
**What we are looking for**

Are you an accomplished humanitarian leader with the strategic vision, fundraising expertise, and leadership influence to shape refugee and humanitarian portfolio in Jordan?

This is not simply a programme management position. We are looking for a strategic leader who can identify opportunities, influence key stakeholders, strengthen localization, and secure the funding required to expand impact for refugees and vulnerable communities across Jordan.

You will be entrusted with shaping the future direction of NRC's programme portfolio while ensuring excellence in programmatic delivery, accountability, compliance, learning, and organisational growth.

***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Jordan, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***

**What you will do**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking an exceptional **Head of Programme** to join its senior leadership team in Jordan. This is a pivotal Country Management Group (CMG) role, responsible for leading programme strategy, resource mobilization, grants, MEAL, partnerships, and programme quality across a complex and dynamic humanitarian environment.

As a key member of the country leadership team, you will play a central role in delivering NRC Jordan's 2026-2030 Country Strategy while driving sustainable growth through innovative programming, strategic donor engagement, and strong partnerships with national and international stakeholders.

Key responsibilities:

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight to the Programme, Grants, and MEAL functions.
- Lead the implementation of NRC Jordan's strategic objectives and ensure alignment with country priorities and annual action plans.
- Drive the development and execution of NRC Jordan's fundraising and resource mobilization strategy.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, strategic partners, consortium members, government bodies, and humanitarian actors.
- Identify emerging funding opportunities and position NRC competitively for future growth.
- Lead grant portfolio management, ensuring high-quality proposal development, compliance, reporting, and donor stewardship.
- Champion programme quality, evidence-based programming, accountability, and organisational learning.
- Strengthen partnerships with local and national actors and lead NRC's transition towards more locally led programming approaches.
- Foster collaboration between technical and operational teams to ensure effective programme delivery.
- Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of technical specialists and programme support functions.

**What you will bring**

- Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies, Social Sciences, International Relations, or a related field**.**
- Minimum 6 years of experience in a senior management position within a humanitarian or recovery context, with responsibility for programme and/or project management.
- Experience in NRC Core Competency programming (ICLA, Shelter, and Education) is an asset.
- A strong and demonstrated track record in fundraising and donor engagement, including securing significant institutional funding, developing donor relationships, identifying funding opportunities, and shaping winning resource mobilization strategies.
- Deep knowledge of humanitarian programming, programme quality standards, grants management, and MEAL systems. Experience in integrating evidence-based approaches and programme quality standards throughout the project cycle.
- Strong understanding of donor priorities, compliance requirements, and the evolving humanitarian and refugee landscape in Jordan and the region
- Proven experience building and managing partnerships with local and national actors.
- Experience leading multi-sector, consortium-based, and partnership-driven programmes.
- Outstanding stakeholder engagement, influencing, and representation skills with strong strategic, analytical, problem-solving, team-building, interpersonal and conflict-resolution capabilities.
- The ability to lead, inspire, and develop diverse teams in complex and rapidly changing environments.
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal and excellent writing skills.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDLfnFLI5MKTaemBSTg1EC-Adc-h353hZJskxlm_J4cHhM?e=zKz0i0) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Amman, Jordan
- Fixed term contract: 12 months, renewable based on funding, performance and the need for the position
- Travel: 30% to Area and Field Offices (NRC Operational Areas)
- Salary/benefits: Grade 11 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Jordan, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Jordan](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/jordan)
