**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Stagiaire comptabilité siège
jobs.body:
## Rejoignez MSF OCG en tant que Stagiaire comptabilité siège !

**Nous cherchons des personnes passionnées et prêtes à contribuer à notre mission humanitaire.**

**Découvrez ci-dessous les détails du poste et les qualifications que nous recherchons.**

Ce stage s'inscrit dans le cadre d'un programme de formation académique, professionnelle ou d'insertion socioprofessionnelle, et doit répondre aux [conditions](https://www.ge.ch/engager-personne-stage/stages-formation-insertion-reconnus) fixées par le Conseil de surveillance du marché de l'emploi (CSME). La durée du stage, fixée par la convention tripartite, est de 6 à 9 mois à 100 %.

### Inclusivité et Diversité chez MSF

Vos qualifications et votre expérience ne correspondent pas exactement à toutes les exigences ?

À MSF OCG, nous nous engageons à promouvoir une culture inclusive qui soutient et amplifie les voix diverses de nos collaborateurs. Nous nous efforçons de créer des environnements de travail où des équipes de personnes aux parcours, caractéristiques, perspectives, idées et expériences variés collaborent pour faire avancer la mission sociale de MSF et améliorer les résultats pour nos patients et les communautés avec lesquelles nous travaillons.

Nous comprenons que certaines personnes peuvent hésiter à postuler si elles ne répondent pas à toutes les exigences du poste. Les recherches montrent que cela est particulièrement vrai pour les femmes. Si vous pensez que votre profil correspond bien à ce poste, nous vous invitons à postuler, même si vous ne remplissez pas toutes les qualifications listées.

Nous encourageons les candidatures de personnes de tous genres, âges, orientations sexuelles, ethnies, origines, religions, croyances, situations de handicap et toutes autres caractéristiques de diversité.

MSF ne tolère aucune exploitation ou abus sexuels, aucune forme de discrimination ou de harcèlement, y compris le harcèlement sexuel. Tous les candidats sélectionnés feront l’objet de vérifications de références

### Contexte & Mission

Médecins Sans Frontières est une organisation médicale et humanitaire internationale indépendante qui fournit des soins aux personnes dans le besoin, aux personnes touchées par des catastrophes naturelles ou causées par l'homme et aux victimes de conflits armés, sans discrimination et sans tenir compte de la race, de la religion, des croyances ou de l'appartenance politique (Charte de MSF).

Le service de la comptabilité à Genève est composé de deux unités, l’une ayant la charge des activités comptables HQ (fournisseurs, trésorerie, taxes) et l’autre assurant le suivi comptable des missions dans les pays d’intervention de MSF (comptabilité terrain). Le·la stagiaire sera intégré·e à l’équipe comptabilité HQ et collaborera principalement avec le·la comptable fournisseurs. Il·elle pourra ponctuellement appuyer le reste de l’équipe comptable, HQ et/ou terrain.

### Principales responsabilités

L’intervention du·de la stagiaire est orientée sur l’apprentissage autour de projets précis récurrents, et en priorité autour du traitement complet du cycle des factures fournisseurs, dont notamment :

- Réception, vérification (aspects légaux et fiscaux) et comptabilisation (comptabilité générale et analytique) des factures fournisseurs via le logiciel de traitement des factures et l’ERP comptable (MS Dynamics D365).
- Justification des comptes fournisseurs via la réalisation de certains contrôles clés mensuels/trimestriels (fournisseurs débiteurs, analyse de la balance âgée, etc.).
- Participation aux travaux de clôture annuelle et préparation des audits selon les périodes.

Le·la stagiaire pourra par ailleurs, selon les besoins, être impliqué·e dans diverses tâches comptables (analyses ponctuelles, appui au traitement des notes de frais, documentation du contrôle interne).

### Profil recherché

- En cours d’études supérieures ou en fin de cycle d’études supérieures.
- Être éligible à une convention de stage avec un tiers.
- Français courant à l’écrit et à l’oral, bon niveau d’anglais à l’écrit, allemand un plus.
- Connaissance des outils bureautiques usuels.
- Connaissance d’un ERP, un atout.
- Organisé·e et rigoureux·se.
- Proactivité et dynamisme.
- Capacité à gérer plusieurs activités.
- Esprit de synthèse.
- Intérêt ou engagement pour la solidarité internationale.
- Expérience préalable dans un département financier/comptable, un atout.

### Conditions de stage

- Convention de stage tripartite obligatoire
- Stage de 6 à 9 mois (en fonction de la convention de stage)
- Stage à 100% (40h par semaine)
- Basé à Genève
- Date d’entrée en fonction : fin mars 2027
- Rémunération mensuelle brut : CHF 2’000.-

jobs.title: Instructional Design and E-Learning Consultant
jobs.body:
**Background**

Medair is seeking an experienced **Instructional Design and E-Learning Consultant** to develop an engaging, learner-centered online course for humanitarian health and nutrition staff.

Medair's International Department Advisor Team works to strengthen the capacity of field health and nutrition staff and increase knowledge and use of sector-specific evidence-based approaches. Rapid changes in health and nutrition interventions, together with the need for greater standardization and effective onboarding of new and experienced staff, have increased the need for updated, user-friendly online training.

The assignment involves developing **one online course with two main sections: Health and Nutrition**:

- **Health:** Review, update and improve an existing unpublished Articulate 360 course section of approximately eight hours of learner seat time.
- **Nutrition:** Transform an existing PowerPoint-based training of approximately 170 slides into an interactive Articulate 360 course section.

**Purpose of the Consultancy**

The purpose of this consultancy is to produce a **SCORM-compliant, learner-centered e-learning course** aligned with adult-learning principles and humanitarian health and nutrition training needs.

The course is intended to equip new Medair health and nutrition staff with knowledge relevant to the technical implementation of Medair's health and nutrition programmes.

**Scope of Work**

Working in close collaboration with Medair's Health and Nutrition Advisors, the consultant will develop:

**Content analysis and instructional design**

- Review existing Health Articulate 360 and Nutrition PowerPoint materials.
- Assess alignment between course content, learning objectives and assessments.
- Identify redundancies, gaps and opportunities to improve learner engagement.
- Recommend instructional-design improvements to support knowledge retention and practical application.

**Storyboarding and course structure**

- Develop or update the course storyboard/course map.
- Review and refine learning objectives.
- Establish an appropriate module structure and sequencing.
- Define screen flow, interactions, activities and assessment approaches.
- Ensure appropriate pacing for self-directed learning.

**E-learning development**

- Update and improve the existing Articulate 360 Health section.
- Convert the approximately 170-slide Nutrition PowerPoint into an interactive Articulate 360 course section.
- Use Articulate Storyline 360 and/or Rise 360, as appropriate.
- Apply adult-learning principles and instructional-design best practices.
- Incorporate engaging and appropriate interactive learning elements.
- Apply consistent organizational branding and visual-design standards.
- Apply responsive design where appropriate.

**Assessment development**

- Review existing assessment questions.
- Revise and/or develop assessments as required.
- Ensure assessments are aligned with learning objectives.
- Incorporate appropriate knowledge checks and interactive learning activities throughout the course.

**Review, quality assurance and testing**

- Support up to two stakeholder review and revision cycles.
- Incorporate agreed technical and instructional-design feedback.
- Conduct functionality, navigation and usability testing.
- Resolve identified technical issues.
- Verify LMS compatibility and successful SCORM export.
- Conduct appropriate cross-browser testing.

**Accessibility and user experience**

Apply accessibility and usability principles where feasible, including:

- Clear navigation
- Readable typography
- Appropriate color contrast
- Alternative text for graphics
- Keyboard accessibility where applicable.

**Key Deliverables**

The consultant will provide:

1. Course review and instructional-design recommendations.
2. Updated storyboard/course map.
3. Updated Health section in Articulate 360.
4. New Nutrition section developed from the existing PowerPoint materials.
5. Interactive learning elements and assessments.
6. Draft integrated Articulate 360 course for stakeholder review.
7. Revised course following stakeholder feedback.
8. Final editable Articulate 360 source files.
9. SCORM/xAPI package ready for LMS upload.
10. Quality assurance and testing report.
11. All multimedia assets developed or used under the assignment.

**Tools and Technical Standards**

The consultant should be able to work with:

- Articulate Storyline 360 and/or Rise 360
- Microsoft PowerPoint
- Microsoft Word and Excel as required
- Appropriate graphic-design software
- SCORM-compliant outputs
- Learning Management Systems
- Responsive e-learning design where appropriate.

All agreed editable source files and other final deliverables must be provided to Medair upon completion.

**Timeframe and Availability**

The assignment is expected to commence in **November 2026**, with the final completed course due by **21 December 2026**.

The consultant should be available for at least **50% capacity, approximately 20 hours per week**, to support timely collaboration, review and feedback.

The consultant should propose the estimated number of working days required for:

- Reviewing existing materials and providing recommendations
- Updating content and developing/updating the storyboard
- Converting the Nutrition PowerPoint to Articulate 360
- Developing interactive learning elements
- Assessment review and development
- Quality assurance, testing and SCORM validation
- Incorporating stakeholder feedback and finalizing the course for LMS deployment.

**No travel is required. The consultancy is remote.**

**Required Experience and Competencies**

Applicants should demonstrate:

- Strong professional experience in **instructional design and e-learning development**.
- Demonstrated experience developing interactive online learning using **Articulate Storyline 360 and/or Rise 360**.
- Strong knowledge and practical application of **adult-learning and learner-centered instructional-design principles**.
- Experience converting PowerPoint or other existing training materials into interactive digital learning.
- Experience reviewing and improving existing e-learning courses.
- Experience developing interactive learning activities and assessments.
- Ability to transform complex technical information into clear, engaging and accessible digital learning.
- Experience producing **SCORM-compliant** courses suitable for LMS deployment.
- Strong quality-assurance and attention-to-detail skills.
- Ability to collaborate remotely with technical subject-matter experts and incorporate stakeholder feedback.

**Highly desirable**

- Instructional-design experience in **humanitarian action, public/global health, nutrition or international development**.
- Experience developing technical learning for humanitarian or NGO staff.
- Experience designing learning for diverse international audiences.
- Experience applying accessibility and usability principles to online learning.

**Consultant Responsibilities**

The consultant will:

- Fill Medair Supplier Registration Form and provide RIB-Banking details
- Provide their own computer, software and other equipment necessary to undertake the assignment.
- Complete the agreed outputs within the established timeframe.
- Provide proof of registration as a consultant before contracting, where such registration is normal practice in the consultant's country of residence.
- Provide required progress information and documentation for invoicing.

**Medair Responsibilities**

Medair will:

- Provide access to existing training materials required for development of the course.
- Review agreed outputs and provide feedback and technical support at defined stages of the consultancy.

jobs.title: Community Liaison focal person- MMC and Jere
jobs.body:
**JOB PURPOSE**

Under the supervision of the Livelihood Project Manager, the Community Liaison Focal Person is the project's day-to-day presence in each LGA. They are the trusted link between the project team, the facility committees, landowning families, traditional leaders and community members at the livelihood facilities in MMC, Jere and Mafa.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

## Key responsibilities

### 1. Community entry, mobilisation and communication 

- Introduce the project to traditional leaders (District Head, Lawans, Bulamas), religious leaders, landowning families, women and youth groups, and IDP and returnee representatives in the assigned LGA.
- Mobilise participants for consultations, dialogues, trainings, elections and General Assemblies. Make sure women, youth, persons with disabilities, IDPs and returnees are invited and able to attend.
- Explain project decisions, selection criteria, fees and agreements clearly in Hausa, Kanuri or other local languages.
- Share information on the Feedback and Complaints Response Mechanism (FCRM) in every meeting.

### 2. Support to ownership and social cohesion activities 

- Support the Social Cohesion Officer in the ownership and tenure audit by locating documents, identifying landowners and arranging consultations.
- Organise and record landowner consultations, community dialogues, public validation of agreements, recognition events and community open days.
- Support the Peace and Grievance Committees: arrange meetings, take notes and follow up on agreed actions.
- Report any tension, dispute or rumour about the facilities to the Social Cohesion Officer the same day, and log it in the tension log.

### 3. Facility committee support 

- Attend Facility Management Committee meetings and help with agendas, minutes and follow-up actions.
- Support transparent selection of members and supervised elections, and help committees apply their constitutions.
- Check that membership lists, plot allocations, fees and monthly accounts are publicly displayed.
- Remind committees of their reporting duties to the LGA Facility Oversight Committee, and support preparations for quarterly social audits.

### 4. Day-to-day enterprise facilitation 

- Visit each facility in the LGA at least once a week.
- Coach treasurers and records keepers on the cash book, sales records, fee registers and stock records, following the Business Development Officer's tools.
- Check that maintenance logs, equipment logs and asset registers are kept up to date, and report faults to the relevant officer.
- Follow up on production plans, water schedules (irrigation), stocking and harvesting plans (fish farms) and order books (tailoring), and flag problems early.
- Support logistics for trainings, deliveries and commissioning events at the facilities.

### 5. Data collection and reporting 

- Collect routine monitoring data using digital or paper tools from the MEAL Officer: attendance, facility days operational, sales, fees collected, maintenance and complaints.
- Submit a weekly activity report and photos, and contribute to monthly reports.
- Support baseline, endline and perception surveys.

### 6. Accountability and referrals

- Receive feedback and complaints from community members, record them accurately and pass them to the FCRM focal point within 24 hours.
- Refer protection and safeguarding concerns immediately and confidentially, only through the approved channels. Never investigate such cases personally.

### Cross-cutting duties

- Stay neutral and never make promises on behalf of the project, government or landowners.
- Follow PSEA, safeguarding, confidentiality and security procedures, and report any security incident immediately.
- Carry out any other reasonable duties related to the project, as assigned by the supervisor.

**Essential requirements:**

## Qualifications, experience and competencies

### Education

- **Essential:** an OND, NCE or HND in Social Sciences, Community Development, Agriculture, Business, Adult Education or a related field.
- **Desirable:** a B.Sc in one of these fields, or certificates in community mobilisation, facilitation, record keeping or peacebuilding.

### Experience

**Essential**

- At least 2 years of experience in community mobilisation, community development or field work with an NGO, UN agency or government programme.
- Experience organising and facilitating community meetings with mixed groups, including women, youth and displaced persons.
- Good knowledge of the assigned LGA, its communities, traditional structures and local dynamics. Residence in or strong ties to the LGA are a strong advantage.

**Desirable**

- Experience supporting community committees, cooperatives, VSLAs or Water User Associations.
- Experience with livelihoods, agriculture, aquaculture or tailoring activities.
- Experience collecting data with mobile tools such as KoBoToolbox or ODK.
- Experience with complaints and feedback mechanisms.

### Skills and competencies

- Excellent communication and listening skills; able to explain ideas simply and respectfully.
- Trusted by and able to relate well to leaders, elders, women, youth and vulnerable groups.
- Neutral, discreet and honest, with good judgement in sensitive situations.
- Organised and reliable; able to work independently in the field with little supervision.
- Basic numeracy and record keeping, and basic smartphone and MS Office skills.
- Commitment to inclusion, PSEA and humanitarian principles.

### Languages

- **Essential:** fluent Hausa and Kanuri; good written and spoken English.

jobs.title: Communication Officer_Maiduguri
jobs.body:
**Job Purpose**

Contribute to the **implementation of operational communication strategy and the strengthening of external communications** in the mission according to INTERSOS standards.

Aim at **building INTERSOS visibility, acceptance and leverage** inside the country.

Focus on media alert, local media management and content diffusion and support the production of quality multimedia materials.

**Reporting to:**

**Hierarchical:** Communication Coordinator (in absence: Head of Mission)

**Functional**: HQ Communication Coordinator

**Key Responsibilities**:

**Internal Communications and Accountability**

- Help in promoting INTERSOS external communications principles and material towards the National Staffs. Sensitize National Staffs about potential external communications risks
- Monitor the international and national media and social media highlighting any relevant content for the humanitarian response in the country and for INTERSOS’ programmes
- Implement an ‘early warning system’ on national/regional issues and news
- In collaboration with Project/Programme Managers, ensure the respect of visibility guidelines and donors’ compliance
- Ensure the respect of INTERSOS’ protection, communications, and privacy policies and guidelines
- Ensure the proper allocation and management of the communication budget at country level, in coordination with the Finance department
- Provide technical training to staff members to increase their ability of producing multimedia content material
- Establish and manage INTERSOS mission Facebook page, including developing and publishing posts in adherence with communication guidelines and ensure its appropriate functioning as a tool for accountability and communication with communities
- Analyze and report traffic on INTERSOS Facebook page
- If needed edit the production of internal communication tools (newsletter, etc.)

**External Communications**

- Identify opportunities to communicate based on INTERSOS operations and context news (humanitarian, social and security updates), supporting the definition of a dissemination strategy for each identified topic
- Manage the production of multimedia materials for external communications, as well as the materials requested by donors for their internal and external communications. Is directly involved in collecting stories, aggregating data, pitching news, taking pictures, filming and editing videos thorough frequent field visits to be planned accordingly to security and mission’s priorities
- Support Project/Programme Managers in documenting project activities and related humanitarian issues by producing multimedia materials for external communications
- Produce written contents such as press releases, reactive lines, Q&As, op-eds and updates on INTERSOS’ activities
- Establish and maintain regular relations with international and key local media contacts (journalists, bloggers, photographers and cameramen). Handle local media requests and contact local media proactively to introduce INTERSOS and identify opportunities and facilitate interviews with INTERSOS spokespeople
- Provide guidance on how to deal with local media at time of crisis
- Monitor local media and flag significant articles, trends, news or reports of importance for INTERSOS or on the context to Head of Mission
- Organize events for local media (press conference, press briefing…). May act as a spokesperson for local media, particularly in local languages not spoken by members of the field coordination team. Support operational communications by providing tools and directly engaging in the production of specific materials
- Actively diffuse INTERSOS content in the country in local languages and among local media. If judged applicable, use social media (twitter, blogs, Facebook....) to promote this content
- Supervise the production of institutional communication and visibility materials (leaflets, brochures, posters, radio spots, articles, photos, videos) according to local strategy and budget
- Help in identifying the right communications tools and adapt/translate communications materials to targeted local audiences
- Produce strategic reports on the local media landscape (key media, audience numbers, political affiliation, ownership, freedom of speech, use of social media) and regularly report on new developments. Participate in communication data-collection and reporting as required
- Support the organization of Media field visits in coordination with the HQ
- **Requirements**

Education

- Preferable degree in Journalism, Communications or related university degree

Professional experience

- Minimum 3 years work experience in communications, journalism or public relations in the country.
    
    Language Requirement: English, Hausa, Kanuri very cruical.

jobs.title: Venezuela - Asesor de Seguridad (national)
Venezuela - Coordinador/a de Operaciones (National)
jobs.body:
## Acerca de COOPI

COOPI Cooperazione Internazionale es una ONG laica e independiente, fundada en Milán en 1965. Lleva a cabo proyectos de desarrollo para contribuir a la lucha contra las desigualdades y programas de emergencia para apoyar a las personas afectadas por desastres naturales o conflictos. Actualmente, COOPI está presente en 33 países de África, Oriente Medio, América Latina y Caribe.

Desde 2019 COOPI establece una presencia en Venezuela y, a partir de julio de 2020, inicia un programa regional que se implementa en asociación con organizaciones venezolanas y en coordinación con instituciones locales e internacionales, en el marco de los planes de respuesta vigentes. En los últimos años COOPI ha ampliado sus intervenciones y actualmente ejecuta proyectos con diferentes donantes en Caracas, Sucre, Delta Amacuro y Bolívar, en protección, salud sexual y reproductiva, WASH (agua, saneamiento e higiene), alimentación escolar, ambiente y fortalecimiento institucional.

Tras los sismos ocurridos el 24 de junio de 2026, COOPI en Venezuela ha ampliado adicionalmente su cartera de intervenciones mediante proyectos de respuesta a la emergencia.

## Objetivo/descripción del puesto

Bajo la supervisión directa de la Coordinación País, el/la Coordinador/a de Operaciones será responsable de supervisar y acompañar la implementación operativa del portafolio de proyectos de COOPI en Venezuela, asegurando el cumplimiento de planes de trabajo, cronogramas, presupuestos y compromisos operativos.

Acompañará a los/las Jefes/as o Gerentes de Proyecto en la gestión de sus proyectos, facilitando el seguimiento de la ejecución, el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades y la resolución oportuna de bloqueos y desviaciones.

Trabajará en estrecha coordinación con Programas, Administración, Logística, MEAL, RRHH, Coordinaciones de Base y otras funciones de la misión, respetando los ámbitos de responsabilidad técnica y funcional de cada departamento.

La función estará principalmente orientada a la gestión y ejecución de proyectos, sin sustituir las responsabilidades de las Coordinaciones de Base en la gestión territorial de las oficinas y servicios de soporte, ni las responsabilidades técnicas y programáticas de la Coordinación de Programas.

El puesto buscará reforzar la autonomía y capacidad de gestión de los/las responsables de proyecto, proporcionando acompañamiento y soporte proporcional a las necesidades y experiencia de cada perfil. Se priorizarán perfiles nacionales.

**Áreas de responsabilidad**

**1. Supervisión de la implementación de proyectos**

- Acompañar y dar seguimiento a los/las Jefes/as y Gerentes de Proyecto en la definición de prioridades, objetivos y mecanismos periódicos de seguimiento.
- Asegurar que cada proyecto disponga de planes de trabajo, cronogramas, herramientas de seguimiento y responsabilidades claramente definidas y actualizadas.
- Dar seguimiento sistemático al avance de actividades, productos, resultados y principales hitos contractuales, identificando oportunamente retrasos, desviaciones y riesgos de implementación.
- Trabajar con los/las responsables de proyecto en la definición y seguimiento de medidas correctivas cuando existan retrasos o dificultades de ejecución.
- Promover una gestión proactiva de los proyectos, apoyando a los PM en la identificación de alternativas y soluciones ante bloqueos operativos.
- Asegurar el seguimiento y cierre oportuno de decisiones, procesos y acciones pendientes relacionados con la ejecución de los proyectos.
- Realizar visitas regulares a las áreas de intervención y reuniones de seguimiento con los equipos de proyecto y de base.
- Informar regularmente a la Coordinación País sobre avances, riesgos, necesidades de decisión y situaciones que puedan comprometer la ejecución de los proyectos.

**2. Gestión y desarrollo de los/las Jefes/as de Proyecto**

- Acompañar a los/las Jefes/as y Gerentes de Proyecto en la planificación, organización y priorización de su trabajo y en la gestión de los equipos bajo su responsabilidad.
- Fortalecer capacidades y desempeños en gestión del ciclo de proyecto, planificación, seguimiento financiero, gestión de equipos, anticipación de riesgos y resolución de problemas.
- Realizar reuniones individuales y colectivas de seguimiento y proporcionar retroalimentación periódica sobre desempeño y prioridades.
- Participar, junto con RRHH y la Coordinación País, en los procesos de selección, inducción, evaluación y desarrollo de los/las Jefes/as de Proyecto.
- Identificar necesidades de formación y acompañamiento, particularmente para perfiles nuevos o junior.
- Favorecer una cultura de responsabilidad, iniciativa, cumplimiento de compromisos y colaboración entre proyectos y departamentos.

**3. Seguimiento financiero y planificación operativa de los proyectos**

- Asegurar, en coordinación con Administración País y sin sustituir sus responsabilidades de control financiero y administrativo, el seguimiento periódico de la situación financiera de sus proyectos.
- Revisar con los PM el presupuesto, burn rate, previsiones y proyecciones de gasto, verificando su coherencia con los planes de actividades y cronogramas.
- Identificar tempranamente desviaciones entre ejecución programada y ejecución financiera y asegurar la preparación de medidas correctivas.
- Asegurar que las proyecciones financieras y necesidades operativas de los proyectos sean preparadas con suficiente anticipación y compartidas con Administración.
- Facilitar la coordinación entre PM y Administración cuando existan bloqueos o decisiones que puedan afectar la ejecución presupuestaria.
- Dar seguimiento, desde la perspectiva de ejecución del proyecto, a modificaciones presupuestarias, realineamientos y otras necesidades identificadas durante la implementación.
- La validación contable, financiera y de elegibilidad de los gastos seguirá correspondiendo a Administración.

**4. Seguimiento de procurement y logística de proyecto**

- Asegurar, en coordinación con Logística País, Administracion y las Coordinaciones de Base, que cada proyecto disponga de un plan de compras y adquisiciones actualizado y coherente con su plan de trabajo y cronograma.
- Asegurar que los PM y equipos de proyecto anticipen adecuadamente las necesidades de bienes, servicios, transporte y demás recursos necesarios para la ejecución.
- Dar seguimiento al estado de los principales procesos de compra y contratación vinculados a proyectos, identificando tempranamente posibles retrasos que puedan afectar actividades o resultados.
- Facilitar la coordinación entre PM, Logística y Base cuando existan bloqueos operativos.
- Asegurar que los PM integren adecuadamente los tiempos de los procedimientos logísticos y administrativos en su planificación.
- Dar seguimiento a la disponibilidad y utilización de recursos de proyecto desde la perspectiva de su impacto sobre la implementación.
- La gestión de proveedores, procedimientos de adquisición, flota, almacenes, activos y demás funciones logísticas institucionales seguirá siendo responsabilidad de Logística País y, en su ámbito territorial, de las estructuras correspondientes de Base.

**5. Coordinación de la ejecución y relación con otros departamentos**

- Actuar como principal punto de articulación entre los PM y las diferentes funciones de coordinación cuando existan necesidades o bloqueos relacionados con la ejecución.
- Mantener una coordinación sistemática con Programas sobre aspectos técnicos, calidad programática, indicadores, MEAL y modificaciones que puedan afectar el diseño de las intervenciones.
- Coordinar con Administración los aspectos financieros y contractuales vinculados a la ejecución.
- Coordinar con Logística los procesos operativos necesarios para la implementación.
- Coordinar con RRHH sobre necesidades de personal, desempeño y gestión de equipos de proyecto.
- Mantener una coordinación regular con las Coordinaciones de Base para asegurar la adecuada articulación entre la gestión del proyecto y las condiciones operativas de cada territorio.
- Favorecer una comunicación clara sobre responsabilidades, decisiones y plazos entre proyectos, departamentos y bases.
- La Coordinación de Operaciones no ejercerá supervisión jerárquica sobre las Coordinaciones de Base ni sobre los departamentos de soporte, salvo delegación temporal y expresa de la Coordinación País.

**6. Seguimiento de reporting y compromisos de proyecto**

- Asegurar que los PM mantengan actualizado el calendario de principales entregables, hitos contractuales y obligaciones de sus proyectos.
- Dar seguimiento a la preparación oportuna de los insumos técnicos, operativos y financieros requeridos para informes internos, informes a donantes, modificaciones y otros procesos contractuales.
- Asegurar que los PM proporcionen información completa y dentro de los plazos establecidos a las funciones responsables de consolidación y revisión de informes.
- Alertar oportunamente sobre retrasos o dificultades que puedan comprometer entregables contractuales.
- La revisión técnica, consolidación programática y gestión especializada de grants se realizará en coordinación con las funciones responsables de Programas/Grants.

**7. Gestión de riesgos y resolución de bloqueos**

- Identificar, junto con los PM, riesgos operativos, financieros, contractuales, de recursos humanos o de implementación que puedan afectar los proyectos.
- Asegurar que se definan medidas de mitigación, responsables y plazos para los principales riesgos identificados.
- Facilitar la resolución de bloqueos entre proyectos, bases y departamentos y escalar a la Coordinación País aquellos que requieran decisiones de nivel superior.
- Mantener una visión consolidada de los principales riesgos y necesidades operativas del portafolio de proyectos.
- Contribuir al aprendizaje institucional identificando problemas recurrentes, cuellos de botella y oportunidades de mejora de los procesos internos.
- Los riesgos técnicos serán abordados con Programas; los financieros con Administración; los logísticos con Logística; y los relativos a seguridad de acuerdo con la estructura y responsabilidades establecidas por la misión.

**8. Apoyo temporal a proyectos, bases y nuevas intervenciones**

- Por solicitud expresa de la Coordinación País, proporcionar refuerzo operativo temporal durante el lanzamiento de nuevos proyectos, transiciones, fases críticas o períodos de alta carga de trabajo.
- Asumir temporalmente funciones de gestión de proyecto cuando exista una vacante de PM, hasta la incorporación de la persona responsable.
- Apoyar excepcionalmente una Base cuando exista una vacante o necesidad temporal de refuerzo de coordinación, con un mandato y período previamente definidos.
- Apoyar la puesta en marcha de nuevas operaciones y facilitar su posterior transferencia al responsable correspondiente.
- Contribuir a respuestas de emergencia o incrementos rápidos de operaciones cuando la misión requiera capacidad adicional de gestión.
- Estas funciones tendrán carácter temporal y no modificarán las responsabilidades permanentes de las estructuras de Proyecto, Base o departamentos nacionales.

**9. Actividades complementarias**

- Promover el cumplimiento de los procedimientos institucionales de COOPI y del Código de Conducta en los equipos bajo su supervisión.
- Contribuir a un ambiente de trabajo profesional, colaborativo y respetuoso.
- Participar en reuniones de coordinación y planificación de la misión.
- Representar a COOPI, cuando sea delegado por la Coordinación País, en reuniones vinculadas específicamente a la implementación operativa de proyectos.
- Ejecutar aquellas tareas inherentes al puesto y que sean solicitadas por la Coordinación País, según contexto y necesidades de la misión.

## Perfil deseado

Profesional con sólida experiencia en gestión e implementación de proyectos humanitarios y/o de desarrollo, supervisión de Project Managers y coordinación entre equipos multidisciplinarios. Se busca especialmente un perfil con fuerte capacidad de project management, seguimiento, resolución de problemas y desarrollo de equipos, capaz de combinar una visión global del portafolio con acompañamiento práctico a los responsables de proyecto.

### ESENCIALES

- Título universitario en Cooperación Internacional, Gestión de Proyectos, Ciencias Sociales, Administración, Ingeniería, Relaciones Internacionales o áreas afines.
- Al menos 5 años de experiencia relevante en gestión de proyectos humanitarios o de desarrollo con ONG internacionales, agencias internacionales u organizaciones similares.
- Experiencia demostrable como Coordinador/a de Proyectos Senior, Coordinador/a de Operaciones o posición equivalente.
- Experiencia comprobada en supervisión, acompañamiento y desarrollo de Project Managers o equipos de gestión de proyectos.
- Dominio del ciclo de gestión de proyectos: planificación, ejecución, seguimiento, reporting y cierre.
- Experiencia en seguimiento financiero de proyectos, incluyendo presupuestos, forecast, spending plans, análisis de ejecución y planificación de gasto.
- Experiencia en planificación y seguimiento de adquisiciones y necesidades logísticas vinculadas a proyectos.
- Conocimiento de procedimientos y requisitos de donantes institucionales, particularmente Unión Europea/ECHO, Naciones Unidas y/o cooperación bilateral.
- Capacidad demostrada para detectar bloqueos, analizar problemas y desarrollar soluciones prácticas.
- Experiencia en gestión de equipos, evaluación de desempeño, feedback y fortalecimiento de capacidades.
- Excelentes capacidades de organización, priorización y seguimiento.
- Capacidad para trabajar de manera transversal con equipos técnicos, administrativos, logísticos y territoriales, respetando los diferentes ámbitos de responsabilidad.
- Liderazgo colaborativo, orientación a resultados y capacidad para acompañar y desarrollar equipos.
- Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión y gestionar simultáneamente múltiples proyectos y prioridades.
- Excelente comunicación interpersonal, capacidad de negociación y manejo constructivo de desacuerdos.
- Idioma castellano imprescindible; buen nivel de inglés oral y escrito.
- Manejo de herramientas informáticas y ofimáticas, con buen dominio de Excel.
- Disponibilidad para viajar regularmente a las diferentes áreas de intervención de COOPI en Venezuela.
- Respeto de la Visión y Misión de COOPI, de su carta de valores y de las políticas institucionales.

### DESEABLES

- Experiencia previa en Venezuela o en contextos latinoamericanos de elevada complejidad.
- Experiencia en contextos de emergencia y en lanzamiento o escalamiento rápido de proyectos.
- Experiencia previa con COOPI.
- Experiencia en proyectos financiados por ECHO, Unión Europea, AICS y agencias de Naciones Unidas.
- Formación de posgrado en gestión de proyectos, acción humanitaria, cooperación internacional o áreas relacionadas.
- Nacionalidad venezolana o permiso de residencia en el país.

jobs.title: Venezuela - Gerente de Socios y Subvenciones (Nacional)
jobs.body:
## Acerca de COOPI

COOPI Cooperazione Internazionale es una ONG laica e independiente, fundada en Milán en 1965. Lleva a cabo proyectos de desarrollo para contribuir a la lucha contra las desigualdades y programas de emergencia para apoyar a las personas afectadas por desastres naturales o conflictos. Actualmente, COOPI está presente en 33 países de África, Oriente Medio, América Latina y Caribe.

Desde 2019 COOPI establece una presencia en Venezuela y, a partir de julio de 2020, inicia un programa regional que se implementa en asociación con organizaciones venezolanas y en coordinación con instituciones locales e internacionales, en el marco de los planes de respuesta vigentes. En los últimos años COOPI ha ampliado sus intervenciones y actualmente ejecuta proyectos financiados por distintos donantes en Caracas, Sucre, Delta Amacuro, Bolívar y otros estados del país, en los sectores de protección, salud, WASH, ambiente, seguridad alimentaria, fortalecimiento institucional y respuesta a emergencias.

En el marco del crecimiento y diversificación de su portafolio, COOPI Venezuela busca reforzar la gestión de subvenciones y alianzas mediante una función especializada que asegure el seguimiento contractual, la calidad y oportunidad de los procesos de reporting y formulación, y una coordinación eficaz con socios de los consorcios actuales y donantes.

## Objetivo/descripción del puesto

Bajo la supervisión de la Coordinación País y con acompañamiento funcional de la Coordinación de Programas, el/la Gerente de Socios y Subvenciones será responsable de asegurar la gestión coordinada del portafolio de subvenciones y alianzas de COOPI Venezuela, garantizando el seguimiento oportuno de obligaciones contractuales, propuestas, modificaciones, reporting y procesos de coordinación con socios.

El puesto actuará como punto focal para la planificación y seguimiento de los principales procesos de gestión de subvenciones, facilitando la coordinación entre Programas, Operaciones, Administración, MEAL, Jefes/as de Proyecto, socios, Coordinación Regional y Sede.

Asimismo, apoyará en la coordinación institucional y contractual del Consorcio ÍNTEGRAS y de futuras alianzas o consorcios en los que COOPI ejerza funciones de liderazgo, adaptando el nivel de coordinación a la complejidad y características de cada alianza.

La posición se coordinará estrechamente con Programas, los equipos de proyecto y Administración País, articulando sus respectivos aportes para asegurar una gestión coherente, oportuna y alineada con los compromisos asumidos con donantes y socios.

**Áreas de responsabilidad**

**Gestión del portafolio de subvenciones:**

- Mantener actualizado un calendario consolidado de obligaciones contractuales, reportes, modificaciones, auditorías, entregables y principales hitos de todos los proyectos de la misión.
- Dar seguimiento a los plazos y responsabilidades asociados a cada subvención, alertando con suficiente anticipación sobre entregables y riesgos de incumplimiento.
- Asegurar la adecuada circulación de información entre Jefes/as de Proyecto, Programas, Operaciones, Administración, MEAL, Coordinación País, Región y Sede.
- Mantener organizados y accesibles los principales documentos contractuales, versiones aprobadas, modificaciones, comunicaciones con donantes y documentación relevante para la gestión de cada subvención.
- Apoyar la interpretación y difusión interna de requisitos contractuales y lineamientos de los donantes.
- Identificar oportunamente riesgos de cumplimiento, reporting o gestión contractual y escalarlos a las funciones responsables.

**Reporting y seguimiento contractual:**

- Coordinar el calendario y proceso de preparación de informes narrativos intermedios y finales.
- Solicitar y consolidar los aportes de Jefes/as de Proyecto, equipos técnicos, MEAL, Administración y socios.
- Revisar la coherencia, integridad y consistencia de los informes antes de su validación por Programas y Coordinación País.
- Asegurar la coherencia entre información narrativa, indicadores, ejecución operativa y datos financieros, en coordinación con las áreas responsables.
- Dar seguimiento a comentarios y solicitudes de aclaración de donantes hasta su cierre.
- Mantener control de versiones y trazabilidad de los principales documentos enviados y aprobados.
- Coordinar la revisión y consolidación de informes y otros entregables, articulando la validación técnica con Programas y los equipos técnicos, y la validación financiera con Administración País.

**Formulación y modificaciones de proyectos:**

- Coordinar, en estrecha articulación con Coordinación País y Programas, los procesos de preparación de nuevas propuestas, notas conceptuales y expresiones de interés.
- Establecer cronogramas de formulación, distribuir responsabilidades y asegurar la entrega oportuna de los distintos componentes.
- Consolidar los aportes de Programas, MEAL, Administración, Operaciones, equipos de proyecto y socios.
- Asegurar la coherencia entre narrativa, marco lógico, indicadores, cronograma, plan operativo y presupuesto.
- Coordinar los procesos de modificación contractual, extensiones, realineamientos, adendas y reprogramaciones.
- Preparar o consolidar las justificaciones y documentación requerida por donantes.
- Mantener actualizada la información sobre oportunidades de financiación y apoyar a Coordinación País y Programas en la planificación del pipeline de propuestas.
- Apoyar la formulación de nuevas propuestas a partir de las prioridades estratégicas y orientaciones técnicas definidas por Coordinación País y Programas, asegurando su adecuada traducción en los documentos de proyecto.
    
    **Gestión de socios y alianzas:**
- Mantener una visión consolidada de los socios institucionales, co-solicitantes, co-partners y organizaciones implementadoras vinculadas a los proyectos de COOPI.
- Facilitar la coordinación contractual y documental con socios durante formulación, implementación, reporting y cierre.
- Dar seguimiento a acuerdos de partnership, calendarios de reporting y otras obligaciones de los socios, en coordinación con Administración y los responsables de proyecto.
- Facilitar procesos de due diligence, documentación institucional y seguimiento de capacidades cuando corresponda.
- Identificar dificultades recurrentes en la gestión de alianzas y proponer medidas de mejora.
- Contribuir al fortalecimiento de herramientas y procedimientos internos de COOPI para la gestión de socios.
- Coordinar con los/las Jefes/as de Proyecto el seguimiento de los socios implementadores en los aspectos contractuales, documentales y de reporting, articulando los requerimientos del grant con la gestión operativa del proyecto.

**Apoyo a consorcios y alianzas:**

- Apoyar la gestión de consorcios y alianzas en los aspectos vinculados a grants, reporting, propuestas, modificaciones y obligaciones contractuales.
- Facilitar la consolidación de aportes de socios y equipos internos para propuestas, informes y otros entregables conjuntos.
- Dar seguimiento a compromisos, plazos y requerimientos documentales vinculados a subvenciones gestionadas en consorcio.
- Apoyar, junto con Coordinación País y Programas, los procesos de formulación y gestión contractual con donantes y socios.

**Coordinación interna y calidad de la gestión de subvenciones:**

- Trabajar estrechamente con Programas para asegurar la coherencia técnica y programática de propuestas, modificaciones e informes.
- Coordinar con Operaciones y los equipos de proyecto el seguimiento de avances, hitos y riesgos de implementación relevantes para las obligaciones contractuales.
- Coordinar con Administración la preparación de presupuestos, modificaciones financieras, informes y seguimiento de requisitos administrativos.
- Coordinar con MEAL la disponibilidad y consistencia de indicadores, medios de verificación y resultados reportados.
- Promover herramientas comunes para calendarios, reporting, seguimiento contractual y archivo.
- Facilitar reuniones de lanzamiento, revisión y cierre de subvenciones cuando resulte necesario.
- Contribuir a identificar aprendizajes y mejoras en los procesos de gestión de subvenciones de la misión.

**Relación con donantes y representación:**

- Mantener, por delegación de la Coordinación País, comunicación operativa con donantes sobre reporting, modificaciones, aclaraciones y procesos contractuales.
- Apoyar en la preparación de reuniones, revisiones y visitas de donantes asegurando la disponibilidad y coherencia de la información requerida.
- Apoyar a Coordinación País y Programas en reuniones de seguimiento, negociación y diseño de nuevas intervenciones.
- Representar a COOPI en espacios relacionados con gestión de subvenciones y partnerships cuando sea requerido.

**Actividades complementarias:**

- Promover el cumplimiento de las políticas, procedimientos y Código Ético de COOPI.
- Contribuir a un ambiente de trabajo colaborativo y a una comunicación fluida entre departamentos.
- Apoyar el fortalecimiento de capacidades de equipos y socios en gestión de subvenciones, reporting y requisitos de donantes.
- Ejecutar aquellas tareas inherentes al puesto y que sean solicitadas por la Coordinación País, según contexto y necesidades de la intervención.

## Perfil deseado

Profesional con experiencia sólida en gestión de subvenciones, formulación de propuestas, reporting y gestión de alianzas en organizaciones humanitarias o de cooperación internacional. Se busca un perfil altamente organizado, con capacidad para manejar simultáneamente distintos donantes, proyectos y plazos, coordinar aportes de múltiples departamentos y socios y producir documentos de elevada calidad.

### ESENCIALES

- Título universitario en Cooperación Internacional, Relaciones Internacionales, Ciencias Sociales, Administración, Economía, Derecho o áreas relacionadas.
- Al menos 5 años de experiencia relevante en cooperación internacional o acción humanitaria, incluyendo experiencia demostrable en gestión de subvenciones con donantes institucionales.
- Experiencia en formulación de propuestas, notas conceptuales, marcos lógicos, modificaciones contractuales y preparación/consolidación de informes narrativos.
- Conocimiento de procedimientos y requisitos de donantes institucionales, particularmente Unión Europea/ECHO y/o agencias de Naciones Unidas.
- Experiencia en trabajo con consorcios, alianzas y socios implementadores, incluyendo seguimiento de compromisos, reporting y coordinación documental.
- Capacidad para coordinar procesos complejos con múltiples actores, áreas y plazos simultáneos, asegurando coherencia entre componentes programáticos, operativos y financieros.
- Excelentes capacidades de redacción, análisis, síntesis y atención al detalle, manteniendo al mismo tiempo una visión global de los procesos.
- Alta capacidad de organización, planificación y priorización, con orientación a resultados y cumplimiento de plazos.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, trabajo en equipo y coordinación transversal, con capacidad para facilitar acuerdos y mantener relaciones de trabajo constructivas con equipos internos, socios y donantes.
- Empatía, escucha activa, flexibilidad y adaptabilidad, especialmente en contextos de trabajo exigentes y con prioridades cambiantes.
- Autonomía, proactividad y capacidad para trabajar bajo presión y gestionar varios procesos concurrentes manteniendo rigor y calidad.
- Dominio del español e inglés oral y escrito.
- Buen manejo de herramientas de Microsoft Office.
- Compromiso con los principios, Código Ético y políticas institucionales de COOPI.
- Nacionalidad venezolana o permiso de residencia en el país.

### DESEABLES

- Experiencia con AICS, Unión Europea/INTPA, OIM, UNICEF u otras agencias de Naciones Unidas.
- Experiencia en due diligence y gestión de acuerdos con socios locales.
- Experiencia previa con COOPI.

Senior Corporate Development Officer
jobs.body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

JOB SUMMARY  
Leads advanced fundraising projects and initiatives, ensuring effective donor engagement, grant identification, and proposal development.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Join a Global Mission That Changes Lives**

When you join Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI), you join a movement that believes every person deserves a safe and affordable place to call home. As our next **Senior Corporate Development Officer**, you will help build the partnerships that make this mission possible.

In this role, you will focus on cultivating and expanding relationships with corporate partners in the New York City market, with a particular emphasis on the banking and financial services sector. Your work will help generate critical revenue that fuels Habitat’s mission and supports families and communities around the world.

You will shape national and global corporate relationships that fuel Habitat’s work in more than 70 countries. Your creativity, strategy, and relationship-building skills will directly support families and communities around the world.

**Location and Travel**

This position is fully remote in New York or New Jersey. You will have the flexibility to work from home while collaborating with colleagues and partners across the country and around the world.

This role requires approximately 25 percent domestic travel for partner meetings, prospecting activities, events, and other key engagements.

**Role Purpose**

You will lead the development, cultivation, and stewardship of high-value corporate partnerships, primarily with Fortune 500 companies. You will manage a portfolio that generates between 5 and 10 million dollars annually and collaborate across HFHI’s global network to design innovative, mission-aligned partnerships that advance affordable housing worldwide.

**Key Responsibilities**

\*Develop and execute strategic, partner-centered plans that align corporate goals with Habitat’s mission.  
\*Identify, cultivate, and secure new national and global corporate partnerships while strengthening existing relationships.  
\*Create and deliver compelling proposals and presentations that inspire corporate engagement.  
\*Negotiate complex, multi-year commitments in collaboration with legal, finance, and program teams.  
\*Provide high-touch stewardship that ensures partner satisfaction and long-term growth.  
\*Collaborate with HFHI affiliates and global teams to maximize partnership value and ensure seamless execution.  
\*Track, analyze, and report on partnership performance using CRM systems and forecasting tools.

**Must-Have Qualifications**

\*Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience  
\*5+ years of experience in fundraising, sales, or prospect development  
\*Proven success securing six and seven figure multiyear commitments from Fortune 500 companies  
\*Experience with international partnership strategy and development  
\*Strong understanding of corporate social responsibility, sponsorships, and employee engagement  
\*Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and negotiation skills  
\*Highly proactive, solutions-oriented, and comfortable navigating a complex organization  
\*Strong project management, analytics, and reporting capabilities  
\*Commitment to HFHI values: Humility, Courage, Accountability, and safeguarding practices

**Nice-to-Have Qualifications**

\*Experience with Blackbaud CRM or similar platforms  
\*Background in sales, marketing, or public relations  
\*Knowledge of and passion for Habitat’s global mission

**Culture and Values**

At Habitat for Humanity International, you join a community that believes in:  
**\*Humility:** We are part of something bigger than ourselves.  
**\*Courage:** We do what is right, even when it is difficult.  
**\*Accountability:** We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission.  
**\*Safeguarding:** We protect the rights, dignity, and safety of all people we serve and work alongside.

**Ready to Build Something Bigger Than Yourself**

If you are excited to create partnerships that change lives and strengthen communities, we would love to hear from you. Your leadership can help families around the world build strength, stability, and self-reliance through shelter.

**Apply today and help us build a world where everyone has a decent place to live.**

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$97,300.00 USD

\-

$144,775 USD

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.body:
## **About CBM**

CBM (registered as CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V.) is an international development organisation committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the persons communities of the world. Based on our Christian values and more than 100 years of professional expertise, we address poverty as a cause and a consequence of disability. We work in partnership to create an inclusive society for all.

**About the role:**  
We are looking for a Communications & Visibility Officer to support the implementation of communication and visibility activities across our programmes in Ukraine.  
In this role, you will help ensure that CBM’s work is effectively communicated and visible, in line with donor requirements (including EU ECHO), while contributing to storytelling, content development, and stakeholder engagement.  
**This position is fixed-term until 31.07.28 and only filled locally. With contractual conditions of the respective country. An expatriation is not intended.**

## **These are your responsibilities**

Communication Planning & Compliance

Content Development & Storytelling

Visibility & Outreach

Coordination & Partner Support

Monitoring, Reporting & Knowledge Management

## **These are your qualifications**

- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, particularly for compliance and reporting
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team
- Professional proficiency in Ukrainian; English is an asset
- Experience with EU or other institutional donor-funded projects is an advantage
- Identification with the Christian values and mandate of CBM

## **What we offer**

- A meaningful position with a lot of creative freedom in the world's leading organisation in the field of Disability Inclusive Development
- A fair salary and other social benefits based on the local conditions in the country you apply for
- An approachable, agile organisation with self-reliant people in a diverse and collegial team and great team spirit

jobs.title: Aquaculture & Feed Production Officer
jobs.body:
**JOB PURPOSE:**  
Under the supervision of the Livelihood Project Manager, the Aquaculture and Feed Production Officer is the technical lead for the fish farms in MMC, Jere and Mafa and for the Mafa Fish Feed Production Centre. The goal is that all four run as productive, profitable community enterprises, with affordable local feed, good fish husbandry and value addition.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**1. Assessment and planning:**

• Carry out a technical assessment of each fish farm: pond condition and capacity, water source and quality, stocking history, mortality, growth rates, feeding practices and records.

• Lead the fish farm profitability diagnostic with the Business Development Officer. Analyze stocking density, feed conversion ratio (FCR), survival, harvest weights, selling prices and cost per kilogram.

• With the Agricultural and Infrastructure Engineers, define the technical requirements for pond rehabilitation at MMC and Jere and for the replacement feed mill line.

• Prepare a production plan for each farm: species (mainly catfish), stocking density, staggered stocking and harvesting calendar, and expected output.

**2. Fish farm rehabilitation and restocking:**

• Advise the engineers on pond layout, depth, inlets and outlets, and water management needs during rehabilitation.

• Oversee pond preparation before stocking: liming, fertilizing where appropriate, filling and water quality checks.

• Source certified, healthy fingerlings or juveniles from reputable hatcheries. Supervise transport, acclimatization and stocking.

• Set up a staggered stocking cycle so ponds are harvested in rotation and income is regular.

**3. Production management and fish health:**

• Train and coach pond teams in feeding schedules, water quality monitoring (temperature, dissolved oxygen, pH, ammonia), grading, predator control and pond hygiene.

• Set up disease prevention and biosecurity: quarantine of new stock, safe handling and the right response to mortality. Link to veterinary and fisheries extension services.

• Monitor growth through regular sampling and adjust feeding to improve the FCR and reduce waste.

• Make sure every farm keeps pond-by-pond records of stocking, feeding, sampling, mortality, harvest and sales.

**4. Fish Feed Production Centre:**

• Work with the Agricultural Engineer on specifying, installing and commissioning the replacement feed line (hammer mill, mixer, pelletizer or extruder, dryer, bagging).

• Develop feed formulas for each growth stage (starter, grower, finisher) using local ingredients such as maize, soybean, groundnut cake, fishmeal, premix and binders. Balance protein, energy and cost.

• Set up quality control: ingredient checks (moisture, mould, aflatoxin risk), batch records, pellet size, stability and floating or sinking behavior, and safe storage.

• Train 5–8 operators, mainly youth, in machine operation, formulation, hygiene, safety, stock control and record keeping.

• Plan ingredient procurement with the Business Development Officer, including bulk buying at harvest when prices are lowest, and plan feed supply to the three project farms and other buyers.

• Run the centre as a practical training hub for youth groups and other fish farmers in feed formulation and processing.

**5. Processing, value addition and marketing:**

• Train members in fish processing: smoking and drying with improved kilns, hygiene, packaging and storage. The aim is to reduce post-harvest losses and add value.

• Help set up fee-based smoking services for non-member producers where feasible.

• With the Market Linkages and Digital Solutions Officer, link farms to buyers in Maiduguri markets, restaurants, institutions and traders. Plan harvests to match demand and use price information to time sales.

• Provide production data to the Business Development Officer for pricing, business plans and cost recovery.

**6. Sustainability, monitoring and reporting:**

• Develop simple SOPs for pond management, feed production and fish processing, in English and Hausa.

• With the Asset Management Officer, make sure aquaculture equipment and inputs are recorded and maintained.

• Link each farm and the feed centre to the fisheries department and ADP extension officers who will support them after handover.

• Submit monthly technical reports with production, FCR, survival, feed output, sales and challenges. Provide MEAL data and contribute to the handover readiness assessment.

**Cross-cutting duties:**

• Promote environmentally sound practices: responsible water use and discharge, and safe handling of chemicals and feed ingredients.

• Make sure women and youth have fair access to roles in production, feed processing and fish processing.

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

• **Essential:** a university degree (B.Sc. or HND) in Fisheries and Aquaculture, Animal Science (with a fisheries or nutrition option), or a related field.

**• Desirable:** An M.Sc. in Agriculture.

**Professional experience Essential:**

• At least 4 years of practical experience in fish farming, preferably catfish in earthen or lined ponds, including production planning, fish health and record keeping.

• Hands-on experience in fish feed formulation and production using local ingredients, including running or supervising a small feed mill.

• Experience training farmers or community groups in fish production.

• Experience with NGOs, UN agencies or government agricultural programmes in North-East Nigeria or a similar setting.

**Desirable:**

• Experience with feed extruders or pelletizers, and with feed quality control.

• Experience with fish processing (smoking and drying) and market linkages.

• Experience supporting cooperatives or community-run aquaculture enterprises to become profitable.

• Knowledge of the fish value chain and markets in Borno State.

**Personal requirements**

• Strong technical knowledge of fish nutrition, water quality, biosecurity and fish health.

• Able to analyze production data such as FCR, survival and cost per kg, and turn it into practical advice.

• Excellent practical training and coaching skills, suited to adults with low literacy.

• Problem-solver who is comfortable working hands-on at pond side and in the mill.

• Integrity in input, procurement and quality checks.

• Commitment to inclusion, PSEA and humanitarian principles.

• Proficient in MS Office or Google Workspace, especially spreadsheets.

**Languages**

• **Essential:** fluent English; good spoken Hausa.

• **Desirable:** Kanuri.

jobs.title: Agricultural Engineer
jobs.body:
**JOB PURPOSE:**  
Under the supervision of the Livelihood Project Manager, the Livelihood Agricultural Engineer is the project's technical lead for all engineering works. They design, supervise and commission the irrigation, aquaculture, feed mill and greenhouse infrastructure in MMC, Jere and Mafa LGAs, and train the community operators who will run and maintain it.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**1. Technical assessments:**

• Carry out condition assessments of all agricultural facilities: irrigation systems, ponds and water supply, the feed mill and its power supply, and the greenhouse.

• Run a hydraulic assessment at the MMC and Jere irrigation farms: water source yield, command area, crop water demand, head and flow, drainage and return flow, and sump location.

• Assess whether any existing feed mill parts can be reused, and whether the building and power supply can carry the replacement line.

• Identify risks to the sites, including flooding, theft and power supply, and propose engineering measures to reduce them.

• Produce an assessment report for each facility, with bills of quantities (BoQs) and cost estimates, for approval by the Project Manager and the LGA Oversight Committee.

**2. Design and specification:**

• Size and design the recirculation pumping systems: pump, solar array and inverter, sump or collection tank, intake screens, filters, valves, pipework and pump house.

• Prepare drawings and specifications for pond rehabilitation (desilting, liners or embankments, inlets and outlets, overflow) and the related water supply works.

• Write the technical specification for the replacement feed production line: hammer mill, mixer, pelletiser or extruder, dryer, sieving and bagging, and power supply.

• Specify greenhouse repairs and any minor civil works (pump houses, ingredient stores, fencing).

• Get technical sign-off from the Ministry of Water Resources (pumps) and the relevant fisheries and agriculture departments.

**3. Procurement support:**

• Prepare technical specifications, BoQs and evaluation criteria for tenders. Value warranty, local after-sales service and spare parts availability as well as price.

• Sit on technical evaluation panels and advise on contractor and supplier selection.

• Inspect goods on delivery against specifications before acceptance.

**4. Construction and installation supervision:**

• Supervise contractors and installers on site daily. Check workmanship, materials, measurements and compliance with drawings.

• Keep site diaries, issue instructions and record any variations, and certify work for payment.

• Enforce health, safety and environmental standards on site, including safe electrical installation and safe working around water and machinery.

• Escalate delays, defects or cost overruns to the Project Manager immediately.

**5. Testing, commissioning and handover of works:**

• Lead testing and commissioning: trial irrigation cycles, pump performance (flow and head), pond water-holding tests, and feed mill test runs with pellet quality checks.

• Commission jointly with the government technical counterpart, the facility committee and the supplier, and record results in commissioning certificates.

• Collect as-built drawings, operation manuals, warranties and starter spare parts for every installation.

**6. Operator training and maintenance systems:**

• Train irrigation operators (5–7 per scheme), pond teams and feed mill operators in operation, troubleshooting, preventive maintenance and safety.

• Develop simple SOPs and preventive maintenance schedules for each asset, in English and Hausa with pictures where useful.

• With the Asset Management and Logistics Officer, enter every engineered asset into the asset register: specifications, serial numbers, warranty, expected useful life and condition rating.

• Build a list of local technicians and spare parts suppliers for each asset type.

• Advise the facility committees and the Enterprise Development Officer on maintenance and replacement costs, so the asset renewal reserves are set at the right level.

**7. Monitoring, reporting and documentation:**

• Submit weekly site progress reports with photos and monthly engineering reports.

• Track the indicators the MEAL Officer needs on infrastructure functionality: pump hours, breakdowns, repair times and asset condition.

• Take part in quarterly joint monitoring visits and the annual asset verification. Prepare the engineering part of handover inventories.

**Cross-cutting duties:**

• Use designs that are climate-smart and low-cost to run, such as solar pumping and efficient water use, and suitable for community management.

• Apply do-no-harm and conflict sensitivity: consult landowners and communities before any works that affect site boundaries or access.

• Follow PSEA, safeguarding and security procedures. Make sure contractors and their workers sign and respect the Code of Conduct.

*Carry out any other reasonable duties related to the project, as assigned by the Project Manager*.

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

• **Essential:** a B.Eng. or B.Sc. in Agricultural Engineering, Agricultural and Bio-resources Engineering,

**• Desirable:** An M. Eng or M.Sc. in irrigation, water resources or agricultural mechanization. Membership of the Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE) or the Nigerian Institution of Agricultural Engineers. Training in solar pumping systems.

**Professional experience Essential:**

• At least 4 years of hands-on experience in agricultural engineering.

• Experience designing and supervising small-scale rural infrastructure works preparing BoQs, supervising contractors, certifying work and commissioning.

• Experience training community operators in operation and maintenance.

• Experience with NGOs, UN agencies or government agricultural programmes in North-East Nigeria or a similar setting.

**Desirable:**

• Experience with aquaculture infrastructure and with agro-processing equipment such as fish feed mills, pelletizers or extruders.

• Experience with solar-powered irrigation and greenhouse systems.

• Experience with handing assets over to communities, and with asset registers or maintenance management systems.

**Personal requirements**

• Strong technical design skills, including hydraulic calculations and solar pump sizing. Able to use AutoCAD or similar drawing software.

• Able to write clear technical specifications, BoQs and site reports.

• Practical problem-solving on site, with high standards for quality and safety.

• Able to explain technical concepts simply to community members and operators with low literacy.

• Integrity in procurement and contractor management.

• Commitment to safeguarding, PSEA, gender inclusion and humanitarian principles.

• Proficient in MS Office or Google Workspace.

**Languages**

• **Essential:** fluent English; good spoken Hausa.

jobs.title: Finance Manager, South Korea
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**

Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in some 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient.

The IRC global network has its headquarters in New York and London. IRC Europe is part of this network with offices in the UK, Germany, Sweden, Belgium and Switzerland. In addition, the IRC has a partnership with Stichting Vluchteling in the Netherlands.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

Read more about the IRC here: [https://www.rescue.or.kr](https://www.rescue.or.kr/)

**EXTERNAL RELATIONS AND THE PRIVATE FUNDRAISING FUNCTION**

The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions, including Private fundraising, in which this role falls under. To enable IRC to deliver its organizational commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance its ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally.

Within Private Fundraising sits the Mass Markets unit. This unit is currently made up of seven teams – US, UK, Germany, Sweden, Korea, Digital & Remote Markets and our Supporter Journey and Acquisition teams. Mass Market’s primary goal is to increase the number of sustainers we have globally, via targeted and cost effective acquisition and by building meaningful connections with our donors to ensure we can retain them. By increasing our sustainer numbers and capitalizing on cash giving moments we aim to grow unrestricted revenue for IRC and the people we serve.

**STRUCTURE AND PURPOSE OF THE ROLE**

In the role of Finance Manager, you will be the strategic finance leader for IRC Korea, responsible for driving financial results, transparency, and system modernization – most immediately through leading the rollout and localization of Integra, IRC’s global finance system, for the Korea office. You will manage and mentor the Finance team and serve as the primary liaison for other functional areas supporting the Korea office, contributing to strategic direction and operational problem-solving through your area of professional expertise.

**KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Working within a Finance matrix structure, you will be responsible for and oversee:

 **1. Controllership:**

- Ensure compliance of donor funds in Korea with local and relevant international regulations, including tax, accounting standards, and reporting requirements.
- Manage the financial records of IRC Korea and responsible for timely monthly/annual closing, financial reporting.
- Managing Audit and financial compliance, acting as a key point of contact with external parties including auditors and tax authorities.
- Lead the deployment of IRC’s global ERP system “Integra” for IRC Korea, ensuring both IRC and local statutory requirements are met.
- Act as primary focal point for the Integra Delivery team during the deployment period.
- Preparation of annual statutory financial statements and other local financial regulatory reporting as required, in coordination with HQ Global Finance and external parties where required.
- Provide monthly payroll information to the outsourcing firm and review calculations before finalizing.
- Maintain an appropriate financial control environment, ensuring financial records are maintained and that weekly and monthly financial routines are completed.
- Ensure accurate data between Integra and fundraising system (Donus), maintaining monthly financial reconciliations.
- Ensure regular communications with the IRC Global Finance Accounting & Consolidation team, particularly during month end/year end.
- Ensure internal IRC financial reporting is carried out to time and quality.
- Prepare reports for the Executive Director on an agreed basis

 **2. Treasury & Risk Management:**

- Identify and manage financial risks, including currency exchange. Provide insights into the financial health of IRC Korea.
- Working with the treasury team, identify and recommend appropriate banking service providers and lead setting up banking relationships, if needed.

 **3. Financial Planning & Analysis**:

- Lead the annual budget and planning process for IRC Korea in cooperation with the Executive Director, including reporting and follow-up.
- Work in conjunction with the Executive Director and Global FP&A team to finalize annual budgets.
- Ensure appropriate financial planning, budgeting and monitoring for IRC Korea and in line with IRC requirements.

 **4. Functional Leadership**:

- Manage, train and mentor the Finance team members in using Integra and as the finance function grows.
- Foster a high-performance culture of learning and best practice to ensure the finance function’s goals are met.

**OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- To comply with the culture and policies governing IRC Korea.
- To represent IRC in a manner that ensures appropriate communication with our supporters and stakeholders.
- To develop and maintain a positive working relationship with other departments and teams in IRC Korea and IRC globally.
- To attend meetings, conferences, and training courses as directed.
- Abide by organizational policies and practices, and the Code of Conduct.
- Support diversity and equality of opportunity in the workplace

**WORKING RELATIONSHIPS:**

- You will report to the Executive Director of South Korea, in partnership with the Director of Finance, Europe.
- Regular liaison with the Global Finance Accounting & Consolidation team and Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) team in HQ.
- External Relations colleagues as needed.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

**Qualifications:**

**Essentials:**

- Multi-year background from qualified financial work (Min. 10 years of experience in Fiance with more than 3 years of managerial roles)
- Academic education (degree) business administration and accounting
- Strongly preferred experience with finance/ERP systems (e.g., Microsoft D365 Finance & Operations, or similar)
- Fluent Knowledge of English and Korean

**Preferrable:**
