- **Pricing: T**he agreed implementation pricing will remain fixed unless a change is approved through the formal written change-control process.
- **Expenses:** Only reasonable expenses approved in writing in advance will be reimbursable. Reimbursable expenses must be supported by appropriate documentation.
- **Intellectual Property:** Girl Effect will own all foreground intellectual property, deliverables, source code, configurations, designs and documentation created specifically under the engagement, subject to agreed treatment of pre-existing tools and third-party materials.
- **Source Code and Access:** The partner must maintain current source code and documentation in repositories approved by Girl Effect and provide Girl Effect with appropriate administrative access throughout the engagement.
- **Open-Source and Third-Party Components:** All open-source and third-party components must be disclosed, appropriately licensed, maintained and approved for use.
- **Confidentiality and Data Protection:** The partner must protect Girl Effect’s confidential information and personal data and comply with applicable data-protection requirements.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct:** Appointment is subject to satisfactory due diligence, reference, safeguarding, information-security and compliance checks. The successful bidder must comply with Girl Effect’s code of conduct, safeguarding and anti-fraud requirements.
- **Subcontracting:** No material part of the assignment may be subcontracted without Girl Effect’s prior written approval. The lead bidder remains responsible for all subcontracted work.
- **Warranties and Defects:** Bidders should propose a warranty period during which defects in accepted deliverables will be corrected at no additional cost.
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Bidders must disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest.
- **Tender Costs:** Girl Effect will not reimburse costs incurred in preparing or submitting a proposal or participating in clarification, pitch or negotiation stages.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may clarify, negotiate, amend, suspend or cancel the procurement; reject any or all proposals; award the full or partial scope; award in phases; or make no award.
- **No Commitment:** Publication of this RFP does not constitute a commitment to enter into a contract.
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes submissions from qualified organisations that meet the stated regulatory, technical and service requirements.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: MEAL Manager (National Position) -Re Advertised
jobs.body:
Near East Foundation (NEF)

**Title:** Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Manager (National Position)

**Reports to:** Country Director

**Location:** Damascus, Syria

**Travel:** Up to 25% within Syria

**The Near East Foundation (NEF)** is seeking candidates for a **MEAL**[**\[1\]**](https://reliefweb.int/#_msocom_1) **Manager** to be based in Damascus, Syria. NEF is a non-profit international development organization that has supported livelihoods recovery and community-based economic development in the Middle East, Africa, and Caucasus since 1915. NEF draws on local teams, experience, and partnerships in these regions to create community-led solutions to reduce poverty, create economic opportunity, and empower conflict and crisis-affected groups to improve their outlook and wellbeing. Working through a network of country offices and local partners, NEF has operations in ten countries: Armenia, Lebanon, Iraq, Mali, Morocco, Palestine, Sudan, South Sudan, and Syria. HQ offices are based between Syracuse, NY, Washington, DC, London, UK, and Brussels, Belgium. Our programs are organized around three pillars: Inclusive Economic Development, Climate-resilient Development, and Stabilization and Peacebuilding.

**Position Description**

The MEAL Manager is a member of the NEF Syria team, reporting to the Syria Director. The purpose of the MEAL Manager is to ensure all MEAL responsibilities are performed to the highest standards and according to donor and NEF guidelines. The post-holder also assumes communication and visibility responsibilities for the Syria operation.

**Responsibilities**

- **Proposal Development and MEAL Planning:**
    - Participate in the development of project proposals, including designing logframes, selecting and defining indicators, and developing MEAL plans.
    - Design and update the project logframes and MEAL plans in collaboration with relevant team members.
- **MEAL System Implementation and Oversight:**
    - Ensure an appropriate MEAL system is in place, functioning effectively, and periodically reviewed to adapt to changing program and operating contexts.
    - Manage and report on the implementation of project MEAL plans, including regular progress tracking and reporting to the Director.
    - Coordinate closely with program team counterparts and ensure data is available in a timely and easily digestible format (e.g. dashboard creation) to facilitate data-informed and robust adaptive management processes
- **Data Management and Analysis:**
    - Operationalize NEF MEAL procedures and tools, including data collection, storage, analysis, and reporting (using KOBO, and other relevant tools).
    - Ensure the quality and accuracy of data collected and stored, overseeing data cleaning and validation, and conducting statistical analysis using tools such as SPSS and Excel.
    - Ensure appropriate data protection, confidentiality, access, and secure storage practices are applied across MEAL systems and datasets.
    - Analyze performance against indicators and targets, flag significant deviations, and work with program teams to identify appropriate corrective or adaptive actions.
    - Conduct qualitative and quantitative data analysis to provide comprehensive insights into project performance.
    - Facilitate various types of assessments, including impact, outcome, and process evaluations, in coordination with the HQ MEAL team.
- **Data Quality Assurance:**
- Lead and oversee internal Data Quality Assessments (DQAs), with support from the Data Analyst and relevant program teams, to ensure the validity, reliability, completeness, and consistency of program data. This includes:
    1. Conducting ongoing analysis of MEAL databases or trackers to identify data quality strengths, gaps, and inconsistencies.
    2. Supporting the development, implementation, and supervision of procedures to improve data quality and reporting.
    3. Ensuring identified data quality issues are documented, addressed, and followed up with relevant program and MEAL staff.
    4. Collecting and verifying, where applicable, supportive documentation to ensure consistency and accuracy in data management.
- **Training and Capacity Building:**
    - Train, support, and supervise MEAL staff, volunteers, and field agents on data collection, surveys, and project monitoring.
    - Where relevant, conduct capacity-building training for partner organizations and team members, including institutional needs assessments and socio-economic assessments.
- **Accountability and Feedback Mechanisms:**
    - Ensure accountability and feedback mechanisms are applied consistently across all projects, locations, and partners, including appropriate recording, referral, response, follow-up, and closure of feedback and complaints, in line with ethical, confidentiality, and transparency standards.
- **Learning and Documentation:**
    - Facilitate periodic learning sessions, reflection workshops or post-action reviews with project teams to identify lessons learned and best practices.
    - Contribute to project learning and adaptive management by documenting and sharing findings, lessons learned, learning papers, case studies, and beneficiary profiles.
    - Develop and disseminate communication and visibility materials (e.g., project overviews, fact sheets).
- **Evaluation and Reporting:**
    - Facilitate mid-term, final, and other ad hoc evaluations in coordination with the HQ MEAL team and regional office.
    - Contribute to and lead on projects' narrative reporting requirements, ensuring quality, data accuracy, and analysis.
    - Review and finalize MEAL reports (e.g., semiannual, endline) and provide feedback on project strategies to enhance performance and sustainability.
- **Collaboration and Coordination:**
    - Participate in monthly country coordination calls organized by HQ-based Program Officers.
    - Collaborate with the broader Syria team to ensure alignment on data collection, and MEAL system implementation.
    - Coordinate with the HQ MEAL Team backstop on technical guidance, MEAL standards and tools, organizational data requirements, learning priorities, and regional or global MEAL initiatives.
    - Participate and contribute to donor meetings as required.
- **Field Monitoring and Support:**
    - Conduct and oversee regular field monitoring follow-up activities, including focus group discussions with NEF beneficiaries.
    - Support partner capacity assessments and build capacity where necessary.
- **Additional Duties:**
    - Prepare field visits for NEF and external visitors, including photographers, journalists, or media if relevant.
    - Perform other duties as required and requested by the direct line manager or technical supervisor.

**Position Criteria**

- Strategic thinking, including identification of MEAL system weaknesses and initiative to address problem(s);
- Excellent organizational skills, accuracy and attention to detail;
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and meet deadlines;
- Ability to operate both independently and collaboratively as required.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in social sciences, humanities, quantitative/qualitative research methods, or a related field;
- At least Seven years of relevant professional experience in data collection, preferably with a national or international NGO, or other civil society organization;
- Fluent in written and spoken Arabic and English;
- Proficient in MS Office applications, particularly Word and Excel;
- Experience using digital data collection applications (e.g., KoboCollect, Akvo) is an asset;
- Plays an effective role within a team, able to communicate, develop, and maintain effective working relationships within a dynamic team environment.

• سيتم تعيين واجبات السائق في عطلات نهاية الأسبوع والعطلات وبعد ساعات العمل العادية المطلوبة وفقًا لتقدير المشرف.

• سيتم الاتصال بالسائق قبل 24 ساعة على الأقل عندما تكون خدماته مطلوبة لتلبية احتياجات النقل في IRC

• سيوفر السائق مركبة (مركبات) في حالة صالحة للسير ، وسيقوم بانتظام بفحص المحرك ، والمكابح ، والتكييف ، والإطارات ، وما إلى ذلك ، ويقوم بإصلاحها أو استبدالها حسب الحاجة.

• تخضع المركبات لفحص دوري ، وتحتفظ لجنة الإنقاذ الدولية بالحق في رفض أي مركبة أو خدمة لا تفي بالمواصفات المتفق عليها.

• لن تكون IRC مسؤولة عن أي ضرر أو عمالة أو خدمة أو أجزاء.

• سيضمن السائق أن السيارة مجهزة بما يلي:

 . أحزمة الأمان تعمل بشكل صحيح

 . الأطار الأحتياطي

 . حقيبة إسعاف أولي

 . طفاية حريق

 . مجموعة الأدوات الأساسية

• يجب أن يعامل السائق ركاب IRC بطريقة محترمة، وأن يضمن توفير أقصى درجات الراحة الممكنة للركاب (على سبيل المثال ، استخدام السخانات ومكيف الهواء عند الاقتضاء) ، والالتزام بمدونة قواعد السلوك الخاصة بلعبة IRC والإرشادات العامة لاستخدام السيارة المقدمة من IRC.

• فقط موظفي IRC، و / أو الأشخاص الآخرين المصرح لهم من قبل IRC، يمكن حملهم في المركبات أثناء الخدمة.

• يجوز فقط نقل مواد / سلع IRC، أو العناصر الأخرى المصرح بها من قبل IRC في المركبة أثناء تشغيل السيارة المذكورة.

• لا يجوز حمل أسلحة أو مواد / بضائع غير قانونية في السيارة في أي وقت.

• يمنع منعا باتا نقل الممنوعات أو المواد الممنوعة. أي انتهاك لهذه اللائحة سيعطي IRC خيار إنهاء هذا العقد، دون سابق إنذار.

• في حالة تعطل السيارة (المركبة)، يجب على السائق اتخاذ جميع الترتيبات اللازمة للاستبدال الفوري للمركبة (المركبة) المذكورة أثناء إصلاح السيارة (المركبة) الأصلية.

• سيتحمل السائق وحده المسؤولية عن أي إصابات، أو وفاة، أو خسارة أو ضرر يلحق بأطراف ثالثة ناتج عن تشغيل المركبات قيد الاستئجار من قبل IRC.

• لن تتحمل IRC أي مسؤولية في حالة وقوع حوادث.

• يجب أن يلتزم السائق بإجراءات السلامة والأمان IRC كما هو موضح من قبل إدارة السلامة والأمن.

• الدفع لمقدم الخدمة سوف يعتمد على الحضور الفعلي / الرحلة بناءً على طلب IRC على أسس يومية.

• الدفع لمقدم الخدمة سوف يكون بالليرة السورية .

jobs.title: Country WASH & Infrastructure Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Overall purpose of the role**

Under the direct supervision of the Head of Programme, the Country WASH & Infrastructure Coordinator provides technical leadership, strategic guidance and quality assurance for DRC Sudan's WASH and WASH infrastructure portfolio, covering emergency, nexus and long-term WASH, water resources, sanitation and hygiene, climate resilience and preparedness, and WASH in institutions. The role also supports programme development and positioning, working with DRC technical and area teams, global advisors, and partners and authorities.

**Responsibilities**

The post holder acts as DRC Sudan's national technical advisor for WASH and WASH infrastructure, working closely with Area Managers and technical teams to ensure timely, high-quality implementation. Area Managers retain operational management and delivery; the Coordinator sets technical standards, provides oversight and quality assurance, and supports planning, proposals and technical documents (e.g. designs, BoQs, tools, SoPs). To achieve the overall and specific position's objectives, the job holder's tasks and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

***Technical Leadership, Strategy and Programme Quality***

- Provide technical leadership on WASH: develop and update the WASH strategy under the Sudan Country Strategy, and produce standards, guidance, tools and SoPs aligned with Sphere, national codes, Cluster guidance and DRC frameworks.
- Ensure coherent approaches across emergency, protracted-displacement and nexus/long-term WASH, moving from emergency response towards sustainable, climate-resilient services with sound O&M and local ownership.
- Integrate WASH with Protection, Shelter/Site Management, and Economic Recovery, including cholera response.
- Support field teams in needs identification and RNAs; conduct field visits (including Darfur) or remote follow-up where access is constrained, to quality-assure design, construction and implementation.

***Water, Sanitation, Hygiene and Community-Led Approaches***

- Water supply and resources: advise on hydrogeological and source assessments, groundwater and surface water options (e.g. boreholes, hafirs), solar systems, water quality and conflict-sensitive access, promoting IWRM.
- Sanitation: guide safe, inclusive sanitation across the service chain (household, communal, camp and institutional), including excreta management, market-based sanitation, solid waste and vector control.
- Hygiene and behaviour change: promote evidence-based hygiene promotion and social and behaviour change approaches, including menstrual health, adapted to context and informed by community feedback.
- Community-led WASH: promote community-led approaches (e.g. CLTS, WASH committees, community management of services, local service providers) for ownership, O&M and sustainability.
- WASH in schools and public institutions (incl. health facilities, IPC): standards, designs and sustainable management.

***Climate, Resilience, AA and Preparedness***

- Integrate climate risk, DRR, nature-based solutions and IWRM into WASH strategy and design, promoting climate-resilient infrastructure (e.g. solar, flood-proofing).
- Lead WASH preparedness and anticipatory action: contingency planning, early warning and trigger-based action for floods, drought and cholera, prepositioning of supplies and surge readiness, with the WASH Cluster and authorities.

***Infrastructure, Engineering Review and Procurement***

- Lead the technical review and clearance of WASH designs, drawings, BoQs, specifications and cost estimates (water, sanitation, schools and public institutions), ensuring feasibility, cost-effectiveness and compliance with standards.
- Guide tendering, contracting, supervision, quality control, handover and O&M, including rehabilitation of damaged systems.
- Support Area WASH Managers and Supply Chain in procurement and pipeline planning, including market-based approaches.

***Proposals, Monitoring, Reporting and Accountability***

- Lead technical WASH and infrastructure inputs to proposals, concept notes, budgets, donor reports and advocacy notes, and to business development including nexus opportunities; apply DRC's Operational Handbook.
- With MEAL teams, ensure projects are designed and monitored to DRC and sector standards and donor requirements (including water quality, infrastructure functionality and remote monitoring), and capture learning and good practice.
- Ensure accountability mechanisms and mainstreaming of protection, gender, disability and PSEA.

***Capacity Building, Partners and Technical HR***

- Design and deliver capacity building for DRC and partner staff (e.g. Sphere, cholera and flood response, water quality, O&M, behaviour change, infrastructure design), strengthening local partners and localisation.
- Advise on technical recruitment and competency frameworks; promote the code of conduct.

***Representation and Coordination***

- Represent DRC in national and sub-national WASH Cluster and coordination forums, feeding 5Ws and insights to teams.
- Build relationships with authorities, donors, UN agencies and partners to maintain trust in DRC's technical standards; with Area WASH Managers, maintain mapping of WASH actors and identify potential partners.

**Qualifications, Experience and Technical Competencies**

- Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering (or Water/Environmental Engineering) required; Master's degree in WASH, water resources management, hydrogeology or a related field desirable.
- Minimum 5 years relevant WASH experience, including at least 3 in a technical advisory or coordination role.
- Proven experience in complex emergency and protracted-displacement contexts (Sudan/Darfur or comparable).
- Solid engineering background: technical design and review of BoQs, specifications and drawings for water supply (groundwater, solar pumping), sanitation and WASH in schools and public institutions.
- Strong knowledge of sanitation, hygiene and behaviour change, community-led approaches (e.g. CLTS), cholera response, water resources management, and climate-resilient WASH and anticipatory action.
- Experience in standards and tool development, proposals, donor reporting and WASH Cluster coordination.
- Proven ability to live and work in an unstable, insecure environment.

**Languages:**

- Proficiency in written and spoken English.
- Fluency in Arabic is desirable

**About you**

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:*

- *Striving for excellence:* You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- *Collaborating:* You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- *Taking the lead:* You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- *Communicating:* You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- *Demonstrating integrity*: Upholding and promoting the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Conditions**

*Contract:* One-year contract with possibility of extension, subject to funding and performance. Salary and conditions in accordance with the Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for International staff. This position is graded at Band NM.F

*Start Date:* December 2026

*Duty Station:* Khartoum, Sudan (with regular field travel)

Reports to: Head of Programme

jobs.title: Environment and Social Safeguards Officer
jobs.body:
**About CRS**

Catholic Relief Services (CRS) is the official international humanitarian agency of the Catholic community in the United States. CRS works in around 100 countries to *save, protect, and transform* lives, serving people in need regardless of race, religion, or nationality. Through trusted local partnerships, CRS delivers relief and development programs in emergency response, disaster risk reduction, health, agriculture, education, community savings, livelihoods, and peacebuilding.

CRS began working in the Philippines in 1945, making it the longest-running continuous CRS country program in the world. Today, CRS Philippines implements programs in emergency response and recovery, disaster risk reduction, climate resilience, livelihoods, and peace and development. With more than 70 staff across Manila, Cotabato City, Tagbilaran City, Iloilo City, Virac, and Malaybalay City, CRS works closely with church and civil society partners, government agencies, and other organizations to serve vulnerable communities across the country.

The **Innovative Climate Financing - Philippines Carbon Finance Pilot** is an 18-month initiative (April 2026 – September 2027) which seeks to assess and advance the readiness of indigenous peoples’ ancestral domains in Bukidnon and Davao del Norte for participation in high-integrity forest carbon markets while delivering biodiversity, livelihood, and governance co-benefits. It likewise aims to support overall investments readiness by ensuring robust technical requirements are complied with, particularly on establishing the baseline and baseline, and calculation of project removals in line with the industry’s standards. CRS works with the Philippine Eagle Foundation (PEF) as the local implementing partner, the IP organizations, government agencies, and local stakeholders, to support IP governance strengthening, forest restoration, agroforestry and livelihoods skills strengthening, FPIC processes, biodiversity assessments, land and carbon suitability assessments, safeguarding, and the development of investment-ready carbon project opportunities.

On the other hand, the Restoration through Science-based Execution and Established Biodiverse Registry Philippines (RESEEDPH) project is a five year initiative designed to restore degraded forest and agro biodiverse landscapes by combining science-based planning, community participation, and strengthened policy support. Operating in Catanduanes, Bohol, and North Cotabato, the project focuses on climate-adapted species selection, improved seed and nursery systems, and the development of evidence-based restoration models that enhance both ecological health and community livelihoods.

**Job Summary**

The Environmental and Social Safeguards (ESS) Officer supports the implementation, monitoring, documentation, and continuous improvement of the Environmental and Social Safeguards system of the Philippines Carbon Finance Pilot and the RESEED project. The position assists in ensuring compliance with applicable donor and/or investment requirements, CRS policies, national regulations, environmental and social safeguards frameworks, and relevant carbon finance investment standards. Working closely with the Senior ESS Officer and Senior Project Officer for Social Standards, the incumbent will help ensure that environmental and social risks are identified, managed, monitored, and documented throughout project implementation.

## Responsibilities

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

**1. Environmental and Social Safeguards Implementation**

- Support implementation of the project's Environmental and Social Safeguards Frameworks, management plans, protocols, and procedures.
- Assist in environmental and social screening of project activities and interventions.
- Support monitoring of environmental and social risks associated with project implementation.
- Ensure safeguard requirements are integrated into workplans, field activities, and partner implementation processes.
- Monitor compliance with approved safeguard mitigation measures and management plans.

**2. Risk Monitoring, Compliance, and Verification**

- Conduct routine field monitoring and verification visits to assess safeguard compliance.
- Assist in identifying environmental and social risks, issues, and emerging concerns
- Support preparation and updating of risk registers, safeguard trackers, and compliance monitoring tools.
- Follow up implementation of agreed corrective and preventive actions.
- Escalate significant risks and non-compliance issues to the Senior ESS Officer.

**3. Environmental Monitoring and Documentation**

- Support monitoring of environmental safeguards related to reforestation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, forest protection, and natural resource management activities.
- Assist in documenting environmental impacts, mitigation measures, field observations, and compliance status.
- Maintain safeguard documentation, monitoring records, and evidence files.
- Coordinate with GIS and technical teams to support environmental monitoring and reporting.

**4. Accountability and Grievance Monitoring**

- Receive, document, track, and monitor safeguard-related concerns, complaints, and grievances.
- Maintain confidential records and databases related to grievances and safeguard issues.
- Support timely referral and resolution of cases in accordance with approved protocols.
- Generate regular summaries and analyses of safeguard-related grievances and trends.

**5. Stakeholder Engagement Support**

- Support community consultations, safeguard orientations, disclosure activities, and engagement processes.
- Document stakeholder consultations, meetings, and safeguard discussions.
- Assist in ensuring project participants understand safeguard commitments, grievance channels, and project responsibilities.
- Coordinate closely with the Senior Project Officer for Social Standards on FPIC, Indigenous Peoples engagement, and social safeguard activities.

**6. Reporting and Knowledge Management**

- Prepare regular safeguard monitoring reports, compliance updates, and field visit reports.
- Support consolidation of environmental and social safeguard data for donor and management reporting.
- Maintain safeguard records, databases, and document repositories.

**7. Partner Capacity Strengthening**

- Support training and coaching of project staff, partners, and community stakeholders on safeguard requirements.
- Assist in delivering orientations on environmental and social safeguards, grievance mechanisms, and risk management procedures.
- Monitor partner compliance and provide technical support as needed.

## Qualifications

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Forestry, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Planning, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Community Development, or a related field.
- Minimum of 3 years of relevant professional experience in environmental safeguards, social safeguards, environmental compliance, risk management, conservation, natural resource management, or related development programs.
- Experience formulating ESS Plan and supporting implementation for donor-funded projects is preferred.
- Experience conducting field monitoring, compliance verification, and stakeholder consultations is highly desirable.
- Experience working with indigenous people's communities and local partners is an advantage.
- Experience working in Mindanao, particularly Bukidnon and Davao del Norte, is highly desirable.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to field sites and remote communities.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Familiarity with environmental and social safeguard principles and risk management approaches.
- Understanding of environmental compliance requirements and mitigation planning.
- Knowledge of grievance management and accountability mechanisms.
- Strong organizational and documentation skills.
- Ability to collect, organize, and analyze field monitoring information.
- Strong report-writing and communication skills.
- Ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders and communities.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and digital monitoring tools.
- High attention to detail and commitment to accountability and compliance.

**Required Languages**:

- Excellent spoken and written English.
- Working knowledge of Bisaya is highly desirable.

**Travel**: Must be willing to travel up to 50% of the time to Malaybalay, Bukidnon and/or Talaingod, Davao del Norte.

**Key Working Relationships:** TBD

**Agency-wide Competencies (for all CRS Staff)**

These are rooted in the mission, values, and guiding principles of CRS and used by each staff member to fulfill his or her responsibilities and achieve the desired results.

- **Integrity**
- **Continuous Improvement & Innovation**
- **Builds Relationships**
- **Develops Talent**
- **Strategic Mindset**
- **Accountability & Stewardship**

The **Innovative Climate Financing - Philippines Carbon Finance Pilot** is an 18-month initiative (April 2026 – September 2027) which seeks to assess and advance the readiness of indigenous peoples’ ancestral domains in Bukidnon and Davao del Norte for participation in high-integrity forest carbon markets while delivering biodiversity, livelihood, and governance co-benefits. **Job Summary**

The Senior MEAL Officer is responsible for ensuring the availability of quality data and evidence to support adaptive management, donor reporting, strategic decision-making, partner accountability, and learning. S/he will lead the development and operationalization of the project's results framework, indicators, monitoring plans, databases, reporting systems, accountability mechanisms, and learning agenda. S/he will work closely with Philippine Eagle Foundation (PEF) MEAL officer to strengthen evidence generation, knowledge management, and organizational learning throughout the project lifecycle.

## Responsibilities

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

**1. MEAL System Design and Management**

- Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the project's MEAL framework, systems, processes, and tools.
- Develop and maintain indicator reference sheets, monitoring plans, data flow procedures, databases, dashboards, and reporting templates.
- Ensure alignment of MEAL systems with CRS program quality standards, policies and procedures, and relevant carbon finance project requirements.
- Establish systems for data management, quality assurance, storage, confidentiality, and accessibility.
- Support the development and refinement of project results frameworks, logframes, and performance indicators.

**2. Monitoring, Data Collection, and Verification**

- Coordinate routine project monitoring activities, field verification, assessments, surveys, and data validation exercises.
- Develop quantitative and qualitative data collection tools and methodologies.
- Oversee data collection, entry, cleaning, analysis, and reporting to ensure accuracy, completeness, and timeliness.
- Monitor implementation progress against workplans, targets, milestones, and performance indicators.
- Identify implementation gaps, emerging risks, and challenges and provide recommendations for corrective action.

**3. Evaluation, Research, and Learning**

- Lead or support baseline studies, endline surveys, evaluations, and learning studies.
- Analyze quantitative and qualitative data to generate actionable insights for program improvement and decision-making.
- Facilitate quarterly reflection sessions, after-action reviews, and learning events.
- Coordinate documentation of lessons learned, best practices, innovations, and project achievements.
- Produce learning briefs, case studies, success stories, presentations, and knowledge products.

**4. Accountability and Community Feedback Mechanisms**

- Lead the implementation and strengthening of Feedback and Complaints Response Mechanisms (FCRM) across pilot sites.
- Ensure accessible, inclusive, and culturally appropriate feedback channels for all stakeholders, including indigenous people's communities.
- Monitor feedback trends, complaints resolution, response timelines, and documentation.
- Generate analyses and recommendations from stakeholder feedback to improve project implementation and accountability.

**5. Reporting and Data Utilization**

- Develop regular monitoring reports, dashboards, and analytical summaries for management, partners, and donors.
- Support preparation of quarterly, annual, and other reports through provision of quality data and analysis.
- Promote evidence-based decision-making and adaptive management across project implementation teams.

**6. Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support**

- Design and facilitate training, coaching, and mentoring activities on MEAL concepts, tools, methodologies, and data use.
- Provide technical guidance to project staff and partners on indicator measurement, reporting requirements, and learning processes.
- Support partners in reflecting on project experiences and using evidence to improve implementation effectiveness.

## Qualifications

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Economics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Environmental Science, Forestry, Agriculture, Public Administration, Data Science, or a related field.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in MEAL.
- Experience designing and managing MEAL systems for donor-funded development, environmental, natural resource management, climate, or conservation projects.
- Demonstrated experience in quantitative and qualitative data collection, analysis, and reporting.
- Experience managing accountability and feedback mechanisms.
- Experience facilitating learning, reflection, and adaptive management processes.
- Experience working with local partners, indigenous peoples, and community-based organizations is highly desirable.
- Experience working in Mindanao, particularly Bukidnon and Davao del Norte, is highly desirable.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to field sites and remote communities.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Strong understanding of results-based management and theory of change approaches.
- Proficiency in data analysis software and digital data collection platforms (e.g., Excel, Power BI, KoboToolbox, or similar).
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.
- Excellent report writing, presentation, and communication skills.
- Ability to transform complex data into practical recommendations.
- Strong facilitation and capacity-strengthening skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and commitment to data quality and accountability.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams).
- Ability to use online collaboration, project management, and data management platforms.

**Required Languages**:

- Excellent spoken and written English.

With more than 70 staff across Manila, Cotabato City, Tagbilaran City, Iloilo City, Virac, and Malaybalay City, CRS works closely with church and civil society partners, government agencies, and other organizations to serve vulnerable communities across the country.

The **Innovative Climate Financing - Philippines Carbon Finance Pilot** is an 18-month initiative (April 2026 – September 2027) which seeks to assess and advance the readiness of indigenous peoples’ ancestral domains in Bukidnon and Davao del Norte for participation in high-integrity forest carbon markets while delivering biodiversity, livelihood, and governance co-benefits. It likewise aims to support overall investments readiness by ensuring robust technical requirements are complied with, particularly on establishing the baseline and baseline, and calculation of project removals in line with the industry’s standards. CRS works with the Philippine Eagle Foundation (PEF) as the local implementing partner, the IP organizations, government agencies, and local stakeholders, to support IP governance strengthening, forest restoration, agroforestry and livelihoods skills strengthening, FPIC processes, biodiversity assessments, land and carbon suitability assessments, safeguarding, and the development of investment-ready carbon project opportunities.

Given the highly spatial nature of carbon project development, a **GIS Specialist** is essential to support the collection, management, analysis, and visualization of geospatial data.

**Job Summary**

The GIS Specialist provides critical technical support in assessing land eligibility and suitability, analyzing land-use and land-cover (LU/LC) and land cover changes (LCC), ex ante LC/LU classification, stratification and mapping, feeding the result to the calculation of carbon yield, , mapping biodiversity and environmental, and producing spatial outputs needed for prefeasibility, feasibility analysis, and project design.

## Responsibilities

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

**1. Spatial Analysis, Mapping, and Geodatabase Management**

- Lead the collection of map inputs, GIS processing of geospatial data for the Carbon Finance Pilot.
- Develop and maintain project geodatabases and metadata systems, and GIS mapping documentation.
- Produce high-quality maps, dashboards, spatial reports, and decision-support products for project planning, reporting, and stakeholder engagement.
- Analyze and interpret satellite imagery, drone imagery, and other remote sensing products relevant to project objectives.
- Support delineation and validation of project boundaries, intervention areas, ancestral domain boundaries, restoration areas, and monitoring sites.

**2. Carbon Readiness, Forestry, and Biodiversity Assessments**

- Conduct land-use and land-cover (LULC) analysis, landscape characterization, and spatial suitability assessments.
- Conduct land-cover classification and accuracy assessment using industry-standard approaches including confusion matrix analysis, producer's accuracy, user's accuracy, overall accuracy, and other classification validation methods.
- Develop historical land-use and land-cover assessments to support ARR land eligibility determination, baseline establishment, and carbon project development requirements.
- Support ex-ante carbon assessments through biomass estimation, carbon stratification, growth potential analysis, and estimation of potential carbon sequestration under restoration and agroforestry scenarios.
- Support development of carbon baselines through spatial analysis of historical land-use trends, degradation patterns, and landscape dynamics.
- .
- Conduct land eligibility and suitability screening using biophysical, environmental, tenure, accessibility, and risk-related criteria consistent with international carbon standards and best practices.
- .
- Support other mapping needs related to vegetation, forest condition, biodiversity, hydrology, land tenure, infrastructure, and threats.
- Participate in field validation and ground-truthing activities to verify analytical results and improve spatial accuracy.

**3. GIS-Based Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification**

- Provide mapping support to the identification/enrollment of eligible areas for the development of agroforestry carbon project.
- Support the development of Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) systems through spatial data management and analysis.
- Develop spatial indicators and monitoring tools aligned with the project's MEAL framework.
- Generate regular spatial progress reports, maps, and analytical products to support project management and adaptive decision-making.
- Develop guidelines on the application of the GIS mapping support to MRV, particularly on tracking land cover changes attributable to the project.

**4. Partner Capacity Strengthening and Technical Assistance**

- Coordinate with GKIM and other CRS technical units as needed regarding GIS standards, data management, and spatial analysis approaches.
- Provide GIS and spatial analysis technical assistance to CRS staff, PEF, IP Organizations, and other project stakeholders.
- Support partners in interpreting maps, spatial outputs, and technical analyses for planning and decision-making.
- Strengthen partner capacities in data collection, field validation, and GIS-based monitoring methodologies.

**5. Knowledge Management and Reporting**

- Coordinate GIS-related activities with CRS teams, PEF, consultants, and other stakeholders.
- Contribute technical inputs to workplans, reports, presentations, concept notes, learning products, and donor deliverables.
- Maintain organized archives of maps, spatial datasets, analyses, and technical references.
- Support project documentation, knowledge management, learning, and dissemination of good practices.
- Provide regular updates to the Senior Program Manager regarding progress, risks, data gaps, and technical recommendations.

## Qualifications

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in Forestry, Environmental Science, Geomatics, Natural Resource Management, , or related field; Registered Forester is an advantage.
- Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in GIS, remote sensing, land cover change analysis, and general spatial analysis as applied to forestry, natural resource management, or environmental conservation.
- Demonstrated experience in developing and managing geospatial databases and conducting spatial analysis.
- Experience working with forest landscapes, biodiversity conservation, restoration, climate resilience, or carbon-related projects.
- Experience working with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, LGUs, government agencies, and development organizations.
- Preferable experience working in Mindanao, particularly Bukidnon and Davao del Norte.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to field sites and remote communities.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

**GIS and Technical Skills**

- Proficiency in GIS and spatial analysis software such as ArcGIS, QGIS, Google Earth Pro, Google Earth Engine, and related applications.
- Ability to manage, analyze, validate, and interpret spatial and environmental datasets.
- Ability to prepare maps, technical reports, presentations, and visual products to support planning and decision-making.
- Experience conducting field validation and integrating field data with spatial analysis outputs.

**Technical Knowledge**

- Strong knowledge of forestry, forest landscape restoration, agroforestry systems, biodiversity conservation, watershed management, and natural resource management.
- Familiarity with climate action projects, carbon finance, and nature-based solutions is desirable.
- Understanding of stakeholder engagement processes involving IP communities, government agencies, and local communities.
- Knowledge of project management principles, monitoring processes, and development programming approaches.

**Organizational and Management Skills**

- Strong organizational, coordination, and follow-up skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines with minimal supervision.
- Strong analytical thinking and decision-making abilities.
- Ability to work independently while maintaining effective collaboration within a multidisciplinary team.
- Results-oriented, proactive, and highly responsive to project and partner needs.

**Computer Skills**

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams).
- Ability to use online collaboration, project management, and data management platforms.

**Required Languages**: Excellent spoken and written English.

**Travel**: Must be willing to travel up to 50% of the time to Malaybalay, Bukidnon and/or Talaingod, Davao del Norte.

jobs.title: Resilient Shelter Coordinator (Technical Advisor I)
jobs.body:
**About CRS**

Catholic Relief Services is the official international humanitarian agency of the Catholic community in the United States. CRS works to save, protect, and transform lives in need in more than 100 countries, without regard to race, religion or nationality. CRS’ relief and development work is accomplished through programs of emergency response, HIV, health, agriculture, education, microfinance and peacebuilding.

CRS in the Philippines, though a pilot project, will support the government’s efforts to make communities safer and more climate resilient by promoting the use of digital tools for smarter land use and urban planning. Working closely with DHSUD, the pilot will help local governments become more familiar with modern, risk informed planning approaches, gather lessons from early adopters, and encourage wider use of innovative planning technologies across the country. It will also help strengthen partnerships and explore long term funding opportunities to ensure that these digital solutions can continue to grow and benefit more communities nationwide. CRS will also coordinate with MHSD in BARMM, building on the existing CRS–MHSD partnership to scale resilient shelter solutions across the region.

**Job Summary**

You will provide technical advice, coordinate with government partners and support to a range of program design and implementation issues in Urban Development in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices to Country Program (CP) teams to advance the delivery of high-quality programming to the poor and vulnerable. Your advice, knowledge, and support will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive and innovative CRS’ Urban Resilience programming such as land use and shelter planning is across the globe. You will lead the implementation of the resilient shelter pilot implemented by CRS Philippines.

## Responsibilities

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

• Support the development and contribute to the implementation of agency-wide strategies, standards, tools and best practices in Urban Development and Resilience, Resilient land use and shelter planning processes, that effectively engage partners, donors, and governments. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, protection mainstreaming, and disaster risk reduction.  
• Provide technical solutions to CP teams and government partners, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and the application of standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools, and M&E, helping to ensure high-quality implementation. Apply experience in comprehensive land use planning (CLUP), Local Climate Change Action Plans (LCCAP), and the integration of Climate and Disaster Risk Assessment (CDRA) into local government unit (LGU) planning.  
• Contribute to, and in some cases lead, the development of the technical design for proposals. Support the process of preparation, design, submission and approval of project concepts and full-fledged proposals. As needed, act as a technical writer on proposal development teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities and technical requirements into CRS’ approach.  
• Support capacity strengthening initiatives in Urban Development and Resilience programming for staff and partners through helping develop learning and training strategies and agendas/curriculums, conduct trainings and workshops, and coaching.  
• Collect and analyze program data, capture and share lessons learned and best practices for specific projects to facilitate improvements in decision-making and contribute to the Urban Resilience, Shelter and Settlements Planning learning agenda.  
• Contribute to maintaining relationships with donors, peer organizations, research and other institutions, participate in forums in Urban Development and Resilience to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work.  
• Lead the development, co-development of climate resilient proposals defined in the project.

## Qualifications

**Basic Qualifications**

- Master’s degree in urban development, or Environmental Management, Nature-based Solutions, or similar fields related to Climate Resilience. required. A registered architect and/or environmental planner is a plus.
- Minimum of three years’ relevant work experience with progressive responsibilities, ideally with an international NGO, with minimum of three years’ relevant field-based experience in Climate Resilience and urban development.
- Knowledge of technical principles and concepts in Urban Development and Resilience. General knowledge of other related disciplines such as climate change adaptation and mitigation, to ensure proper cross-sectoral approach.
- Experience in project design and proposal development. Experience in writing content for proposals.
- Knowledge of capacity strengthens best practices.
- Experience with program monitoring and evaluation and analysis.
- Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, peer organizations, and faith-based and civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information and budget management systems, knowledge-sharing networks.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Strong relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings
- Good strategic, analytical, problem-solving and systems thinking skills with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment
- Good technical writing skills
- Presentation, facilitation, training, mentoring, and coaching skills
- Proactive, resourceful and results-oriented

**Required languages** – English proficiency in speaking and writing.

**Travel** – Must be willing and able to travel up to 30%.

**Supervisory Responsibilities** – None.

**Internal:** Head of Programs, programming teams – emergency response, climate resilience  
**External:** DHSUD, MHSD, DENR, CCC, LGUs and NGOS supporting the project

jobs.title: Rwanda District Senior Supervisor (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

## About the Role

Seeking a strong field leader to drive Forest and Landscape Restoration and seedling production, lead field teams, achieve ambitious targets, and work closely with farmers and local governments to deliver impact.

## Responsibilities

Forestry & Seedling Production Operations

- Drive the execution of the Forest and Landscape Restoration (FLR) Program and oversee high-quality seedling production across assigned district sites.

Field Team Leadership & Capacity Building

- Direct and supervise Sector Supervisors, Site Supervisors, and Senior Field Officers, conducting regular training to build staff capacity and manage turnover.

Target Tracking & Operational Problem-Solving

- Monitor district performance metrics against key seasonal milestones, proactively identifying and resolving field operational or weather-related production challenges.

Stakeholder Management & Government Engagement

- Maintain strong collaborative relationships with local government officials, community leaders, and regional coordinators to support seamless program delivery.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor's Degree in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, or a closely related field.
- 2 years of practical field experience in forestry, agroforestry, or agricultural project implementation.
- Demonstrated leadership experience in managing field teams, including Sector Supervisors and Field Officers.
- Experience in data analysis and tracking operational performance against field targets.
- Proven problem-solving ability to address seedling production challenges and seasonal field constraints.
- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills to engage local government authorities and smallholder farmers.
- Fluency in Kinyarwanda and English is required.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Bugesera, Rwanda or Rwamagana, Rwanda or Rwanda, Karongi

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Contract Duration

2 years

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

## Application Deadline

20 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Switzerland Philanthropy Lead (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

One Acre Fund seeks an entrepreneurial executive with a high level of autonomy, to spearhead our strategic expansion in Switzerland.

As Switzerland Philanthropy Lead , you will have the unique opportunity to build our profile, network, and fundraising capacity from the ground up while being supported by an established, high-performing global team. Working closely with our writing, finance, and program teams, your objective will be to secure new donor relationships and grow our fundraising portfolio in Switzerland.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong, relevant network in Switzerland and a proven personal track record of originating new relationships and securing substantial funding or comparable commitments. You will enjoy building trusted relationships with donors and advisers, engaging senior decision-makers, and turning new opportunities into lasting partnerships. Working with One Acre Fund’s leadership, you will shape our Swiss fundraising strategy and build towards consistent annual 7–8 figure fundraising results after a realistic ramp-up period. You will agree annual targets and milestones with your manager that reflect the time needed to develop a qualified pipeline, establish new donor relationships, and secure funding, with performance assessed against those goals.

Our social enterprise model, business mindset, and the autonomy to build a significant portfolio are central to this opportunity. We welcome relevant backgrounds in philanthropy, foundations, or wealth advisory, family offices, impact investing, and related fields, with evidence of personally originating new funding opportunities.

If successful, you will help raise the funds to catalyze the next phase of One Acre Fund’s growth, supporting our ambitious 2030 vision to deliver $1B in impact to 10 million smallholder farmers and their families, including 55 million individuals. This role offers a powerful opportunity for personal impact on pressing global challenges. Your skillset and energy will measurably help and sustainably improve the lives of the world's largest population living in extreme poverty.

## **Responsibilities**

- Fundraising. You will work independently to build a pipeline of donors and high-net-worth individual prospects, converting new leads into high-value relationships for One Acre Fund. Within 6-12 months, you will be expected to independently bring in new relationships incremental to One Acre Fund’s existing network of donors. This early relationship-building expectation is distinct from the longer-term annual revenue ambition.
- Stewardship. You will steward the high-value relationships you secure, with the goal of driving renewals and, where appropriate, increasing giving over time. This may involve activities such as coordinating with program teams to ensure grant milestones are met, preparing formal progress updates for donors (with support from the writing team), and supporting donor visits to our program areas.
- Market Strategy. You will maintain a laser focus on Switzerland across all sectors and donor types, with particular emphasis on private foundations, high-net-worth individuals, family offices, and their advisers. Regional, language, and cantonal credibility and a visible local presence will support your work.
- Spokesperson for farmers. One Acre Fund contributes to global discussions involving smallholders, including for example resilience building and the agricultural financing gap. You will be a spokesperson for our organization and for farmers, presenting at high-value events and conferences across Europe.
- Entity setup, operationalization and team leadership. Support the exploration and potential setup of a new One Acre Fund legal entity in Switzerland. If approved, help establish and operationalize it by managing key steps such as registration, board formation, and development of governance structure. As the Swiss portfolio grows, you may also build and lead a team, subject to organisational needs and approval.

Overall, we are prioritising an individual with a strong origination mindset and the skills and experience to identify, develop, and secure new funding opportunities, complemented by the ability to steward these relationships over time.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Senior experience, visionary leadership, and market building. 10+ years of relevant experience in fundraising or related origination roles, with steadily increasing scope and complexity, and a clear track record of building fundraising operations or developing new markets.
- Personal fundraising results. Consistent fundraising results in the 7–8 figure range annually over the past five years, with clear evidence of your personal contribution to new funding. For candidates from advisory, wealth, family-office, or investment backgrounds, we will consider comparable origination results and evidence of the ability to translate these into fundraising.
- Independent portfolio growth. Experience independently managing the full fundraising cycle, from prospecting to stewardship, with support from writing and finance teams. Comfort working toward annual fundraising targets, with performance assessed against those goals.
- An incremental network. Strong networks within the philanthropic community in Switzerland, including relevant private foundations, high-net-worth individuals, family offices, or advisers. You can demonstrate access to new opportunities beyond One Acre Fund’s existing relationships and credibility in the regions and communities you serve.

The role also requires:

- Willingness to travel up to 40-60 nights per year. Travel dates are flexible.
- Language proficiency: English required; German and/or French required depending on market base.

The following are strong advantages:

- Experience in the international development sector
- Experience working in Africa
- Experience working in agriculture
- Experience working with a social enterprise model
- Experience working for philanthropic organisations
- Strong networks within other markets (e.g., wider DACH region, the U.K. or Scandinavia).

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Switzerland

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Contract Duration**

1 year and 5 months

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Switzerland.

## **Application Deadline**

17 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Officer, Events and Entertainment Relations Engagement
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**  
Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**IRC UK**  
IRC UK is part of the IRC global network, which has its global headquarters in New York. Our team in the UK works to raise profile, deliver policy and practice change, and increase funding to help restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Since 2021, IRC UK has also provided integration services directly to refugees in England.  
In Europe, the IRC also has offices in Berlin, Bonn, Brussels, Geneva and Stockholm.

**The Purpose of the Role**

As part of the Experiential Marketing Team—working across the Marketing & Mobilization (M&M) Team and the UK Communications Team—this role is primarily responsible for elevating the IRC’s profile, brand, and influence, while supporting fundraising efforts. This will be achieved through event support, strategic engagement of celebrity ambassadors and digital tactics. In alignment with our Strategy100 commitments and the UK strategic plan, the position will deliver event production and talent-focused strategies that enhance the impact of IRC campaigns, initiatives, and appeals.

**Scope and Authority**

- Oversee the UK and European market events portfolio with flexibility to support other priority markets on a case-by-case basis as directed by leadership
- Lead and oversee various aspects of event project management (in-person and virtual), including team coordination, logistics, production, and execution from planning through post-event wrap-up. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

\- Drafting concept notes

\- Creating creative briefs

\- Conducting venue/vendor searches or setting up virtual platforms

\- Collaborating with various teams to align on event messaging and donor engagement strategies

\- Preparing and distributing event materials, communications, and other professional documents

\- Evaluating event effectiveness and analyzing audience data

- Assist on management of a global entertainment relations portfolio  
    \- Help identify and create opportunities to leverage existing talent in support of events and digital campaigns that advance the IRC’s fundraising, brand and advocacy goals (listed in order of priority)  
    \- Support Director with IRC’s celebrity supporters by managing ongoing communications to keep them informed, engaged, and aligned with IRC’s mission.
- Support in proactively identifying current events and cultural trends to leverage events and celebrity partners to meaningfully engage in support of IRC initiatives and events.
- Be available for occasional travel and work outside of standard hours, including evenings or weekends, to attend meetings or events.

**Key Working Relationships**

Ability to work effectively and creatively with a diverse array of external and internal collaborators in a way that represents the best of the IRC. These include IRC Fundraising, Policy & Advocacy, Digital and Media teams, as well as Celebrity representatives and contacts.

Strong social skills and project management skills, with emphasis on creating tangible outcomes. Ability to thrive in an fast-paced environment, to be flexible, to work across various internal teams and manage high-profile stakeholders.

Eager to learn about the entertainment industry and build meaningful relationships to help continue growing talent relations.

**Person Specification**

**Experience**

- Strong experience in event planning with the ability to organize events through all phases of development.
- Knowledge and experience of using social media channels as part of celebrity engagement and PR campaigns.
- Demonstrable experience of working strategically, identifying opportunities to support organisation-wide marketing strategies.

**Skills**

- Proven ability to project manage campaigns and events; working with a variety of internal and external stakeholders.
- Outstanding written and oral communication skills, and the ability to interact with a diverse range of people. In this post this would include senior leadership, celebrities, agents and journalists.
- Excellent relationship management skills.
- Exceptional judgement, analytical and prioritizing skills and experience of applying these in a fast-moving environment.
- Proven ability to take responsibility for tasks and act on own initiative particularly to solve problems and find solutions.
- Outstanding MS office and Event database management skills (Salesforce and Pardot, aka Salesforce Marketing Cloud Account Engagement, experience preferred).

Candidates must have the right to work in the UK.

**Compensation:** (GBP46,780 - GBP57922.78 GBP/Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

IRC UK strives to be an equal opportunities employer. IRC UK is committed to equality of opportunity and to non-discrimination for all job applicants and employees, and we seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce regardless of gender, race, religious beliefs, nationality, ethnic/national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability.  
  
IRC UK welcomes applications from all candidates, including underrepresented groups and refugees who have the right to work in the UK.

  
IRC UK will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable adjustments to participate in the job application and/or interview process, and for essential job functions if appointed to a role. Please contact us if you may need such adjustments.   
  
If you have any questions or need assistance with the online recruitment process, please contact the IRC UK HR team at applications@rescue-uk.org

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Oficial De Recuperación Y Desarrollo - Carabobo
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.body:
Acted es una ONG internacional sin ánimo de lucro con sede en París, Francia con operaciones en más de 40 países a nivel mundial. La misión de Acted es aportar asistencia humanitaria inmediata a aquellos que se encuentren en situación de necesidad al mismo tiempo que genera oportunidades a largo plazo para un crecimiento durable. Acted opera en contextos de catástrofe natural, conflicto armado y crisis socioeconómica.

Actualmente, Acted está buscando un/a Oficial de recuperacion y desarrollo para integrar nuestro equipo en la misión de Venezuela.

El/la Oficial de recuperación y desarrollo se encargará de supervisar y ejecutar las actividades del componente de recuperación temprana, medios de vida y resiliencia comunitaria en respuesta a la emergencia humanitaria post terremotos ocurridos en Venezuela el 24-06-2026, concentrando las acciones en la zona impactada de Morón y municipios priorizados del estado Carabobo.

Entre sus principales tareas, tendrá que liderar la implementación de estrategias de rehabilitación socioeconómica, reactivación de medios de vida, apoyo a microemprendimientos y fortalecimiento institucional/comunitario para garantizar que el alcance, el presupuesto, el cronograma y la calidad estén de acuerdo con las especificaciones del proyecto, los requisitos del donante y las reglas y procedimientos de Acted.

**Funciones**

**Diseño y Planificación Técnica**

- Diseñar e implementar diagnósticos socioeconómicos rápidos, evaluaciones de mercado y análisis de medios de vida en las comunidades afectadas.
- Formular e implementar planes de recuperación económica local y activos productivos.
- Planificar la ejecución de obras de infraestructura que apoyen la reactivación de mercados y medios de vida.
- Contribuir al desarrollo de notas conceptuales, propuestas de proyectos y estrategias del nexo Humanitario-Desarrollo, cuando sea requerido.

**Implementación y Supervisión de Campo**

- Liderar la ejecución de actividades de reactivación de pequeños negocios, capacitaciones socio-productivas y programas de empleo temporal / rehabilitación de infraestructura comunitaria ligera.
- Coordinar con Logística y Finanzas la adquisición y entrega transparente de kits de capital de trabajo y herramientas.
- Identificar, anticipar y mitigar riesgos sociales, económicos o de protección asociados a las intervenciones en campo.
- Acompañar a socios locales en la planificación e implementación de sus actividades respectivas de medios de vida: viabilidad económica, planificación operativa y financiera, consultas comunitarias y visitas de campo.

**Gestión Social y Fortalecimiento de Capacidades**

- Desarrollar talleres de formación en educación financiera, gestión de microempresas, resiliencia comunitaria y gestión de riesgos ante desastres.
- Crear y fortalecer comités de desarrollo comunitario para garantizar la sostenibilidad y apropiación local de los proyectos.
- Promover la inclusión financiera y social de grupos vulnerables (mujeres, jóvenes, personas con discapacidad).

**Monitoreo, Reporte y Representación**

- Elaborar y validar informes técnicos de progreso, historias de vida, lecciones aprendidas y bases de datos con indicadores desagregados.
- Representar a la organización en el Clúster/Eje de Recuperación Temprana y Medios de Vida, así como en mesas de trabajo locales.
- Garantizar el cumplimiento de los estándares de rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP).

**Perfil deseado**

**Requisitos**

Obligatorios:

- Profesional titulado (pregrado o maestría) en Ingeniería Civil, Ambiental, o disciplinas relacionadas.
- Mínimo tres (3) años de experiencia en la implementación y coordinación de proyectos de desarrollo y recuperación , preferiblemente en contextos de emergencia humanitaria y ONGs internacionales.
- Manejo de estándares internacionales (Manual Esfera, MERS) y normativas nacionales (COVENIN, gacetas oficiales) para infraestructuras de mercado.
- Dominio de AutoCAD, Maprex, EPANET, QGIS y paquete Microsoft Office.
- Precisión en el diseño de infraestructura y alta atención al detalle en la supervisión de obras.
- Disponibilidad total para desplazamientos a comunidades afectadas por el doblete sísmico.

Competencias:

- Gestión de Equipos: Liderazgo para supervisar al personal a cargo y coordinar con socios implementadores
- Comunicación Asertiva: Habilidad para interactuar con autoridades gubernamentales y poblaciones multiculturales.
- Orientación a Resultados: Autonomía para cumplir metas bajo cronogramas estrictos y transparencia en la gestión de recursos.

**Condiciones**

- Contrato de prestación de servicios bajo la figura de honorarios profesionales durante 3 meses con posibilidad de renovación según disponibilidad presupuestaria y desempeño.
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina de Acted en Carabobo.
- Honorarios profesionales según la escala de la organización.
- Prestación de Servicios de forma presencial y traslados frecuentes a zonas afectadas por el doblete sísmico.  
    **Moron - Carabobo**

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche.
