The work of DCAF’s Africa Americas entity the LAC (Latin America and the Caribbean) region aims to support governments, parliaments, security providers and civil society by developing capacities and promoting norms and good practices to contribute to a more effective, efficient and transparent security sector that is properly overseen by the relevant authorities, responsive and accountable to the people they serve.

To advance our LAC work, we are looking for a highly dedicated and dynamic professional to be our next **Senior Advisor to the National Police of Haiti – Latin America and the Caribbean**.

**Location: Port-au-Prince, Haiti**

**Starting date: as soon as possible, subject to funding**

**Work rate: 100%**

**Duration: 12 month fixed-term contract, with possibility of extension**

**The Role**

The international senior advisor will be embedded within the National Police of Haiti (PNH), and specifically in the Bureau de Coordination Conjoint (BCC) at PNH headquarters, working in close collaboration with the Directorates of International Relations and Strategic Planning. Through high-level advisory, mentoring and operational support, the Senior Advisor will contribute to the development of the BCC as a fully functional coordination hub, strengthening the PNH’s capacity to manage external support both internally, coordinating requests for assistance, and externally, through engagement with all actors actively supporting the PNH. This approach will ensure that the BCC’s development is anchored within the PNH’s core management structure and that external assistance is strategically aligned with institutional priorities.

**Key Areas of Operation**

The Senior Adviser works in close coordination with, and under the guidance of DCAF HQ Programme Manager. Hierarchically, the Senior Adviser reports to Deputy Head of Entity.

Through advisory, mentoring, operational and project management work, the Senior Adviser will be responsible for the following:

**\*Institutional Development**

- Assist in defining the Police Coordination Cell’s (BCC) scope, objectives, organizational placement, and staffing, drafting the formal normative directive.
- Lead the mapping and analysis of past and ongoing international support to the PNH. Design and establish a sustainable, centralized database to align external aid with the PNH Strategic Plan and operational priorities.
- Identify critical capacity gaps (e.g., public financial management, data systems, procedural development) to guide strategic donor investments and improve aid alignment with a view to contributing to greater police performance and enhanced public confidence in the police.
- Incorporate Human Rights and Gender Equality Approaches throughout all work-related duties.

\***Stakeholder Engagement & Partnership Management**

- Establish a functional coordination mechanism with key international actors (political, donor, humanitarian actors, and project leadership) to streamline communications, enhance transparency, and ensure all aid is channelled through the BCC. Where relevant, facilitate coordination and communication between the PNH and humanitarian actors to ensure that humanitarian perspectives and operational needs are reflected in international assistance.
- Support drafting of the international partner coordination strategy and BCC action plan; mentor PNH personnel to ensure full national ownership and leadership over time.
- Build strong working relationships across the PNH and partner organizations, establishing a network among all embedded international advisors to drive operational and tactical synergies.
- Support agenda-setting, prepare background analytical briefs, and drive decision follow-up for internal and external coordination meetings.

\***Programme Coordination & Management**

- Monitor and regularly assess the security situation on the ground, in coordination with the National Expert and key stakeholders, providing timely security updates and risk analysis to DCAF HQ, particularly ahead of missions.
- Support the day-to-day management and implementation of the programme, including monitoring progress against objectives and M&E targets, following up on implementation and deliverables, preparation of narrative reporting, supporting financial reporting and different programme areas as required.
- Provide guidance, supervision and ongoing support to the National Officer, ensuring effective coordination, alignment with programme objectives, and timely delivery of assigned tasks and outputs.
- Represent DCAF in relevant international coordination mechanisms and clusters, as well as in engagements with donors, embassies and other key external partners.
- Support the preparation and coordination of missions by DCAF HQ teams, including logistical arrangements, stakeholder engagement, meeting preparation and follow-up.
- by identifying emerging intervention opportunities and contributing to new activity or project design in close coordination with DCAF HQ and National Officer.

**Key qualifications, skills and experience**

- Advanced university degree in security studies, political science, law, public administration, international relations, or a related field (a combination of relevant qualifications and extensive experience may be accepted in lieu).
- Fluency in oral and written French and English required, Spanish an asset. Creole language skills (or willingness to learn) are an advantage.
- Past work experience in Haiti or Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), alongside a deep understanding of Haiti’s political and security dynamics will be a strong asset.
- 10+ years of relevant work experience in the justice and security sector reform and governance, including 5+ years in advisory, mentoring, or program management roles within police reform contexts, and at least 2 years in highly complex or volatile security environments.
- Senior leadership track record, extensive experience within national police is a strong asset (ideally equivalent to Lieutenant-Colonel / Commissaire de Police / senior national HQ post or equivalent civilian executive leadership).
- Proven ability to strengthen security sector architecture, strategy, oversight, and training while navigating complex political economy dynamics.
- Demonstrated experience in international cooperation frameworks, including mapping aid flows, building centralized database/digital tracking tools, and aligning donor investments with national priorities.
- Previous experience in programme design and fundraising is an asset.
- Strong capability to lead, delegate, and mentor diverse teams, fostering professional growth and high performance.
- Exceptional interpersonal, negotiation, and mediation skills to build trust, resolve conflicts, and manage strategic relationships across executive and operational levels under challenging conditions.
- Proven ability to translate operational data into concise policy briefs, strategic knowledge products, and executive briefings for senior decision-makers.
- Excellent organizational, process management, and planning skills; proven ability to manage competing priorities, mitigate risks, and deliver high-quality outputs under tight deadlines.
- High cultural sensitivity and ability to operate effectively within multi-cultural environments.

**We Offer**

- a rewarding, dynamic and meaningful work experience
- the chance to be part of a diverse team of collaborative, respectful, hardworking, and values-driven people
- the chance to contribute to advancing the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices

jobs.title: Team Leader, Syria Education Programme III (SEP III)
jobs.body:
**SYRIA EDUCATION PROGRAMME III (SEP III)**

Building on SEP I (2018–2022) and SEP II (2022–2027), which supported primary educatio in Idleb and Aleppo, FCDO plans to procure a new Technical Assistance (TA) contract, SEP III, to support the Syrian Ministry of Education (MoE) in implementing its nationally-led reform agenda, complementing the Ministry's wider reform programme, including support provided through the Global Partnership for Education (GPE). Since December 2024, the MoE has begun to reunify a fragmented education system, but progress has been constrained by limited institutional capacity, a lack of data, weak policy development processes and the absence of a clear long-term strategy for recovery. Unlike earlier phases, which focused primarily on service delivery in northwest Syria, SEP III will work directly with the MoE and local Education Directorates, generally at national level and directorate level, in partnership with Ministry officials, to help the Ministry translate its policy and process reforms into practice through technical advice, capacity building, coaching and support to implementation.

SEP III has two components. The first, which is the subject of this contract, is politically informed TA to the MoE and Education Directorates to strengthen inclusive, effective and evidence-based policy making. The second is non-formal education (NFE) for returning refugees and internally displaced persons, which is outside the scope of this contract and will be delivered by a separate provider. The TA supplier will be required to work collaboratively with the NFE component.

The exact scope of the TA work will be determined jointly with FCDO and the MoE through a demand-led, co-designed and flexible approach. No reform priorities are set in advance; they will be identified with the Ministry during inception. The work is expected to focus on strengthening the education system to improve foundational learning outcomes for primary-school-aged children across Syria, delivered through: 1) Services and Analysis to inform TA and policy decisions; 2) Foundational Learning thematic TA (for example teacher development, coaching and supervision, safeguarding, learning data generation and use, and inclusive education); and 3) Education Systems Strengthening TA (sector planning and prioritisation, policy development, financial management, and monitoring and accountability). Given the difficult fiscal choices likely to shape the sector over the coming years, the programme is also expected to support the Ministry's public finance and value-for-money decision-making. Illustrative technical priorities include: supporting policy reform and Ministry-led coordination, standard-setting, and system strengthening; supporting the roll-out of child safeguarding and Codes of Conduct; improving the quality and consistency of teaching through professional development and a national Teacher Competency Framework; and data-driven planning, including through education management information systems (EMIS/SIMIS).

Given the fluid transition context, the programme will need to operate flexibly, respond quickly to changes, and seize windows of opportunity for reform as they arise. FCDO expects a politically informed, 'test, learn, adapt' approach rather than a fixed blueprint. Delivery must be aligned with government systems, avoiding parallel platforms and the substitution of government functions, and must be underpinned by gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) and conflict sensitivity. This requires strong political judgement, including a clear understanding of how decisions are made within the Ministry and government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, an in-depth understanding of the Syrian education system and its institutional actors, and the ability to sustain trusted relationships with the Ministry, FCDO, and other sector stakeholders, including UNICEF, GPE, Education Cannot Wait (ECW), and the World Bank.

The anticipated delivery model comprises i) a **Core Delivery Team** responsible for overall leadership, technical oversight, coordination, MEAL, governance and quality assurance, which should be predominantly Syrian and mostly based in Syria; and ii) a **demand-led TA Pool** of experts with education and governance backgrounds. The contract is expected to begin on 1 July 2027 with a six-month inception period, during which the supplier must mobilise rapidly, establish a presence in Damascus and operationalise its delivery systems. Details are indicative and will be confirmed in FCDO's Tender Notice.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Team Leader holds overall accountability for the design, rapid mobilisation, and delivery of SEP III, including leading the Core Delivery Team and overseeing the TA Pool, ensuring the programme is implemented in accordance with the contract, FCDO requirements, IRC policies and principles, and internationally recognised quality of assistance standards. The Team Leader is the primary point of contact with FCDO and, working closely with the ESS Technical Director and senior Ministry counterparts, provides strategic direction to support the Ministry's implementation of its reform priorities.

The Team Leader is responsible for the programme's overall management, including budget oversight and value for money, performance against contractual KPIs, and risk management (including fiduciary and reputational risk in a sensitive political environment), with the technical quality of the programme's workstreams assured by the ESS Technical Director. The postholder ensures the programme operates adaptively — using political analysis, evidence, monitoring data, and regular review points to prioritise, test, learn and adapt in response to a fast-moving political and institutional context — while maintaining the flexibility needed to respond to emerging windows of opportunity for reform.

The Team Leader maintains strong working relationships with the implementing team, consortium/delivery partners (if applicable), the MoE and Education Directorates, FCDO, the provider of the NFE component, and other education sector stakeholders, and represents the programme and IRC in relevant coordination fora, technical working groups, and policy dialogues. The postholder also oversees programme staffing, procurement, and administrative functions, and ensures robust communications and knowledge management, both internally and with external stakeholders, to share progress, evidence, and lessons learned.

**JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Leadership**

● Provide overall strategic leadership for SEP III, ensuring the programme's support to the MoE and Education Directorates, led technically by the ESS Technical Director, is relevant to, and aligned with, the Ministry's evolving reform priorities and helps translate these priorities into practice.

● Lead the six-month inception period (July –December 2027), including establishing the Damascus presence, mobilising the Core Delivery Team and TA Pool, operationalising delivery systems, formalising ways of working with the MoE, developing the screening and prioritisation framework and Tasking Order criteria, and delivering inception milestones to FCDO's standard and timetable.

● Provide strategic oversight of the ESS Technical Director's technical leadership, ensuring the programme's technical direction remains aligned with strategic priorities and senior-level MoE relations.

● Ensure the programme operates flexibly and applies a 'test, learn, adapt' approach: agreeing clear reform objectives and decision criteria with the Ministry, co-designing and trialling options, using evidence and learning to decide whether to continue, scale, adapt, pause or pivot workstreams, and documenting adaptation decisions.

● Think and work politically, with a strong understanding of how decisions are made within the Ministry and government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, drawing on strong contextual and institutional analysis to ensure these opportunities are identified early and acted upon in a timely way.

● Take explicit responsibility for reform sequencing, political economy analysis, and navigating institutional constraints, ensuring a regularly updated PEA and periodic political reviews inform programme design, prioritisation and delivery, and that support is prioritised and paced in line with the Ministry's capacity and the political space available for reform.

● Ensure delivery remains aligned with government systems, avoids parallel platforms and substituting for government functions, and is designed for sustainability and capacity transfer, while supporting coalitions of reform-minded actors within and beyond government.

● Champion evidence-based, gender-responsive, and inclusive approaches throughout programme design and delivery, including dedicated attention to the needs of girls and children with disabilities, and ensure conflict sensitivity is embedded throughout.

● Provide leadership on GEDSI, ensuring diversity and inclusion are reflected in team and partner selection, programme design and implementation, and programme reporting.

**Donor, Government and Stakeholder Relations**

● Serve as the primary point of contact and representational link with FCDO, ensuring high-quality, timely reporting through formal and informal debriefings, and annual and semi-annual reports.

● Build and maintain a trusted, politically informed working relationship with senior officials in the MoE and other relevant government counterparts, supporting the Ministry's stewardship of the education sector and complementing the ESS Technical Director's ongoing technical-level engagement with MoE and Education Directorate representatives at all levels to identify technical assistance needs and design and implement ESS interventions.

● Coordinate with sector stakeholders, including UNICEF, GPE, ECW, the World Bank, and other donors and implementing partners, to support coordinated reform efforts across government and development partners, and to ensure the programme complements ongoing initiatives and other TA investments and adheres to national and global standards.

● Ensure close coherence and collaboration with the provider of the separate NFE component of SEP III, including joint planning, information sharing and coordination of engagement with the Ministry.

● Represent the programme and IRC at national and international forums, including technical conferences and policy dialogues, sharing programme achievements and lessons learned.

● Champion accountability to affected populations, partners, and diverse stakeholders, ensuring that feedback and complaints mechanisms, transparent communication, and participatory approaches inform programme design, delivery, and adaptive management.

**Programme, Risk and Financial Management**

● Oversee overall programme and budget management, ensuring value for money across all components, informed by a sound understanding of the Ministry's public finance context, and robust compliance with FCDO and IRC financial and procurement requirements.

● Oversee the Tasking Order mechanism for the TA Pool, ensuring requests are screened and prioritised against agreed criteria, co-created with the Ministry and Education Directorates, approved by FCDO, costed transparently against the agreed rate card with clear milestones, and delivered to a high-quality standard.

● Lead on identification and management of programme risks, including fiduciary, safeguarding, political, and reputational risks associated with operating within Syrian government structures during a period of political transition.

● Develop, review, and monitor, in coordination with key programme staff, the annual work plan (updated quarterly) and performance plans, and ensure quarterly and annual reports are submitted in the agreed format and to the required standard, so that long-term and short-term priorities remain on track.

● Take responsibility for contractual performance against FCDO's KPIs (indicatively covering reporting, work planning, expenditure variance, risk, safeguarding and fraud notification compliance, political analysis, timely delivery of TA outputs, Ministry adoption of TA outputs, and evidence of adaptive management), taking early corrective action where performance is at risk.

● Ensure monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) data systematically feed into adaptive management processes, including regular reviews of cost-effectiveness and progress against outcomes.

**People and Operations Management**

● Manage programme staff, including through direct line management of the ESS Technical Director and other senior team members, and, where applicable, consortium or delivery partners, ensuring proper reporting, financial management, and compliance with donor and organisational requirements.

● Build a Core Delivery Team and TA Pool, drawing on national and international expertise only, and ensure all consortium or delivery partners can deploy Syrian expertise, with at least one member registered in Syria.

● Create and maintain a work environment that promotes teamwork, trust, mutual respect, and empowers staff to take responsibility.

● Oversee procurement, logistical, and administrative functions in support of programme delivery.

● Ensure appropriate internal and external communications and knowledge management, sharing achievements and lessons learned with diverse audiences.

**PROFILE AND QUALIFICATIONS**

● Advanced degree (Master's or equivalent) in education, public administration, international development, or a related field; equivalent experience may be substituted for a graduate degree.

● Minimum of 10 years' experience managing large-scale, complex, donor-funded technical assistance or education programmes, ideally including experience with FCDO-funded contracts and performance-based or KPI-linked payment mechanisms.

● Significant prior experience working directly with government ministries or line departments on system-level policy and process reform, ideally within the education sector.

● Substantial experience working in conflict, crisis, or politically sensitive transition contexts; experience in Syria or the broader MENA region strongly preferred.

● Sound understanding of public finance and value-for-money principles, with the ability to support the Ministry in navigating the fiscal choices shaping education sector reform.

● Proven ability to provide strategic leadership while harnessing the multi-disciplinary skills of technical personnel, consortium or delivery partners, and government counterparts.

● Demonstrated ability to create and nurture strong, trusted working relationships with Ministry of Education representatives and other relevant government, donor, and sector stakeholders.

● Strong political judgement, including a sound understanding of how decisions are made within government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, and demonstrated ability to apply thinking and working politically, using PEA to inform decisions, and to operate flexibly and adaptively in a fast-moving, sensitive institutional environment, responding to windows of opportunity as they arise.

● Demonstrated ability to build and sustain effective, trusted relationships with senior government officials, donors, and a broad range of stakeholders, including civil society and multilateral partners.

● Familiarity with the Syrian education system, or comparable fragile/post-conflict education systems, and with the priorities of foundational learning, safeguarding, and inclusion, including for girls and children with disabilities.

● Experience with adaptive management approaches and evidence-based programming, ideally including leading demand-led technical assistance facilities that use tasking orders or similar call-down mechanisms.

● Experience rapidly mobilising a programme team and establishing an operational presence in a new or complex setting, ideally Syria or a comparable context.

● Demonstrated commitment to localisation, including experience leading predominantly national teams and working in partnership with national and sub-national organisations.

● Strong analytical, communication, and writing skills, with the ability to articulate evidence-based positions to influence sector and government stakeholders.

● Demonstrated ability to apply safeguarding, ethics, and do-no-harm principles throughout programme delivery, particularly when working with or on behalf of children.

● Fluency in English required; Arabic language skills strongly preferred.

***Please note that this position is contingent on the outcome of the FCDO procurement and award of SEP III (tender publication currently anticipated for January 2027 and award for May 2027). Programme details are indicative and remain subject to FCDO approval and the final Tender Notice.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development – Geneva, Switzerland
jobs.body:
**Department:** Operations

**Duty Station:** Geneva

**Contract Type:** Full-time (100%)

**Direct report:** Director of Operations

**Grade:** Head of

## **Mission**

Geneva Call is a neutral and impartial non-governmental organisation dedicated to promoting respect by Armed Groups and De Facto and/or Provisional Authorities (AGDAs) for international humanitarian norms in armed conflict and other situations of violence, in particular those related to the protection of civilians. Geneva Call focuses its efforts on banning the use of anti-personnel mines, protecting children from the effects of armed conflict, prohibiting sexual violence in armed conflict, working towards the elimination of gender discrimination, protecting civilian infrastructure, and ensuring humanitarian access.

## **Why this role?**

Under the overall supervision of the Director of Operations, the role of Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development (DDOPD) is to lead the Programme and Development unit and develop standardised programmatic approaches and models in alignment with programmatic cycle management tools and ensure programmatic interventions are based on Geneva Call’s mission – Theory of Change, strategic priorities, conflict specification framework and humanitarian principles. The DDOPD is accountable for the global programme strategy and quality.

## **Work Relations**

The DDOPD will partner and coordinate as a peer with other operational heads of units such as Policy, Research and Legal (PRL), MEAL and Donor Relations units, and with the Deputy Director of Operations for Africa, to promote coherence in programmatic plans and strategies for internal applications and external dissemination. The DDOPD will be the functional manager of the Regional Heads of Programme and Development to ensure technical guidance and support on programme models and designs from inception to implementation and end evaluation is provided at a regional and country-level, and medium to long term impact is generated. The position in coordination and collaboration with other units will develop strategic programmatic partnerships with other international organisations and networks and organise events in global capitals on protection of civilians through AGDA engagement.

## **Duties and Responsabilities**

**Programme Quality Assurance and Standards**

- Sets global Project Cycle Management standards and ensures the dissemination and application of the Project Cycle Management handbook across all existing and new missions. In consultation with PRL and MEAL units, leads the design, development and streamlining of specific programme models, particularly for new missions, based on Geneva Call’s conflict spectrum framework while incorporating humanitarian engagement principles and thematic priorities in line with Geneva Call’s mission and strategy.
- Leads programme quality reviews at a global level, based on the results matrix and evaluation methodologies developed by the MEAL unit, and contributes to the development of Geneva Call’s internal programmes audit framework in consultation with relevant programme focal points at HQ and regional levels.
- Identifies and coordinates learning needs at a global level and supports the Regional Heads of Programme & Development in building the capacities of programming teams to develop long-term sustainable programmes and measurable impact by incorporating data and lessons learnt from the MEAL unit.
- Uses the progress tracker system designed by MEAL across all missions and produces quarterly reports on programme progress and implementation quality against agreed targets. Develops a standardised programme versus cost estimation simulation model based on GC AGDA engagement programme design.
- Provides functional guidance to Regional Heads of Programme and Development in their technical advisory role to country teams, facilitating the coordination and implementation of projects and programme activities in close consultation with country teams, which retain ownership and accountability for programme delivery. Owns global learning approaches and supports Regional Heads of Programme & Development to host regular learning and collaboration opportunities for field and HQ staff to discuss programme/project implementation strategies and good practices.

**Operational Coordination**

- In close coordination with the Deputy Director of Operations for Africa and Director of Operations, aligns programmatic plans and supports Geneva Call’s institutional strategic development through the implementation of the updated Theory of Change and Strategic Plans in line with GC mission.
- Designs thematic programmes with policy and legal input from the PRL unit on protection of civilians in different conflict context situations.
- In coordination with the MEAL unit, ensures the organisational MEAL framework is fully integrated into programmatic designs from inception to end evaluation stages, utilising data from MEAL activities to enhance programme quality. Ensures all programme designs fully incorporate conflict sensitivity, gender equality, diversity and inclusion, and do not harm principles.
- Provides technical guidance in developing high-quality new project proposals for cross-regional programme design and multi-country donors and leads the management of multi-regional grants.
- In coordination with the Humanitarian Diplomacy & Communications unit, guides programme team to produce impact stories based on successful programmatic intervention. Develops global strategic partnerships and relationships with international organisations to support country missions.

**Fundraising, Grant Management and Donor Briefings**

- Coordinates programme input globally for overall fundraising and relationship building efforts, in close collaboration with the Donor Relations unit.
- Provides regular updates and briefings to donors on programmatic updates and impacts and leads global programme briefings and reporting.
- Provides programmatic guidance to the Grants and Reporting Coordinator.

**Representation and Strategic Partnerships**

- Maintains and strengthens Geneva Call’s role as a neutral, impartial and independent humanitarian actor, positioning the organisation and its operations within the geographical areas to gain maximum access to AGDAs, influential stakeholders and affected populations.
- Engages frequently with high‑level stakeholders and international organisations to secure appropriate support for Geneva Call operations.
- In coordination with the Director of Operations, the DDOPD represents Geneva Call in global forums and performs such other duties as may be assigned.

**Management**

- Shared direct line management of the Regional Heads of Programme and Development, with clearly defined and complementary areas of responsibility. The DDOPD exercises line management authority over programmatic strategy, technical quality, programme delivery, and achievement of functional objectives, while the Deputy Director of Operations exercises line management authority over regional operational management, coordination, and alignment with regional priorities.
- Direct line management of the Programme and Reporting Coordinator at headquarters.

## **Requirements**

**Education (Essential)**

- Master’s degree in political or social sciences, Humanitarian Affairs, International Relations, International Humanitarian Law, Human Rights Law or a related field.

**Experience (Essential)**

- 14+ years of highly relevant experience, with a minimum of 8 years of experience in the field and 3 years of experience at headquarters.
- A minimum of 3 years of experience leading and managing senior managers, included within the overall professional experience requirement.
- Demonstrated experience in implementing programme cycle management tools and leading programme development and quality assurance, as well as experience in humanitarian settings and/or crisis and post-crisis settings.
- Progressively responsible experience in liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities and international institutions. Demonstrated experience in engaging with armed actors and facilitating constructive dialogue on humanitarian concerns, particularly to promote respect for international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians.
- Advanced understanding of the complex needs of humanitarian operations. Proven experience in resource mobilisation.

**Job related Competencies (Essential)**

- Sound knowledge of financial and business administration and of the principles and practices of management.
- Outstanding interpersonal communication skills and ability to work in a team and across departments to ensure an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment.
- Sound knowledge of the project cycle, as well as of monitoring and evaluation.
- Strong analytical thinking, planning and organising skills, with attention to detail, and structured, strong planning and organisation skills.
- Strategic thinking combined with strong execution skills.

**Organisational Competencies**

- Strong leadership and people management skills.
- Ability to build and maintain trusting and collaborative relationships.
- Ability to promote teamwork and effective collaboration across departments.
- Commitment to fostering an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment.
- Ability to demonstrate accountability, sound judgement and alignment with Geneva Call’s organisational values.

**Language (Essential)**

- Fluency in English and French both spoken and written.

**Language (Desirable)**

- Knowledge of Spanish, Arabic, or any other language relevant to Geneva Call’s operations is an advantage.

## **Why join Geneva Call?**

Geneva Call brings together people of diverse nationalities, cultures, languages and perspectives, fostering an inclusive working environment for all staff.

This role offers the opportunity to advance a meaningful humanitarian mission by strengthening the protection of civilians in armed conflict. The role combines strategic leadership, programme quality and innovation to develop sustainable, impactful programmes, strengthen partnerships and foster collaboration across missions, ultimately contributing to lasting change for communities affected by armed conflict.

jobs.title: Research Manager
jobs.body:
We’re hiring

Research Manager

**LOCATION:** Freetown, Sierra Leone

**GROSS SALARY RANGE:** $4,725.85 – $5,608.40 (gross monthly)

**CONTRACT:** Indefinite

Laterite is looking for an experienced professional to lead research teams, strategy, and operations in our office in Freetown, Sierra Leone.

**WHO WE ARE**

Laterite is a data, research, and analytics firm working on complex development challenges. We partner with universities, global think tanks, international NGOs, multilateral donors, and government ministries. Our clients include the World Bank, TechnoServe, the Mastercard Foundation, and others.

We operate across the Netherlands, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and Peru, with 90+ full-time staff and more than 2,000 enumerators. We believe meaningful impact requires being on the ground, building local teams, and establishing long-term trust. Our office culture is collaborative and gives people autonomy to grow into their roles. Learn more: [www.laterite.com](http://www.laterite.com)

**THE ENVIRONMENT YOU’RE STEPPING INTO**

You will join our Sierra Leone team in a high-trust environment. We are low on bureaucracy but high on individual accountability. You won’t be micromanaged here—we want you to use your judgment to solve problems, support our fast-paced field teams, and actively improve the systems you work with.

Laterite Sierra Leone started operations in 2023. Our office in Freetown is Laterite’s first step in West Africa and will build on our 12+ years of experience of research and data collection. Since then, our Freetown office has been using innovative techniques to study education outcomes in the region. Our team in Freetown currently consists of four team members.

**HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT**

As a Research Manager based in Freetown you will:

- Oversee the technical delivery and operations of a portfolio of research projects, from design to data collection, analysis and follow-through.
- Provide technical advice, coaching and steering for research design, project management, analysis, and reporting to ensure we deliver value for our clients and use rigorous and innovative research methods.
- Manage the country office, including structuring Laterite’s research agenda, contributing to corporate strategy, overseeing process improvements, and financial and personnel management.
- Design and lead training and professional development activities for the research team and the wider Laterite team.
- Build and manage the pipeline of research projects, turning internal research ideas into externally funded projects and designing evaluations for clients.

As a member of Laterite’s senior management team, you will consult on corporate strategy, business operations, and opportunities for growth. You will serve as role model for the team, actively promoting our corporate culture, mentoring colleagues, and helping us to achieve our mission as an organization.

Laterite is expanding rapidly, and we are open to the possibility of hiring exceptional candidates at a higher grade.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

We are looking for an accomplished researcher who combines excellent technical skills with management experience. This role is based in Freetown, Sierra Leone, and requires relocation to Sierra Leone as well as a minimum commitment of two years in-country.

Our future colleague has:

- Demonstrated experience leading an organization, department, or program, including financial and operational management.
- Direct supervisory experience and demonstrated experience training and mentoring researchers.
- Demonstrated experience designing and overseeing complex research projects.
- Demonstrated experience building business pipelines and nurturing relationships with clients and stakeholders from the public and private sectors.
- Motivation to work in social and economic research in Sub-Saharan Africa
- 5+ years of research or project management experience and at least 2 years in a management role in education, youth, public health, agriculture and/or urbanization.
- A postgraduate degree (master’s or above) in Economics, Econometrics, Development Research, or in one of Laterite’s core sectors

*Additionally, we are looking for:*

- A self-motivated team leader with excellent interpersonal skills who thrives in a fast-paced environment where timelines can be unpredictable
- Technical expertise in quantitative or qualitative research methods.
- Excellent written and oral communication skills (in English)
- Proficiency in STATA, R, or Python.

**WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU**

- **Competitive compensation. $4,725.85 – $5,608.40** gross monthly salary (exact grade determined by experience/interviews), medical insurance, pension contribution, and 25 days of annual leave.
- **Professional growth.** We are also committed to supporting our staff’s learning, providing an annual learning budget of up to USD 1,000 per person and 10 days of time off for professional learning each year.
- **Flexibility**: Laterite has a hybrid work policy, with employees expected to work from the office three days per week and the flexibility to work from home for the remaining two days. Employees can also work remotely, away from their home office, for up to six weeks (30 working days) per year.

jobs.title: Functional Lead, Humanitarian ERP
jobs.body:
NGO finance & procurement · Business analysis

**Remote · EuropeContract4 days / week**

Relief Applications is a humanitarian tech company headquartered in Toulouse, France. We build digital tools with and for NGOs, UN agencies and mission-driven organisations, bringing solutions to those changing the world.

We are growing our ERP offer for NGOs: Finance, Procurement and HR modules designed for how humanitarian organisations actually work.

## **About the role**

You will be the business brain of the project. Working side by side with our project manager, you will turn NGOs’ finance, procurement and HR needs into features.

Your work makes our ERP stronger with every deployment and decides whether client teams adopt it. You will run workshops with them, shape the workflows, test what is built and train the users. Occasional travel to clients is expected.

## **Key responsibilities**

### **Requirements & functional design**

- Co-run user-requirement workshops with client Finance, Procurement and HR teams
- Write clear user stories, workflows and acceptance criteria
- Own the functional design of the Finance, Procurement and HR modules: approval chains, budgets and cost codes, data model and reporting
- Flag early when deeper expertise is needed, such as local payroll or HR law

### **Building & testing**

- Prototype and ship features, screens and fixes with AI-supported tools (Claude, Cursor or similar)
- Work through Git with the tech lead and developers, who review your code
- Test features against real NGO scenarios and run user acceptance testing with clients

### **Adoption**

- Review and complete user guides
- Design and deliver trainings for finance, procurement and HR users
- Collect feedback after go-live and turn it into improvements

## **Candidate profile**

### **Additional assets**

- Previous ERP implementation or rollout (Sage, Dynamics, Odoo, SunSystems…)
- Experience with charity finance across several countries
- MEAL or logframe exposure
- Training and documentation experience

### **Experience**

- 3–5+ years in NGO or humanitarian operations, ideally in finance, grants or procurement
- Solid working knowledge of donor rules, budget lines, cost codes, purchase-to-pay flows and grant reporting
- Hands-on experience building with AI

### **Languages**

- Fluent English; French is a plus

### **Skills**

- Business analysis: running workshops, mapping processes, writing user stories
- Comfortable with Git, reading code, and basic data and SQL
- Able to turn rules into working features

### **Soft skills**

- Autonomous and pragmatic
- Confident facing a client’s team
- Honest about what you know and what you don’t

jobs.title: Responsable Analyse Médicale et Plaidoyer - Est de la RDC (h/f/x) - Médecins Sans Frontières
jobs.body:
**CONTEXTE**

En République Démocratique du Congo (RDC), Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) travaille en collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé afin de fournir des soins médicaux aux victimes des conflits et des violences, aux personnes déplacées ainsi qu'aux personnes affectées par des épidémies ou pandémies telles que le VIH/SIDA, la tuberculose, le paludisme, la malnutrition, entre autres. Ces situations sont souvent associées à la faiblesse des institutions étatiques, aux capacités limitées du système de santé public et à une compréhension insuffisante des besoins et des lacunes réels sur le terrain. La contribution de MSF s'appuie sur ses projets réguliers ainsi que sur ses équipes de réponse d'urgence, prêtes à intervenir sur l'ensemble du territoire en cas d'épidémie, de catastrophe naturelle ou de conflit.

En 2023, face à l'intensification de la violence dans l'est de la RDC, qui a entraîné le déplacement d'un nombre record de civils, MSF a renforcé ses activités afin de répondre à l'augmentation des besoins humanitaires. Depuis l'année dernière, l'ensemble des missions MSF au Nord-Kivu est confronté à d'importants défis liés aux ruptures de stocks de médicaments contre la tuberculose, le VIH et le paludisme, ainsi qu'à des pénuries d'intrants médicaux (cartouches GeneXpert, tests VIH et paludisme, etc.) et à une capacité limitée de réponse face à l'augmentation des cas de violences sexuelles, de malnutrition et d'épidémies. Le nombre élevé de déplacements de population complique également l'accès aux soins de santé. Les réductions de financement du Fonds mondial ainsi que le conflit en cours dans l'est de la RDC contribuent à ces perturbations.

En tant que **Responsable Analyse Médicale et Plaidoyer - Est de la RDC**, vous êtes responsable de l’analyse médicale et du développement des activités de plaidoyer liées à l’accès aux soins et aux services de santé dans l’est du pays. Placé(e) sous la supervision hiérarchique du Représentant Médical du BALI (Bureau administratif et de liaison intersectionnel de MSF) et en lien fonctionnel et technique avec les Conseillers en politiques de santé suivant la RDC, vous contribuez à l’identification, la documentation et l’analyse des principaux obstacles à l’accès aux soins ainsi qu'à l'élaboration des positionnements et messages de plaidoyer de MSF. Vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes projets et les Coordinateurs Médicaux des différentes sections MSF présentes au Nord-Kivu afin de collecter et consolider les informations issues du terrain. Vous collaborez également avec le Responsable Plaidoyer VIH/TB basé à Kinshasa afin de relayer les enjeux identifiés dans l'Est auprès des autorités nationales, des bailleurs et des autres acteurs de santé concernés. En tant que membre de l'équipe de coordination, vous assurez le lien entre les réalités opérationnelles observées dans les projets et les initiatives de plaidoyer menées aux niveaux provincial, national et international.

**RESPONSABILITES PRINCIPALES**

**Analyse des obstacles à l'accès aux soins**

- Collecter, centraliser et analyser les informations relatives aux barrières d'accès aux services de santé, notamment dans les domaines du VIH, de la tuberculose, du paludisme, de la vaccination, de la nutrition et de la prise en charge des violences sexuelles. Produire des analyses permettant de mieux comprendre les défis rencontrés par les populations et d'orienter le positionnement de MSF

**Suivi des financements et cartographie des acteurs**

- Assurer une veille sur les financements des programmes de santé et sur les évolutions du paysage humanitaire et sanitaire. Analyser l'impact des financements sur la disponibilité des services de santé et maintenir une cartographie actualisée des acteurs intervenant dans les zones couvertes par MSF

**Consolidation et analyse des données issues des projets**

- Consolider les données et informations remontées par les projets MSF concernant les ruptures de stocks, les difficultés d'accès aux traitements et diagnostics, les tendances épidémiologiques, la malnutrition ou les violences sexuelles. Transformer ces informations en analyses permettant d'identifier les principales lacunes et risques pour les populations

**Suivi de la disponibilité des intrants médicaux**

- En collaboration avec les équipes pharmacie et supply, suivre la disponibilité des médicaments, tests diagnostiques et autres intrants de santé essentiels. Participer aux mécanismes de coordination concernés et contribuer à l'identification précoce des risques de rupture ou de difficultés d'approvisionnement pouvant affecter les activités médicales

**Développement et mise en œuvre du plaidoyer**

- Contribuer à l'élaboration et à la mise en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer de MSF en documentant les besoins, les insuffisances de réponse et les conséquences pour les populations. Participer à la rédaction de messages clés, notes de briefing, analyses et autres documents destinés aux autorités, bailleurs de fonds et partenaires

**Coordination et collaboration intersectionnelle**

- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes médicales, opérationnelles et de plaidoyer des différentes sections MSF intervenant au Nord-Kivu. Participer aux discussions internes visant à développer des analyses communes, harmoniser les positionnements de MSF et renforcer la cohérence des actions de plaidoyer aux niveaux provincial, national et international

**PREREQUIS**

**Education & Expérience**

- Diplôme universitaire en santé publique, politiques de santé, sciences de la santé, affaires humanitaires ou dans un domaine connexe. Une spécialisation en plaidoyer, sciences politiques ou communication constitue un atout
- Minimum 2 ans d’expérience internationale dans différents contextes humanitaires ou de santé publique est requis
- Expérience du secteur de la santé publique ainsi qu’une bonne compréhension des mécanismes de financement de la santé et du fonctionnement des systèmes de santé est un atout important
- Une expérience au sein de MSF ou d’une autre INGO médicale est indispensable
- Une expérience en plaidoyer auprès des autorités sanitaires, des bailleurs de fonds ou d’autres acteurs de la santé constitue un atout
- Un intérêt marqué pour la région ainsi que pour les enjeux humanitaires est attendu

**Compétences**

- Capacité à analyser et à synthétiser des données médicales, épidémiologiques et opérationnelles
- Capacité démontrée de représentation, du réseautage, et de négociations
- Forte sensibilité interculturelle et aptitude à travailler dans des environnements multiculturels
- Résistance au stress
- Travail d’équipe et coopération
- Agilité et diplomatie
- Excellente maîtrise du Pack Office 365 est obligatoire

**Langues**

- Très bonne maitrise orale et écrite du **Français**
- Bonne connaissance d’Anglais est un atout

**CONDITIONS**

- Date de début : **Dès que possible**
- Localisation : **Béni**, Est de la RDC
- Mobilité : **mobilité importante dans les projets et les coordinations**
- Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée – Temps plein
- Durée du contrat : **9 mois** (prolongeable)
- Salaire selon la grille salariale internationale de MSF
- Les termes contractuels, les conditions et le salaire seront établis en fonction de la résidence officielle des candidats sélectionnés et dans le respect des grilles standard de fonction et de salaire de MSF
- **Pas de poste en famille ou couple**
- ***Adhésion aux valeurs managériales de l’organisation : Respect, Transparence, Responsabilisation, Intégrité, Confiance, Autonomisation***
- ***Adhésion aux engagements pour un comportement responsable***

**Date limite pour postuler : 15th of November 2026**

***Les femmes sont encouragées à postuler.***

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.body:
**OB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to project locations

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, and agricultural and irrigation-related interventions. Through these complementary activities, the project aims to address urgent household needs, restore essential infrastructure and support agricultural livelihoods and community recovery.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking an experienced Project Manager to lead the overall planning, implementation, monitoring and closure of the project, ensuring that all activities are delivered effectively, on time, within the approved budget, and in compliance with IHH policies and OCHA SHF requirements.

The Project Manager will oversee the implementation of integrated Shelter/NFI and Food Security and Agriculture/Livelihoods (FSAL) activities, providing leadership to the project team and ensuring effective coordination between technical teams, support departments, local authorities, community representatives and relevant humanitarian stakeholders.

The role requires strong project management and organizational skills, sound financial oversight, and the ability to manage multidisciplinary teams and address operational challenges in the Syrian humanitarian context. The successful candidate will ensure that project activities achieve their intended results while maintaining high standards of programme quality, accountability, safeguarding and donor compliance.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Project Planning and Implementation**

**·** Lead the planning, implementation and closure of the project in accordance with the approved proposal, logical framework, work plan, budget and donor requirements.

**·** Develop and regularly update detailed implementation plans, activity schedules, procurement plans and resource requirements in coordination with relevant technical and support teams.

**·** Oversee the implementation of shelter, NFI, food security, agriculture and livelihoods activities, ensuring that project outputs, targets and milestones are achieved within the approved timeframe.

**·** Monitor progress against the approved work plan and indicators, identify implementation delays and operational challenges, and implement appropriate corrective measures.

**·** Ensure effective integration and complementarity between project components to maximize impact and avoid duplication of assistance.

**·** Conduct regular field visits to assess implementation progress, verify the quality of activities, engage with project teams and communities, and address implementation challenges.

**·** Ensure that project documentation, implementation records and supporting evidence are complete, accurate and maintained in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.

**Technical Oversight and Programme Quality**

**·** Coordinate with engineering staff to ensure the effective implementation of shelter rehabilitation activities, including household assessments, preparation and review of Bills of Quantities (BoQs), contractor supervision, quality assurance and verification of completed works.

**·** Oversee winterization and Core NFI assistance, ensuring transparent beneficiary selection, appropriate verification, clear communication of assistance modalities and coordination between SHF-funded and IHH-funded caseloads.

**·** Supervise the implementation of cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread activities, ensuring compliance with approved targeting criteria, delivery arrangements and monitoring requirements.

**·** Coordinate with agriculture and field teams to support the effective implementation and monitoring of agricultural assistance, irrigation-related interventions and activities supporting farming livelihoods.

**·** Ensure that project activities comply with approved technical specifications, implementation procedures and relevant quality standards.

**·** Work closely with technical staff to identify implementation gaps, address quality concerns and ensure that interventions respond to identified household and community needs.

**·** Promote coordination across technical components to ensure consistent implementation and efficient use of project resources.

**Team Leadership and Coordination**

**·** Provide day-to-day management, supervision and guidance to project staff, ensuring clear responsibilities, effective communication and accountability for results.

**·** Coordinate closely with engineering, FSAL, finance, procurement, logistics, monitoring and other relevant teams to ensure timely and effective project delivery.

**·** Monitor staff performance, identify capacity-building needs and support professional development and continuous improvement.

**·** Maintain effective working relationships with local authorities, community representatives, contractors, service providers and relevant humanitarian actors.

**·** Represent IHH in relevant coordination meetings and external engagements related to the project, as delegated by senior management.

**·** Organize regular project review meetings to assess progress, discuss challenges, agree on corrective actions and follow up on outstanding issues.

**·** Ensure that field teams receive the guidance, information and resources required to perform their responsibilities effectively.

**Budget Management and Donor Compliance**

**·** Monitor project expenditure against the approved budget and implementation plan in coordination with the finance team.

**·** Review budget utilization, expenditure forecasts and financial progress, identifying variances and proposing corrective actions when required.

**·** Coordinate with finance, procurement and logistics teams to ensure that project expenditures, procurement processes, contracts and payments comply with IHH procedures and donor requirements.

**·** Ensure that project activities and expenditures remain within the approved scope and budget and that any proposed changes follow established authorization procedures.

**·** Monitor financial and operational risks, identify potential overspending or implementation bottlenecks, and take timely action to address them.

**·** Ensure that financial and programme documentation is accurate, complete and available for internal reviews, audits and donor verification.

**·** Escalate significant financial, contractual, operational or compliance issues to senior management in a timely manner.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Reporting**

**·** Ensure systematic monitoring of project implementation against approved indicators, targets, milestones and means of verification.

**·** Coordinate with monitoring and evaluation staff to support data quality, activity monitoring, post-distribution monitoring and other required assessments.

**·** Ensure that beneficiary selection, registration and verification processes are transparent, properly documented and consistent with approved eligibility criteria.

**·** Oversee household-level de-duplication and the separate tracking of SHF-funded and IHH-funded assistance, where applicable.

**·** Ensure that feedback and complaints mechanisms are accessible to affected communities and that feedback is documented, referred and addressed through established procedures.

**·** Prepare, review and submit timely, accurate and evidence-based donor reports, internal progress updates and other required project documentation.

**·** Maintain effective project management systems and ensure that implementation records and indicator-tracking tools are regularly updated.

**·** Document implementation challenges, lessons learned and good practices, using monitoring findings to improve programme quality and inform management decisions.

**Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement**

**·** Maintain effective coordination with relevant local authorities, community representatives, service providers and other stakeholders in the targeted locations.

**·** Coordinate with relevant humanitarian coordination mechanisms and sector actors to promote complementarity, information sharing and alignment with identified needs.

**·** Facilitate communication between field teams, technical specialists and support departments to resolve implementation challenges.

**·** Support coordination with relevant stakeholders involved in shelter rehabilitation, food security, agricultural livelihoods, bakery operations and irrigation-related activities.

**·** Ensure that community engagement is conducted transparently and that beneficiaries receive clear information about project objectives, eligibility criteria, assistance modalities and feedback channels.

**Protection, Safeguarding and Risk Management**

**·** Ensure that protection mainstreaming, gender sensitivity, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations and the principle of do no harm are integrated throughout project implementation.

**·** Work with the designated GBV Programme Focal Point to identify and mitigate potential gender-based violence risks associated with project activities.

**·** Ensure compliance with IHH safeguarding policies, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), the organizational code of conduct and relevant reporting procedures.

**·** Promote safe, dignified and non-discriminatory access to project assistance, with particular attention to vulnerable and marginalized groups.

**·** Identify and monitor operational, security, access, financial, procurement and implementation risks, and develop appropriate mitigation measures.

**·** Ensure that safeguarding concerns, protection risks and other incidents are reported and referred through established organizational channels.

**·** Promote a culture of accountability, integrity, transparency and responsible use of humanitarian resources.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

**·** Bachelor's degree in engineering, agriculture, economics, business administration, project management, international development or another relevant discipline. A master's degree is an advantage.

**·** At least five years of progressively responsible experience in similar positions within the humanitarian sector, including project planning, implementation, team management, budget monitoring and donor reporting.

**·** Demonstrated experience in at least one of the following sectors: Shelter and Non-Food Items (SNFI) or Food Security and Agriculture/Livelihoods (FSAL). Experience in both sectors is highly preferred.

**·** Proven experience managing donor-funded humanitarian projects and ensuring compliance with organizational policies, approved budgets and donor requirements.

**·** Experience in work planning, indicator tracking, financial monitoring, risk management and preparation of donor reports.

**·** Demonstrated ability to supervise multidisciplinary teams and coordinate effectively with technical and support departments.

**·** Experience working with local authorities, community representatives, contractors, service providers and humanitarian coordination mechanisms in Syria.

**·** Experience with OCHA or the Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF) is highly desirable.

**·** Familiarity with shelter rehabilitation, cash-based assistance, food security, agricultural livelihoods or early-recovery programming is an advantage.

**·** Strong organizational, analytical, leadership, communication and problem-solving skills.

**·** Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word. Familiarity with project monitoring and digital data-collection tools is an advantage.

**·** Fluency in Arabic and excellent proficiency in English, both written and spoken, are essential. Knowledge of Turkish is an advantage.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

**·** Project planning, implementation and results-based management.

**·** Team leadership, staff supervision and multidisciplinary coordination.

**·** Budget monitoring, financial accountability and donor compliance.

**·** Analytical thinking, risk management and problem-solving.

**·** Effective communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement.

**·** Monitoring, reporting and evidence-based decision-making.

**·** Accountability, integrity, confidentiality and commitment to humanitarian principles.

**·** Adaptability and the ability to manage competing priorities in a complex operational environment.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

The position will be based at the IHH Idlib Office, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, as required by project implementation needs. The successful candidate must be able to coordinate effectively with field teams and travel to project locations when required.

jobs.title: Business Support Assistant to the Deputy Regional Director
jobs.body:
**DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS**

10 November 2026-23:59-GMT-05:00 Eastern Standard Time (Panama)

*WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability.*

**ABOUT WFP**

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks.

At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: [https://www.wfp.org](https://www.wfp.org/) and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/c/worldfoodprogramme), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/unwfp/), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/worldfoodprogramme/), [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/WorldFoodProgramme/), [Twitter](https://twitter.com/WFP?ref_src=https://reliefweb.int/twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Eauthor), [TikTok](http://www.tiktok.com/@worldfoodprogramme?lang=en).

**WHY JOIN WFP?**

- WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.
- WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.
- WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.
- A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.
- We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the **Terms and Conditions** section of this vacancy announcement).

**ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT**

This position is based in Panama and reports to Deputy Regional Director.

**THE ROLE**

To deliver a wide range of business support processes and activities for a specific professional area of work, to facilitate effective service delivery.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES** (not all-inclusive, nor exhaustive):  
1\. Collate information for inclusion in reports, documents, and correspondence, to support the effective work of other staff.  
2\. Respond to standard queries and provide timely and accurate guidance.  
3\. Process and manage routine administrative and financial tasks in various functional areas, to contribute to the effective and timely management of resources  
4\. Manage and maintain records and databases, to ensure information is organized and readily available for staff.  
5\. Maintain relationships with a range of individuals through provision of business support to assist in information sharing and service delivery to staff.  
6\. Proof-read reports, documentation, correspondence, etc., making changes in line with established guidelines where appropriate.  
7\. Contribute to improvement of business procedures and processes.  
8\. Collect and perform basic analysis of data to contribute to quality business information management.  
9\. Provide guidance to junior colleagues in performing their duties.

**ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Support the planning and execution of events organized by the Regional Director´s Office, including Leadership meetings and government fora.
- Support business processes related to the implementation of programs and projects led by the Regional Director Office.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:**  
**Education:** Completion of secondary school education. A post-secondary certificate in the related functional area is desirable.

**Experience:** Five or more years of progressively responsible work experience in the relative business stream with experience in general administrative work.

**Knowledge and Skills:**  
• Knowledge of specialized common business practices and methods, gained through relevant technical training and experience.  
• Ability to develop and maintain relationships with a range of individuals in order to provide a high-quality support service.  
• Ability to carry out basic data analysis and independently rectify problems requiring attention.  
• Ability to monitor and record financial transactions.  
• Good communication skills required to give and receive information and work with a variety of individuals.  
• Ability to maintain confidentiality

**Language:** General Service (Headquarters): Fluency (level C) in English language. Fluency (level C) or intermediate knowledge (level B) of another official language may be required depending on the location of the post or area of responsibility.

General Service (Field): Fluency in both oral and written communication in the UN language in use at the duty station and in the duty station’s language, if different.

**TERMS & CONDITIONS:**

Number of openings: 1

Based in: Panama City, Panama

Type of Contract: General Service

Level: 5

Duration: 12 months  
This position is open to Panamanian citizens or residents with a permanent visa.You can consult the UN Salary Scale for Panama page for your reference. Fixed-Term appointments are for a continuous period of one year or more and shall have a specified expiration date. The initial appointment is subject to a probationary period of one year.Successful candidates will be placed in a roster for two (2) years.

**WFP LEADERSHIP FRAMEWORK**

WFP Leadership Framework guides to the common standards of behavior that guide HOW we work together to accomplish our mission.

[**Click here to access WFP Leadership Framework**](http://docs.wfp.org/api/documents/WFP-0000157166/download/)

**REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION**

WFP is committed to supporting individuals with disabilities by providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process. If you require a reasonable accommodation, please contact: global.inclusion@wfp.org
