- Participer aux processus de diligence raisonnable et à la gestion collaborative des risques liés aux partenariats, selon les besoins
- Promouvoir activement la pleine participation des partenaires à la mise en œuvre des programmes dans le cadre des PCM.

**Conformité bailleurs (15%)**

- Fournir aux équipes Programmes et Opérations des orientations techniques courantes afin de garantir que toutes les subventions sont mises en œuvre conformément aux règlements de l'IRC et des bailleurs.
- Coordonner avec le siège sur les questions de conformité spécialisées, selon les besoins.
- Signaler proactivement les problèmes potentiels de conformité à la direction ; collaborer étroitement avec les collègues de conformité du siège pour résoudre toute préoccupation connexe.
- Diffuser les ressources existantes sur la conformité bailleurs et collaborer avec les homologues régionaux pour développer et actualiser les fiches synthétiques de conformité pour chaque subvention.
- En coordination avec le DDP et l’équipe communication, contribuer à garantir une visibilité appropriée et efficace de l'IRC et des bailleurs sur les sites et dans les supports du programme.

**Rapportage (10%)**

- Superviser le développement et la remise de tous les rapports internes et externes, en collaboration avec les départements Programmes, Finance et MEAL.
- Maintenir un tableau de suivi des rapports complet et communiquer régulièrement avec les membres d'équipe concernés au sujet des échéances à venir et des exigences spécifiques de chaque rapport.
- Diriger la production de rapports de haute qualité et bien rédigés répondant aux exigences des bailleurs et de l'IRC.
- Réviser minutieusement et confirmer que tous les rapports et documents complémentaires sont complets et exacts.
- Coordonner les révisions et approbations du siège et des unités techniques avant soumission aux bailleurs.
- Garantir le respect strict des échéances internes et des bailleurs.

**Leadership départemental et gestion du personnel (15%)**

- Diriger les unités Subventions et Partenariats et offrir des opportunités de développement professionnel au personnel selon les besoins.
- Assurer une délimitation claire des rôles et responsabilités et une répartition logique du portefeuille entre les membres de l'équipe.
- Coordonner la gestion de la performance au sein du département et favoriser une culture de haute performance à travers l'engagement et la redevabilité du personnel.
- Identifier et soutenir le renforcement des capacités de l'équipe Subventions et partenariats et, sur demande, des autres membres du personnel, afin qu'ils comprennent les processus de subventions de l'IRC.
- Superviser le recrutement de nouveau personnel selon les besoins. Assurer un accueil,une intégration et une formation complets pour les nouvelles recrues

**Autre**

Toute autre tâche pertinente assignée par le superviseur afin de faire progresser les programmes de l'IRC

**Exigences du poste**

- Expérience significative en gestion de subventions humanitaires dans un environnement multi-bailleurs et multisectoriel, incluant la supervision de portefeuilles de subventions de grande envergure.
- Expérience démontrée dans un rôle de coordination interdépartementale et capacité à communiquer avec un ensemble de parties prenantes et à équilibrer leurs priorités.
- Vaste expérience dans le pilotage du développement de propositions de financement multisectorielles de grande envergure.
- Compétences avancées en rédaction et compilation de rapports bailleurs, y compris la coordination des contributions et le développement de documents complexes entre différents départements.
- Connaissance approfondie de la conformité des bailleurs institutionnels requise. La connaissance des exigences de DG INTPA, ECHO, SV, UNHCR, UNICEF, UNFPA constitue un atout majeur.
- Excellentes compétences en expression, rédaction et édition requises, en anglais comme en français. Capacité à rédiger et éditer des documents détaillés pour soumission aux bailleurs avec un minimum de supervision.
- Expérience préalable dans un contexte de conflit ou de crise prolongée souhaitée.
- Excellentes compétences en planification et en organisation. Capacité à prioriser et à suivre plusieurs activités et échéances simultanément.
- Excellentes compétences interpersonnelles et attitude positive démontrée, permettant un engagement constructif avec les départements programmatiques et supports.
- Excellente maîtrise de la suite MS Office et des outils d'intelligence artificielle d'usage courant.
- Capacité à travailler de manière autonome ainsi qu'au sein d'une équipe dynamique et transversale.

**Environnement de travail** ***:***

**Sécurité et logement :** Le/la Coordinateur/trice des Subventions et Partenariats sera basé(e) à Bujumbura, avec des déplacements occasionnels sur le terrain où l'IRC met en œuvre ses projets. La situation sécuritaire au Burundi est stable, même si parfois quelques alertes mineures surviennent en lien avec le conflit en cours en RDC. Les modalités de logement seront précisées par le bureau pays conformément à sa politique en vigueur.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Administrative Assistant, Policy & Advocacy and Marketing & Mobilization
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background**  
Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**External Relations**

The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions: Private fundraising, Mobilization & Marketing, Policy & Advocacy and Operations & Analytics. To enable IRC to deliver our Strategy100 commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance our ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally.

**The Purpose of the Role**

The Admin Assistant is a critical member of the team and we are seeking dynamic Administrative Assistant to support the administrative and logistical needs of the VP of Policy & Advocacy and the VP of Marketing & Mobilization. The role varies in what it covers and will suit somebody good at prioritizing effectively, multi-tasking and working autonomously. The right candidate can make judgements on what is important, will have the ability to solve problems, be efficient, diplomatic and have the inter-personal skills to deal with senior staff, colleagues and networks internationally.

***Support to the VP of Policy & Advocacy and the VP of Marketing & Mobilization - (50%)***

- Support the daily workflow of the VP of Policy & Advocacy and the VP of Marketing & Mobilization including handling appointments and complex calendar management
- Coordinate international travel as needed, including travel briefs, flights, accommodation, visa application and ground transportation
- Collate and submit expense reports, purchase orders, contract payments and other finance transactions for approval. Support department-wide rollout of systems and processes related to expensing
- Provide finance operations support including vendor onboarding, invoice/PO/payment follow-up, workflow approval monitoring in Integra, and basic budget coding guidance as needed.

***Team administrative support and coordination (50%)***

- Schedule department/team meetings included reserving conference rooms and setting up IT for meetings
- Manage onboarding materials for new staff (includes onboarding experience, coordination with IT and office services, integra training admin paperwork, maintaining docs, email distribution lists, internal newsletter, and IRC policy and process)
- Maintain and update key team-wide materials (e.g., org charts, onboarding materials, and internal intranet/team pages) to ensure accuracy with staffing and structural changes.
- Develop collaborative relationships with the teams
- Coordinate staff offboarding logistics including equipment return and timely updates to access, distribution lists, Teams, and reference materials.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:**

**Indirect reporting: Other internal and/or external contacts:** Works closely with other colleagues and departments across the organization.

**Candidate Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Bachelor’s degree preferred but not required.

***Work Experience:***

- At least one year in a fast-paced office setting (internship experience counts too!)

***Preferred:***

- Experience working in a non-profit development department
- Prior experience working as an administrative assistant
- Interest in a fundraising career
- Experience working with high net-worth individuals and/or senior partners a plus

**Demonstrated Skills and Proficiencies:**

Minimum

- Work successfully in a sophisticated, fast-paced organization serving multiple partners
- Experience with Outlook email and calendar and familiarity with complex scheduling
- Solid Microsoft Office, database management, and Adobe Acrobat Pro experience
- Have a can-do attitude with a flexible disposition to handle fast-paced, shifting priorities
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, interacting with a variety of internal and external contacts with confidence and poise
- Strong listening skills and the ability to accurately follow guidance
- Outstanding attention to detail and dedication to timelines
- Ability and interest to work both independently and in a multifaceted, cross-functional team structure
- Ability to handle change in a proactive and positive manner
- Dedication to respect and maintain confidentiality of donor and employee information

**Working Environment:** This role is hybrid and requires the ability to work on-site in the NYC office or Remote working. Applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation:** ($21-26/hour). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Tax Site Coordinator
Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor
jobs.body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Background/IRC Summary:**  Each year the IRC in New York provides support to more than 1500 refugee, asylee and other humanitarian entrants seeking to start new lives in the New York City area. The IRC in New York aims to help these clients achieve self-sufficiency and adapt to and become engaged citizens of their new communities. The Education & Learning unit strives to serve the entire family unit, and the need all family members have for access to relevant educational opportunities in order to thrive in the U.S.

**Job Overview/Summary:** The Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor coordinates educational programming for newcomer youth, including planning, implementation, and reporting for 2-4 Youth Education Programs, including but not limited to World Explorers, Youth ESOL, Mini-NYSA, and Tutoring. The Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor collaborates closely with the other supervisors and Youth Education Manager to ensure all programs integrate best practices for teaching and tutoring English Language Learners and students with interrupted education, as well as social-emotional learning principles, and to ensure that IRC NY’s Youth Education goals and objectives are accomplished using a holistic, collaborative approach, in partnership with school staff, caregivers, and newcomer youth themselves.

In addition, the Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor will steward relevant partnerships for the Youth Education Department as needed to ensure program implementation. This will include coordinating with community-based organizations for collaboration and locations.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Oversee 2-4 youth programs including but not limited to Work Explorers, Youth ESOL, and other programs as needed.
- Develop logical framework and program design in alignment with IRC Outcomes and Evidence Framework for all programming in consultation with the M&E specialist
- Oversee recruitment of all staff, interns, and volunteers needed for programs
- Manage 2-3 Youth Education Coordinators and Specialists responsible for program implementation
- Ensure all programming follows all IRC policies and procedures, particularly concerning child safeguarding
- Design and implement opportunities for parent/caregiver engagement
- Oversee planning of all programs, including but not limited to space allocation and field trips.
- Manage participant recruitment, retention, attendance, and family engagement
- Oversee Monitoring and evaluation for all programs
- Manage program files and databases (enrollment, attendance, outcomes monitoring); maintain accurate and complete records according to IRC and funder policies
- Implement all programs in accordance with the IRC Multi-Tiered Systems of Support
- Serve as a school leader for the Newcomer Youth Summer Academy, responsible for planning, staff and volunteer recruitment, hiring, and training
- Supervise program Academic Lead Teachers, Classroom Culture Lead Teachers, SEL Teacher and Physical Education Teacher
- Oversee teachers to coordinate, plan and develop a 6 week culturally responsive and age-appropriate curriculum, lesson plans and assessment tools using student centered teaching methodologies for English Language Learners
- Ensure effective implementation of IRC’s Multi-tiered System of Support
- Design progress report and report card templates and coordinate related systems of data collection and dissemination
- Plan and coordinate caregiver and teacher conferences
- Conduct teacher observations and coaching using the IRC Framework for Effective Teaching
- Co-lead and plan weekly community events and student award ceremonies in collaboration with other Deans
- Provide technical assistance to internal IRC programs (such as mini academies, School Success Coaching) as well as to external subgrantee organizations
- Deliver workshops on supporting refugee and immigrant students to NYC schools and other community based organizations
- Coordinate with community based organizations as needed for program implementation with consultation with the Youth Education Manager
- Maintain existing partnerships as well as seek out new partnerships that align with Youth Education Department goals
- Prepare internal and external reports for programs supervised
- Ensure program data is consistently collected and entered in relevant databases
- Other related duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

- Master’s degree in education or related field required
- Must be available on Saturdays as needed to oversee youth programs
- A minimum of 2 years’ professional experience working with children and youth, specifically in the context of educational and social programs, required. Teaching certification and experience in the NYC public school system desirable.
- Experience as Head of Teaching, Instructional Coach, or School Leader, highly desirable
- Responsive Classrooms and/or Restorative Justice trained, highly desirable
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations, highly desirable
- Proven success planning and delivering creative and engaging curricula for beginner to intermediate ELLs
- Cultural competency training experience, desirable
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead in a way that recognizes that IRC’s work is best accomplished through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives
- Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills
- Fluent in MS Office applications, especially MS Excel
- Organized, responsible, and flexible: able to maintain responsibility for multiple tasks in the context of a diverse, fast-paced work environment and maintain composure under pressure
- Fluency in a second language highly desired (such as: Spanish, Dari, Pashto, Arabic, French, Haitian-Creole)

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, with the potential for remote work on a limited basis.
- Occasional weekend and/or evening work required.
- Staff are required to adhere to IRC’s COVID risk mitigation policies, which may include masking, physical distancing, enhanced hygiene practices, symptom screening, and isolation and quarantine when needed. IRC policies may be stricter than federal, state, or local level policies.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $72,700/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement
jobs.body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to humanitarian crises in over 40 countries and in communities across the United States and Europe, helping people whose lives have been shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and rebuild their futures.

Global Procurement, within the Global Supply Chain function, leads sourcing strategy, category management, and supplier management for the organization. As IRC continues to test and adopt new technology to support its mission, Global Procurement is establishing a dedicated Procurement Manager role to provide procurement capacity for emerging technology and digital innovation.

**Position Overview**

The Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement supports fast-moving technology sourcing needs across IRC, with a focus on early-stage digital innovation, pilots, proofs of concept, trials, and emerging tools. The role helps teams test and evaluate new technology quickly while maintaining procurement discipline, vendor due diligence, risk review, documentation, and compliance.

For this role, “digital innovation” refers to early-stage, small-scale, fast-moving technology initiatives where IRC teams are testing a new idea, tool, platform, vendor, or digital approach before deciding whether to scale. The portfolio covers AI and generative AI tools where applicable, SaaS and digital platforms, automation, data and analytics, migration and testing tools, cybersecurity tools, collaboration platforms, digital service delivery tools, field and mobile technology, low-code and no-code platforms, and other emerging digital solutions.

This role is an execution-focused, hands-on individual contributor role. It enables IRC to move quickly on emerging technology and digital innovation requests without bypassing procurement controls, vendor due diligence, information security, data protection, legal review, donor compliance, or documentation requirements. The Procurement Manager serves as the day-to-day procurement focal point for these requests

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Sourcing Execution**

- Provide hands-on sourcing support for pilots, trials, proofs of concept, small-scale SaaS, emerging vendors, startup-style tools, and digital innovation requests across IRC.
- Execute sourcing activities in line with the IT category strategy and under the guidance of the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Conduct early market scans and market intelligence for emerging tools, vendors, pricing models, and digital innovation categories.
- Support requirements gathering, supplier identification, RFI/RFQ/RFP preparation, evaluation support, award recommendation, and contract finalization.
- Build supplier visibility for innovation and emerging technology vendors, including startup and niche providers that may later become larger enterprise solutions.
- Help bring new tools into proper procurement channels, reducing shadow IT, credit-card purchasing, and unmanaged technology spend.
- Support SaaS rationalization, renewal planning, demand management, and license optimization at the innovation and pilot tier.
- Help business teams translate technical needs into clear scopes of work, evaluation criteria, and vendor questions.

**B. Pilot, Trial, and Proof-of-Concept Procurement Frameworks**

- Build and maintain a lightweight, repeatable procurement pathway for pilots, trials, and proofs of concept.
- Develop checklists, decision tools, and methodology for short-term technology engagements.
- Define the minimum documentation required before a pilot, trial, or proof of concept can begin.
- Maintain clear approval checkpoints and escalation criteria so teams understand when a pilot can proceed and when it requires further review.
- Track emerging technology requests from intake through pilot, decision, and possible scale-up.
- Ensure required reviews and approvals are completed and all necessary checks are documented before tools are tested or used.
- Help document whether a pilot should end, continue, scale, or move into a formal sourcing process.
- Coordinate NDAs and pre-procurement documentation when teams need to test or evaluate multiple tools before selecting a vendor.
- Ensure pilots and trials are set up in a way that allows long-term success if IRC later moves to a larger phase or formal sourcing process.

**C. AI-Enabled and High-Risk Technology Procurement Support**

- Support sourcing for AI-enabled tools as part of the broader emerging technology portfolio, applied only when AI functionality is in scope.
- For AI-enabled tools, support the application of IRC’s AI assessment requirements, including use-case risk classification, provider/deployer determination, GenAI tool checks, and required approvals.
- Coordinate with the AI Governance and Risk Committee and AI Department Focal Points when applicable.
- Identify and escalate sourcing requests that may involve high-risk technology, AI functionality, personal information, confidential data, client-facing tools, cybersecurity concerns, or unapproved tools.
- Support procurement documentation for AI-enabled tools, including evidence of approvals, vendor assessments, risk reviews, and contract requirements.

**D. Vendor Due Diligence, Risk Review, and Documentation**

- Coordinate required vendor risk assessments (VRA) and due diligence across cybersecurity, privacy and data protection, legal, donor compliance, sanctions and ATC screening, financial viability, implementation risk, integration risk, operational support model, and vendor lock-in and exit risk.
- Coordinate with Information Security, Data Protection, Office of General Counsel, Risk and Compliance, and Finance to ensure required reviews are completed before pilots, trials, awards, or contract signature.
- Ensure procurement files are complete, audit-ready, and aligned with IRC sourcing policy and donor requirements.
- Support compliance with institutional donor requirements that may affect technology, AI, data hosting, data residency, and vendor selection.
- Track and follow up on missing documentation, approvals, vendor information, and risk reviews.

**E. Tool and Vendor Visibility**

- Maintain or support a list of emerging technology tools and vendors, indicating status (under review, in pilot, approved, rejected, expired) and the approved use case for each tool.
- Document the business owner, contract status, contract dates, and renewal timing for each tool.
- Document what each tool is approved for and what use would require additional approval or new procurement action.
- Help connect business owners, end users, IT, Procurement, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance around emerging technology tools and vendors.
- Reduce situations where approved tools are used in non-approved ways, and flag misuse for review.

**F. Contracting and Commercial Support**

- Support commercial negotiation and contracting across the emerging technology portfolio, including NDAs, trial agreements, pilot agreements, proof-of-concept agreements, SaaS agreements, subscriptions, software licenses, cloud services, implementation services, and renewals.
- Review pricing models, including seat-based licensing, usage-based pricing, token usage, API calls, implementation fees, renewal escalators, and support fees, and provide commercial analysis.
- Coordinate with Legal, IT, Finance, and business owners to ensure contracts include appropriate terms on data protection, confidentiality, intellectual property, service levels, audit rights, incident reporting, termination, data return, and exit provisions.
- For AI-enabled tools, ensure contracts also address AI-generated outputs, model training restrictions, and AI-specific risk allocation.
- Support renewal planning and help prevent last-minute renewals or unplanned vendor commitments.

**G. Stakeholder Engagement and Service Support**

- Provide practical, service-oriented procurement support to teams exploring new tools, pilots, digital services, automation platforms, AI solutions, or other emerging technology.
- Help stakeholders move through the procurement process without unnecessary delays, while maintaining compliance and risk controls.
- Coordinate between business owners, IT owners, Procurement, end users, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance to ensure tool usage remains aligned with approved scope, contract terms, procurement files, risk approvals, and any applicable usage guidelines.
- Reduce workarounds, shadow IT, and credit-card purchasing by making the correct procurement process easier to follow.
- Guide stakeholders on procurement routes, required documentation, approval steps, and realistic timelines for emerging technology procurement.
- Support early engagement with teams considering new tools, pilots, or digital approaches, before commitments are made to vendors.

**H. Reporting and Continuous Improvement**

- Track the emerging technology sourcing pipeline, renewal calendar, cycle time, savings, risk flags, documentation completion, and approval status.
- Track pilot outcomes (end, continue, scale, or formal sourcing) and capture lessons learned.
- Track user adoption issues, non-approved usage of approved tools, and other compliance signals, and surface these to the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Identify recurring issues in emerging technology sourcing and recommend improvements to frameworks, checklists, templates, and decision tools.
- Contribute to knowledge sharing across Global Procurement on emerging technology, SaaS, AI, and digital innovation sourcing practices.
- Support the role’s value contribution by improving visibility over fast-moving technology spend, reducing duplicated tools, undocumented pilots, and audit risk.

**Key Working Relationships**

- **Reports to:** Senior Category Manager, IT.
- **Internal:** Office of the CIO and IT teams; Senior Category Manager, IT; Information Security; Data Protection; Office of General Counsel; Ethics and Compliance; Risk and Compliance; Finance; Airbel Impact Lab; Data and Analytics; External Relations; Country Program supply chain and innovation leads; program innovation teams; fundraising and digital teams; AI Governance and Risk Committee when applicable; Global Procurement peers.
- **External:** Emerging technology vendors and resellers; SaaS, cloud, cybersecurity, automation, data, and AI providers; startup and niche technology vendors; industry analysts; peer humanitarian and development organizations.

**Minimum Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in procurement, supply chain, business administration, information technology, engineering, law, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered.
- Minimum 5 to 7 years of procurement, sourcing, contract management, or vendor management experience.
- Of the required 5 to 7 years above, at least 3 years must be in IT procurement, SaaS and software sourcing, software licensing, cloud services, cybersecurity tools, data platforms, or similar technology categories.
- Experience supporting pilots, trials, proofs of concept, or other early-stage technology procurement activities.
- Experience coordinating vendor due diligence and technology risk reviews, including cybersecurity, data protection, financial, and operational risk.
- Experience supporting sourcing events, supplier evaluations, commercial analysis, and contract coordination.
- Good understanding of technology procurement risks, including data protection, information security, intellectual property, software licensing, vendor lock-in, and third-party risk.
- Ability to work effectively with IT, Legal, Information Security, Data Protection, Finance, and business teams.
- Demonstrated ability to work quickly while maintaining compliance, controls, and documentation standards.
- Strong stakeholder service orientation and ability to balance procurement standards with customer needs.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Good judgment and ability to balance speed, compliance, risk, and stakeholder needs.
- Experience in an NGO, donor-funded organization, humanitarian agency, UN agency, or complex global organization.
- Knowledge of donor compliance requirements such as USAID/BHA, FCDO, ECHO, EU, UN agencies, or private foundations.
- Professional certification such as CIPS, CPSM, or equivalent, completed or in progress.
- Working knowledge of French, Spanish, or Arabic is an advantage.

**Working Environment**

Flexible (IRC hub city preferred; remote considered). Travel of up to 10% domestically and internationally, including occasional travel to IRC country offices.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Lebanon, Germany, Kenya, Pakistan, and Jordan.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Middle East Humanitarian Appeal Evaluation
jobs.body:
## **About The Role**

**Middle East Humanitarian Appeal Evaluation Consultant**

**Location: Gaza** (across accessible governorates and via remote reach where physical access is prohibited) and **Lebanon** (national-level analysis, with reference to operational areas of South Lebanon, Nabatieh, Baalbek-Hermel and Mount Lebanon as relevant)

**Rate: £60,000 total budget (inclusive of expenses) - maximum of £500 per individual per day.**

**Duration: Approximately 16 weeks (starting ideally from December 2026 until March 2027)**

**Contract: Self-employed Consultant / Contractor / Sole Trader / Limited Liability Companies**

**Please note:** We welcome applications from both **UK-based and overseas contractors**.

*Can you help shape the future of humanitarian response in the Middle East?*

We're seeking an experienced and insightful Humanitarian Evaluation Consultant to lead an independent evaluation of the British Red Cross Middle East Humanitarian Appeal response in Gaza and Lebanon.

This consultancy presents a unique opportunity to assess the effectiveness, relevance, coherence and impact of humanitarian interventions delivered in response to one of the most significant humanitarian crises in recent years. The successful consultant will be responsible for proposing and applying an appropriate evaluation methodology and delivering independent, evidence-based findings and recommendations. Working closely with key stakeholders, you will help improve future humanitarian programming and support better outcomes for affected communities.

We're looking for an experienced evaluator who can work independently, navigate complex operating environments and deliver robust, high-quality analysis that informs strategic decision-making.

Please refer to the Terms of Reference (ToR) for full details of the assignment, including proposal submission requirements, evaluation scope and deliverables.

**What will a day in the life of a MEHA Evaluation Consultant involve?**

- Leading the design and delivery of an independent evaluation of humanitarian programmes across Gaza and Lebanon.
- Developing evaluation methodologies, data collection tools and analytical approaches aligned with recognised humanitarian evaluation standards.
- Conducting document reviews, stakeholder consultations, interviews, focus groups and data analysis to generate evidence-based findings.
- Producing high-quality reports, facilitating validation workshops and presenting recommendations to a range of humanitarian stakeholders.

**To be a successful MEHA Evaluation Consultant, what will you need?**

- Significant experience leading complex evaluations within humanitarian, international development, emergency response or recovery programmes.
- Strong understanding of humanitarian principles, evaluation methodologies, MEAL frameworks and internationally recognised evaluation standards.
- Demonstrable experience evaluating health, cash assistance, humanitarian response, resilience or related programmes in complex contexts.
- Excellent research, analysis, report-writing and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to turn complex findings into clear and actionable recommendations.

**It would also be advantageous if you met the following desirable criteria:**

- Previous experience working in or evaluating programmes in the Middle East.
- Familiarity with Red Cross / Red Crescent Movement.
- Experience managing remote or hybrid evaluation approaches in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
- Proficiency in Arabic, or access to appropriately qualified language support.

**Interested?** The **closing** **date** for applications is 23.59 on **Wednesday 4th November**.

This is a short-term consultancy, **not** a salaried staff role. We’re looking for an experienced contractor with a proven track record in humanitarian evaluation, research and learning. You **must** be self-employed and operating as an independent contractor or consultancy; Self-employed workers are not paid through PAYE, and they do not have the rights and responsibilities of an employee.

**Together, we are the world's emergency responders**

jobs.title: National Professional Officer (Health Financing)
jobs.body:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

WHO’s work in countries operationalizes the General Programme of Work (GPW14) and the European Programme of Work 2025-2029 (EPW2). GPW14 focuses on accelerating progress toward Health for All by strengthening systems for health, improving access to essential services, advancing preparedness and resilience, and reducing health inequalities. EPW2, endorsed at RC75 following extensive consultation with Member States, reaffirms WHO/Europe’s role in bringing unique value to countries through five core functions:  
1\.  **International knowledge hub for health** – providing authoritative evidence, norms, policies and best practices from across the Region and globally to inform national public health decision-making.  
2\. **Impartial coordinator for everyone’s health** – convening national stakeholders and partners to align strategies and support coherent, multisectoral responses to shared health challenges.  
3\. **Leader in tracking and managing cross-border health threats** – supporting surveillance, preparedness, and coordinated action on public health emergencies in line with the Preparedness 2.0 agenda.  
4\. **Driver of health system transformation** – advising national authorities on evidence-informed reforms and policies that strengthen health systems and improve performance.  
5\. **Voice for health equity** – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

With the overall aim of advancing progress towards Universal Health Coverage, promoting good practices in health financing and reducing financial hardship, the incumbent leads WHO's health financing work in Ukraine and provides technical advice to national counterparts on health financing policy and reform.

Key duties:   
1\. Coordinate and provide technical leadership for the design, implementation and monitoring of WHO's health financing workstream, as programmed in the Country Cooperation Strategy (CCS) Biennial Collaborative Agreement (BCA), including WHO's contribution to health sector coordination and national policy dialogue.   
2\. Provide technical advice to the Ministry of Health, the National Health Service of Ukraine (NHSU) and other national partners on the development, implementation and evaluation of health financing policies and reforms at national and subnational levels, including strategic purchasing, the design of the Programme of Medical Guarantees, public financial management, to improve health system performance, including financial protection and progress towards universal health coverage.  
3\. Identify and guide priority areas for collaboration, capacity development and technical assistance in health financing, and translate these priorities into deliverable and costed workplans under the CCS BCA and donor-financed projects.  
4\. Lead and oversee the generation and use of evidence to support health financing policy and reform. This includes overseeing the analysis of health financing data and the planning, commissioning and quality assurance of studies, policy briefs, situation analyses, reports and other technical products on health financing, health system performance, service coverage and aid effectiveness. Work closely with WHO technical programmes to ensure that evidence generated is used to inform policy advice and dialogue, as well as the monitoring and evaluation of health financing reforms.  
5\. Lead and oversee the effective and high-quality implementation of health financing activities under donor-financed initiatives and agreed partnerships at country level. Provide technical direction for technical assistance, policy dialogue and capacity development, ensuring that activities are aligned with agreed objectives, priorities and deliverables. Monitor implementation and results and ensure timely and appropriate reporting to relevant stakeholders and donors.  
6\. Represent WHO, as appropriate, in discussions with national authorities, development partners and other stakeholders on health financing. Lead and contribute to technical discussions, coordination mechanisms and policy dialogue, and strengthen collaboration among partners to support coherent implementation of health financing reforms.  
7\. Supervise and provide technical direction to the staff working on health financing. Assign and prioritize work, clarify responsibilities, review the quality and timeliness of technical outputs, provide feedback and guidance, and support their performance and professional development. Ensure effective coordination between their respective areas of work and coherence across the health financing portfolio.  
8\. Contribute to strengthening national capacity in health financing through technical guidance, knowledge sharing and capacity development activities, in collaboration with national institutions and relevant partners.  
9\. Organize and substantively support WHO missions, visits and high-level engagements on health financing, and follow up on agreed recommendations and actions to ensure appropriate implementation.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential:** A university degree (Bachelor's level) in business administration, management, economics or health economics, health policy, public health, social and political sciences, with concentration in health financing.  
**Desirable:** Master's degree or postgraduate degree in any of the above fields.

### Experience

**Essential**: At least five years of professional experience in health systems strengthening, including substantial experience in health financing. Experience working with national health authorities, purchasing agencies, academic institutions, international organizations and/or non-governmental organizations. Demonstrated experience contributing to or providing technical input to national health financing policy processes and policy dialogue.  
**Desirable**: Experience in WHO/UN and international agencies; Experience providing policy advice on health systems strengthening, health financing and health sector reform, particularly in transition, reform or post-crisis settings.

### Functional Skills

- Demonstrated knowledge of health systems and health financing policy in the countries of the WHO European Region, including purchasing, benefit package design, public financial management and financial protection monitoring.
- Proven ability to translate technical analysis into policy advice for senior decision-makers and to formulate technical positions independently.
- Ability to interact appropriately and with credibility with high-level stakeholders, including senior officials and ministers.
- Ability to lead high performing teams. Ability to work within significant uncertainties in a rapidly changing environment and to set priorities with limited supervision.
- Data management and data analysis skills.
- Good computer skills (word processing, spreadsheet, PowerPoint presentations).
- Strong written and oral communication skills, including drafting for policy audiences.
- Emotional intelligence: ability to identify and manage one's own emotions, as well as helping others to do the same.

### WHO Competencies

1\. Teamwork  
2\. Respecting & promoting individual and cultural differences  
3\. Communication  
4\. Moving forward in a changing environment  
5\. Building and promoting partnerships across the Organization and beyond

### Use of Language Skills

**Essential**: Expert knowledge of English. Expert knowledge of Ukrainian.

**Desirable:** Intermediate knowledge of any other UN language.

## REMUNERATION

Remuneration comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 64,825 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable) and 30 days of annual leave.

**Link to apply:** [**Job Description - National Professional Officer (Health Financing) (2604631)**](https://careers.who.int/careersection/ex/jobdetail.ftl?job=2604631&tz=GMT%2B03%3A00&tzname=Europe%2FKiev)

jobs.title: Documentary Film Production Consultant
jobs.body:
**Terms of Reference (ToR):** Documentary Film Production Consultant, STRIVE Program – Indonesia

**Location:** Indonesia

**Assignment Date:** Until May 2027

**Contract Type:** Consultant (6 months)

**A. BACKGROUND**

Nurani Perdamaian Indonesia (NPID), through the GCERF, is implementing the Strengthening Rehabilitation and Reintegration and Improve Social Cohesion against Violent Extremism (STRIVE) Program from January 2025 to December 2027.

Implemented in partnership with national and local civil society organizations and in close collaboration with relevant government institutions, the STRIVE Program seeks to strengthen Indonesia's efforts in preventing violent extremism by supporting the reintegration and rehabilitation of returnees, former violent extremist offenders, and individuals at risk, while fostering resilient and inclusive communities. The program is implemented across three primary intervention areas:

- Jakarta
- Bima, West Nusa Tenggara
- Poso, Central Sulawesi

Throughout its implementation, STRIVE has promoted multi-stakeholder collaboration involving government agencies, civil society organizations, community leaders, religious leaders, youth, women, and beneficiaries to strengthen social cohesion and sustainable reintegration.

As the program approaches its completion, NP Indonesia intends to produce a high-quality documentary film that captures its journey, achievements, lessons learned, and the human stories behind the intervention. The documentary is expected to serve as a legacy product, an advocacy tool, and a knowledge resource that highlights the importance of sustained investment in community resilience and reintegration beyond the program period.

**B. PURPOSE**

The purpose of this consultancy is to produce a compelling documentary film that captures the overall implementation and impact of the STRIVE Program while communicating the continued importance of community-based reintegration and resilience-building efforts.

The documentary should present authentic stories, demonstrate evidence of program achievements, and inspire continued collaboration among governments, communities, civil society, and development partners.

**C. OBJECTIVES**

The documentary shall aim to:

1. Document the implementation of the STRIVE Program across Jakarta, Bima, and Poso.
2. Capture stories of transformation among beneficiaries, families, communities, and institutional stakeholders.
3. Showcase collaborative efforts between government institutions, civil society organizations, and local communities.
4. Demonstrate the program's contribution to strengthening community resilience, social cohesion, and sustainable reintegration.
5. Produce a high-quality legacy documentary suitable for advocacy, public communication, knowledge sharing, and future resource mobilization.

**D. SCOPE OF WORK**

The selected consultant shall be responsible for the complete production process, including pre-production, production, and post-production.

**1. Pre-Production**

The consultant shall:

1. Participate in inception meetings with NP Indonesia.
2. Review program documents and communication materials.
3. Develop a creative concept and documentary treatment.
4. Prepare storyline, interview framework, and production schedule.
5. Identify key interviewees together with the program team.
6. Prepare filming plans and logistics.

**2. Production**

The consultant shall conduct field production in:

1. Jakarta
2. Bima, West Nusa Tenggara
3. Poso, Central Sulawesi

The filming should include, but not be limited to:

1. Program implementation activities
2. Beneficiary interviews
3. Family member interviews
4. Community leaders
5. Religious leaders
6. Government representatives
7. Consortium partners
8. Community interactions
9. Environmental and supporting footage
10. Drone footage (where permitted)

The consultant is expected to adopt a cinematic documentary approach that emphasizes authentic storytelling and high-quality visual production.

**3. Post-Production**

The consultant shall:

1. Develop the documentary narrative.
2. Edit all footage.
3. Produce motion graphics and animated statistics where appropriate.
4. Add background music and sound mixing.
5. Prepare English and Bahasa Indonesia subtitles.
6. Incorporate revisions based on feedback from NP Indonesia.
7. Deliver final mastered versions.

**E. DOCUMENTARY APPROACH**

Rather than producing a chronological record of program activities, the documentary should adopt a story-driven, human-centered approach.

The documentary should:

1. Highlight authentic experiences.
2. Balance emotional storytelling with evidence-based program achievements.
3. Showcase collaboration among communities, government institutions, and civil society.
4. Present transformation at individual, community, and institutional levels.
5. Maintain a professional cinematic quality suitable for international audiences.

The documentary should conclude with a forward-looking message that emphasizes the importance of sustaining the gains achieved through the STRIVE Program and continuing collective efforts toward resilient communities.

**F. DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE**

The consultant shall deliver:

**Deliverables**

- One documentary film.
- One shortened version of the documentary film.
- One promotional trailer.
- Five short social media video clips.
- Subtitles in English and Bahasa Indonesia.
- High-resolution photographs from field production.
- All raw video footage.
- Editable project files, upon request.

**Timeline**

- **December:** Procurement process, inception meeting, desk review, development of the creative concept and storyline, preparation of the interview list, shooting plan, and logistics.
- **January to March:** Field production in Jakarta, Bima, and Poso.
- **April:** Editing, script writing, motion graphics development, subtitling, music scoring, and preparation of the first cut.
- **May:** Review and revision process, final cut, mastering, and submission of all final deliverables.

**G. CONSULTANT QUALIFICATION**

The consultant or production company should possess:

- Minimum five (5) years of professional experience in documentary film production.
- Demonstrated experience producing documentaries for international development programs, humanitarian organizations, or donor-funded projects.
- Strong storytelling and cinematic production capabilities.
- Proven experience conducting field production in diverse cultural contexts.
- Ability to produce bilingual documentary outputs.
- Availability to travel to all program locations.
- Experience working with government institutions and civil society organizations is considered an asset.

**H. PROPOSAL REQUIREMENTS**

Interested consultants shall submit:  
**1. Technical Proposal**

1. Understanding of the assignment.
2. Proposed documentary concept.
3. Creative treatment.
4. Storytelling approach.
5. Production methodology.
6. Workplan and timeline.
7. Team composition and roles.
8. Relevant portfolio.
9. Risk management approach.

**2. Financial Proposal**

1. Professional fees.
2. Travel costs.
3. Accommodation.
4. Equipment.
5. Editing.
6. Production expenses.
7. Applicable taxes.

**I. BUDGET**

The estimated total production film is **IDR 250,000,000**, from budget lines: CWW.076 Produce a film adaptation based on one Human Interest stories from Poso ( B11.1 )

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector.NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [InterAgency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE**

**We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted** [**here**](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/) **on our website.**

jobs.title: Safety & Security Officer (Ukrainian Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
**Job Title:** Safety & Security Officer (Ukrainian nationals)

**Department:** Safety & Security

**Division:** Operations

**Duty Station:** Mykolaiv, Ukraine

**Line Manager:** Safety & Security Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Full-time

**Overview:**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014/2015 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022. NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**Job Summary:**

The Safety and Security Officer works directly with the Head of Operations and Security to contribute to the safety and security of NP staff in Ukraine. The position will support with analysis and security inputs and will engage directly with programmes teams for security monitoring and guidance. The position contributes to making sure effective safety and security arrangements are in place for NP staff.

The ideal candidate will bring security expertise developed through experience working in the security and/or humanitarian sector. They are focused and driven by a keen interest and personal commitment to civilian protection – the core of NP’s work.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Safety & Security Management**

- Implement and uphold NP safety and security policies, procedures, SOPs, and contingency plans at field and office level.
- Conduct regular security and risk assessments to identify threats, vulnerabilities, and mitigation measures.
- Support the operationalisation of security plans including travel management, incident response, emergency communications, evacuation, relocation, and hibernation procedures.
- Ensure offices, guesthouses, and programme sites meet minimum physical security standards through regular infrastructure and security audits.
- Immediately report and document all security incidents, breaches, threats, or near-misses affecting staff, assets, or operations.

**Operational Support & Staff Movement**

- Provide real-time tracking, monitoring, and oversight of staff and vehicle movements in line with established procedures.
- Ensure vehicles, communications equipment, and personal protective equipment are available, functional, and compliant with minimum standards.
- Work closely with Logistics to identify, procure, and maintain safety and security equipment and resources.

**Information Management & Analysis**

- Collect, verify, analyze, and disseminate security-related information from formal and informal sources.
- Maintain up-to-date records of security incidents, trends, and contextual developments.
- Provide timely security briefings, updates, and advisories to staff and management in response to changes in context.
- Contribute to weekly and monthly security reports relevant to NP areas of operation.

**Training & Capacity Building**

- Deliver regular security briefings, inductions, and awareness sessions for staff.
- Identify security capacity-building needs and support the design and delivery of relevant trainings.
- Train, mentor, and support designated Security Focal Points across field offices.
- Supervise, train, and develop security staff at office or area level where applicable.

**Coordination, Liaison & Access**

- Maintain strong working relationships with NGOs, UN agencies, INSO, security providers, and relevant coordination platforms.
- Liaise with local authorities, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders to support safe access and programme implementation, in line with humanitarian principles.
- Participate in security coordination forums and inter-agency meetings as required.
- Support access analysis and security input for programme planning and expansion into new areas of operation.

**Assessments & Compliance**

- Participate in security assessments for new locations and evolving operational areas.
- Ensure adherence to NP security risk management standards and country-specific SOPs.
- Support senior management in internal security reviews and audits.

**Safeguarding & Conduct**

- Comply with and uphold NP safeguarding policies, including child protection, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), and policies on bullying and harassment.
- Act in accordance with NP Codes of Conduct at all times.

**Critical Interfaces**

- All NP staff and departments.
- Senior Management Team.
- Programme and Operations teams.
- Logistics and Administration.
- External coordination and security actors.

**Qualifications:**

- Post-secondary education in a related field with at least 2 years related work experience or equivalent in work experience.
- Relevant security experience in humanitarian settings / previous experience working with security providers, law enforcement entities, and/or intelligence resources and utilizing information to create and deploy actionable security plans and programs.
- Understanding of current security management good practice.
- Good grasp of various communications technologies commonly used, including VHF radio systems, satellite phones, cell phones, Power Bi, etc.
- Excellent interpersonal, representation and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence, build consensus and develop partnerships.
- Ability to work well under pressure in unstable and frequently changing security environments.
- Training and facilitator skills; ability to support training sessions is a plus.
- Commitment to and understanding of NP’s methodologies, core values and mission.
- Advanced proficiency in written and spoken English, Ukrainian and Russian.
- Computer literacy, particularly in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, databases.
- Valid Ukrainian driving license.
- Knowledge of and commitment to safeguarding, whistleblowing, PSEA and anti-corruption.

**Skills and Competencies:**

**Independent Judgment/Analytical:**

- Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data.
- Ability to manage information with discretion.
- Identify safety and security issues and propose solutions.

**Interpersonal:**

- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and motivate and provide leadership to team and to work and live in a multi-cultural environment.
- Ability to exert solutions-focused, creative behaviour.

**Job Title:** Policy & Advocacy Assistant

**Department:** Advocacy

**Division:** NPUS

**Duty Station:** Washington D.C., U.S. (hybrid)

**Administrative Line Manager:** U.S. Policy and Advocacy Manager

**Technical Line Manager:** U.S. Policy and Advocacy Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Part-time, non-exempt

**OVERVIEW**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

Since 2020, NP has worked alongside local communities in the U.S. to interrupt cycles of violence and build bridges across polarized communities. Responsive to community needs, NP builds relationships with community members, leaders, and organizations to identify risks to safety and ways to work together to keep communities safe through nonviolent strategies. These strategies include protective presence, training, safety planning, and rapid response. This work takes us to demonstrations, marches, courts, voting centers, health facilities, pantries, and other public spaces where people may face violence and intimidation. In partnership with local organizations we help build stronger protection networks, coordinate responses to emerging risks and advance the practice of nonviolent community-led approaches to protection in communities across the country.

**JOB SUMMARY**

Nonviolent Peaceforce U.S. (NPUS) is seeking a Policy and Advocacy Assistant to support NP's Advocacy team within the External Engagement function. The Policy and Advocacy Assistant will support NP’s advocacy to the U.S. government and the broader work of the global Policy and Advocacy team, with a special focus on the federal appropriations process. Under the supervision of the U.S. Policy and Advocacy Manager the Policy and Advocacy Assistant will represent NP in coalition meetings, submit congressional appropriations requests, and meet with congressional staffers to educate on the importance of key foreign assistance funds. The role will support NP’s mission and advocacy for the use of UCP methodologies through legislative, policy, and other advocacy opportunities. Training and feedback will be provided.

These principles and beliefs guide our actions and relationships, supporting our mission to protect civilians in violent conflicts through unarmed strategies

**QUALIFICATIONS**
