A travers une approche multisectorielle d’urgence en abris/AME, CCCM et Protection, Acted répond aux besoins vitaux des déplacés sur les sites informels et les camps d’accueil.

Enfin, Acted intervient régulièrement en réponse aux chocs cycliques, tels que la soudure et les inondations, particulièrement dévastatrices.

Les actions d’Acted au Tchad reposent sur une expertise technique multisectorielle reconnue, une capacité de déploiement rapide, une approche basée sur les données, une forte acceptance locale, et la participation accrue des communautés.

## Rôle et responsabilités principales

Le/la Responsable projet, sous la conduite opérationnelle du Coordinateur de zone et la conduite technique du Coordinateur technique des programmes est responsable d’assurer la mise en œuvre du projet d’Acted. Le/la Responsable projet supervise les opérations de terrain et assure l’achèvement effectif et dans les délais des activités ; il/elle assure également des restitutions de qualité et la réalisation des résultats avec un maximum d’impact pour les bénéficiaires. Le/la Responsable projet supervise le staff projet, dans la gestion au jour le jour de tous les aspects du projet et fait le lien avec les départements internes pertinents, les partenaires externes et les parties prenantes du projet.

***Principales Responsabilités***

1\. Planification des projets

2\. Suivi de mise en œuvre des projets

3\. Administration et gestion opérationnelle de mise en œuvre du projet

- *Finances*
- *Logistique*
- *Administration/RH*
- *Transparence*
- *Sécurité*

4\. Relations externes

5\. Contrôle qualité

6\. Rapports

## Qualifications et compétences requises

- Expérience en lien avec le type de projet requise, dans un contexte d’urgence et/ou de développement
- Une expérience de travail avec des bailleurs de fond institutionnels est un plus
- Expérience en gestion de budget
- Capacité à coordonner et gérer une équipe
- Capacité à travailler de manière indépendante et créative sur le terrain et en capitale
- Excellente expression orale et écrite
- Forte habilité à travailler dans un contexte interculturel

## Conditions

- Salaire défini par la grille des salaires Acted en fonction du niveau d’études, de l’expertise, du niveau de sécurité et du niveau d’expérience : entre 2600 et 2800€ net mensuel (avant impôts sur le revenu)
- Indemnité mensuelle de frais de vie 300$
- Logement en guesthouse et nourriture pris en charge par Acted
- Sécurité sociale, mutuelle (MSH) et assistance rapatriement (SOS International) pris en charge par Acted
- Transport vers la mission et billet retour totalement pris en charge tous les 6 mois (vers l’adresse spécifiée sur le contrat de travail)
- Frais de visa pris en charge par Acted
- R&R tous les 3 mois (billet d’avion pris en charge jusqu’à 500$ + indemnité supplémentaire de 200$)
- Une semaine de préparation au départ comprenant 4 jours de formation sécurité en immersion
- Possibilité d’avoir un appel de 30minutes avec un.e consultant.e en fiscalité
- Soutien psychologique (rendez-vous avec un.e professionnel.le)
- Ce poste est classé comme un poste international dans la grille de recrutement d’Acted. L’éligibilité à un contrat international est donc requise.

jobs.title: MEAL Coordinator
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**ORGANIZATIONAL BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home.

The IRC began planning to reopen an oPt country program in mid-2022 and launched an emergency response in Gaza in October 2023. The organization is currently supporting a network of local partners in both Gaza and the West Bank to sustain critical health, protection, food security, cash, education, and early childhood development interventions. The IRC is working to scale its emergency response while building a longer-term oPt country program in parallel. This effort is being jointly managed by the Emergencies Unit (EmU) and the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, with a view to eventually transition the country program fully under the MENA region.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The MEAL Coordinator will provide national leadership and management oversight to ensure that the oPt country program develops and achieves MEAL commitments.

This position is responsible to ensure that data and learning are applied towards continuous improvements in program quality and evidence-based program design. The MEAL Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and data management systems are in place, sufficiently resourced, and successfully implemented from collection to visualization. Core to this will be providing strategic direction to, and harmonization of, MEAL efforts in both West Bank and Gaza operations with focus on supporting partners’ approaches to MEAL.

The Coordinator will ensure that MEAL principles are integrated into every step of the project cycle. In support of these goals, this position provides technical assistance, facilitates capacity sharing, and ensures ongoing mentoring and training in MEAL concepts for IRC and partner staff including evidence-based program design and continuous improvements of program quality based on data, feedback, and learning.

The MEAL Coordinator reports to the Deputy Director for Programs and is supported technically by the Emergency MEAL technical Advisor.

Position is based in Ramallah, with travel to Amman & Gaza as needed.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Technical Oversight**

- Provide technical leadership to ensure strong data systems and processes throughout the project cycle for both IRC and partner projects, from design and implementation to close-out and learning.
- Use learning and evidence from internal and external sources to inform proposal design and theories of change.
- Participate in partner capacity assessments and evaluate the strength of partners’ MEAL systems. Identify actionable areas for learning and technical support.
- Develop and operationalize logical frameworks, MEAL plans, data collection tools, reach tracking tools, processes for data management, client feedback approaches, quality checks and audits, and real-time data visualization.
- Provide MEAL technical assistance to program teams and partners during the design and inception stages, including support with logframes, indicator selection and measurement methodologies, and the development of data collection plans and tools.
- Develop a MEAL budget and staffing structure for all projects that is responsive to planned activities and data requirements. Ensure partners have sufficient MEAL budget and structure.
- Ensure the effective set-up and use of data platforms to ensure effective data collection, management and presentation.
- Produce high-quality data, analysis, reports, presentations, and dashboards of key findings that foster learning and decision-making.
- Present findings in project cycle meetings and strategic management team meetings as required.
- Provide technical leadership for the design, method, and conduct of surveys and assessments, such as MSNAs, baseline post-distribution monitoring and endline, and the commission of evaluations and surveys as required in coordination with program coordinators, technical advisors, and external partners where vital.
- Lead the expansion of standard mobile data technology and online dashboards to enhance timeliness and quality of data collection, analysis, and visualization.
- Provide technical leadership to external accountability commitments through the implementation of sound accountability, client feedback, and response mechanisms.
- Strengthen client feedback and response mechanisms based on regional standards and expectations
- As needed, oversee Third party Monitoring efforts, including internal efforts to use TPM to supplement IRC’s own data collection efforts.

**Strategic Leadership**

- Lead all aspects of MEAL functions across multiple sectors and multiple geographical areas.
- Champion an organizational culture where data is routinely analyzed, reviewed and used for evidence-based decision making and program adaptation.
- Establish and drive response-level MEAL strategies and approaches that are fit for rapid scale-up, wide reach, partner-led implementation, access constraints and evolving emergency response realities.
- Shape and implement MEAL systems and approaches that meet IRC standards and practices, are responsive to program needs, and enable accountability to clients, partners, and donors.
- Lead the harmonization of MEAL approaches across IRC and partner-led projects, including partner MEAL capacity sharing, data quality assurance, feedback systems, reporting processes and routine use of evidence.
- Develop, coordinate and strengthen capacity sharing partnerships with MEAL counterparts of partner agencies, local organizations, and government as required.
- Reinforce integration of cross-sectoral priorities in MEAL, including gender, protection, safeguarding, disaster risk reduction, Diversity-Equality-Inclusion and Do No Harm.
- Contribute to regional and global MEAL initiatives as required and participate in regional MEAL cross-learning events and activities.

**Staff Management and Development**

- Establish an efficient and responsive staffing structure for the MEAL department which considers a balanced workload and optimal ways of working to support a large multi-sector program.
- Supervise the MEAL team across multiple sectors and geographical areas. Set clear performance objectives, schedule regular check-in meetings, manage staff work plans, conduct regular performance reviews, champion a positive working environment for professional development, and foster an inclusive and respectful team climate.
- Coach, train, supervise, and mentor MEAL department staff. Promote the growth and development of the team. Assess proficiencies and develop and lead a targeted learning and training strategy.
- Develop and implement remote management capacity building approaches to build the strengths of the MEAL team.
- Design and implement capacity sharing plans with partner MEAL staff including MEAL capacity assessments, MEAL sharing/capacity building gaps, and MEAL capacity and system support
- Lead or support the recruitment, onboarding and technical support of MEAL staff, consultants, temporary technical assistance and partner MEAL focal points, as required.

**Other**

- Other relevant duties as assigned by supervisor to further IRC MEAL objectives.

**Key working relationships**

Position reports to: Deputy Director of Programs

**Technical support:** Emergency MEAL Technical Advisor  
**Position directly supervises:** MEAL Managers, MEAL Officers, MEAL Assistants and CRA staffs

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

**Internal:** Program Coordinators and Managers throughout the country program, Emergency MEAL technical Advisor Regional Measurement Advisor, Client Responsiveness & Accountability (CRA) Technical Advisor, Grants Coordinator and Managers, Finance Coordinator, relevant Regional/HQ-based colleagues.

**External:** partners, governments, clients.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- A university degree in a relevant subject area (statistics, data management, social sciences, public health, economic development, or a related field). A technical degree together with additional relevant work experience may substitute for education.
- A minimum of 5 years of work experience within MEAL-related functions, including experience leading data collection and analysis for multi-sector and multi-donor funded humanitarian programs.
- Experience setting up or strengthening MEAL systems in emergency, remote management, access-constrained or partner-led programming contexts is strongly preferred.
- Excellent understanding of a range of quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis methods required.
- Demonstrated ability to develop functional and user-friendly systems to utilize routine and survey data in program quality improvement and evidence-based decision-making.
- A strong understanding of accountability mechanisms and proven ability to build responsive client feedback systems is a distinct advantage.
- Leadership experience and demonstrated ability to transfer knowledge to diverse audiences through training and mentoring.
- Proficiency and experience with mobile data collection software such as Kobo, CommCare, and ODK Collect is essential, as well as proficiency with Microsoft Excel, SPSS, STATA, or other similar software. Knowledge of Tableau, PowerBI, or GIS software are additional assets.
- Excellent verbal and written data presentation and reporting skills. Able to interpret data and communicate complex analysis to external audiences in a concise and easy to understand manner.
- Excellent advance planning and organizational skills. Able to effectively prioritize and follow multiple activities and deadlines simultaneously.

**Proven Technical Skills:**

- Excellent technical understanding of contemporary MEAL methods and practices, with hands-on experience in qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis.
- Strong program/technical and budget management skills, planning, reporting, monitoring and evaluation skills.
- Proven ability to transfer knowledge to diverse audiences through training, mentoring, and other formal and non-formal methods together with strong oral communication skills, presentation and reporting skills.
- INGO experience required; experience working with the interagency coordination mechanisms desirable.
- Comprehensive knowledge of humanitarian accountability principles and their translation into practice.
- Experience with multi-sectoral and multi-donor funded programs.
- Strong technical and operational knowledge of humanitarian programming in a remote context.

**Languages:**

- Professional fluency in spoken and written English required, Arabic language proficiency preferred.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Asistencia técnica para el desarrollo e implementación de una formación en gestión de establecimientos educativos
jobs.body:
**Duración de la asistencia técnica**

6 semanas

**Ámbito**

Gestión y fortalecimiento de establecimientos educativos

**Destinatarios**

Directores/as y equipos de dirección de centros de secundaria y formación profesional en Haití

**Proyecto**

«Por una EFTP inclusiva y alineada con el empleo» — CTR CRIS 446340 (Ref. NDICI LA 2023/446-340), financiado por la Unión Europea

**Entidad contratante**

Fundación Jóvenes y Desarrollo (JyD), en colaboración con la Fundación Rinaldi.

**Idioma de trabajo**

Francés y Español

## 1. Contexto y justificación

La mejora de la calidad de los establecimientos educativos requiere equipos directivos capaces de gestionar de manera organizada, planificar, tomar decisiones, realizar el seguimiento de sus acciones y orientar adecuadamente los recursos disponibles. Para ello, es necesario fortalecer sus capacidades de gestión y dotarlos de conocimientos, metodologías y herramientas que puedan aplicar en la realidad cotidiana de sus centros.

En este marco, se prevé desarrollar una acción formativa dirigida a directores/as y equipos de dirección de establecimientos de enseñanza secundaria y formación profesional, tanto salesianos como públicos, en Haití. La formación deberá responder a las necesidades reales de gestión de los centros y contribuir a mejorar sus capacidades de planificación, seguimiento, toma de decisiones y mejora institucional.

Esta asistencia técnica se enmarca asimismo en el fortalecimiento del ENTEC, como estructura de formación y perfeccionamiento de los profesionales del sistema de enseñanza técnica y profesional en Haití, cuya misión incluye contribuir al desarrollo de las capacidades de los distintos actores del sistema, entre ellos los equipos directivos de los centros. En este sentido, la formación contribuirá tanto a mejorar la gestión de los establecimientos participantes como a reforzar las capacidades del ENTEC para promover la mejora de la calidad y el funcionamiento de los centros de formación profesional.

Para ello se requiere una asistencia técnica especializada que formule y desarrolle una propuesta de formación adecuada al contexto, prepare los contenidos y materiales necesarios y lleve a cabo la formación en coordinación con el equipo de formadores del centro.

## 2. Objeto de la asistencia técnica

Contratar una asistencia técnica especializada para diseñar, desarrollar e implementar una formación dirigida a directores/as y equipos de dirección de establecimientos de enseñanza secundaria y formación profesional, orientada al fortalecimiento de sus capacidades para la gestión, planificación, seguimiento y mejora de los centros, contribuyendo asimismo al fortalecimiento de las capacidades del ENTEC para apoyar la mejora de la gestión de los establecimientos educativos del sistema de formación técnica y profesional en Haití.

## 3. Objetivo general

Fortalecer las capacidades de los directores/as y equipos de dirección para mejorar la gestión de sus establecimientos, favoreciendo una gestión más planificada, fundamentada, eficiente y orientada a la mejora de la calidad educativa y al uso adecuado de los recursos, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo al fortalecimiento de las capacidades del ENTEC para promover la mejora de la gestión y del funcionamiento de los centros de enseñanza técnica y profesional en Haití\*\*.\*\*

## 4. Objetivos específicos

- Reforzar las competencias de los equipos directivos en materia de gestión y planificación de los establecimientos.
- Mejorar la capacidad de los centros para disponer, organizar y utilizar información relevante para la gestión y la toma de decisiones.
- Fortalecer la capacidad para identificar necesidades, establecer prioridades y planificar acciones de mejora.
- Favorecer el seguimiento de la gestión y de los resultados obtenidos por los establecimientos.
- Mejorar la capacidad de los equipos directivos para identificar y fundamentar sus necesidades de recursos y apoyos.
- Promover la utilización de herramientas prácticas y adaptadas a la realidad de los centros.

## 5. Alcance de la asistencia técnica

La persona responsable de la asistencia técnica deberá, como mínimo:

- Analizar el marco y las necesidades que justifican la acción formativa.
- Elaborar una propuesta técnica y metodológica para el desarrollo de la formación.
- Diseñar y desarrollar los contenidos de la formación de acuerdo con los objetivos establecidos.
- Preparar los materiales pedagógicos, actividades, herramientas e instrumentos necesarios para su implementación.
- Coordinar la preparación de la formación con el equipo de formadores del centro.
- Realizar la formación dirigida a los directores/as y equipos de dirección, con el acompañamiento del equipo de formadores del centro.
- Acompañar el proceso de aplicación práctica de los aprendizajes durante el periodo de la asistencia técnica.
- Recoger los principales resultados del proceso y formular recomendaciones para su seguimiento y continuidad.
- Diseñar e implementar mecanismos sencillos de evaluación de la formación que permitan valorar la participación, adquisición de aprendizajes y utilidad percibida de los contenidos y herramientas.

## 6. Orientaciones generales para la propuesta formativa

La propuesta deberá presentar de manera clara el enfoque de la formación, su metodología, organización, contenidos, duración, actividades, resultados esperados y mecanismos de evaluación. Deberá tener un carácter eminentemente práctico, estar adaptada al contexto de los establecimientos participantes y favorecer la aplicación de los aprendizajes a situaciones reales de gestión.Asimismo, la propuesta deberá tener en cuenta, un enfoque de género transversal en los contenidos, actividades y herramientas de gestión planteados.

La persona candidata propondrá la estructura y el desarrollo concreto de la formación, así como las herramientas e instrumentos que considere más adecuados para alcanzar los objetivos establecidos en estos Términos de Referencia.

## 7. Productos esperados

### Producto 1. Propuesta formativa desarrollada

Documento de formación desarrollado para su implementación, que incluya la propuesta metodológica, los contenidos, la planificación, los materiales diseñados/preparados para la formación, las actividades y los instrumentos necesarios para el desarrollo y evaluación de la formación.

### Producto 2. Realización de la formación

### Formación dirigida a los/as directores/as y equipos de dirección, implementada por la persona responsable de la asistencia técnica con el acompañamiento y participación del equipo de formadores del ENTec. El producto incluirá las evidencias de realización de las sesiones, tales como programa definitivo, listas de asistencia, materiales utilizados y, cuando sea posible, registro fotográfico.

### Producto 3. Informe final y materiales consolidados

Entrega de los materiales definitivos utilizados y de un breve informe final que recoja el desarrollo de la formación, los principales resultados observados, las dificultades encontradas y recomendaciones para el seguimiento, la continuidad y, cuando proceda, la posible réplica de la experiencia.

Todos los productos se entregarán en francés y español, en versión definitiva y maquetada conforme a las normas de visibilidad de la Unión Europea. El informe final incluirá las listas de asistencia de cada jornada de formación, desglosadas por sexo, y fotografías de las sesiones.

## 8. Duración y calendario

La asistencia técnica tendrá una duración máxima de 6 semanas durante los cuales se desarrollarán las diferentes etapas necesarias para el diseño, preparación, realización y cierre de la acción formativa. La distribución definitiva de las Fases será presentada por la persona candidata en su propuesta técnica y acordada posteriormente con la institución contratante:

### Fase 1. Diseño y desarrollo de la propuesta formativa

Comprenderá el análisis de las necesidades planteadas en los presentes Términos de Referencia, la definición del enfoque técnico y metodológico y el desarrollo de los contenidos, materiales, actividades e instrumentos necesarios para la realización de la formación.

### Fase 2. Preparación y coordinación con el equipo de formadores

La propuesta será revisada y ajustada en coordinación con el equipo de formadores designado por el centro, que participará en la preparación, desarrollo y seguimiento de la formación. Se acordarán la organización de la formación, la metodología de trabajo, la participación del equipo y los aspectos necesarios para adaptar la acción formativa a las características de los participantes y de los establecimientos.

### Fase 3. Desarrollo de la formación y acompañamiento

Se realizará la formación dirigida a los directores/as y equipos de dirección. La persona responsable de la asistencia técnica conducirá el proceso formativo con el acompañamiento del equipo de formadores del centro y realizará el seguimiento de las actividades prácticas y de la aplicación de los aprendizajes.

### Fase 4. Cierre, sistematización y recomendaciones

Finalizada la formación, se consolidarán los materiales y productos desarrollados durante el proceso y se elaborará un breve informe final que recoja los principales resultados, dificultades y aprendizajes, así como recomendaciones para el seguimiento y continuidad de la acción.

## 9. Perfil profesional requerido

Se requiere una persona con un perfil profesional que combine una sólida experiencia en educación y cooperación para el desarrollo, conocimiento del contexto haitiano, capacidad de gestión y planificación, y experiencia en el diseño e implementación de procesos formativos. Se valorarán especialmente los siguientes aspectos:

- Formación universitaria en educación, humanidades, ciencias sociales u otros ámbitos afines, complementada preferentemente con formación especializada en cooperación internacional para el desarrollo y/o educación.
- Amplia experiencia profesional en Haití y conocimiento del contexto institucional, educativo y socioeconómico del país.
- Experiencia demostrable en el sector educativo y, particularmente, en formación profesional y fortalecimiento de capacidades de instituciones y centros educativos.
- Experiencia en el diseño, desarrollo y adaptación de módulos, contenidos y materiales pedagógicos, preferentemente mediante el Enfoque por Competencias (EPC/APC).
- Experiencia en preparación, organización e impartición de talleres y acciones formativas dirigidas a formadores, responsables de centros y/o equipos de gestión.
- Experiencia en acompañamiento de equipos de formadores y en procesos de revisión, validación y mejora de materiales y herramientas pedagógicas.
- Experiencia sólida en gestión, planificación estratégica, seguimiento y evaluación de programas y proyectos, especialmente en el ámbito de la cooperación y el desarrollo.
- Capacidad para relacionar la gestión educativa con la planificación, el seguimiento de resultados, la utilización de información para la toma de decisiones y la identificación de necesidades de mejora.
- Experiencia en coordinación de equipos y en el trabajo con instituciones públicas, organizaciones educativas, actores locales y organismos de cooperación.
- Capacidad para trabajar de manera autónoma y, al mismo tiempo, en estrecha colaboración con equipos locales, favoreciendo la transferencia de capacidades y la apropiación de los procesos.
- Excelente dominio oral y escrito del francés. Se valorará especialmente el conocimiento del criollo haitiano y del español.

## 10. Coordinación y supervisión

La persona responsable trabajará bajo la supervisión de la institución contratante y en coordinación con el equipo de formadores del centro. La institución realizará el seguimiento del encargo y validará los productos previstos.

## 11. Presupuesto y condiciones financieras

El presupuesto total disponible para esta consultoría es de un máximo de **12.000 euros**, sin impuestos incluidos. La persona o entidad consultora deberá presentar una propuesta técnica y económica, incluyendo los honorarios profesionales, y en su caso, los costos logísticos y operativos asociados.

jobs.title: Senior Specialist, MEAL – TCIS
jobs.body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

The Senior Specialist, MEAL provides senior technical MEAL expertise and support to Terwilliger Center for Innovation in Shelter (TCIS) projects across Southeast Asia, including the Philippines, Indonesia and Cambodia and to assigned regional programmes, including Housing Finance Systems (HFS) and Small and Growing Business (SGB).

Working towards HFHI’s One MEARL Vision, the Senior Specialist helps ensure agreed organisational standards, indicators, systems and practices are consistently applied and that evidence informs programme improvement and wider organisational learning.

**Key Responsibilities:**

## Essential Duties

- Lead the technical development and application of theories of change, results frameworks, MEAL plans, indicators and measurement approaches for projects, programmes and relevant proposal development, across the region
- Provide senior technical MEAL support, coaching and guidance across assigned projects in Southeast Asia, advising programme and project teams and promoting consistency and alignment across countries and programmes.
- Collaborate with programme and project teams to integrate MEAL requirements into project management, reporting and organisational systems throughout the programme or project lifecycle, in line with agreed structures and standards.
- Develop and review monitoring, data-collection, reporting and data-quality approaches and provide technical quality assurance to strengthen the reliability and use of programme evidence.
- Design and lead internal evaluations, assessments and applied research, and lead technical inputs to external evaluations, including development of scopes of work, review of methodologies and deliverables, and coordination with evaluators as required.
- Analyse and synthesise evidence across projects and programmes to identify trends, risks, learning and evidence gaps, and translate findings into practical recommendations for programme adaptation and decision-making.
- Facilitate reflection, learning and knowledge-sharing processes and contribute to learning agendas, evidence products and cross-country learning.
- Contribute technical expertise, evidence and learning from assigned projects to relevant Collective Impact Initiative workstreams, including advancement of the One MEARL vision, and support the application of agreed approaches

## Minimum Requirements

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, social sciences, economics, statistics, monitoring and evaluation or related field; postgraduate qualification preferred.
- 5+ years of progressive MEAL experience, including demonstrated technical experience across multiple countries or regional/complex programmes.
- Demonstrated experience developing theories of change, results frameworks, indicators and MEAL plans and applying qualitative and quantitative monitoring, research and evaluation methods, including evaluations, data-quality assurance, reporting and evidence synthesis.
- Strong analytical, project management, facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to independently manage complex technical assignments and work effectively across countries, cultures and functions.
- Knowledge of current MEAL practice, including accountability, safeguarding, participatory approaches and relevant data collection/analysis tools.
- Proficiency with relevant data-collection, analysis and visualisation tools, including Excel and tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
- Knowledge of current MEAL practice, including accountability, safeguarding and participatory approaches.

## Preferred Requirements

- Experience in market systems development, housing, housing finance, financial inclusion, private-sector development or related programming.
- Familiarity with systemic MEAL approaches for market systems development.
- Experience working with enterprises, small and growing businesses (SGBs), or innovation programmes.
- Familiarity with impact investment metrics, enterprise performance measures and basic financial analysis.
- Experience with applied research, accountability and feedback mechanisms, and capacity strengthening.

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.title: Financial Planning & Analysis Advisor
jobs.body:
**Selection Criteria:** The Financial Planning and Analysis Advisor position is open to candidates residing in countries where Medical Teams International can legally employ staff, either directly or through an approved third-party Employer of Record (EOR). To support collaboration with global teams, candidates must be located within the UTC-8 to UTC+3 time zone range.

The Financial Planning and Analysis Advisor contributes to the calling of Medical Teams International by providing financial and business analytics support to drive financial planning and help make informed business decisions. This senior level role serves as a strategic business partner to executive and departmental leadership by providing forward-looking financial insights, enterprise performance analytics, and decision-support tools that optimize organizational resources and advance strategic priorities. The Financial Planning and Analysis Advisor leads organization-wide forecasting, scenario planning, performance measurement, and financial modeling activities to support sustainable growth, operational effectiveness, and mission impact.

**Medical Teams International Calling:**

Daring to love like Jesus, we boldly break barriers to health and restore wholeness in a hurting world.

Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates’ eligibility, thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Reporting and Analysis**

- Manage the financial planning and analysis (FP&A) process. This includes financial reporting, creating various financial metrics and dashboards, and scenario and predictive modeling.
- Lead indirect cost rate calculations and create cost recovery models across all business units.
- Prepare reports for Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA).
- Develop and report monthly, quarterly, and annual metrics pertaining to departmental efficiencies, cost recovery, labor optimization, revenue, etc.
- Review, analyze, and distribute financial reports to budget holders and support interpretation of financial results.
- Create presentations for senior and executive management that provide insightful analysis, identify required action items, and effectively frame decisions to be made.
- Identify and research discrepancies and variances to forecast, budget, and prior-year and proactively identify opportunities for improvement across the enterprise
- Develop and maintain multi-year financial forecasts and strategic planning models to support organizational sustainability and growth initiatives.
- Establish and monitor enterprise key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational scorecards aligned with strategic objectives.
- Lead financial scenario analyses and sensitivity modeling to support executive decision-making, risk assessment, and resource prioritization.
- Partner with Development, Global Programs, and Executive Leadership to analyze funding trends, grant pipelines, donor concentration risks, and revenue sustainability.
- Prepare financial and operational analyses for executive leadership, Board committees, and senior management meetings.

**Budget**

- Oversee and coordinate data collection and input feeding into the annual global budget process.
- Create guidance documentation, and templates for budget holders, budget models for decision making, prior year analysis, current year projections plus providing budget system support and training.
- Identify foreign exchange exposure to include monitoring, reporting, and hedging as appropriate during annual budget and reforecasting cycle.
- Reconcile budget revisions and manage budgets in the ERP system. Input the finance department budget into the ERP system while offering educational assistance to other departments as needed.
- Lead quarterly reforecasting and rolling forecast processes across the organization.
- Evaluate investment proposals, staffing requests, and strategic initiatives through financial analysis and business case development.
- Partner with departmental leaders to identify opportunities for operational efficiency, cost optimization, and resource alignment.

**ERP and Financial Systems Support**

- Serve as a Finance ERP champion and the primary focal point for coaching, support and troubleshooting.
- Identify opportunities for financial process improvements by leveraging the ERP platform and other modules alongside the IS department.
- Develop training material and facilitate knowledge sharing and training on the use of digital tools for budget and reporting evaluations.
- Lead finance data governance initiatives to ensure consistency, integrity, and reliability of enterprise financial data.
- Collaborate with Information Systems to expand business intelligence capabilities through dashboards, automated reporting, and advanced analytics tools.
- Identify and implement automation opportunities to reduce manual effort and improve financial reporting efficiency.

**Other Duties**

- Support safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse & Harassment, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding code of conduct and behavior expectations.
- Support the Finance department as needed, while having a line of sight into the financial metrics and performance of Philanthropy, Marketing & Mobilization, Global Programs, and Executive Management.
- Facilitate cross-functional financial reviews and business performance discussions with organizational leaders.
- Support enterprise risk assessment activities by identifying financial, operational, and funding risks and recommending mitigation strategies.
- Participate in organizational transformation initiatives and support change management efforts related to finance systems, processes, and reporting.
- Participate in and support strategic projects as requested.
- Utilize volunteers when appropriate.
- Additional duties as assigned.

## **Qualifications**

**EDUCATION, LICENSE & CERTIFICATIONS**

**Required:**

- Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business, economics, or closely related fields
- Valid passport

**Preferred:**

- Master’s degree and/or finance/accounting related certification
- Certified Corporate FP&A Professional (FPAC), CPA, CMA, CGMA, CFA, or equivalent professional designation
- Training or certification in business intelligence, data analytics, or financial systems administration

**EXPERIENCE**

**Required:**

- Minimum 6 years’ relevant experience in an NGO context
- 4 years’ financial planning, analysis, and non-profit budgeting experience
- 4 years’ indirect cost rate / NICRA modeling and reporting
- Prior experience in public accounting, audit, data analytics, business operations or relevant field
- Experience with Power BI, Tableau, Adaptive Planning, Workday Adaptive, or equivalent platforms
- Experience leading process improvement, automation, or finance transformation initiatives

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES**

**Knowledge:**

- US-GAAP
- Non-profit financial statements and corporate finance reports
- Financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis principles
- Nonprofit accounting, restricted funding, grant budgeting, and donor compliance
- Indirect cost allocation, cost recovery, and NICRA principles
- ERP-based financial reporting and data structures
- Internal controls, financial policies, and audit-ready documentation practice
- Strategic planning and enterprise performance management frameworks
- Business intelligence, data governance, and analytics best practices
- Financial risk assessment and scenario planning techniques

**Skills:**

- Spreadsheet proficiency
- Data manipulation
- Data visualization
- Building business, operational, or financial reports
- Financial modeling from multiple data sources
- Strategic financial analysis and decision support
- Long-range financial planning and enterprise forecasting
- ERP/NetSuite, expense management systems, and Microsoft Office
- Facilitation and stakeholder management
- Data visualization and storytelling
- Exceptional communication skills, especially with executive and non-financial audiences

**Abilities:**

- Commitment to Medical Teams International Calling statement and Values
- Ability to manage multiple and shifting priorities while meeting deadlines
- Strong ability to analyze details, identify issues, and communicate with courage
- Strong Ability to learn new technologies quickly
- Ability to navigate complex business environments
- Ability to work proactively and collaboratively
- Ability to communicate difficult or detailed issues with courage
- Ability to translate complex financial information into actionable insights for executive and non-financial audiences
- Ability to think strategically while maintaining operational excellence
- Ability to influence organizational decision-making through data-driven recommendations
- Ability to lead change initiatives and drive adoption of new processes and technologies
- Ability to anticipate emerging financial and operational challenges and proactively recommend solutions

**Compensation:**

The anticipated hiring range for this position is **$86,000-$92,000 USD annually**. Final compensation will be determined based on the selected candidate's qualifications, relevant experience, internal equity considerations, and geographic location.

While the salary range listed applies to candidates residing in the United States, compensation for candidates located outside the U.S. will be determined using Medical Teams International's international compensation framework and may vary based on local market conditions and organizational compensation practices.

jobs.title: RESPONSABLE PROGRAMME NUTRITION ET SANTE - TCHAD
jobs.body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision du Responsable Terrain, votre mission sera de mettre en place une prise en charge médicale et nutritionnelle de qualité pour les enfants souffrant de malnutrition aiguë sévère.  
Dans ce cadre, vos responsabilités seront de :  
Mettre en place et superviser la qualité des activités des projets Nutrition-Santé  
Assurer une gestion de projet efficiente et contribuer aux développements des programmes Nutrition-Santé mis en oeuvre à l'Est  
Former, encadrer et manager les équipes ACF Nutrition-Santé   
Participer à la coordination de la crise à l'Est, représentation et au partenariat d'ACF auprès des partenaires et autres acteurs dans sa zone d'intervention  
Représenter ACF et développer les partenariats locaux

  
Profile :

 Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme d'Infirmier·ère ou de Médecin, complété par une expérience en PCIMA, PCIME et SSR dans des contextes d'urgence.  
Vous justifiez d'au moins 5 ans d'expérience dans le secteur humanitaire au sein d'une ONG internationale, en tant que Responsable de Projet ou de Programme, incluant le management d'équipes et le renforcement des capacités.  
Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans la coordination des réponses aux urgences sanitaires et nutritionnelles, en collaboration avec d'autres ONG, des partenaires étatiques et des organisations communautaires.  
Vous êtes organisé·e, autonome et capable de prioriser vos activités, et de vous adapter à des environnements complexes.  
Une expérience dans des centres de santé, dans des zones isolées ou difficiles d'accès, dans un contexte sécuritaire instable, ainsi qu'une expérience au Tchad, constitueront des atouts appréciés.  
  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
Contrat à durée déterminée d'usage de droit français : 3 mois jusqu'au 31/01/2027  
Salaire mensuel brut : de 2130 à 2475 euros en fonction de l'expérience, incluant 13ème mois  
Remboursement assurance retraite pour les citoyens non français : 16% du salaire mensuel brut  
Augmentation du salaire de base : 6% tous les 12 mois de contrat continu  
Per diem et frais de vie mensuels : 838euros nets, versés sur le terrain  
Allocation contexte mensuelle : 300euros  
Allocation enfant : 1500euros par an et par enfant présent dans le pays d'origine (plafond de 6000euros/an)  
Transport et logement : Prise en charge des déplacements et logement collectif  
Couverture Médicale : 100% de la prise en charge des cotisations santé et assurance rapatriement, de vos frais médicaux (ainsi que celle de vos ayants droit si poste famille) et ce jusqu'à 1 mois après la fin de votre contrat  
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)  
Congés et RnR : 25 jours par an de CP et 20 RnR par an ; prise en charge du billet avec plafond pour se rendre sur la zone de break choisie, et 215euros d'indemnité forfaitaire par RnR  
Accompagnement et formation  
Suivi et accompagnement parcours professionnel  
Accès illimité et gratuit à la plateforme d'e-learning Talentsoft  
Déplacements terrains : toute la province du Silas  
  
ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.

jobs.title: Monitoring and Evaluation Advisor
jobs.body:
## About the Role

All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Advisor to build and lead the monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems for its humanitarian response in Gaza. Operating in a fast-changing environment with constrained access, AHAH needs reliable, timely evidence on what is reaching communities, what is working, and where programs must adapt. The successful candidate will focus primarily on nutrition Monitoring and Evaluation, ensure quality data collection and reporting to leadership and donors, and put in place mechanisms that let affected communities give feedback and hold the organization accountable.

## Key Responsibilities

- **M&E Systems and Frameworks:** Design and roll out AHAH's M&E framework for Gaza nutrition program, including results frameworks, data collection and analysis, indicator reference sheets and performance monitoring plans aligned with donor requirements and cluster standards.
- **Distribution and Commodity Monitoring:** Establish post-distribution monitoring, commodity tracking and verification processes to confirm that AHAH assistance reaches intended civilian beneficiaries, and flag diversion or access risks to leadership.
- **Data Collection and Management:** Develop data collection tools and lead the use of mobile data platforms; ensure data quality, security, beneficiary data protection and safe storage.
- **Assessments and Evaluations:** Lead or support needs assessments, baseline and endline surveys, and periodic program reviews; manage external evaluations where required.
- **Reporting and Learning:** Produce timely, accurate reports and dashboards for AHAH leadership and donors; document lessons learned and use findings to guide program adaptation.
- **Coordination:** Represent AHAH in inter-agency information management and assessment working groups; contribute data to cluster reporting, as appropriate.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor field staff, on M&E methods, data collection and ethical data practices.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute M&E plans, indicators and budgets to proposals for institutional and private donors.

## Qualifications & Experience

- Master's degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Public Health, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of M&E experience, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated expertise in designing M&E systems, quantitative and qualitative methods, and donor reporting.
- Proficiency with mobile data collection platforms and data analysis tools
- Excellent analytical, communication and report-writing skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is an 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

jobs.title: Senior Nutrition Advisor
jobs.body:
All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Senior Nutrition Advisor to lead the design, delivery and quality of its emergency nutrition programming in Gaza. Acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women has risen sharply amid prolonged conflict, displacement and severe restrictions on food access. The successful candidate will provide technical leadership on nutrition across All Hands and Hearts' humanitarian response, ensure programs meet international standards, and represent the organization with the Nutrition Cluster, UN agencies, donors and partner NGOs. The Advisor will also help integrate nutrition into AHAH's wider food distribution, community health, shelter and education programs, and build the capacity of local staff and community health workers.

## Key Responsibilities

- **Technical Leadership:** Serve as AHAH's lead technical expert on nutrition in emergencies, setting program strategy and ensuring all nutrition activities align with Sphere standards, Nutrition Cluster guidance and Ministry of Health protocols.
- **Program Design and Delivery:** Design, launch and oversee nutrition interventions, which may include community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM), MUAC screening and referral, supplementary feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and infant and young child feeding in emergencies (IYCF-E).
- **Integration with Food Assistance:** Advise AHAH leadership and logistics teams on the nutritional adequacy of food baskets and distributions, targeting of vulnerable groups, and safe handling of specialized nutrition commodities (RUTF, RUSF, LNS).
- **Assessment and Surveillance:** Lead or support nutrition assessments, screening campaigns and surveillance (including SMART-style surveys where feasible) to identify needs, track trends and guide program decisions.
- **Coordination and Representation:** Represent AHAH in the Nutrition Cluster and relevant working groups; build partnerships with UNICEF, WFP, WHO, health facilities and local NGOs to strengthen referral pathways and avoid duplication.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor AHAH staff, partner organizations and community health workers on nutrition screening, counseling, IYCF-E and the Code on breastmilk substitutes.
- **Monitoring, Reporting and Accountability:** Develop indicators and monitoring tools, ensure quality data collection, and report program results to AHAH leadership and donors. Ensure feedback and accountability mechanisms are in place for affected communities.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute technical content to proposals, budgets and donor reports for institutional and private donors (e.g., USAID/BHA successor mechanisms, ECHO, UN pooled funds, foundations and Gulf donors).

## Qualifications & Experience

- MD or Master's degree in Public Health, Nursing, Nutrition, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of experience in health or nutrition programming, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in nutrition programming.
- Proven experience managing teams, training staff and working through local partners.
- Excellent analytical, communication and representation skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is a 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

jobs.title: Executive Director
source: Trust for Indigenous Culture and Health
jobs.body:
**WE ARE HIRING AN EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR!**

**ABOUT TICAH**  
TICAH is a feminist organization that works to promote health, equitable relationships, and  
community action. We dream of safe and just societies where barriers to equitable health and social outcomes are removed including for the most marginalized populations, where rights are realized, holistic health is attained and where the beauty of culture and diversity is celebrated.

Our definition of health recognises the links between health, values and culture, the role of art in activism and social change and the elevation of marginalised voices and ideas, that there is much to be gained by engaging with our traditional cultures, that access to quality health information services is critical and the power of nutrition and herbs in overall wellness cannot be overlooked.  
We work toward communities driving and owning all implementation through our tried and tested methodologies: Listening and Co-Creation of interventions with communities, Creation of Safe Spaces for Values Clarification and Training of Trainers; Advocacy, where we raise our voices to advocate for better laws, policies and practices to protect rights, access to holistic health services, freedom of expression and sexual &amp; reproductive health rights. We celebrate the beauty and diversity of ideas, ethnicities, religions, sexuality, music, art, genders, indigenous cultures, and traditions as expressions of a healthy society.

Our priority areas are Gender Justice, Climate Justice and Holistic Health.  
TICAH’s 4 program areas are:  
 Art for Connection & Healing: Working with artists and through arts practices to build community, raise marginalized voices, activate and revitalize public spaces, and find  
healing and wellness.  
 Healthy Households working with households to build wellness and prevent illness by  
incorporating practical, affordable, and sustainable practices by focusing on food and  
herbal remedies.  
 Indigenous Knowledge and Culture: Working closely with cultural practitioners and  
elders to bring positive indigenous knowledge, practice and culture into holistic health  
and solving community challenges.  
 Our Bodies, Our Choices, a SRH program encouraging more honest and healthy  
approaches to sexual life through curricula, trainings, peer discussions and a hotline. With  
like-minded organizations we advocate for comprehensive sexuality education, and  
access to safe legal abortion.

From our beginnings in 2003, TICAH has been rooted in health, healing, culture, and justice.  
Deeply embedded in the communities we work with, ours has always been a story of us, for us - walking alongside communities, listening, staying curious, and learning as we go. We wanted to be an organization that itself embodies the values and tenets of wellness, rights, and connection that we aimed for in our work.This grounding continues to shape how we work, how we lead, and where we are going next.  
Over the years, TICAH has evolved from providing information and programs to empowering communities to take control of their health, rights, and futures. Our early work connected health with culture, rights, relationships, and indigenous knowledge, fostering open conversations on sexuality, HIV, nutrition, traditional medicine, and social justice.

By 2019, we further strengthened our focus on women and girls, gender equality, community leadership, and advocacy.  
We’ve seen impact not just in numbers reached, but in people making informed choices,  
changing practices at home, indigenous women leading, artists driving social change, and  
communities shaping policies. By 2025, communities were reorganizing after disruptions, young women were influencing policy, families were blending nutrition with local knowledge, indigenous women were leading on land and climate justice, and artists were creating spaces for healing.

In addition, TICAH also plays a strategic movement-building role, convening and hosting  
networks advancing SRHR and other rights nationally and regionally, including MAMA Network (a regional network of 70+ organizations in 26 African countries), and various national networks in Kenya.

In so doing TICAH creates the connective infrastructure that enables organisations and activists to organise, learn, respond and act collectively. Through these networks, we help turn individual organisations and community action into collective power capable of influencing systems at scale.

The 2022-2026 Strategic Plan further solidified TICAH's commitment and methodology for  
building power and systems change. With a team of 25, TICAH’s work has impacted over  
407,000 people, equipping them with the knowledge, agency, and collective power to lead  
change. In this period, TICAH began to see communities not just as participants, but as leaders with collective power and agency. Our focus has thus moved from providing information to supporting informed choices, advocacy, and collective action. Our programs have become more integrated, connecting health, rights, gender, climate, art, and indigenous knowledge through an intersectional approach. This has led to greater influence on policies and systems at all levels. By the end of the strategy, TICAH’s role will be less about delivering solutions and more about creating conditions for communities to lead, systems to listen, and people to shape their own  
futures.

As our current Strategic Plan comes to an end, we are looking ahead with ambition and curiosity, asking ourselves what is possible as TICAH enters its next strategic plan cycle: how do we hold on to the depth, creativity and community-rootedness that have always defined us, while growing our ability to scale and influence the systems that shape people’s health and lives. How do we build an even stronger, more resilient and sustainable organisation, one that can navigate an increasingly complex political and funding environment, deepen our impact, strengthen our partnerships and continue to challenge conventional ways of thinking about health and  
wellbeing?

TICAH’s next Executive Director will have the exciting responsibility of helping us imagine, shape and lead this next chapter building on more than two decades of learning and impact while taking the organisation boldly into its future.  
Learn more: [https://www.ticahealth.org/](https://www.ticahealth.org/)

TICAH’S SHARED LEADERSHIP MODEL:  
TICAH has adopted a shared leadership model where the Executive Director and Deputy  
Executive Director share responsibility, authority, and decision-making for the organization.

Rather than a traditional hierarchical structure centered on a single leader, shared leadership emphasizes collaboration, mutual accountability and complementary strengths.  
In addition, shared leadership is embedded in TICAH’s DNA through listening and consensus- building, trust and delegation, a highly collaborative Leadership Team and cross-functional committees that steer program development, MEL, fundraising, communications, staff welfare, procurement and more.

This model is deeply aligned with TICAH’s values in a number of ways:  
● Shared leadership reflects feminist values by promoting shared power, equality, and  
inclusive decision-making.  
● Indigenous principles emphasize collective leadership, inclusive stewardship, and  
respect for relational decision-making.  
● Sustainability: Sharing leadership responsibilities reduces burnout, builds institutional  
memory, and supports healthier, more stable operations over time.  
● Better outcomes for communities: Shared Leadership brings complementary skills and  
insights, enhancing strategic thinking, innovation, and the overall impact of TICAH’s  
mission.  
As a result, the ED role includes both, shared leadership responsibilities and areas of sole  
ownership, which are outlined below to provide clarity on roles and accountability.

ROLES SHARED BETWEEN ED & DEPUTY ED (20%):  
Strategy Development  
 Lead the expansion of TICAH’s vision & advance opportunities to realise its unique  
mission &amp; approach in Kenya, regionally and globally.  
 Hold the SP’s vision and goals, steer implementation and learning through 2027–2030,  
and lead the development of the SP 2030+.  
 Provide technical leadership for the annual reviews of the Strategic Plan. Ensure all  
Programs and MELS strategies, frameworks, and SOPs align with the Strategic Plan and  
its revisions  
 Provide effective representation of TICAH’s transformative agenda and goals to influence  
relevant actors and actions in Kenya, regionally and globally.  
Governance / Board Management &amp; Development  
 Lead board development as needs evolve.  
 Coordinate Board Meeting Schedule.  
 Prepare for, attend and ensure follow-up from board meetings.  
 Ensure board decisions are documented and implemented.

Legal  
 Oversee the organization’s legal and compliance matters, including emerging issues and  
risk management, working closely with legal counsel and the board as needed.

**EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR ROLES:**  
Fundraising & Donor Communication &amp; Engagement (25%):  
● Hold overall accountability for TICAH’s fundraising and donor engagement, working  
closely with the Head of Partnerships and Deputy Executive Director to ensure adequate,  
sustainable and values-aligned resource mobilisation.  
● In collaboration with the Head of Partnerships, cultivate and steward strong relationships  
with current and prospective donors, effectively communicating TICAH’s distinctive value,  
impact and relevance to health and social justice priorities in Kenya, the region and globally.  
● Ensuring donor relationships are held by the organisation rather than concentrated in any one individual. Donor relationships may be primarily led by the Executive Director, Deputy Executive Director, Head of Partnerships or other relevant team members, while ensuring that each key donor has meaningful relationships with more than one person within TICAH.  
● Provide strategic leadership for the retention of existing donors and Cultivation and  
progressing onboarding of new donors in close collaboration with HoPa to ensure that  
donors understand the value and relevance of TICAH’s uniqueness to a range of current  
topical health and social issues in Kenya, regionally and globally.  
● Ensure adequate funding to support the SP through Donor Relations with all current  
donors and high-value prospects. (progressive onboarding of new donors and retention  
of current donors)  
● Ensure strategy- and value-aligned communication with all donors through the review of  
key donor communication tools (grant applications, donor reports, annual reports, pitch  
decks).  
● Maintain overall oversight of TICAH’s donor portfolio and relationships, including those  
managed day-to-day by other members of the team, and ensure emerging opportunities,  
risks and relationship needs are appropriately managed.

Organizational Leadership, Talent & Culture (20%):  
● In collaboration with the Leadership Team, spearhead the organizational design, talent  
management strategy, culture, and structure in service of our Mission and Strategic Plan,  
in line with our values.  
● Ensure wellness, self-care and collective care are deeply embedded in the organizational  
culture through policy and practice.  
● Oversee staff development to realize TICAH’s strategic plan, strengthen its ability for  
impact and growth, and stay responsive to evolving realities and needs.  
● Support and manage the Deputy ED, Head of Partnerships and Head of Finance and  
Operations, and enable them to drive the organizations results through their teams.  
● Committees of the ED: Actively participate in the Communications and Fundraising  
Committee and opportunity to join MELS or Programs Committee as needed.

External Influence, Communications & Visibility (10%):  
In collaboration with Head of Partnerships & Communications:  
● Lead effective representation of TICAH’s transformative agenda and goals to influence  
relevant actors and actions in Kenya and the region and globally.  
● Build relevance and visibility in key spaces by representing TICAH and our beliefs, and  
provide thought partnership externally through strategic speaking engagements, industry  
networking, and collaboration on op-eds, articles, research, publications, reports, media  
engagements, etc.  
● External Communications Oversight:  
○ Ensure strategic and value-aligned external communications.  
○ Provide strategic leadership in moments of crisis communication.  
○ Act as the main spokesperson and ensure oversight of external communications  
by the team.

● Strategic Internal Communication:  
○ In collaboration with the leadership team ensure that information flows  
transparently, clearly and consistently across teams, fostering collaboration,  
alignment, and a strong organisational culture

Partner & Stakeholder Engagement (15%):  
● Engage regularly with diverse audiences and communities across our programs and  
methodologies, building relationships, deepening understanding of our work in action,  
and staying grounded in community realities through presence and listening.  
● Cultivate relationships with partners and stakeholders to ensure they understand the  
value and relevance of TICAH’s unique approach to current topical health and social  
issues in Kenya, the region and globally.  
● Grow non-funding partnerships in service of Strategic Goals, e.g., replication of our model, advocacy efforts, organizational and technical learning, etc.  
● Steward relationships with strategic partners hosted by the organization, ensuring strong  
collaboration, alignment and mutual value creation. Join strategy committees, oversee  
operational plans and staff as needed.

Financial Management (10%):  
● In collaboration with the Head of Finance;  
○ Oversee the overall budgets, grant management, and systems that comprise  
TICAH’s financial direction, sustainability, and practice.  
○ Provide strategic oversight of TICAH’s financial health and stewardship of  
resources, ensuring funds are used responsibly, effectively, and in alignment with  
organizational priorities, while the DED leads operational decisions related to  
grants, expenditures, and reporting

● Steward a long-term financial sustainability strategy, including diversifying revenue  
streams through innovative models such as social enterprise, strengthening reserves and  
investment strategies, and ensuring the organization is positioned for long-term resilience  
and independence.

**WHO ARE LOOKING FOR:**  
We are looking for a deeply mission-aligned, bold feminist leader with demonstrated  
conviction and experience in rights-based programming and advocacy, who believes  
communities own their challenges, solutions and decisions and is committed to self-  
determination, bodily autonomy, holistic health, human rights, and addressing the intersections of health, culture, art, climate, and inequality.  
You have a robust understanding of SRHR issues in East Africa and in-depth knowledge of  
relevant laws, policies, regulations, and trends, including anti-rights actors and are comfortable working on access to safe abortion and the rights of LGBTQI+ people.  
You embody a deeply relational worldview: You have a deep appreciation for culture and  
creativity and understand the interconnectedness of people, community, wellbeing, justice, truth, beauty, and everyday life. And you bring this whole-person perspective to leadership and in how you listen, create and lead decisions on the role of the creative sector in social change.  
And you move fluently across worlds: You have lived and worked across diverse contexts, and cultures and know how to move between with humility, curiosity, and ease.

EXPERIENCE & TRACK RECORD:  
● Fundraising: You have successfully led fundraising across a diverse portfolio of  
institutional, philanthropic, and individual donors, including securing significant multi-  
year and unrestricted funding, and worked closely across fundraising and programme  
teams to translate programme priorities into compelling funding opportunities and  
proposals.  
● Relationship-led donor stewardship:  
○ Demonstrated track record of representing an organization compellingly, building  
and retaining long-term donor relationships, with strong retention while building  
the credibility and partnerships needed to resource complex systems-change  
work. Recognizes that fundraising at TICAH is fundamentally relationship-based  
rather than proposal-based.  
○ Strategic resource mobilisation: Understands the changing funding landscape,  
thinks beyond traditional fundraising and explores diverse approaches to  
resource mobilisation and long-term organisational sustainability.

● Team size: You have experience leading an organisation of 20+ staff, including a senior  
leadership team of at least three people, with an appreciation for building and managing  
well motivated and self-driven diverse teams and navigating organisational transitions and  
evolving leadership structures.  
○ People leadership: Strong influencing, coaching, conflict resolution and  
performance management skills, with the ability to support managers lead and  
build self-driven motivated, healthy teams that achieve their goals

○ Experience promoting a culture of wellness, self- and collective care through  
practices that support staff well-being, while modeling these values through your  
own leadership and working style.

● Financial Management: Sound understanding of financial management, budgeting,  
planning, accountability, and organizational systems, with a track record of ensuring  
resources are used effectively and sustainably towards organization’s strategic goals.  
○ Has managed an organisational budget of at least $1M, ideally in an organisation  
of comparable size and complexity.  
○ Demonstrated long-term thinking about organisational financial sustainability  
and resilience, with an interest in diversifying revenue and exploring innovative  
approaches to building greater financial independence.

● Programme complexity: Experience working across multiple, multidisciplinary  
programmes, ideally spanning areas such as SRHR, health, food systems, climate justice,  
art and culture.  
○ Programmatic curiosity and credibility: Brings sufficient depth in at least one of  
TICAH's areas of work and stays connected to the wider conversations, networks  
and emerging thinking shaping holistic health, gender justice, climate justice and  
rights-based work. Working with indigenous communities is an added advantage.  
○ Program leadership: Ability to provide strategic leadership to ensure TICAH’s  
programs evolve with learning, respond to emerging opportunities and needs, and  
remain deeply aligned with the organization’s mission, strategy and long-term  
vision.

● Movement building: Experience working within or alongside diverse social Justice  
movements and advocacy spaces, particularly in SRHR and gender justice, including  
navigating politically complex environments and advancing work beyond conventional  
approaches.  
● Government & policy: Experience engaging with government ministries, technical  
working groups and/or policy spaces, and bringing technical or programmatic expertise  
into these spaces.  
● Conference & network engagement: Demonstrated ability to use conferences and  
convenings strategically for fundraising, partnerships, and influence.

**LEADERSHIP SKILLS:**  
1\. Strategic and grounded leadership  
● You have a track record of 10+ years of leadership advancing social justice work in East  
Africa, with experience working alongside community-focused organizations.  
● Strategic leadership: You have proven senior leadership experience, ideally as an ED or  
equivalent, with the strategic thinking and judgment to guide TICAH through its next  
stage of growth and deepen its contribution to systems change.  
● Complexity & adaptability: You have proven ability to hold complexity and connect the dots across global, national, and local contexts, balancing scale and systems change with TICAH’s bespoke, community-centred approach. You know when to challenge,  
when to steady and when to listen and learn before changing.  
● Organizational stewardship: You have the ability to translate strategy into effective planning, execution and ways of working, while strengthening organisational systems  
and maintaining high standards of accountability, transparency, financial stewardship and operational effectiveness.

2\. Relationship-centred, people-powered leadership  
● Trust-based and developmental: You intentionally build trust, listen deeply, understand people and their strengths, and create an environment where the team and all stakeholders feel supported, connected to leadership and empowered to grow.  
● Shared and participatory: You believe in shared leadership and distributed power, with  
the emotional intelligence and facilitative skills to navigate difficult conversations, bring diverse perspectives together and enable collective decision-making.  
3\. Deep cultural and values alignment  
● Humility, integrity & generosity: You lead with authenticity and integrity, and bring  
generosity to colleagues, partners and allies.  
● Learning &amp; growth: You are curious and committed to your own development, with the self-awareness to reflect, learn and evolve their leadership and ways of working.  
● People & organisational wellbeing: You care deeply about the long-term sustainability  
of the organisation and the conditions in which people thrive, creating psychological  
safety, transparency and an environment where people can do their best work.  
4\. Movement-builder and ecosystem leader  
● Movement-minded: You understand TICAH’s distinctive role across feminists,  
indigenous, SRHR, health and social justice movements, and its role as a convener, weaver and incubator.  
● Builds across boundaries: You bring people together around shared purpose, build  
coalitions and lasting relationships, and inspire collective action beyond organisational  
boundaries.  
● Generous collaborator: You have proven ability to nurture relationships, including inherited ones and you see collaboration (not competition) as a way to strengthen the wider movements and ecosystem.

**OTHER INFORMATION:**  
Anticipated start is the first half of 2027. The role will be based in our Karen office with two days working from home flexibility. The role will involve regular travel within Kenya, regionally and internationally (approximately 5 international and 7 local/regional trips annually, in addition to regular engagements in/around Nairobi) to engage with communities, partners, donors, movements and other strategic spaces relevant to TICAH’s work.

We are looking for candidates who are excited to make a long-term commitment in seeing TICAH through its next level of growth.  
There will be a six-month probationary period and we will agree on performance and learning objectives.
