jobs.body:
**CDD | 12 mois | ASAP**

## **Acted**

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## **Acted Haïti**

Présente en Haïti depuis 2004, Acted répond aux urgences et soutien le relèvement des populations dans le besoin, notamment dans les domaines de l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement, de la sécurité alimentaire et de la reconstruction. En collaboration avec la société civile et les institutions, Acted développe et met aussi en œuvre des programmes axés sur le développement socio-économique et l’adaptation au changement climatique. Acted travaille actuellement dans 5 départements en Haïti à savoir la Grand’Anse, le Sud, le Sud-Est, l’Ouest, et le Centre, et prochainement dans les Nippes.

Concernant les réalisations majeures d’Acted en 2020-2021 :

• 5 562 personnes ont reçu une assistance monétaire afin de subvenir à leurs besoins prioritaires  
• 12 centres de santé réhabilités et soutenus afin de répondre à la pandémie de COVID-19  
• 35 réseaux d’eau et infrastructures réhabilités pour améliorer l’accès à l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement  
• 1 125 personnes relogées grâce à la reconstruction de leur maison  
• 394 532 personnes sensibilisées aux mesures de prévention contre la Covid-19

Suite au tremblement de terre du 14 aout 2021 qui a dévasté les départements du Sud, de la Grande Anse et des Nippes en Haïti, Acted recrute. Acted a été une des première organisation humanitaire à mener des évaluations rapides pour déterminer l’ampleur des dégâts et des besoins, et est déjà fortement mobilisée pour apporter une aide d’urgence aux victimes du séisme, en étroite collaboration avec les autorités haïtiennes. Les activités menées actuellement concernent l’acheminement d’eau potable, la distribution de kits d’hygiène et la conduite de travaux d’assainissement et de réhabilitation des réseaux d’eau, mais aussi la distribution de nourriture, le versement d’aides financières d’urgence, la distribution de biens de première nécessité et, prochainement, la mise en place de solutions de logement pour les personnes les plus vulnérables, dans 12 communes des 3 départements.

## **Rôle et responsabilités principales**

Le/la Directeur.rice Pays Adjoint soutient le/la Directeur.rice Pays en représentant les intérêts d’Acted dans le pays vis à vis du gouvernement, des bailleurs et autres partenaires clef. Le/la Directeur.rice Pays Adjoint.e participe à l’élaboration du profil du Programme en accord avec la stratégie régionale et globale d’Acted . Le/la Directeur.rice Pays Adjoint.e soutient les équipes pour atteindre l’excellence dans le programme et assure les plus hauts niveaux de redevabilité.

***Principales Responsabilités :***

1\. Positionnement et fundraising

- *Analyse du contexte ;*
- *Développement et déploiement de la stratégie ;*
- *Networking, positionnement et représentation générale ;*
- *Relation avec les bailleurs et élaboration de propositions de projets ;*
- *Plaidoyer : (Co-)produire des notes stratégiques, des notes de plaidoyer, communiqués de presse pertinents sur les questions humanitaires et de développement.*
- *Communication : Superviser et assurer la production, dans les délais, d’éléments de communication externe en termes de programming, de méthodes et d’enjeux critiques.*
- *Promotion des organisations sœurs d’ Acted;*

2\. Management et Coordination interne

- *Gestion d’équipe ;*
- *Coordination interne ;*
- *Gestion de crises/conflits ;*
- *Mettre en place et former une équipe de crise au sein du pays ;*

3\. Suivi de la mise en œuvre des projets

- *Mise en œuvre et suivi des projets ;*
- *Grant Management ;*
- *Contrôle qualité des projets ;*
- *Gestion des partenaires ;*

4\. Management FLATS

- *Gestion Financière ;*
- *Gestion Logistique & IT ;*
- *Gestion RH et Administration ;*
- *Suivi des audits externes ;*
- *Gestion Transparence/Conformité ;*
- *Gestion sécurité ;*
- *Suivi de légalisation et d’enregistrement.*

## **Qualifications et compétences requises**

- Etudes supérieures (Master) ;
- Capacités rédactionnelles ;

jobs.title: Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Science)
jobs.body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, proudly supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are renowned for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME) Division** is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the 165 plus staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Science)** will support the Coastal Fisheries Science Team with providing advice to governments, stakeholders and the private sector in planning and implementing coastal fisheries science activities, focusing on coastal finfish and/or invertebrate resources and their supporting habitats.

**The key responsibilities of the role include the following:**

**Assist the CFAP Science team in providing support and training to PICT members to enhance science capacity and capability in coastal living resources data collection, entry, quality control, analysis, interpretation and reporting in support of sustainable management.**

- Assists in the development of coastal fisheries survey (independent and dependent) training materials for countries through needs-based stakeholder consultations, taking into account gender, culture and human rights in the country or territory.
- Assists in the training of local staff in-country and/or online in all areas of data collection, data management, analysis and reporting for coastal fisheries and associated habitats.
- Ensure there are no gender or social inclusion barriers to training activities.

**Contribute to the design and implementation of assessments of coastal living resources, the development and application of innovative tools and approaches for data collection, data management and reporting to inform coastal fisheries management.**

- Participates in the design of surveys based on standardised methodologies and lessons learned.
- Assists in the promotion of the standardisation of data collection and assists with the expansion of standardised data collection and/or monitoring systems for coastal fisheries (finfish, invertebrates, habitat and catch and effort) and programmes at the national level
- Assists in the development and implementation of data systems, tools and approaches that will improve data collection and monitoring of coastal fisheries at the national and regional levels.
- Assists in the collection of biological samples to help inform coastal fisheries assessments.
- Support PICTs to analyse available scientific data on coastal finfish and invertebrate fisheries and associated habitats to provide updates on the status of coastal fishery resources.

**Promote inter-agency networking and cross-sectoral collaboration with partners in coastal fisheries and aquaculture science in support of evidence-based management**

- Liaises, encourages collaboration and works with national, regional and international organisations, research institutes and NGOs on coastal finfish and invertebrate fishery issues.
- Assists in collaboration with other sections/programmes/Divisions within SPC on issues such as food security, small-scale livelihoods, climate change adaptation, etc.

**Contribute to Section administration and communication**

- Maintains up to date corporate and administrative procedures including training data for all activities undertaken.
- Contributes where applicable to Programme, Divisional and Corporate publications, such as Fisheries Newsletters, annual reports, Programme reports to RTMCFA and HoF.
- Contributes to peer-reviewed scientific publications that highlight results and/or developments of international interest.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Pacific Islands**

- Only applicants from Pacific Island countries are eligible to apply.
- Applicants must be employed in a Pacific Island fisheries or conservation / environment department or a recognised NGO working in the field of fisheries science, management or monitoring in a Pacific Island country.

**Qualifications**

- A recognised degree in a discipline relevant to coastal fisheries science (finfish and/or invertebrates), or related field or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least two years’ direct relevant experience in PICT coastal fisheries, particularly applied field research for coastal finfish and/or invertebrates
- Demonstrated experience in undertaking surveys for coastal finfish and/or invertebrates using a range of methodologies
- Understanding of current Pacific Island regional coastal fisheries management and science issues, and experience of working with gender issues relating to fisheries
- Strong PC based computer skills (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook) with knowledge of software programmes for data entry and analysis

**Language skills**

- Excellent communication skills (oral and written) in English

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in a team as well as undertake unsupervised work, and communicate with people from various ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds
- Willingness to travel and undertake overseas assignments in SPC member countries, sometimes under difficult physical conditions.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Requirements:** Only applicants who are nationals and residents of Pacific Island countries are eligible to apply. Applicants must be employed in or contracted by a Pacific Island fisheries or conservation / environment agency, or a recognized NGO working in the field of fisheries science, management or monitoring in a Pacific Island country.

**Letter of endorsement –** A signed letter from the employer, stating they agree to release the applicant for the attachment and that the position will be held for the applicant to return to at the end of the attachment with SPC must be provided before an appointment can be finalized.

**Contract duration –** This appointment will last for a duration of 364 days and will not be renewable.

**Remuneration –** The **Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Science)** is a Band 8 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a salary of SDR (special drawing rights) 3,038 per month, which currently converts to approximately XPF 438,381 (USD 4,071; EUR 3,674). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea –** SPC provides housing support in Noumea and an establishment grant, return airfare, and will reimburse excess accompanied luggage of up to two additional bags. Employees are entitled to: 25 days annual leave and 30 days sick leave per annum; medical and life insurance; and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

We encourage all eligible candidates to apply but please note that as this is a special short-term contract, the full list of benefits included in other international contract types are not available. Appointees may bring their families, but all extra costs for travel, insurance, education, housing and other additional expenses will be their own responsibility.

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Human Resource Administrative Specialist
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Summary**

Under the direct supervision of the HR Manager, the HR Administrative Specialist supports the HR administration affairs for the IRC New Jersey and New York offices. They will assist in the human resources administrative tasks including recruitment and onboarding, personnel files, time attendance management, and orientation. They serve as a knowledgeable resource for staff and management, coordinate employee lifecycle processes, and support special project and initiatives.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Serve as the offices’ first point of contact on employee lifecycle matters, including but not limited to recruitment, new hire setup and orientation, benefits, payroll, on-boarding, leaves of absence, status changes, and separations.
- Assists with HR administrative activities including new hire and hire change paperwork processing, managing background checks for staff.
- Administer the organization’s applicant tracking system, posting and closing locally managed requisitions, and providing related coordination.
- Support compliance with HR-related IRC policies and procedures and state-specific labor laws.
- Coordinate HQ initiatives related to the IRC Way, Duty of Care, Safeguarding, and related content.
- Liaise with HR Manager to escalate issues and connect staff with appropriate HR-related training and other resources.
- Support special projects and initiatives.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for interns throughout the program, providing guidance, support, and direction
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Undergraduate degree in related field preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years of relevant work experience in office administration; human resources, or related field, preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and oral.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.

**Work Environment:**

- Standard office work environment combined with some travel throughout service delivery area.

**Compensation:** ($26.50- $28.04/hour). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Job Overview:**   
The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. The Caseworker connects clients to appropriate financial, medical, social, vocational, and community resources in alignment with program requirements, eligibility guidelines, and IRC standards.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure clients have access to housing, food, medical care, transportation, and community orientation.

- Purchase and transport program-related items; lift, move, and deliver materials necessary for service delivery.
- Conduct client intake assessments and develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with clients.

- Monitor client progress toward established goals, identify barriers, and adjust service plans as needed.

- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and service providers.
- Participate in program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with grant requirements.
- Use a personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation to travel within the service delivery area as needed.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required.
- Experience providing casework, pre-arrival, or intensive case management services preferred.
- Demonstrated experience navigating program eligibility requirements and ensuring accurate service documentation.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.

- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to use digital tools for data entry, research, and reporting.
- Ability to lift and carry items weighing 50+ pounds, including furniture and household goods.
- Ability to drive a large van or passenger vehicle, as required for program delivery.

**Compensation:** ($20.97). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Working Environment**

**This position operates in a hybrid environment that includes office-based work, remote work, and fieldwork within the service delivery area. Typically, the role is based in the office four days per week and remotely one day per week, with field responsibilities possible on all workdays. Schedule flexibility is required, including occasional evenings and weekends for activities such as airport pick-ups.**

At the IRC, we seek to build a welcoming, inclusive environment not only for our refugee clients, but for all of our employees. As an equal opportunity employer, we value the strength found in the diversity of voices, experiences, and backgrounds who join us in our work. Fostering an inclusive culture with equitable practices is everyone's responsibility, and we regularly offer trainings and opportunities to learn more and find ways to do better. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, socioeconomic status, or disability status. We are dedicated to ensuring that disabled individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. In your application, please feel free to indicate your preferred pronouns.

We recognize that few applicants may "check all the boxes," but that each person has their own unique strengths that they would bring to the table. In our commitment to building a diverse and authentic work culture, we invite you to apply anyway. You belong here.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). **Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

jobs.title: HVAC & Cold Chain Mobile Implementation Advisor (f/m/x) – Brussels - MSF Belgium
jobs.body:
**CONTEXT**

At MSF, Logistics aims to provide a safe, functional, and effective care environment for our patients, the populations we assist, and our teams through a pragmatic and solution-oriented approach. Our work involves engineering appropriate solutions that connect medical activities (grouped into Logistics Intervention families) and operational and contextual parameters with technical expertise in medical equipment management, construction, shelter, energy, HVAC, cold chain, motorized fleet, telecommunications, GIS, air operations, and more. Given the diversity and constant evolution of MSF’s operations, Logistics teams are continuously adapting and innovating to meet complex and shifting needs.

The mission of the HVAC team in MSF OCB (Operational Center Brussels) is to design and manage HVAC systems that ensure thermal comfort, optimal air quality, and reduced airborne infection risks in health facilities, while promoting energy efficiency and safeguarding medical stocks by maintaining precise environmental controls in medical warehouses, specifically within the 15°C to 25°C range.

The mission of the Cold Chain team in MSF OCB is to safeguard the integrity of temperature-sensitive medical items in diverse temperature ranges, including refrigerated and ultra-low temperature storage by providing safe, reliable and context adapted solutions for active and passive cold chain infrastructure, equipment, and processes, empowering medical teams to deliver high quality care.

The MIO HVAC and Cold Chain position is related to the fact that MSF’s medical activities require continuous support to ensure a healthy, safe, and suitable environment for patients, medical staff, and supplies by delivering the appropriate temperature, humidity, and indoor air quality conditions.

The MIO HVAC and Cold Chain is part of the Log Support Unit (LSU) under the line management of the Energy & HVAC Team Leader.

As **MIO HVAC and Cold Chain**, you aim to implement or improve practices in MSF projects for an effective and efficient design, management, and use of HVAC and active cold chain equipment, ensuring proper air quality and comfort conditions.

- You contribute to the Energy, HVAC & Cold Chain Team Leader by giving feedback on the functional status of the HVAC and Cold Chain conditions in running projects
- You support the OCB projects in all technical aspects related to the management of HVAC and Cold Chain
- You will be able to provide first-line support to the MSF projects and coordinate with the Energy & HVAC Team Leader to improve and implement the MSF process, tools, and related techniques. You will proactively evaluate and propose solutions in line with their technical domain.
- You assist in implementing HVAC and Cold Chain settings in starting or running projects regarding technical needs, human resources, training, and external contractors according to the MSF framework

**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Provide specialized 1st line support**

- Support the Logistics Teams on HVAC and Cold Chain design, installation, use, maintenance, and decommissioning
- Support the evaluation of HVAC and Cold Chain setups and propose new solutions to improve them where necessary. In addition, support the implementation of the MSF protocols, tools, and techniques related to HVAC and Cold Chain
- Support the development of competencies of the Project technical focal point through HVAC and Cold Chain content-based training
- Support the development of competencies in Cold Chain management for the country and project responsible
- Support the Logistics teams on functional, active cold chain installation according to the needs (including cold room installation and qualification)
- Evaluate the possibilities and advantages of collaboration with other technical families: construction, Water & sanitation, health facility management, pharmacy, vaccination referents, and Biomedical equipment when applicable

**Provide specialized 2nd line support**

- Support the Logistics teams at project level in the evaluation of external suppliers, maintenance contracts, local purchases, and outsourced HVAC and Cold Chain services and equipment such as chillers, air conditioners, central heating systems
- Support the Logistics teams at project level in resolving interdisciplinary technical issues affecting the optimal functionality of the HVAC and Cold Chain conditions concerning electrical or water supply, infrastructural concerns, and infection control matters, among others
- Contribute to ensuring that each/most of the 2nd-line support has an impact on the 3rd-line developments and is properly documented with capitalization reports and sharing of lessons learnt.

**Contribute to the Energy, HVAC, & Cold Chain Team Leader in 3rd line support tools development, such as**

- Guidelines for the design and maintenance of HVAC and Cold Chain settings and active cold chain equipment
- HVAC and Cold Chain technical training
- Follow up and supervise outsourced developments
- Job descriptions of HVAC and Cold Chain Referents and Technicians in the projects

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Education & Experience**

- Technical education (refrigeration technician/engineer) in energy, mechanics, or other formal HVAC training
- Minimum of 2 years professional HVAC experience of which minimum of 1 year of experience in a related position
- Experience in coaching and training of staff is an asset
- Certificates in technical maintenance are an asset
- Relevant work experience in health structures is an asset
- Experience in developing countries is an asset
- Experience of working with MSF or another international humanitarian organization is an asset

**Competencies**

- Ability to design and propose HVAC installations, including maintenance, planning, and procurement
- Ability to compare technical specifications of HVAC equipment
- Ability to design & deliver technical training
- Good understanding of sustainable building design (alt. low energy building design, energy-efficient building design, or passive construction energy systems) and insulation techniques
- Good understanding of electricity and electrical safety
- Good knowledge of HVAC design software: HAP, VRV design tools, AutoCAD, etc.…
- Good analytical skills
- Proactive and willing to propose innovative ideas and solutions rapidly
- Ability to work within an agreed timeline and prioritize activities/tasks
- Results, quality & service oriented
- Strong ability to work in a team and to work in a multi-stakeholder environment
- Willing to take measured risks and responsibility for their choices
- Good communication skills: active listener, communicates clearly and effectively, sense of diplomacy
- Ability to adapt to changing circumstances and contexts

jobs.title: Responsable d’Activités d’Engagement Communautaire et de Promotion de la Santé F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Nous recherchons activement des Responsables d’Activités d’Engagement Communautaire et de Promotion de la Santé pour intégrer les équipes opérant dans les pays d’intervention de MSF France.

**Missions:**

- Etablir une analyse de la situation (population cible, demande de la population, comportements de santé, connaissances en santé, croyances motivant les comportements, facteurs environnementaux, etc.) afin d'élaborer les stratégies d’EC/PS
- Définir et maintenir à jour la stratégie d’EC/PS promotion de la santé et d’engagement communautaire et le plan d’action (objectifs, population cible, campagnes, messages, activités, actions spécifiques, etc.) en impliquant les populations locales.
- Assurer la mise en œuvre des activités d’EC/PS promotion de la santé et d’engagement communautaire et développer les outils de sensibilisation.
- Suivre et évaluer les activités d’EC/PS promotion de la santé et d’engagement communautaire (définition d’indicateurs et d’outils de suivi, collecte et analyse de données).
- Gérer le personnel impliqué dans les activités d’EC/PS promotion de la santé et d’engagement communautaire (recrutement, composition, formation, encadrement, évaluation, etc.).
- Collaborer avec les autres acteurs du projet et les autres partenaires travaillant dans les activités d’EC/PS

**Profil recherché**

**Expérience :**

- 2 ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente (engagement communautaire, promotion de la santé, éducation à la santé, prévention, mobilisation communautaire, etc.)
- Expérience sur les thèmes de santé comme le VIH/sida/hépatite, la tuberculose, la nutrition, la santé sexuelle et reproductive, les maladies chroniques, les épidémies, les violences sexuelles, etc.
- Expérience d'encadrement et de formation souhaitée

**Compétences**

- Une expérience dans l’utilisation d’une méthodologie qualitative
- Une expérience dans la conception, l’implémentation et le suivi de stratégies en Promotion de la Santé et d’Engagement Communautaire
- Une expérience dans des contextes humanitaires
- Une expérience dans la gestion de réseaux sociaux
- Une expérience comme illustrateur ou graphic designer
- Disposition à travailler au sein d'équipes multiculturelles et pluridisciplinaires

**Langue**

- Anglais niveau B1

**Disponibilité** : Engagement 6 à 12 mois

**Ce que nous offrons**

- **Salaire** (à partir du 1er novembre)à déterminer selon la grille salariale MSF Terrain en fonction de l'ancienneté et de l'expérience pertinente
- **Prise en charge** des frais liés à la mission (transport, visas, logement, vaccins, etc.).
- **Assurances** santé, rapatriement, retraite.
- **Perspectives d’évolution** : formations, accompagnement et développement de carrière dans un large éventail de contextes humanitaires.

**Pourquoi vous ?**

Vous êtes rigoureux·se, engagé·e, stratégique, à l’écoute, et vous souhaitez mettre vos compétences au service de populations en situation de vulnérabilité.

**Pour postuler :**

Merci de déposer votre candidature complète sur notre site, à ce lien (candidature spontanée) : [Partir en mission humanitaire avec MSF](https://www.msf.fr/agir/rejoindre-nos-equipes/postuler-pour-mission-terrain)

*Les candidatures féminines sont fortement encouragées.*

jobs.title: NVPPA Supervisor (Service Staff Supervisor)
jobs.body:
**IRC background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job overview**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year:”*

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which IRC will serve newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal.

The NVPPA Supervisor manages the day-to-day work of the program's direct service team across a fully virtual, national caseload. This role is responsible for caseload management, case file review, escalation and resolution of participant issues, and consistent quality across Professional Advancement Plans (PAPs) and uses of direct financial assistance.

**Major responsibilities**

**Supervision and caseload management**

- Manage day-to-day caseloads for direct service staff, including assigning and balancing participants across Career Navigators and routing participants on credentialing and recertification pathways to specialized navigators.
- Conduct regular case file review to confirm that participant records, including eligibility documentation, PAPs, and case notes, are complete, accurate, and timely.
- Resolve escalated participant issues in partnership with the Customer Service Representative, and determine when an issue requires the Deputy Director's involvement.
- Support onboarding and ongoing training of direct service staff.
- Translate program requirements into standard operating procedures and desk guides for the direct service team.

**Program quality and compliance**

- Review PAPs for soundness and confirm that career goals and proposed uses of funds meet ORR eligibility requirements before assistance is requested.
- Ensure required safeguards are applied to higher-risk uses of financial assistance, such as vehicle purchases.
- Work with the data team to ensure required data is recorded in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) and electronic case files are complete for ORR reporting.
- Monitor progress against program targets, identify barriers in the service model such as digital access, language access, or credential evaluation delays, and work with the Deputy Director on practical adjustments.

**Coordination**

- Coordinate handoffs among navigation, training, financial assistance, and job placement so that participants move smoothly through the program.
- Work with administrative and finance staff to ensure financial assistance requests are complete, documented, and aligned with each participant's PAP.
- Coordinate with other resettlement and employment programs, IRC offices, sister agencies, and local partners serving the same participants to support appropriate co-enrollment and avoid duplication of services.

**Job requirements**

- Undergraduate degree required, ideally in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 2 years of management or supervision experience required, including onboarding, coaching, and managing staff performance; experience with remote or distributed teams strongly preferred.
- Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience in human services, preferably in resettlement, workforce development, or employment services.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing high-volume caseloads in a compliance-heavy environment, including case file review and quality assurance.
- Demonstrated skills tracking and reporting information in a database; experience with ETO preferred.
- Familiarity with federally funded program compliance and eligibility documentation; experience with ORR-funded programming preferred.
- Experience developing standard operating procedures or workflow documentation, and familiarity with credential evaluation, professional licensing, or recertification pathways, preferred.
- Demonstrated commitment to client confidentiality and data protection, including oversight of how a remote team handles sensitive personal and immigration documents, required.
- Strong problem-solving, prioritization, and time management skills, and demonstrated success working in a multicultural environment.
- Commitment to anti-racism, ongoing learning, and equitable service to all eligible clients regardless of national origin, language, location, or resettlement agency, required.
- Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and remote collaboration tools required.
- Fluency in spoken and written English required; fluency in an additional language relevant to current refugee populations desired.

**Working environment**

- Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet and a private work space suitable for confidential client conversations.
- Scheduling flexibility is required to serve participants across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

**Compensation:** ($58,000 - $70,000 / Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403(b) retirement savings plan with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, NVPPA
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**SCOPE:**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year.”*

The Deputy Director, NVPPA provides leadership to the National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) funded program implemented in FY27. The Deputy Director leads the NVPPA team and ensures sound program implementation, compliance with ORR regulations, client success, and strong staff supervision and support.

NVPPA is a cooperative agreement carried out over a single 12-month period of performance, September 30, 2026 through September 29, 2027. The Deputy Director is accountable for delivering the program on time, within budget, and in compliance with the terms of the award.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Program Implementation and Deliverables***

- Lead program start-up so that intake, staffing, data tools, and referral protocols are in place as clients arrive, with interpretation and device support where access is a barrier.
- Set and enforce service standards across a high-volume, light-touch model, including a completed Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) and documented career navigation for every enrolled participant.
- Oversee delivery of training, job development, and placement support, and ensure related records are maintained.

***Grant Compliance and Award Management***

- Ensure the program is implemented in accordance with ORR policy, the terms of the cooperative agreement, applicable federal award regulations and cost principles, and IRC policies on data protection, client confidentiality, and safeguarding.
- In partnership with the Senior Director, serve as the program's primary point of contact with the ORR program officer and coordinate with ORR staff, partners, and technical assistance providers.
- Protect the integrity of program eligibility, ensuring eligibility rules are applied consistently and documentation is collected and retained for every enrolled participant.
- Own the internal control environment for direct financial assistance, including documentation before disbursement, alignment with the participant's approved PAP, vendor and training provider verification, and application of IRC Global Supply Chain protocols.
- Maintain audit-ready documentation and ensure required program and financial reports are accurate and submitted on schedule.
- Identify, escalate, and resolve compliance risks, including suspected fraud, working with IRC finance, compliance, and award management colleagues on corrective action.

***Budget and Financial Oversight***

- With the Finance Manager, manage the program budget, monitor spending, and ensure full and timely spend-down and closeout of the award.
- Where a shortfall is projected, provide revised projections and propose reallocation to additional eligible services or a budget revision, at ORR's direction.

***Data, Performance, and Quality Assurance***

- Ensure Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) is configured to program requirements and serves as the system of record, working with the data team on data quality, reporting, and staff training.
- Monitor performance against outcome targets and use data to identify barriers and adjust the service model.
- Establish and oversee a routine quality assurance cycle covering case files, PAPs, and assistance documentation, with findings tracked to resolution.

***Supervision and Staffing***

- Lead recruitment, hiring, and onboarding of a newly formed, fully remote team, and ensure all staff are trained on eligibility rules, eligible uses of funds, documentation standards, and the database.
- Directly supervise the NVPPA Supervisor and the Customer Service Representative, and manage performance, workload distribution, and professional development, and structure staffing so that direct service capacity can be adjusted as enrollment volume becomes known.

***Coordination and Representation***

- In close collaboration with the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR), oversee guidance on appropriate co-enrollment with PIR and other ORR programs, such as Matching Grant, so that participants can meet initial self-sufficiency requirements while pursuing career goals.
- Establish referral and coordination protocols with sister resettlement agencies, IRC offices, and other service providers so that eligible clients can access the program regardless of which agency resettled them, and represent the program to IRC office leadership and external partners.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

**Position reports to:** Senior Director, Economic Empowerment

**Directly supervises:** NVPPA Supervisor; Customer Service Representative

**Indirect supervision:** Direct service team, through the NVPPA Supervisor

**Key relationships:** Internally, the NVPPA team, Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, IRC office leadership, and headquarters finance, compliance, and award management colleagues. Externally, ORR, PIR providers, sister resettlement agencies, training providers, and employers.

**Requirements:**

- University degree in Business, Public Administration, Social Work, Economics, Community Development, or a related field required; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 10 years of experience with progressive responsibility in the design, development, and implementation of workforce, employment, or broader economic empowerment programming, including program monitoring and evaluation.
- Minimum of 5 years' experience managing staff, including remote or geographically distributed teams, with demonstrated ability to coach staff and manage performance directly and through supervisors.
- Demonstrated experience managing federally funded awards and their compliance and reporting requirements; ORR or other HHS award experience strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing client-level direct financial assistance or comparable payment processes, with a strong grasp of internal controls, required; experience with audits or funder monitoring preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to launch a program quickly and manage a budget of comparable scale through spend-down.
- Demonstrated understanding of refugee resettlement and employment services in the U.S. context; familiarity with credential evaluation and professional licensing pathways preferred.
- Excellent communication and organizational skills, including a track record of reporting difficult information to funders accurately and on time.
- Microsoft Office Suite required; ETO or comparable client database experience preferred.
- Commitment to anti-racism and ongoing learning, and English fluency, required.

**Working Environment**

Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet, a private work space suitable for confidential discussions, and scheduling flexibility across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

**Compensation:** ($94,000 - $105,000 \[GEO 1\]). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct).
