jobs.title: Project Financial Audit: English & Ukrainian Speaking
jobs.body:
## 1.Introduction

CBM seeks to engage an **independent external financial auditor or an audit firm providing a suitably qualified audit team** to conduct a final financial audit upon completion of the above-mentioned project. The audit shall cover the **entire 12-month project implementation period**. The audit is commissioned and funded by CBM to fulfil **CBM’s internal audit requirements**. It is *neither* commissioned by DG ECHO *nor* a contractual requirement under the project’s DG ECHO grant agreement.

CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V. (herein referred to as “CBM”), together with the National Assembly of People with Disabilities of Ukraine (herein referred to as “NAPD“) and Momentum Wheels for Humanity (herein referred to as “Momentum”), is currently implementing humanitarian action in **Chernihiv, Sumy, Kharkiv and Poltava** **oblasts** from May 2026 to April 2027 funded by The European Commission’s Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations. The action focuses on health, rehabilitation and protection, with particular attention to persons with disabilities and other groups facing heightened barriers to humanitarian assistance. For more information, please see: [Ukraine: Restoring Access to Health](https://www.cbm.org/news/news-articles/2026/ukraine-restoring-access-to-health.html)

## 2. Scope of services/work

The assignment consists of **one final external financial audit covering the entire 12-month project implementation period,** **May 2026 to April 2027**, including the portions falling within the 2026 and 2027 financial years. The audit shall be conducted following project completion.

For the purposes of this engagement, the project shall be examined as one continuous audit period. Separate annual project audits or separate audit opinions for 2026 and 2027 are not required under these Terms of Reference. The auditor shall nevertheless verify the reconciliation between the project records for both financial years, including year-end balances, amounts carried forward and the correct allocation of transactions to the relevant reporting periods. This arrangement does not alter routine financial reporting obligations or any separate organisational or statutory audit requirements.

The audit is commissioned and financed by CBM to fulfil its internal financial accountability and assurance requirements. It is neither commissioned by DG ECHO nor undertaken as a contractual DG ECHO audit requirement for this project. Any audit separately initiated by DG ECHO falls outside this engagement and remains unaffected by it.

The scope encompasses project funds managed and expenditure incurred by **CBM and both implementing partners, the National Assembly of People with Disabilities of Ukraine (NAPD) and Momentum Wheels of Humanity (Momentum)**. It includes DG ECHO funding, CBM co-financing and relevant project transactions recorded at headquarters level. The assignment is limited to the project’s financial information and related controls; it does not constitute an audit of the organisations’ complete financial statements.

### 2.1Applicable Requirements

The auditor shall assess project financial management and expenditure against the signed grant agreement and its annexes, approved budgets and amendments, partnership agreements, and applicable organisational and national requirements.

For CBM, this includes the relevant provisions of the Finance Handbook and related financial management, procurement and internal control policies. For NAPD and Momentum, the auditor shall assess compliance with their contractual obligations towards CBM and the policies and procedures applicable to their implementation of the project. CBM-specific procedures shall apply to the partners only to the extent required under their agreements.

**Provision and clarification of reference documents**

Before the audit begins, CBM shall provide the auditor with the relevant contractual documents, applicable versions of its Finance Handbook and related policies, and any additional internal audit requirements applicable to this assignment.

Any conflicting or unclear requirements, including questions concerning their applicability or precedence, shall be clarified with CBM during audit planning and documented in the audit work plan.

**Auditing standards and audit opinion**

The audit shall be conducted in accordance with the **International Standards on Auditing (ISA)**, as applicable to the engagement and the financial reporting framework adopted for the consolidated project financial statement.

The auditor shall express an **independent audit opinion** on whether the consolidated project financial statement has been prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework described in the notes to the statement.

The auditor shall also report significant findings concerning compliance with the applicable project requirements and relevant internal controls in the **management letter**.

### 2.2 Areas of examination

**Financial reporting and reconciliation:** Reconcile the consolidated final project financial statement *in EUR* with the project ledgers, transaction listings and financial reports of CBM, NAPD and Momentum. Verify funding received, CBM co-financing, transfers to implementing partners, reported expenditure, outstanding advances, project-related liabilities, refunds and closing balances. Verify that transfers between the organisations are not counted again as expenditure in the consolidated project financial statement.

The financial statement shall include notes disclosing the basis of preparation, the accounting and currency conversion principles applied, and the treatment of advances, liabilities, exchange-rate differences, closing adjustments, project-related transactions settled after the implementation period and, where applicable, non-cash entries. The auditor shall assess whether the disclosed reporting framework has been consistently and appropriately applied.

**Financial-year reconciliation and closing adjustments:** The auditor shall verify that project-related balances and transactions recorded in the 2026 and 2027 financial years are properly reconciled to the consolidated project financial statement. Examine the continuity of records between the two financial years and ensure that the financial-year split has not resulted in omissions or duplication.

This shall include reviewing relevant year-end adjustments, subsequent corrections to project-related accounting records, and the treatment of project-related payments, refunds and liabilities settled after the end of the implementation period, in accordance with the applicable reporting framework and eligibility rules. Any material discrepancies between the annual accounting records and the consolidated project financial statement shall be reported.

**Expenditure and use of funds:** Examine whether expenditure was incurred for the approved project purposes, complies with the applicable funding conditions, is properly authorised and supported by adequate documentation, and is accurately recorded and classified. Review budget amendments, exchange-rate calculations, shared-cost allocations, tax and VAT treatment, and potential duplicate charging or financing. Where indirect costs are reported on a flat-rate basis, verify the applicable contractual rate and calculation base.

**Procurement and contracted services:** Review the application of relevant procurement procedures, including procurement planning, competition, supplier selection, bid evaluation, contract award, documented exceptions, delivery and payment. Examine relevant safeguards against conflicts of interest and compliance with applicable restrictive measures. For medical equipment, assistive devices and other project supplies, review the quality-assurance documentation required under the applicable project rules and evidence of receipt or handover to the intended facilities or recipients.

**Personnel and operating costs:** Examine project-related employment and consultancy contracts, payroll calculations, timesheets or other accepted evidence of staff-cost allocation, payment records, and relevant tax and social contribution documentation. Verify that personnel, travel and office operating costs charged to the project are supported and allocated in accordance with the applicable requirements, including costs paid or recorded at headquarters level.

**Cash, banking and advances:** Review project-related bank and cash records, reconciliations, payment authorisations, fund transfers and the settlement of advances. Trace selected transactions through the accounting records, supporting documentation and proof of payment. Examine outstanding balances and their treatment at the financial-year boundary and at project closure.

**Cash assistance:** Review the financial procedures and supporting records for cash assistance, including Cash for Health where applicable. Examine documented beneficiary eligibility and approval decisions, payment instructions, evidence of transfer or receipt, reconciliations, and the treatment of failed, returned or unclaimed payments. Access to personal and health information shall be limited to what is necessary for the audit and handled confidentially. Where feasible, anonymised or pseudonymised documentation shall be used.

**Assets and stocks:** Examine project-related asset and stock records, supporting procurement documentation, evidence of existence and project use, and relevant handover, transfer or disposal documentation. Review the financial treatment of assets and stocks remaining at project closure, including any documented losses or damage.

**Internal controls, partner oversight and financial monitoring:** Assess the design and operation of controls relevant to project financial management throughout the implementation period, including segregation of duties, delegated authority, payment approvals, record-keeping, reconciliations and management review.

Particular attention shall be given to whether the enhanced staffing, supervision and financial monitoring arrangements envisaged for the project were implemented and operated during the relevant periods. The auditor shall consider changes in these arrangements over time and examine evidence of ongoing financial oversight, early risk identification and corrective action, rather than assuming their effectiveness solely from the existence of policies or staff appointments.

Review CBM’s monitoring of partner expenditure, the review and reconciliation of partner financial reports, documented financial checks and the follow-up of relevant previous findings. Significant weaknesses and recommendations shall be included in the management letter, with findings clearly attributed to CBM, NAPD or Momentum, as appropriate. This review does not constitute a separate audit opinion on the effectiveness of the organisations’ entire internal control systems.

### 2.3 Audit approach and locations

arrangements. The meeting shall take place either in person in Kyiv, subject to security conditions, or online via Zoom. The auditor shall provide a work plan, a document request list and a proposed timetable.

The auditor shall apply a **risk-based audit approach**, independently selecting samples that provide sufficient coverage of all three organisations and the **entire 12-month project implementation period**, including the portions falling within 2026 and 2027. Particular attention shall be given to significant expenditure categories and **high-value or high-risk transactions**. The auditor shall document the materiality applied, the sampling methodology and the coverage achieved by transaction number and value, and shall expand testing where findings warrant it. No fixed sampling percentage or automatic review of 100% of supporting documents is prescribed under these Terms of Reference.

Fieldwork shall include on-site visits to the **offices of CBM, NAPD and Momentum in Kyiv**, subject to security conditions. Relevant project records held at headquarters level shall be reviewed remotely. Any additional visits to health facilities, warehouses or other project locations shall be agreed with CBM in advance, with any additional costs separately identified and agreed.

Where security conditions prevent planned visits, the auditor shall discuss and agree alternative arrangements with CBM. The auditor shall document the alternative procedures performed and report any unresolved limitations affecting the audit.

**Confidentiality and data protection**

*The auditor shall maintain the confidentiality of all financial, contractual and personal information obtained during the assignment.*

*The auditor shall implement appropriate safeguards for the secure transfer, storage, retention and disposal of audit-related information, in accordance with applicable data protection requirements and the engagement agreement.*

## 3. Expected Deliverables

**Before fieldwork**

The auditor shall submit:

- **Work plan:** The proposed audit approach, team responsibilities and arrangements for on-site visits and remote review.
- **Document request list:** The records and supporting documentation to be prepared by CBM and the implementing partners (English & Ukrainian)
- **Proposed timetable:** Dates for fieldwork, draft reports, management responses and final submission, to be agreed with CBM (English & Ukrainian)

These documents shall be provided in English. The document request list and timetable should also be available in Ukrainian where possible.

**Following fieldwork**

The auditor shall provide:

- **Draft audit report and exit meeting:** Present preliminary findings to CBM and the relevant partners and submit a draft audit report and management letter for factual review and written management responses. This review shall not interfere with the auditor’s independent opinion. (English & Ukrainian)
- **Final audit report:** A signed report expressing an independent opinion on the consolidated project financial statement in accordance with its disclosed reporting framework. The report shall include the audited financial statement in EUR, explanatory notes and financial breakdowns by organisation and financial year. It shall state the auditing standards applied, summarise sampling coverage and explain any limitations or modifications to the opinion.
- **Management letter and findings schedule:** Identify weaknesses in financial records, procedures, controls and compliance, with practical recommendations. A supporting schedule shall list questioned or potentially ineligible expenditure by organisation, transaction reference, amount, currency and reason, distinguishing corrected and unresolved items.

All reports shall be submitted to CBM in English. Presentation of findings in English & Ukrainian. The final audit report and audited financial statement shall be provided as a signed PDF, with the management letter also in Word and supporting schedules in Excel. Suspected fraud, corruption or serious irregularities shall be reported promptly through CBM’s designated confidential channels, without waiting for the final report.

jobs.title: Senior AI Technical Specialist
jobs.body:
## About Development Gateway and the Early Grade Education Activity (EGEA)

[Development Gateway: An IREX Venture (DG)](https://developmentgateway.org/) is an international non-profit organization with approximately 80 team members based in more than 10 countries worldwide. By leveraging the combination of programmatic and IT developer capacity and skills within DG, over the last 20 years we have *researched* data ecosystems, *built* digital tools to support those data ecosystems, and *advised* on data strategy and digital transformation to strengthen decision-making, transparency, and service delivery.

DG is one of several consortium partners, led by [IREX](https://www.irex.org/), implementing the Early Grade Education Activity (EGEA, also known as ‘ASAS’) program in Jordan between 2023-2028, funded by the U.S. Department of State. As a large-scale development program, ASAS is a complex, high-paced and outcome-oriented initiative. The consortium itself comprises well over 50 individuals working on the program at any given time (based both in Jordan and abroad). From DG’s side alone, there are likely to be approximately 8-10 personnel supporting implementation at any given time, with at least 4 staff based in Amman, including the Senior AI Technical Specialist.

The overarching objective of ASAS is to improve the quality of early grades (K-G3) education outcomes for children in Jordan. The program aims to achieve this objective by supporting the education of student teachers while they are still at university (pre-service teachers), and also by supporting early grades students and teachers (in-service teachers).

DG’s role within the consortium includes supporting the safe, effective, and responsible integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into Jordan’s education sector, in alignment with the national AI policy. In partnership with the Ministry of Education and Human Resources DevelopmentDG is embarking on an ambitious set of activities that will test AI capabilities in real-world settings.

## Job description

This is an exciting opportunity for an AI specialist who can situate cutting-edge developments in AI within Jordan’s policy context and understand how new technologies can strengthen education systems. Based in Amman, you will turn fast-moving AI advances into practical opportunities for the Ministry of Education, schools, and universities, and explain their value clearly and simply to non-technical audiences.

Rather than executing backend software development or heavy algorithmic coding, your focus is on driving active stakeholder participation, co-designing AI sandbox environments in schools and universities, and explaining complex technical concepts in accessible Arabic and English. You will directly complement IREX’s overarching coordination work by grounding high-level planning into practical, school- and university-level deliverables–ensuring MoEHRD counterparts, school staff, faculty, and administrators remain energized, engaged, and aligned with core project requirements.

Embedded within the ASAS project office in Amman, you will report directly to DG’s Director of Software Development (US) for technical strategy, with a dotted reporting line to DG’s local Project Lead/Advisor for daily operational alignment. Working alongside 30+ Jordan-based consortium colleagues, you will join a creative, globally distributed team that values hard work, practical problem-solving, and collaboration. If you excel at turning institutional friction into clear technical momentum, this role offers the platform to drive meaningful digital adoption across Jordan's education ecosystem.

At DG, we are a creative and dynamic group of people based around the globe. We value and reward hard work, innovative thinking, a commitment to teamwork, and a good sense of humor. With this role, we are looking for a new colleague to join our team and be our Senior AI Technical Specialist on the ASAS program in Amman.

The work you get to do

*In-Service AI: School-Level AI Centers & Sandbox Pilots*

- Provide technical support to establish six AI Centers in MoEHRD-selected schools, including assessing facility readiness, defining equipment and technical specifications, and verifying that installed centers are ready for use.
- Work with the MoEHRD and relevant stakeholders to co-design the scope, governance, school selection, institutional roles and implementation approach for AI sandbox pilots in three schools across the country including facilitating technical consultations and participatory workshops. Support the preparation of a technical brief outlining the objectives, scope, expected outcomes, and implementation approach for the school AI sandbox pilots, aligned with the Year 3 AI Readiness Assessment and policy brief.
- Lead the technical set-up of school sandboxes, support the design and delivery of sensitization workshops and hands-on training, , and help pilot schools shortlist 2–3 priority AI use cases.
- Support monitoring and evaluation of AI sandbox pilots, including assessment of technical performance, usability, pedagogical relevance, user adoption, and documentation of results, challenges, and lessons learned.
- Support the organization and technical facilitation of workshops to present and validate pilot results with MoEHRD, participating schools, and relevant stakeholders.
- Provide ongoing virtual sandboxing support, including a helpdesk that responds to technical questions and pedagogical questions on applying AI to agreed use cases.
- Translate pilot results into evidence and recommendations for MoEHRD leadership, the National AI for Education Forum, and a national approach to scaling successful use cases.
- Support MoEHRD and Field Directorates in assessing technical, institutional, and operational requirements for sustaining school AI Centers and scaling successful AI applications.

*Pre-Service AI: University Engagement & Institutional Integration*

- Serve as the lead technical interlocutor for partner universities, directly tackling engagement friction and driving active academic participation in project activities.
- Uncover operational bottlenecks and university requirements, translating qualitative institutional feedback into structured digital use cases.
- Lead the co-design, testing, and university-level rollout of sandbox AI environments, establishing clear feedback loops with faculty and administrators.

*Requirements Scoping & Technical Translation*

- Scope functional requirements for applied AI initiatives (e.g., automated reporting, documentation synthesis, data collection tools) without needing to write heavy software code.
- Translate complex technical concepts into accessible, bilingual (Arabic/English) specs and guidance notes for non-technical stakeholders, MoEHRD and university leadership, and vendors.
- Establish User Acceptance Testing (UAT) protocols, rollout sequencing, and data stewardship standards for school, university and ministry systems.

*Alignment with IREX Coordination & Programmatic Support*

- Complement IREX's programmatic coordination and oversight by serving as the Jordan-based technical liaison between DG's development team, IREX, MoEHRD, schools, and partner universities, translating agreed plans into actionable technical activities and supporting the timely resolution of implementation challenges.
- Serve as the primary Jordan-based technical liaison between DG's development team, IREX technical teams, MoEHRDHRD counterparts, schools, and partner universities, ensuring timely validation of requirements, coordination of technical implementation, resolution of operational challenges, and alignment with agreed work plans and institutional priorities
- Co-develop SOPs, workflows, and training materials that enable school and university staff to practically adopt AI tools in their daily routines.
- Provide regular, proactive updates on school and university technical readiness, operational risks, and adoption milestones to project leadership.

*Data Governance & Responsible AI*

- Establish practical ethical standards, governance rules, and privacy protections across all school and university AI sandbox pilots.
- Define data de-identification practices, accuracy checks, and hosting protocols to protect sensitive institutional and student data.

## Qualifications and experience requirements

- **Experience:** 5+ years of experience in data systems, digital transformation, or technology adoption, with proven success driving stakeholder engagement within Jordanian universities or national institutions. Experience with AI applications, data science tools, or emerging technologies in education.
- **Technical Alignment:** Demonstrated capacity to map user requirements to applied AI/data tools and structure low-risk use cases (no direct programming required).
- **Language Skills:** Professional fluency in written and spoken Arabic and English, with demonstrated ability to draft technical specifications in both languages.
- **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in STEM, Information Management, Education, or a related field.

## Preferred (desirable) qualifications

- Degree and/or certification in artificial intelligence, machine learning, or computer science is a plus.
- Familiarity with donor-funded programming (e.g., U.S. State Department) and their reporting standards.

Position Details

This is a **full-time staff position**, embedded in the ASAS office in Amman. The role is expected to run for approx. 2 years, pending annual performance reviews. The expected annual salary range is USD 50,000-65,000, depending on relevant experience.

jobs.title: Grants Manager
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Grants Team at IRC in Sacramento works to leverage public and private funding opportunities through prospecting, proposal development, grants, and subaward contract management. The Grants Manager is primarily responsible for overseeing the full range of pre- and post-award activities required to prepare concept notes, proposals, and budgets, comply with internal approval processes, and align with compliance requirements of public agencies and private foundations. Work is performed under the supervision of a Development Director and in collaboration with IRC Sacramento’s leadership, finance, programs, as well as headquarters’ technical team, and awards and business development units.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Development and Grants Management***

Prospecting

- Represent Sacramento office in all regional opportunities, particularly for restricted funding, in close coordination with Site Directors, Development Director, Technical Advisors, relevant program leads, and grant coordinators.
- Collaborate with the Development Director in prospecting efforts, utilizing an internal standard operating procedure to support both restricted and unrestricted fundraising needs.
- In collaboration with IRC Sacramento Development Director, work with the Site Director to develop a funding strategy and timeline and perform prospective research on potential public and private funders.

Proposal Development (Pre-Award)

- Develop and manage the Sacramento region’s proposal calendar.
- Lead concepts note, proposal, and budget development, including ensuring log frames, program design, and narrative meet high quality standards in coordination with Programs/Site director, Finance Director, and headquarters’ Resource Acquisition and Management (RAM), and ensure all supporting documentation in the applications are up to date.
- Provide pre-award support and coverage when needed to the local offices.
- Lead negotiation and agreements stage with donors and ensure contract terms are communicated with Finance and Programs through grant kick off meetings and recorded in Asana project tracking.
- Coordinate grant opening and closing meetings for every funded opportunity across the Sacramento office portfolio.

Grants Management (Post-Award)

- Modify final budgets as requested by donor and Site Director/program lead and communicate with Finance and RAM to ensure incoming restricted funds will be tracked.
- Lead negotiation and agreements stage with donors and ensure contract terms are communicated with Finance and Programs through grant kick off meetings and recorded in Asana project tracking.
- Provide support with reports, including copy-editing, coordinating report timelines with headquarters, and submission.
- Serve as a main point of contact for donors across Sacramento office to ensure communication adheres to IRC policy and best practices.
- Develop and ensure the effective maintenance of contract and grant files for each funded program with consistent documentation standards.
- Be a local subject expert for IRC’s Business Development Standards.
- Be a local subject expert for IRC’s internal grants systems (PEERS and OTIS).

Partnerships

- Be a local subject expert in IRC’s internal partnership process, PEERS, to provide technical support to the Partnership Grants Coordinator to ensure subawardees’ contracts are drafted with detailed information on scope of work, deliverables, fund disbursement, and monitoring plans in coordination with the partners and program staff, and in compliance with Finance and RAM.

***Supervision & training:***

- Provide leadership and management of the Grant Coordinator in Turlock, to ensure all tasks are covered and team workload is managed in a way that respects and promotes work life balance and professional growth.
- Provide training and support to new hires ensuring staff meet the expectations of their role and meet responsibilities in a timely manner.
- Be a local subject expert in OTIS and IRC’ RAM’s Business Development processes, and the local Sacramento/Turlock Business Development workflow.

***Systems & Accountability:***

- Maintain proposal calendar, pipelines, grants tracking, and regularly update senior management with up-to-date data
- Ensure the go/no-go review process of opportunities are consistently applied and strengthened by working with senior management to ensure proposals are of high quality and grants staff are at capacity
- Ensure continuous improvement on the utilization of Asana to track opportunity pipelines, award management, and reporting in coordination with senior management, Finance, and program staff
- Establish and continuously update a Standard of Practice (SOP) for Grants staff in coordination with the Finance team and headquarters’ Resource Acquisition and Management (RAM
- Leverage regular communications with Finance, RAM, and the Sacramento office to improve SOP and workflow

**Secondary duties:**

- Work closely with site leads and program staff to prepare interim and final reports to grantors.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Development Director
- **Position Supervises:** Grants Coordinator (in Turlock office)
- **Indirect Reporting:** Site Director  
    **Other Internal and/or External Contacts:**
- ***Internal:*** Director of Finance, Sacramento/Turlock Executive Director, Sacramento Program Managers & Coordinators, Technical Advisors, HQ Resource Acquisition and Management department
- ***External***: Foundations and public funders at city, county, state, and federal levels

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Bachelor’s Degree required in nonprofit management, community development, social sciences, social work, or related fields, or demonstrated work experience of similar knowledge. Master’s degree a plus.
- Certification or continuing education in project management, proposal development and/or fundraising a strong plus.

***Work Experience:***

- Five+ years of nonprofit or public sector experience in development and grants.
- Five+ years of experience in a supervisory role.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Excellent writing, research, and organizational skills.
- Familiarity with grants process of government funding agency(ies) (federal, state, or county/city level)
- Familiarity with the Sacramento non-profit/philanthropy environment a plus
- Familiarity and comfort working with budgets and finance departments
- Ability to work autonomously in their scheduling and prioritizing within tight deadlines and focused on the work product.
- Self-directed but with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work well within a team
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications: Word, Excel, Outlook, and project management tools, e.g. Asana
- Experience in IRC systems of PEERS and OTIS a plus (for IRC internal candidates)
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

***Language Skills:***

- Excellence in written and spoken English

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard hybrid office environment (this is not a fully remote position)
- Occasional travel to Turlock office site as needed

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Compensation:** ($84,872-$91,137 - Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

jobs.title: Grants and Collaborations Team Leader – Performance Enhancement
jobs.body:
## ***Description***

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Operations and Integration (O&I) collective** delivers essential enabling services that support the organisation’s scientific and technical portfolio. Our key functions include corporate services, programme support, partnerships, resource mobilisation, and strategic engagement. These services are coordinated through our regional and satellite offices across the Pacific and Europe. Additionally, the O&I collective leads a dedicated workstream focused on organisational change and transformation to drive continuous improvement and adaptability.

The role – **Grants and Collaborations Team Leader – Performance Enhancement** will lead a small team within the Grants and Collaborations Team to ensure the effective and timely delivery of high-quality grant management services across SPC. The incumbent will provide expert advice and support on complex grant-related activities, strengthen grants management processes, and drive continuous improvements in grant systems and practices. The Team Leader will also play a key role in fostering strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, ensuring grant activities meet SPC’s standards, comply with funder requirements and contribute to the achievement of SPC’s strategic objectives.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Systems and processes: Grants Performance, Quality and Continuous Improvement**

- Lead the development and implementation of initiatives to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, quality and consistency of SPC's grants and collaborations function.
- Develop practical improvement plans and oversee their implementation, monitoring progress and reporting results to the Grants and Collaborations Manager.
- Identify and implement improvements to Grants and Collaboration Tools and Systems: Enhance the tools and systems used for managing grants and collaborations, ensuring they support better understanding, compliance, and efficiency across SPC.
- Monitor the performance of grants management processes and identify trends, bottlenecks, control weaknesses, recurring issues and opportunities for improvement.
- Establish and maintain appropriate performance indicators, service standards and quality measures for the Grants and Collaborations function.

**Systems, Data, Digitalisation and Process Improvement**

- Lead the review and improvement of grants and collaborations systems, tools and workflows including supporting the evaluation, selection and implementation of a Grants Management System (GMS) including definition of business requirements and integration with Business Central (PR-to-Pay); and contribute to the transition to a Centre-Led operating model for grants management.
- Identify opportunities for automation, digitalisation and improved use of technology across the grants lifecycle.
- Work with ICT and relevant business units to define business requirements for grants management systems and digital solutions.
- Promote the use of reliable grants data to support operational management, performance monitoring, reporting and decision-making.
- Develop and maintain appropriate management information, dashboards and performance reports.

**Advice and Guidance**

- Provide expert advice on SPC grants and collaborations processes: Provide expert advice to the Grants and Collaborations Manager and senior management on grants management performance, risk, systems and process improvement.
- Provide advice to decision-makers on complex grant and collaboration Issues: Provide evidence-based advice to relevant committees and decision-makers on systemic grants management issues and proposed improvements.
- Brief decision-makers on trends, performance issues, risks and opportunities for improvement.
- Prepare high-quality reports, briefing notes, dashboards and management information for internal stakeholders.
- Support the Grants and Collaborations Manager in preparing reports for senior management, the Executive, governing bodies and the Audit and Risk Committee.

**Management of staff**

- Team leadership and supervision: Lead the staff, ensuring clear direction, support, and motivation is provided to staff.
- Recruitment and staffing: Lead the recruitment and selection process ensuring that staffing level and capabilities are appropriate to meet operational needs.
- Performance management, training and development:
- manage the performance management process for staff ensuring that team performance goals are aligned with SPC objectives.
- manage the training and development needs for staff ensuring continuous learning and skill development within the team.

**Outreach, education and training**

- Develop mechanisms to capture, share and institutionalise lessons learned across the Grants and Collaborations Team.
- Lead communication and change-management activities associated with new or revised grants processes, systems and requirements.
- Provide capacity building: Lead the development and delivery of training programs to internal and external stakeholders to enhance understanding and management of grants and collaborations, including pre-award and post-award processes, and as part of SPC’s performance enhancement work.
- Build collaborative relationships: Lead on fostering strong, collaborative relationships with all SPC stakeholders, ensuring alignment and support for grants and collaborative activities.
- Ensure effective communication: Lead on maintaining open and effective lines of communication with key stakeholders, building strong relationships to support the effective implementation of grants and collaborative initiatives.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## ***Key selection criteria***

**Qualifications**

- A postgraduate qualification in a relevant field such as law, finance, grants management, business administration or international development or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 7–8 years of relevant experience in grants management, programme/project management, business administration, finance, risk management, compliance, process improvement, international development, law or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience leading or coordinating teams and/or complex cross-functional initiatives.
- Demonstrated experience reviewing and improving organisational processes, systems or operating procedures.
- Experience in performance monitoring, data analysis and management reporting.
- Experience developing guidance, procedures, tools and training materials.
- Demonstrated ability to translate complex information into practical recommendations.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## ***Salary, terms and conditions***

**Contract Duration** – **3 years** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Grants and Collaborations Team Leader – Performance Enhancement** is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 3,245‒4,057 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 10,028–12,535 (USD 4,349–5,436; EUR 3,924–4,905). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications.Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: DIRECTRICE.EUR REGIONAL.E DES OPERATIONS ADJOINT - AFRIQUE DE l'OUEST
jobs.body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision de la Directrice Régionale des Opérations du Pool Afrique de l'Ouest, Australe et de la Mission France, vous contribuez à la définition et au développement de la stratégie des bureaux pays d'ACF. En étroite collaboration avec les directeurs-trices pays, les directeurs-trices adjoint programmes et l'équipe du pool que vous encadrez. Vous accompagnez la mise en oeuvre des orientations stratégiques et le développement des activités.  
Dans ce cadre, vos missions seront de :  
Manager l'équipe du Pool sous son rattachement hiérarchique  
recruter les membres de l'équipe en lien avec les référent.es fonctionnement et le département RH du siège  
assurer la gestion quotidienne de l'équipe  
fixer les priorités, veiller au respect des règles internes et à la bonne interaction entre les membres de l'équipe  
initier et suivre les plans d'actions individuels de l'équipe   
assurer les entretiens d'évaluation   
organiser des points individuels avec les membres de l'équipe   
Accompagner la définition et la mise en oeuvre des stratégies pays  
Co-animer la réflexion stratégique (programmatique et budgétaire) avec le DRO entre les missions et le pool  
S'assurer de compatibilité et d ela cohérence des programmes à fort enjeux stratégiques avec les stratégies pays  
 Apporter appui et conseil aux missions sur les stratégies de financement   
s'assurer de l'organisation des évaluations externes des programmes   
en accord avec le DRO, exercer un rôle et des responsabilités directes sur la mission   
Accompagner la définition et faciliter le financement de programmes régionaux, multi-pays, multi-acteurs à fort enjeux stratégiques  
Conseiller les bureaux pays dans l'élaboration de nouveaux programmes en fonction des besoins  
contribuer à la coordination du réseau ACF-IN   
Contribuer au recrutement et au développement des RH dans sa filière métier (DPA programmes, grant writer,..)  
Valider techniquement les candidatures des directeurs-trices pays adjoint programmes, responsables de département programmes et coordinateur-trice de consortium  
assurer les briefings et debriefings des membres de la coordination   
assurer le suivi régulier, l'accompagnement et le support aux DPA programmes.   
animer des sessions de formation au siège, en région, sur le terrain.

  
Profile :

 Vous êtes titulaire d'un Master 2 en sciences sociales ou politiques ou équivalent. Vous avec au moins 5 ans d'expérience professionnelle en mission humanitaire sur des postes de coordination dans les domaines d'activité d'ACF (Nutrition, Santé, Sécurité Alimentaire, Eau Assainissement Hygiène, Santé Mentale et Soutien Psychosocial ou fonctions Support).  
Vous êtes reconnu-e pour vos qualités d'encadrement d'équipe et de leadership.  
Votre connaissance de l'Afrique de l'Ouest et Australe, et/ou vos expériences terrains dans cette zone géographique sera un atout.  
Vous maîtrisez l'ensemble des leviers des bailleurs institutionnels (écritures de propositions, financements, orientations, conformité).  
Vous êtes autonome, diplomate et proactif-ve. Vous avez la capacité à porter une vision et à insuffler une dynamique d'équipe. Vous avez d'excellentes capacités rédactionnelles et orales en français et en anglais.  
  
  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
Statut : Cadre Intégré - CDD de 3 mois  
Temps plein  
Lieu : Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis)  
Rémunération :De 47K à 52Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience  
Avantages:25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT  
Couverture santé, prévoyance : Prise en charge à 80% par ACF  
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)  
Indemnités Transport : Prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail

Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)

jobs.title: Haiti - Coordinateur.trice Terrain - Artibonite
jobs.body:
## QUE FAISONS-NOUS...

**Date de début souhaité:** ASAP  
**Durée de la mission:** 6 mois  
**Localisation**: Artibonite

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL** (SI) est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis plus de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans 26 pays, les équipes de SI - 3 200 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de salariés nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

## LA MISSION

La mission Haiti a actuellement une base à Port au Prince et le bureau de la coordination. Les projets concernent la WASH et la SAME/NUT en consortium avec des partenaires nationaux et internationaux. Elle est financée par OCHA, CDCS, SDC, ECHO, UNICEF, IFSAN entre autre. Depuis deux ans, la mission a connu une bonne croissance en terme d'opérations et de budget, répondant aux urgences dans la Zone Métropolitaine de Port au Prince mais également développe des actions de plus long termes. C'est dans cette dynamique que la mission Haiti a décidé d'ouvrir une nouvelle base en Artibonite, basée à Saint Marc afin de répondre aux besoins en EHA des populations dans ce département. La base est en début d'ouverture à l'heure actuelle, la mission principale du.de la CT aura pour but de régulariser la base après son ouverture et de la terminer.

17 expatriés et 80 staffs nationaux dans l'unique base et coordination de Port au Prince. Un premier set-up de 2/3 expats et une petite vingtaine de staffs nationaux est à entrevoir pour la base d'Artibonite.

## DESCRIPTIF DE POSTE

**OBJECTIF GENERAL**

Le/la Coordinateur.trice Terrain a un rôle de Directeur Pays (DP) par délégation sur l'Artibonite pour SI.  
Il/elle propose en fonction du contexte géopolitique et humanitaire la stratégie sur l'Artibonite et s'assure de sa mise en œuvre une fois validée.  
Il/elle contrôle et garantit que les projets se déroulent en adéquation avec la charte de Solidarités International et dans   
le respect des procédures internes et contractuelles.  
Il/elle mobilise les moyens matériels et financiers nécessaires à la bonne conduite des programmes et en supervise la gestion.  
Il/elle coordonne les équipes en place et est le garant de leur sécurité sur sa zone d’affectation.  
Il/elle est l’interlocuteur.trice direct.e et privilégié.e du/de la DP

**ENJEUX ET DEFIS SPECIFIQUES**

Ce poste est une création suite à l'ouverture de la base Artibonite. Nous attendons un.e CT expérimenté sur ce type de niveau sécuritaire mais aussi possédant une grande expérience dans la structuration d'une nouvelle base après la phase d'ouverture.  
Les enjeux sécuritaires - niveau 4 chez SI - sont nombreux notamment dans le cadre d'une base nouvelle.

**PRIORITES SUR LES 2-3 PREMIERS MOIS**

Gestion et de la mise en place des projets

Gestion opérationnelle de la sécurité sur la zone et continuité du travail d'accès engagé

Support au développement de nouvelles propositions de projets sur la zone

Travailler en interne sur la structuration de la base, finaliser les recrutements, finaliser l'installation de la base vie et bureaux, formation au travail chez SI, mise en place des procédures.

Accompagner la stratégie sur l'Artibonite et continuer son développement

Contribuer à renforcer le lien avec nos partenaires locaux et internationaux et les clusters de la zone

**CONTRAINTES SECURITAIRES**

Haiti est catégorisé en Niveau 4, La sécurité est très volatile/dégradée en Artibonite dû à la présence des groupes armés et d'affrontements quotidiens, mais n’empêche pas la conduite des activités. Les règles de sécurité de la mission sont strictes (couvre-feu au coucher du soleil).

## VOTRE PROFIL

**DIPLÔME ET EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Niveau Master

Experience dans le secteur humanitaire : 5 ans et plus

Experience sur un poste similaire : 3/4 ans

**COMPETENCES**

COMPETENCES TECHNIQUES

1. Capacité à suivre et analyser le contexte humanitaire, politique, culturel, social, économique
2. Compétences pour garantir la coordination, le développement, le suivi et l’évaluation des programmes mis en œuvre sur sa zone d’intervention
3. Proposer le dimensionnement humain, financier et logistique pour sa zone d’intervention ainsi que son organisation
4. Gestion des RH, recrutement, induction, création de dynamiques d'équipes, mise en place de la relation base éloignée - coo pour Haiti (l'autre base est à Port au Prince, directement en lien avec la coo)
5. Etre responsable de la sécurité des équipes et des biens sur sa zone d’affectation, sur délégation de la DP

COMPETENCES TRANSVERSALES

1. Analyse, décision et gestion de crise : capacité à évaluer les risques, anticiper, décider et agir sous pression.
2. Leadership et communication : encadrer, former, sensibiliser et transmettre des consignes claires aux équipes et partenaires.
3. Diplomatie et adaptabilité : négocier avec divers acteurs, entretenir des relations de confiance et s’ajuster à un environnement instable.

**LANGUES**

1. Français
2. Anglais apprécié

## SI VOUS OFFRIRA LES CONDITIONS SUIVANTES...

**Un poste salarié :** Selon l'expérience, à partir de EUR 3080 bruts par mois (2800 salaire de base + 10% d'indemnité de congé annuel versée mensuellement) et un Per Diem mensuel de USD 750.

SI couvre également les frais de logement et les frais de déplacement entre le pays d'origine de l'expatrié et le lieu d'affectation.

**Breaks :** Pendant la mission, un système d'alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois (avec USD 850 alloués par Solidarités International). A ces périodes de pause, s'ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.

**Couverture sociale et médicale :** Les expatriés bénéficient d'une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d'un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

**CONDITIONS DE VIE :**

A l'heure de l'ouverture de ce poste, la mission n'a pas commencé l'ouverture, aucun lieu de vie n'est pour l'instant défini. D'ici l'arrivée du.de la CT, la mission aura identifié un lieu de vie et de bureau.  
A Saint Marc, la sécurité reste volatile avec des restrictions sécuritaires importantes. Vie sociale limitée à quelques restaurants et à la présence de MSF et NRC.

jobs.title: Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies
jobs.body:
ILGA World is seeking an Advocacy Specialist on Treaty Bodies, who will work as part of our advocacy programme and coordinate the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with [the United Nations human rights treaty body system](https://www.ohchr.org/en/treaty-bodies).

**Deadline for applications:** Tuesday, 10 November 2026 – 23:59 (Central European Time, CET)  
**Start of the position:** January/February 2027, subject to successful work authorisation and any applicable notice period

## Who can apply?

Anyone

- with dedication to – and experience in regard to – the human rights of persons with diverse sexual orientations, [**gender**](https://ilga.org/glossary/gender/) identities, gender expressions and [**sex characteristics**](https://ilga.org/glossary/sex-characteristics/)
- who meets the requirements set out below

is welcome to apply.

## Overview

The Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies is part of ILGA World’s advocacy prgramme and coordinates the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with the [**United Nations**](https://ilga.org/glossary/united-nations/) human rights treaty body system.

The role advances the rights of people and communities of diverse SOGIESC by connecting grassroots, national and regional advocacy with international human rights mechanisms. It provides technical assistance to ILGA World members, regions and human rights defenders; supports strategic engagement with treaty bodies; and helps ensure that movement priorities, evidence and lived realities inform [**country reviews**](https://ilga.org/glossary/country-reviews/), normative developments, jurisprudence and follow-up at national level.

Working under the strategic direction of the Advocacy Senior Manager and closely with colleagues across the advocacy programme, ILGA regions, member organisations and partner organisations, the Specialist monitors treaty body processes and opportunities, coordinates submissions and briefings, supports strategic litigation and national follow-up, analyses recommendations and jurisprudence, develops capacity-strengthening resources, and maintains relationships with treaty body members and OHCHR staff. The role also works across ILGA World programmes to connect advocacy with knowledge production and movement strengthening.

## Responsibilities

The Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies reports to the Advocacy Senior Manager and is responsible for the day-to-day coordination and delivery of ILGA World’s Treaty Bodies portfolio within the Advocacy Programme.

### Specific to this position, this includes:

- Implement ILGA World’s Treaty Bodies advocacy workplan and coordinate the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with the UN human rights Treaty Body system, serving as the organisational focal point for Treaty Bodies-related advocacy.
- Monitor Treaty Body sessions, reporting cycles, country reviews, lists of Issues Prior to Reporting (LOIPRs) under the Simplified Reporting Procedure, follow-up procedures, general comments, individual communications and other developments, identifying timely and strategic opportunities for SOGIESC advocacy.
- Develop and implement advocacy strategies to advance the human rights of people and communities of diverse SOGIESC through country reviews, normative development, individual communications and other relevant Treaty Body procedures.
- Provide technical assistance to ILGA World members, regions, LGBTI organisations and human rights defenders engaging with Treaty Bodies, including advocacy planning, reporting, preparation of written and oral submissions, briefings and follow up strategies.
- Coordinate and contribute to ILGA World and joint submissions, shadow report inputs, briefing materials, statements, position papers and other advocacy products in consultation with affected communities, members, regions, partners, and external legal experts
- Facilitate the meaningful participation of human rights defenders in Treaty Body processes, including organising briefings and engagement with Treaty Body members and OHCHR staff.
- Coordinate ILGA World’s strategic litigation engagement before Treaty Bodies, including identifying appropriate opportunities, supporting individual communications and third-party interventions, and contributing to follow-up on decisions in collaboration with members, partners and relevant legal experts.
- Monitor, systematise and analyse SOGIESC-related [**concluding observations**](https://ilga.org/glossary/concluding-observations/), recommendations, general comments, jurisprudence, decisions and other Treaty Body outputs, and contribute to compilations, briefings and analytical resources.
- Support ILGA World members and human rights defenders to use Treaty Body recommendations, decisions and jurisprudence in national advocacy, including follow up and implementation, and document relevant results, challenges and good practices.
- Develop and deliver training, webinars, guidance and other capacity strengthening resources to strengthen civil society engagement with the Treaty Body system.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with Treaty Body members, OHCHR staff, civil society organisations, legal experts, academics and other relevant stakeholders, and represent ILGA World in relevant meetings, consultations and external spaces.
- Monitor and contribute to discussions concerning Treaty Body strengthening, accessibility, effectiveness and other institutional developments affecting the system.
- Work across ILGA World programmes and advocacy portfolios to strengthen coherence between Treaty Bodies, the Human Rights Council, Universal Periodic Review, Special Procedures and thematic advocacy, and ensure that relevant ILGA World research and monitoring data inform Treaty Body engagement.
- Contribute to planning, budgeting, monitoring, evaluation and learning, donor reporting and funding proposals relating to the Treaty Bodies portfolio, and work with the Communications team to make relevant opportunities, developments and outcomes accessible to members, partners and wider audiences.

### **General**

- Actively contribute to promoting and achieving the organisation’s objectives.
- Engage and collaborate with colleagues across the Advocacy Programme and other ILGA World teams to strengthen a shared organisational culture and ensure coordinated, movement-informed work.
- Ensure that all activities are carried out with full regard to ILGA World policies.
- Work as a part of the ILGA World staff team.
- Perform other duties as required.

### **Relationships with colleagues**

ILGA values creative and inclusive approaches to work and management that have been achieved through cross-service area working and the participation of staff at all levels in the organisation. Staff have line management arrangements and specific key relationships, which are detailed in their job descriptions, but they will also need to work collaboratively with their colleagues in order to achieve their agreed targets and outcomes to the required standards.

## Performance of duties, remuneration, and benefits

- This position requires relocation to Geneva, Switzerland.
- This position is subject to the successful granting of the necessary Swiss work authorisation.
    - Where required, ILGA World will submit and support the work permit application for the selected candidate. However, the relevant Swiss authorities make decisions on work authorisation, and ILGA World cannot guarantee that an application will be successful. Any offer of employment and appointment to the position is therefore conditional upon the required work permit being granted. If the necessary authorisation cannot be secured, ILGA World will not be able to confirm or proceed with the appointment.
- The position is advertised at 100% of a full-time position.
- ILGA World remunerates under a three-tiered salary matrix structure. The annual salary offered for the 100% position is 81,060 CHF.
- In addition, ILGA World offers 32 days, inclusive of legal holidays (“bank holidays”) and annual leave and contributions to health care costs.
- ILGA World operates under a flexible working system that – among others – includes flexible working hours.
- The weekly working time is 40 hours on a 100% position.

## Requirements

### **Education and qualifications**

- A master’s university degree or equivalent in [**international human rights law**](https://ilga.org/glossary/international-human-rights-law/), law, political science, international relations or a related field, combined with 6 years of relevant work experience

or

- A first-level university degree in combination with 8 years of relevant and qualifying experience

or

- 10 years of relevant and qualifying experience instead of a master’s or first-level degree

### **Experience**

- A minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in human rights advocacy, policy or legal work, preferably within an international, regional or national civil society organisation, multilateral institution or similar setting.
- At least 2 years of direct engagement with United Nations human rights mechanisms, including substantive experience working with one or more UN Treaty Bodies.
- Experience developing and implementing advocacy strategies relating to Treaty Body country reviews, normative development or other treaty body procedures.
- Experience drafting shadow reports, written submissions, briefing materials, statements, position papers or other advocacy documentation for international human rights mechanisms.
- Experience providing technical assistance, guidance or capacity strengthening to civil society organisations and human rights defenders engaging with international human rights mechanisms.
- Experience analysing international human rights standards, concluding observations, recommendations and/or jurisprudence and translating complex legal developments into accessible advocacy guidance.
- Experience with or strong familiarity with strategic litigation, individual communications or other forms of legal advocacy before international or regional human rights mechanisms.
- Demonstrated experience working collaboratively with grassroots organisations, LGBTI human rights defenders and diverse stakeholders across different national, cultural and political contexts.
- Experience in project coordination, including planning, monitoring, evaluation, learning and narrative reporting, including in donor-funded work.
- Experience building and maintaining working relationships with UN officials and experts, civil society organisations, legal practitioners, academic partners and other relevant stakeholders.

### **Technical requirements**

- Advanced skills in legal and policy analysis, with strong knowledge of international human rights law and its application to [**sexual orientation**](https://ilga.org/glossary/sexual-orientation/), gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics.
- Demonstrated in-depth knowledge of the UN human rights Treaty Body system, including country review processes, normative outputs, follow-up procedures and individual communications.
- Ability to monitor, systematise and analyse Treaty Body recommendations, general comments, jurisprudence and other outputs and identify strategic advocacy opportunities.
- Strong research and drafting skills, including the ability to present complex legal and policy developments clearly and accessibly to different audiences.
- Demonstrated ability to build and sustain partnerships with member organisations, human rights defenders, UN officials, civil society organisations and other stakeholders.
- Strong understanding of SOGIESC human rights issues and commitment to feminist, decolonial, intersectional and anti-oppressive approaches to advocacy.

### **Other requirements**

- Strong communication, facilitation and diplomatic skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with diverse audiences
- Excellent organisational skills, sound judgement and the ability to prioritise work, meet deadlines and adapt to changing advocacy opportunities
- Proven existing professional relationships with the [**Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights**](https://ilga.org/glossary/office-of-the-high-commissioner-for-human-rights/) (OHCHR) Secretariat staff and/or independent Treaty Body experts.
- Ability to work proficiently in English (mandatory). Knowledge of Spanish, French or another UN official language is an asset
- Adherence to and alignment with the ILGA World Code of Conduct, including a strong capacity for confidentiality, tact, discretion and respectful collaboration

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator - UKRAINE (M/F/X)
jobs.body:
**Working environment:**

The humanitarian situation in Ukraine remains critical amid ongoing international conflict. Since the escalation of the armed conflict on 24 February 2022, the destruction of vital civilian infrastructure continues to rise, leading to the destruction of homes across the country and cutting off access to critical services for millions of people. In 2025 in Ukraine, the UN estimates approximately 12.7 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance. Ukrainian refugee numbers abroad stand at about 6,9 million, while 3,7 million people are internally displaced (IDPs) within Ukraine.

The severe damage to critical infrastructure such as hospitals, schools, and water treatment plants has compromised access to clean water, sanitation, and essential healthcare services. Constant and long-lasting disruptions to the power grid have plunged entire regions into darkness, hindering communication and hampering daily life.

With the humanitarian situation in Ukraine being a challenge and may deteriorate further, the International Red Cross & Red Crescent Movement continues mobilising its emergency response mechanisms. Together, ICRC, IFRC, Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) and Partner National Societies (PNSs) are undertaking a coordinated response in contributing to URCS interventions as per One Plan 2023-27 and URCS Strategic Plan 2026-2030.

Reporting to the Head of Delegation, the Programme Coordinator will contribute to the development and implementation of the operational strategy of the Delegation, ensure the effective leadership of the country programme - including design, development, and implementation of the programmatic strategy, and contribute to the representation of the Delegation to partners, humanitarian coordination bodies and other relevant stakeholders.

**Missions:**

- **Strategy Development & Grants Management:** Leads on all aspects of programmatic design and actively develops the strategic & operational positioning as well as the development plan of the FRC UA Delegation, in support of the Head of Delegation. Development and writing of new quality Concept Notes and Project Proposals, in coordination with URCS and in line with the Delegation's annual and multi-annual strategic programming, as validated by FRC and URCS. Leads the monitoring, follow-up and accountability of/on active funding agreements. Follows attentively the “Funding Opportunity Watch” that is shared by FRC HQ; in the context of the transition from non-restricted earmarked funding to back donors-funded resources for the FRC “Ukraine Response”.
- **Projects & Team Leadership and Coordination for “Quality Implementation” Follow-up & Monitoring:** Ensures leadership, effective and dynamic management and good coordination of all projects and programmes, the multi-lateral teams involved (FRC and URCS) and of the interactions with FRC HQ (Desk Manager), to ensure “project implementation & quality” monitoring (working closely with all relevant technical experts and counterparts as well as in constant coordination with URCS); including the adequate support to the URCS Programme & Finance teams in the planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting of projects; in line with FRC's international strategy, procedures and MEAL obligations in the country of intervention.
- **“National Society Development” Focus:** in the spirit of contributing to the partner’s sustainable development, participates actively in identifying the needs and priorities of URCS that are matching FRC’s international expertise and potential added-value; in order to develop FRC’s knowledge & understanding of URCS strategy and the NSD reference framework of IFRC and FRC.
- **PMER/MEAL:** Ensures that all of URCS’s monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning processes and tools are in line with FRC requirements and properly activated and implemented; in order to ensure quality reporting and feedback mechanisms to beneficiaries, partners and potential donors.
- **Partnership Management & FRC Representation:** Proactively contributes to good partnership relations and the sustainable capacity building of URCS, including to any further support activities that the position may require; as well as contributes to the representation of FRC operation and interests, in support of the Head of Delegation.

**Managing lines:**

- **Incumbent reporting line**: Reporting to Head of Delegation
- **Incumbent operational links:** HQ Desk Manager
- Incumbent will manage:1 International staff (team under construction):
    - Incumbent will manage and technically support FRC Delegation’s technical programme/project delegates and managers.
    - Number and positions of technical managers is defined by the Delegation’s approved structure and can/will evolve over time.

**Qualifications and experience**

**Experiences :**

- At least 3 years’ experience in the same type of position in Coordination
- Previous experience in programme coordination positions
- Previous experience in supervising staff and supporting their professional and technical development.
- Experience and/or knowledge in communicating with various partners and donors
- Experience in developing new projects (concept note, proposal, budget, logframe, etc)
- Experience in donor reporting and contract management
- Experience working with local partners and partner-implemented projects / programmes
- Experience working with the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement
- Experience in donor reporting and financial contract management (previous experience with French donors is a strong asset: AFD, Expertise France, CDCS.
- Experience in the region and specifically in conflictual context is a strong asset
- Background in health or in health projects (including emergency medical services, nurse sciences, pre-hospital care, first aid, etc.) is a strong asset

**Education :**

- Studies in humanitarian or development project coordination or technical profile
- Mastery of the project cycle and project management tools
- Mastery of the humanitarian coordination system

**Skills**

**Mandatory job requirements**

- Organisational capacity
- Coordination capacity
- Strong writing and synthesis skills (for both proposals and reporting contributions)
- Effective capacity in grant management
- Effective capacity in MEAL procedures and processes
- Strong communication and diplomatic skills in multicultural work environments
- Teamwork skills (active listening, proactivity and consensus building)
- Experience in team management
- Initiative and ability to work efficiently and effectively without close supervision

**Valued skills**

- Proficiency in Office (Word, Excel, Powerpoint), networking (Google-Suite/Google Workspace)
- Expertise in identifying and implementing jointly capacity-improvement plans
- Experience facilitating trainings and accompanying staff to strengthen their expertise
- In-depth knowledge of the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement’s National Society Development approaches, especially through a Programme Coordination and Development lens

**Skills related to the specific environment of the mission:**

- Flexibility and quick adaptability
- Restraint, patience and diplomacy in institutional relations
- Ability to work within a coordination team and in functional link with the project and field teams
- Ability to work with a multicultural team
- Resilience to stress and high workload
- **International driving licence mandatory**

**Languages**

- English mandatory (oral and written);
- French or other language of the region would be an asset

**Conditions of employment:**

- Type of status: expatriate
- Type of contract: Fixed-term contract under French law
- Salary: According to the classification of the position on the CRf grid and the experience of the candidate
- Per diem: daily per diem which varies according to the country
- Leave: 10 to 15 days minimum every 6 months - Airfare paid at 100% by CRF for home travel
- Health coverage: CFE + Mutuelle MSH (covered 100%) - covered at 75% by the CRF
- MedEvac/repatriation insurance: YES
- Other insurances: Provident insurance (death and disability)

**SUMMARY**

- Location: Kyiv (with planned movements in Lviv, Kharkiv and possible other locations) - UKRAINE
- Duration: 12 months renewable
- Starting date: December 2026
- Mandatory driving licence

The French Red Cross reserves the right to close a recruitment before the closing date of the advertisement and the application deadline. Thank you for your understanding.

If we do not contact you within 3 weeks, please consider that we will not consider your application.

Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

**Online training**

To learn more about the Red Cross Movement, we invite you to follow two online training courses, free of charge and accessible to all. W.O.R.C. (World of Red Cross and Red Crescent): this course covers topics such as the origin and history of the Movement, its fundamental principles, the emblem, the International Federation, the ICRC and the national societies. Stay Safe aims to develop a common culture of security management within the Movement. You can find these courses on the International Federation's Learning Platform: [https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx](https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx)
