Nigeria Regional Warehouse Coordinator (Fixed-term)
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

We started working in Nigeria in 2018, serving just 150 farmers. That figure grew year on year, and we now serve more than 300,000 farmers across three regions in Niger State: Minna, Mokwa, and Iseyin.  
  
Between our tree program and a diverse staple crop program, xx staff are supporting farmers in Nigeria to grow their way to prosperity.

## About the Role

Seeking a supply chain professional with 2-5 years' experience to coordinate warehouse and inventory operations, team supervision, and space optimization to support efficient and scalable program delivery.

## Responsibilities

Regional Warehouse Operations & Performance

- Coordinate day-to-day warehouse operations across assigned regional facilities.
- Ensure warehouses consistently follow approved OAF warehouse processes, and SOPs.
- Monitor warehouse performance against agreed KPIs for inventory accuracy, shrinkage, service, productivity, safety and compliance.
- Identify and share best practices across warehouses to improve consistency and performance.
- Plan ahead for peak periods and ensure warehouses are ready to support field and farmer needs.
- Regularly Go to Gemba to understand operational challenges and drive practical improvements.

Inventory Management & Control

- Lead regular physical stock counts, reconciliations and inventory reviews across assigned warehouses.
- Ensure physical stock is accurately reflected in the relevant inventory management system.
- Investigate inventory variances, identify root causes and ensure corrective actions are completed.
- Monitor inventory ageing, stock movements, transfers and potential losses.
- Strengthen controls that prevent shrinkage, stock errors and unauthorized stock movements.
- Ensure inventory records and supporting documentation are complete and audit-ready.

Warehouse Systems, Documentation & Compliance

- Ensure receiving, dispatch and inter-warehouse movements are properly documented and recorded on time.
- Maintain accurate warehouse records, including stock count sheets, waybills, delivery notes, GRNs, transfer documents and quality records.
- Conduct regular compliance checks and follow up on identified gaps.
- Support internal and external audits by ensuring warehouse records and physical stock are readily available.
- Escalate suspected theft, fraud, significant loss or other serious compliance concerns through the appropriate channels.

Warehouse Layout, Quality & Process Improvement

- Ensure effective warehouse layout, product segregation, palletization, labelling and storage practices.
- Work closely with QA/QC to maintain appropriate product handling, storage and release standards.
- Identify bottlenecks and opportunities to improve warehouse flow, space utilization and productivity.
- Lead practical improvement initiatives using data, root-cause analysis and feedback from warehouse teams.
- Standardize successful improvements across other regional warehouses where appropriate.

Health, Safety & Environment

- Promote a strong safety culture across all assigned warehouses.
- Conduct regular warehouse Gemba walks and safety checks to identify and address hazards.
- Ensure appropriate use of PPE and compliance with warehouse safety standards.
- Maintain clean, organized and safe working environments for employees, casual workers and visitors.
- Ensure incidents, near misses and safety concerns are reported, investigated and followed through to closure.
- Encourage team members to speak up and take ownership of safety.

Distribution & Supply Chain Coordination

- Coordinate with Logistics, Procurement, QA/QC and field teams to ensure smooth warehouse operations and timely movement of inputs.
- Support efficient loading, dispatch and inter-warehouse transfer activities.
- Ensure warehouse capacity and dispatch plans are aligned with operational demand.
- Work with Logistics teams to resolve delivery and dispatch challenges quickly.
- Support efficient use of warehouse and transport resources to reduce avoidable operational costs.

Team Leadership & Development

- Provide day-to-day leadership and support to Warehouse Supervisors and warehouse teams.
- Set clear expectations, priorities and performance standards.
- Coach team members to improve warehouse practices, inventory controls, safety and customer service.
- Build a culture of accountability, teamwork, feedback and continuous improvement.

- Organizational skills to efficiently plan, prioritize and delegate tasks.
- Warehouse operations; inventory management and reconciliation; warehouse systems/WMS; stock control; warehouse layout and capacity planning; HSE; basic data analysis; process improvement; documentation and compliance.
- Makes day-to-day operational decisions within approved policies, SOPs and budgets; escalates significant operational, financial, safety and compliance risks appropriately.

- Efficient time management capabilities to ensure timely execution of deliveries and transport operations.
- Flexibility to adapt to evolving customer needs and requirements.
- Commercial awareness to identify cost-saving opportunities and make profitable decisions.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Bida, Niger State, Nigeria

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Nigeria.

08 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

jobs.title: Grant Management and Learning Coordinator - International
jobs.body:
**Job profile**

The Grant Management and Learning Coordinator fulfils a key function within the Department of Programme Development, Impact and Learning, sitting in the Grant Management Unit. Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Director of Programme Performance and Monitoring, the Grant Management and Learning Coordinator is responsible for ensuring compliance with donor grants, coordinating consolidation of coherent and accurate project data, supporting timely development and submission of high-quality donor reports, building and maintaining relationships with partners and donors, and proactively identifying the need for contract changes. In addition, the role coordinates the production of high-quality research on the organisation's Climate Adaptation work and other programming, translating findings into articles, reports and other documents for donors, the NGO community, and other external audiences.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The position covers the following key areas of responsibility:

- For assigned grants, serve as the focal point for Afghanaid’s policies and donor contract terms and conditions, maintaining comprehensive knowledge and ensuring that all grant documentation (including proposals, reports, and budgets) is properly stored and available to relevant staff, and that key reporting requirements and other compliance obligations are clearly communicated to finance and project teams.
- Upon the signing of a new grant agreement, facilitate a smooth handover of the project to the Grant Management Unit, following up on outstanding project partnership agreement (PPA) tasks, and confirming reporting responsibilities and processes with relevant parties at the project kickoff meeting.
- Maintain internal and external tracking of reporting timelines, including working with relevant departments to coordinate appropriate data collection, analysis and financial and narrative reporting by Afghanaid and its partners.
- Review and refine high-quality financial and narrative project reports, survey and evaluation reports, and other associated donor communications, ensuring timely submission and compliance with Afghanaid, donor and partner requirements.
- Independently troubleshoot issues raised by project and operational teams, serving as liaison between the project team and donor to address and resolve challenges.
- Facilitate and contribute to regular project review processes, and pre-emptively raise concerns where contractual obligations, quality standards or deadlines are at risk of not being met, especially identifying risks of donor ‘clawback’ and reputational damage.
- In coordination with project teams, partners and the finance team, lead on revisions to project budgets, logical frameworks and other project documents for assigned grants, ensuring timely submission to the donor and follow up on approvals, and communicating updates to relevant departments.
- Support the Consortium Manager in strengthening partner performance and report quality by reviewing and providing input on partner organisations’ annual and semi-annual narrative reports.
- Initiate learning exchanges and facilitate reflection and adaptive management sessions with Afghanaid staff and partners.
- Lead organisational research initiatives, including establishing and managing partnerships with research organisations, individual researchers (including PhD candidates/Masters’ students), universities and institutes, and consultants to facilitate the production of research outputs for Afghanaid. Adapt research findings into policy and practitioner briefs tailored to different audiences, including donors and external stakeholders; and producing reports drawing on the organisational database of past reports and data.
- Lead and contribute to the design of impact evaluations and internal studies, including initiating Terms of Reference, to inform the evolution of Afghanaid’s programming and implementation of the organisation’s strategy.
- Represent the organisation at external fora and in meetings with partners and donors to promote the organisation, strengthen external relations and identify opportunities for new and repeat funding and partnerships that contribute to Afghanaid’s funding pipeline.
- Support organisational learning initiatives where possible, for instance through documenting institutional knowledge and expertise and participating in lessons learned workshops.
- Contribute to organisational capacity through developing and facilitating training and workshops for Afghanaid staff, including in provincial offices, on subjects including effective reporting and impact analysis.
- Lead and support on the development of project reporting, analysis and evaluation templates and tools.
- Facilitate field visits with donor organisations, and virtual visits as required.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Requirements**

**Essential**

**Education**

- A Master’s degree in Development Studies, International Relations, Social Sciences or another relevant programme of study

**Experience**

- 3-4 years of experience of working in a development or humanitarian context, in project support, grant management, programme development or a similar role
- Proven experience of synthesising data and input from various sources into clear and cohesive narrative reports
- Strong experience with logical frameworks and/or theories of change
- Experience working in high-risk or volatile contexts, including humanitarian or emergency settings.

**Knowledge and Skills**

- Native English proficiency and demonstrated ability to write high quality, polished documents and reports that are consistent with a set brand and style
- Experience turning data and research into clear reports for a variety of audiences
- Strong data entry skills, familiarity with use of a databases, and office tools (Excel, Word)
- Experience in contract management
- Experience in donor/client relationship management in the humanitarian / development sector
- Experience in humanitarian project design or management, and/or budget development or management
- Strong organisational skills, able to plan effectively, set priorities, and meet tight deadlines under pressure
- Strong people and coalition-building skills and proven ability to form good working relations, both internally within the organisation and externally with people at all levels

**Personal Attributes**

- Intellectually curious and able to question assumptions
- Ability to work independently and as a team member, including in a coordinating capacity with other departments
- Initiative and drive to achieve results, working quickly and accurately with attention to detail
- An outgoing and engaging personality and strong sense of humour, able to build trust and manage relationships with a variety of stakeholders
- Cultural sensitivity and ability to work in diverse multi-cultural environment
- Ability and willingness to travel for work

**Desirable**

- Experience working on Climate Adaptation projects
- Experience working with, or knowledge of, key institutional donors for development and humanitarian programming in Afghanistan
- Experience with EU/INTPA grants
- Training in and/or exposure to M&E
- Understanding of the cultural, security and operating environment in Afghanistan (or in a similar context)
- Understanding of Dari and/or Pashto

jobs.title: ER Doctor for international humanitarian missions
jobs.body:
**Médicos Sin Fronteras en México A.C.**

**Seeks**

## **ER Doctor**

## for International Humanitarian Missions

To join our team in International Projects

(Minimum availability of 6 months)

### **\*\*\* Please upload your CV and motivation letter in English \*\*\***

**THIS JOB PROFILE IS IN ENGLISH SINCE THIS IS THE REQUIRED LANGUAGE FOR THE JOB**

**OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION**

The emergency doctor supervises the operation of the Emergency Service, from the admission to the discharge of the patients, according to the objectives of the project and in relation to the other services of the hospital.

As an ER physician, you are responsible for providing the best medical care to the patient and are involved in the triage system, patient flow, and protocol implementation.

It guarantees the training and supervision of national personnel. For the purposes of knowledge transfer, the training consists of both theoretical and head training to ensure a gradual transfer of responsibilities.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Apply medical knowledge and skills for diagnosis and prevention. Carry out outpatient and hospital consultations, prescribing the necessary treatment respecting MSF protocols.
- Keep the patient and their family informed about the disease and give appropriate explanations about the treatment to be followed, verifying that they have understood it.
- Monitor the evolution of hospitalized patients / IDP through daily visits, consultations and exams. Prescribe the necessary treatment following MSF protocols, deciding in collaboration with other doctors whether patients should be discharged or transferred to other departments, and informing their families about the patient's progress.
- Verify and control under his responsibility the rational distribution of medicines and equipment, and take care of the quality, disinfection and sterilization of medical equipment. Ensure compliance with hygiene standards.
- Participate in the collection and analysis of epistemological data, verifying the validity and informing the person in charge or coordinator of the field about any problem or complication in the patient's illness, or medical error. Controls the proper functioning of the department, equipment or material.
- Ensure continuous training of the multidisciplinary medical / paramedical team to optimize the quality of care.
- Knows and ensures that all MSF medical protocols are still being implemented, verifying that universal precautions are followed at all times, reducing risks of biohazard and improving infection control. Ensures that professional confidentiality is respected.
- Manages the team under his responsibility in accordance with MSF's HR policies and procedures, supervising its performance, organizing and planning shifts and rotations, and directly participating in emergencies or calls if necessary.

**PROFILE**

**Education and formation**

- **Essential**: General Physician Degree.
- **Essential:** Specialty in Emergency Medicine or anesthesia specialization and/or REA/ICU.
- **Desirable** diploma in tropical medicine

**Experience**

- **Essential**: minimum 2 years practicing as Doctor in ER or ICU/REA
- Desirable work experience with MSF and other NGOs in developing countries

**Languages**

- **Essential:** English (B2 or higher level)
- **Essential**: Spanish (C1 or higher level)
- Knowledge of French will be an asset

**Knowledge**

**Essential** computer literacy (word, excel, internet)

**Competencies**

- People Management and Development
- Commitment to MSF Principles
- Behavioral Flexibility
- Results and Quality Orientation
- Teamwork and Cooperation
- Planning and Organizing
- Cross-cultural Awareness
- Stress Management

**POSITION CONDITIONS**

**Work Venue:** Where the needs of the project require it

**Profits:** Monthly remuneration: Approximate gross monthly starts in USD $2,300 and may increase according to related experience. Private insurance coverage that includes medical coverage and hospital, temporary disability and life insurance. The organization also has an arranged medical evacuation if necessary. The expenses of stay in the land are covered: housing, basic services, cleaning and washing. Other expenses such as transportation, visas, transfer to the country of destination and Displacements in the field will also be covered by MSF. Per diem or monthly per diem: mainly to cover meals and small personal expenses.

**Start:** Depending on the needs of the project

**Duration:** **Minimum 6 months**

**Working day:** Full time

jobs.title: Programme Manager - Nutrition
jobs.body:
**Overview and Purpose**

To oversee the design, planning, implementation and monitoring of nutrition activities to ensure that expected outcomes are achieved and quality standards are met.

**Reports to:** Programme Director

**Terms:** 12-month fixed-term contract, full-time, based at the coordination office in Port-au-Prince

**Salary:** GB5: €42,136 - €46,818

**Requirements:** Frequent travel to project areas (West and Centre Departments)

[GB4-6 Unaccompanied International Staff T&Cs](https://concern.icims.com/icims2/servlet/icims2?module=AppInert&action=download&id=299&hashed=-877963960)

**Responsibilities**

*Programme management*

- To ensure the design, planning and implementation of nutrition programmes
- Ensure alignment with national strategies, donor priorities and humanitarian standards
- Contribute to the development of new project proposals and funding opportunities
- Participate in multi-sectoral needs assessments and nutrition surveys
- Oversee project implementation in accordance with action plans, budgets and indicators
- Ensure high-quality management of severe and moderate acute malnutrition, including community mobilisation, screening, strengthening of health systems (training for implementing staff), supply chain monitoring and data monitoring
- Lead the MAMI approach, including adapting the protocol to the local context, monitoring and analysing data, and coordinating with local stakeholders
- Contribute to and implement the behaviour change strategy, including IYCF activities (Parents’ Club, cooking demonstrations), synergies with the WASH and food security sectors, and malnutrition prevention activities (distribution of MNPs and AK1000 flour) in collaboration with health workers from targeted health facilities.
- Facilitate the roll-out of improved flour production, including the development of operational protocols and knowledge sharing to support scaling up
- Work with the MEAL Manager to set up project databases, monitor indicators and collect data.
- Carry out all tasks reasonably assigned and mutually agreed with the line manager.

*Team management and leadership*

- Supervise a team comprising Nutrition Programme Officers, Assistant Nutrition Programme Officers and Nutrition Field Officers
- Set clear objectives and conduct performance appraisals (PDRs) for direct reports
- Identify capacity-building needs and organise training, where necessary in collaboration with other colleagues at Concern Haiti or at head office.
- Promote an inclusive, ethical and high-performing environment

*Financial management and compliance*

- Carry out monthly budget monitoring using the tools provided by the finance department and anticipate variances
- Produce expenditure forecasts

*Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL)*

- Monitor indicators and ensure data quality
- Oversee MEAL systems and databases
- Produce high-quality narrative and technical reports
- Promoting accountability (CHS) and programme-based learning

*Coordination and representation*

- Represent Concern in dealings with authorities, partners and clusters
- Develop and maintain relationships with stakeholders

*Reporting*

- Submit a weekly progress report on activities to the Programme Director;
- Draft and submit, in a timely manner, the minutes of meetings on implemented activities to the Programme Director
- Produce a monthly narrative progress report on the activities of the projects under their responsibility, in accordance with the reporting tools provided by the Programme Director.
- Contribute to the drafting of high-quality contractual reports, including any annexes as required, for donors.

*Partnerships and localisation*

- Develop and maintain close partnerships with state bodies (the Western and Central Regional Health Directorates, and the National Nutrition Directorate within the Ministry of Public Health and Population) in the planning, implementation and monitoring of projects, ensuring a high standard of communication, coordination and information sharing.
- Ensure that communities participating in the project are consulted at various stages of the project cycle, paying particular attention to the proper application of accountability mechanisms and community feedback

*Mandatory cross-cutting responsibilities*

- Uphold and promote Concern’s values, demonstrate leadership on equality, diversity and inclusion in the workplace, and set an example of positive ethics in relation to safeguarding.
- Actively participate in any emergency response, where required

**Role Holder Requirements**

*Required*

- Master’s degree in public health or nutrition, or a degree in medicine or a relevant field
- 3 years’ experience in programme management
- Proven experience working with international NGOs
- Proven experience in community-based approaches
- Proven experience with the CMAM and/or IYCF approaches
- Experience in drafting programme proposals
- Managing relations with government partners
- Team management and supervision, including performance appraisal processes
- Understanding of monitoring and evaluation processes and tools
- Exemplary conduct in terms of safeguarding and upholding the dignity of programme participants, colleagues and partners.

*Desirable*

- Knowledge in MAMI approaches and the production of fortified flour
- Experience in Haiti or a similar context

*Languages*

- Excellent command of French, both spoken and written (essential)
- English (an advantage)
- Haitian Creole (an advantage)

*Technical and soft skills*

- Project management (full cycle)
- Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) and data analysis
- Budget management
- Capacity building / coaching

*Other essential skills*

- Planning and decision-making
- Individual leadership
- Communication and teamwork
- Achieving results

**Other requirements**

- Ability to work in complex and high-pressure environments
- Strong adaptability and mobility
- Commitment to humanitarian principles

jobs.title: Staff Auditor
jobs.body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) is currently seeking a talented professional for the role of a Staff Auditor. The Staff Auditor will help evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of the internal controls of various departments at HFHI's headquarters, HFHI's international area offices, and selected programs of Habitat's U.S. and international organizations.

This position will be remotely based within the US and will require 40-60% domestic and/or international travel.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Assist with the planning, execution, and reporting on operational, financial and compliance audits in the designated areas. (20%)
- Assist in the preparation of the audit planning memo, risk-based audit programs and test plans which defines specific procedures to be performed during an audit. (5%)
- Conduct audit fieldwork work papers, findings, and recommendations for compliance with the Institute of Internal Auditor International Professional Standards and HFHI Internal Audit Department (IAD) Standards. (20%)
- Conduct peer reviews of other audit staff's audit documentation and working papers to ensure consistency, quality and compliance with internal audit standards. Provide constructive feedback to support continuous improvement. (5%)
- Draft finding and recommendations audit report in accordance with and monitor the quality of audit reports to ensure compliance with International Professional Practices Framework (IPPF) and HFHI IAD Standards. (15%)
- Document processes, procedures, and test results. (5%)
- Coordinate the monitoring of outstanding audit recommendations. (5%)
- Plan, coordinate and performing consulting and advisory services as appropriate for the organization. (5%)
- Assist in the development of the IAD annual risk-based internal audit plan. (5%)
- Lead auditor assigned to the audit projects under his/her responsibility, will provide guidance and overall review of deliverables. (10%)
- Assists the VP/Director/Manager of Internal Audit on any other duties as assigned by management of Internal Audit as needed. The above duties could include supporting other internal audit units and audit activities, such as the SOAR process, audit committee package and risk assessment process. (5%)

**Key Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Accounting, Finance, Information Technology, or a related field.
- 3-5 years of professional experience with external and internal audits, forensic accounting investigations, preferably with a public accounting firm.
- Experience with international travel and/or cross-cultural communications.
- Expert level skills with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as a good understanding of the COSO - International Control Integrated Framework.
- Excellent English, verbal and written, communication skills.
- Strong critical thinking and project management skills.

**Preferred:**

- 3 years of domestic and international experience in internal or external audit management, preferably with a large international non-profit government, corporate organizations, or Big 4 Accounting Firm.
- Experience auditing construction activities and Micro-Finance operations.
- Proficiency with auditing software such as Galvanize HighBond or others.
- Experience using data analytics tools to create queries and trend analysis reports.
- Experience in non-profit Internal Audits, particularly executing audits of controls and transactions related to government and corporate grant requirements.
- Spanish, verbal and written, communication skills would be beneficial.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$55,600.00 USD

$82,675 USD

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

**Habitat for Humanity International is an E-Verify employer.**

jobs.title: Technical Advisor II – Climate Change & Landscape Restoration
jobs.body:
**Job Title:** Technical Advisor II – Climate Change & Landscape Restoration

**Reports to:** Head of Programming

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Kampala

This position is open to **Ugandan nationals only**

**Deadline:** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm.

**Job Summary**

You will provide strategic technical leadership, advice, guidance, and support across program design, business development, implementation, learning, and evidence generation in the areas of Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration. Working in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices, you will support Country Office(CO) teams to develop, implement, and scale innovative, high-quality programming that advances resilience, environmental stewardship, and sustainable livelihoods for poor and vulnerable communities. Your technical knowledge, advice and guidance will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive and innovative CRS’ Climate Change and Landscape Restoration programming is across Uganda.

Your technical expertise, strategic vision, and leadership will contribute to the growth and positioning of CRS Uganda's Climate Change and Landscape Restoration portfolio. You will help identify and pursue new funding opportunities, lead technical design for priority investments and proposals, build relationships and partnerships, and support the effective implementation of strategic initiatives that generate evidence, demonstrate impact, and inform future programming. Through collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, you will strengthen CRS' reputation as a trusted partner and technical leader in climate resilience, nature-based solutions, and landscape restoration across Uganda.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Contribute to the development and implementation of CRS Uganda strategies, standards, tools, and best practices in Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration that effectively engage partners, donors and governments. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, protection mainstreaming, and disaster risk reduction, while promoting innovation, learning, and evidence-based programming.
- Provide technical solutions to CP teams, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply program design and implementation standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools, and M&E, ensuring high-quality implementation. Support adaptive management and the use of evidence and learning to strengthen program quality and impact.
- Lead CRS Uganda's technical efforts to position and grow its Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration portfolio by identifying emerging opportunities, strengthening strategic partnerships, and shaping innovative, evidence-based programming approaches. Lead or contribute to the technical design of large and/or complex proposals, including the development of technical strategies, theories of change, and appropriate monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks in collaboration with business development, MEAL, and other cross-functional teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities, and technical requirements into CRS' approach and support the development of programming that strengthens CRS' competitiveness, impact, and thought leadership.
- Lead the design, implementation, and technical oversight of strategic initiatives and discretionary-funded investments in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration that generate evidence, demonstrate impact, strengthen partnerships, and inform future programming and resource mobilization efforts.
- Contribute to technical communications, visibility, and thought leadership efforts by supporting the development of success stories, case studies, presentations, publications, learning products, and other materials that showcase CRS' experience, evidence, and impact in Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration.
- Contribute to capacity strengthening initiatives in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration programming for staff and partners through helping develop learning and training strategies and agendas/curriculums, conducting trainings and workshops, and mentoring and coaching.
- Contribute to knowledge management and learning through collecting and analyzing program data, evaluating strategic projects, assisting with measuring program impact, capturing and sharing lessons learned and best practices, and research and internal reports.
- Establish and maintain relationships with donors, peer organizations, research and other institutions. Participate in forums in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work, support organizational positioning, and identify opportunities for collaboration and resource mobilization.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s Degree in Climate Change, Forestry, Agroforestry, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Ecology, Environmental Management, Agriculture, or a related field required.
- Minimum of eight years relevant international working experience in an advisory or management role with progressive responsibilities, ideally with an international NGO, with minimum of three years working for programming interventions in climate change adaptation and mitigation and/or landscape restoration
- Previous experience providing technical assistance and developing successful proposals for external donor funding is required.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master's Degree in Climate Change, Forestry, Agroforestry, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Ecology, Environmental Management, Agriculture, or a related field is an advantage
- Demonstrated ability to convene, coordinate, and facilitate complex multi-stakeholder consultations and partnerships involving government, development partners, technical agencies, academia, and community stakeholders.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Demonstrated application of technical principles and concepts in climate change adaptation and mitigation and landscape restoration. General knowledge of other related disciplines to ensure a proper cross-sectoral approach.
- Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information and budget management systems, knowledge-sharing networks.
- Experience in business development, project design and proposal development in, including technical writing.
- Experience in mentoring, coaching, facilitation and training applying adult learning principles and practices.
- Experience with program monitoring and evaluation, including applying data collection tools and methodologies, data analysis, and data presentation.
- Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, peer organizations, and faith-based civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles.
- Excellent relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings.
- Strong strategic, analytical, problem-solving and systems thinking skills with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment
- Strong written and oral communication skills
- Strong presentation, facilitation, training, mentoring, and coaching skills
- Proactive, resourceful and results-oriented

**Required Languages** - Fluent English is required. Working proficiency in local language is a plus.

**Travel** - include percentage of required travel, if applicable. Could be stated as Must be willing and able to travel up to 30 %.

**Supervisory Responsibilities: No**

**Key Working Relationships:**

Internal: CRS Country Representative, Head of Programs, Head of Operations, Uganda-based technical experts for MEAL, Emergency focal point, Gender, Youth and Social Inclusion (GYSI) and Partner Capacity Strengthening (PCS), Regional and Headquarters technical staff.

External: Local partner staff, representatives from for-profit and other non-profit organizations and relevant national, district, sub-county, parish and other government stakeholders, community leaders.

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

jobs.title: Agricultural Value Chains - Project Manager (Cashew & Coffee) - Mozambique
Medical Supply Planner
jobs.body:
**\*\*The compensation range for this position is $60,300–$63,000 USD. Compensation will be based on experience, qualifications, and other relevant factors. This is a full-time, hybrid position located in Lindale, Texas, with one in -person workday per week\*\*.**

Mercy Ships is seeking an experienced Medical Supply Planner. In this role, you will be part of the Global Supply Chain Planning department. This department supports our hospital ships operating in Africa.

As a Supply Planner, you are responsible for planning the delivery of Medical Supplies to our Hospital ships serving in Africa. You monitor inventory levels and buffer targets across the supply chain and fulfilling customer special / annual order requests. You work closely with the Medical Demand Planners, a fellow Medical Supply Planner, and various departments within the Global Supply Chain.

The intensive coordination with departments at both the Dutch and U.S. offices, as well as with the ships themselves, makes this a dynamic role at the heart of the organization.

**How You Will Contribute:**

- To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.
- Execute the replenishment of vessels by generating container orders using the Supply Planning Tools
- Aligning operational timelines with Procurement, Logistics and Warehouse departments.
- Monitor inventory health across ships, depots, and ad-hoc/non-inventory streams.
- Establishes, evaluates, and sets Safety Stock (SS) levels across the supply chain.
- Serves as a direct point of contact for customers regarding non-inventory special orders, custom requests, annual orders and ad-hoc operational needs.
- Maintains alignment and upholds Mercy Ships Core Values, Code of Conduct, and follows the policies and procedures published on Compass.
- Follows the model of Jesus and aligns with our core values by Loving God; Loving and Serving Others; Being a Person of Integrity; and a Person of Excellence in all you say and do.

jobs.title: Responsable du Pôle Conformité et Finances CDI (H/F)
jobs.body:
Rejoindre l’ONG Plan International France, c’est donner un sens à sa vie professionnelle en s’engageant dans la solidarité internationale et en adhérant aux valeurs de transparence, de respect, de durabilité, de communauté et d’inclusion.

Notre ONG est fière d’œuvrer pour un monde meilleur dans lequel les droits des enfants, et en particulier des filles, sont respectés. C’est ainsi qu’en 2025, le réseau Plan International a permis à 5,1 millions de filles dans le monde de bénéficier d’un meilleur accès à l’éducation.

Rejoindre notre ONG, c’est aussi intégrer une équipe conviviale d’une quarantaine de salarié·es et de bénévoles, aussi expert·es que passionné·es. Nous travaillons dans la bienveillance et la confiance, en gardant pour objectif le bien-être des salarié·es. Télétravail, flexibilité des horaires, grande autonomie sont autant d’aménagements qui favoriseront votre équilibre vie pro/vie perso. Vous trouverez une palette de métiers variés et une organisation qui s’inscrit dans une dynamique de progression.

Pour compléter cette belle équipe, nous recherchons des talents qui partagent nos valeurs et qui souhaitent apporter leur pierre à l’édifice. Venez donc nous rencontrer pour découvrir les belles missions qui nous animent et nous motivent.

## **Le poste que nous proposons** 

Au sein du Pôle Conformité et Finances de la Direction Administrative et Financière, vous aurez pour objectif de garantir l’expertise en conformité et en finances pour les programmes de développement et d’urgence mis en œuvre.

Directement rattaché·e à la Directrice Administrative et financière, le∙la Responsable du pôle conformité et finances assurera les missions suivantes :

**Sécurisation des volets financiers et contractuels dans la phase de montage et d’élaboration des programmes**

- Valider le montage budgétaire et les informations administratives et financières des programmes en cohérence avec les activités, les procédures de Plan International et les règles des bailleurs de fonds ;
- Valider les volets financiers des conventions signées par Plan International France avec les bailleurs de fonds et avec les bureaux pays ;
- Participer aux négociations sur les aspects budgétaires et contractuels lorsque nécessaire

**Sécurisation des volets financiers, conformité et contrôle interne des programmes**

- Assurer le suivi de conformité finance sur les programmes de son portefeuille ;
- Valider la qualité et la conformité des rapports financiers à destination des bailleurs de fonds ;
- Valider les transferts de fonds liés aux programmes, vers le terrain ;
- Garantir l’utilisation et l’amélioration des outils de gestion financière et contrôle interne existants ;
- Superviser le bon déroulement des missions d’audit demandées par les bailleurs et assurer la mise en œuvre et le suivi des recommandations ;
- Capitaliser sur les recommandations préconisées par les différents organes de contrôle en lien avec la référente audit interne
- Assurer l’identification des risques financiers et/ou de fraude et de corruption sur son activité et la mise en place d’actions préventives et de contrôle.

**Renforcement de la collaboration financière avec les bureaux pays**

- Superviser le suivi conformité et finance des programmes en appui aux bureaux pays et selon les procédures de Plan International et des bailleurs de fonds ;
- Superviser l’accompagnement et la formation des bureaux pays à la mise en œuvre des exigences de conformité spécifiques aux bailleurs français et européens ;
- Assurer et superviser des missions d’appui et de conformité finances lors de déplacements dans les Bureaux pays (1 par trimestre en moyenne).

**Renforcement des capacités du pôle Conformité et Finances**

- Capitaliser les bonnes pratiques de gestion financière et budgétaire et s’assurer de leur respect ;
- Assurer l’actualisation des procédures et des outils en fonction de l’évolution des exigences bailleurs ;
- Assurer la création et l’amélioration d’outils de gestion financière afin de faciliter la gestion quotidienne des programmes et le pilotage financier global du portefeuille de programmes ;
- Intéragir avec l’équipe Finance de Plan international France, dans la gestion et clôture comptable des programmes (transmission informations) ;
- Préparer le budget annuel des recettes Bailleurs institutionnels et privés, ainsi que le budget annuel des dépenses liées aux programmes

**Participation à l’exploration de nouvelles sources de financement innovantes**

En lien avec la direction des Programmes et Partenariats stratégiques :

- Contribuer, à la stratégie de réponse aux appels d’offres de bailleurs publics (contrats commerciaux)
- Identifier les besoins d’accompagnement et de formation de l’équipe
- Participer à l’identification des bureaux pays en capacité de répondre à des appels d’offre
- Mise en place d’une méthodologie de gestion financière des contrats commerciaux

**Management de l’équipe Conformité et Finances**

- Assurer le management quotidien de son équipe ;
- Participer aux recrutements ;
- Créer, organiser et animer des formations pour son équipe
- Coordonner le pilotage de l’activité en lien avec l’équipe Programmes et Partenariats Stratégiques.

## **Le profil que nous cherchons** 

Vous disposez d’un Diplôme de gestion financière, contrôle de gestion/audit, école supérieure de commerce, formation Bioforce administration. Et vous justifiez de 7 ans minimum en contrôle de gestion de programmes dont 2 au sein d’une ONG au siège. Expérience de terrain souhaitée.

Également :

- Très bonne maitrise d’Excel
- Anglais et français courant à l’écrit et à l’oral (B2)
- Maîtrise des exigences financières et de conformité des bailleurs institutionnels français et européens (AFD, Expertise France, CDCS, INTPA, ECHO, …)
- Analyse des risques en matière de conformité et d’éligibilité des dépenses
- Gestion financière, contrôle interne,
- Bonne capacité d’organisation et autonome (prise d’initiative)
- Sens de l’organisation et fort dynamisme
- Résolution de problèmes
- Aisance relationnelle et qualités de communication
- Vous savez vous adapter, êtes rigoureux·reuse
- Première expérience en management

## **Pour postuler** 

- Poste en CDI à pourvoir dès que possible.
- Poste basé à Pantin (93) avec déplacements dans les pays d’intervention ;
- Statut cadre forfait jour, JRTT, 10 jours de télétravail par mois ;
- Rémunération brute annuelle minimum de 43 K€ sur 12 mois, selon l’expérience, le profil et la grille de rémunération interne.
- Carte restaurant 10,83€ / jour travaillé, dont 60% de financement employeur
- 50% de remboursement sur les frais de transport - Forfait mobilité durable

jobs.title: Rwanda Senior Networks Technician
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

## About the Role

Seeking a skilled Networks Technician to maintain high-availability LAN/WAN and telephony systems. You will drive uptime, resolve Tier 2 issues, and ensure reliable connectivity to empower our field operations and scale impact.

## Responsibilities

Network Infrastructure & Telephony Systems

- Maintain high-availability LAN/WAN and VoIP/telephony infrastructure, driving network redundancy and continuous performance optimization across regional field sites.

Incident Response & Tier 2 Troubleshooting

- Resolve complex Tier 2 technical escalations, perform root-cause analyses on network outages, and execute scheduled zero-downtime maintenance.

Cross-Functional Coordination & Influence

- Partner with Country ITO teams to coordinate system upgrades, enforce security policies, and implement standardized network architecture across multi-site field operations.

Operational Excellence & Capacity Building

- Monitor system health metrics to maintain zero-downtime standards while supporting and mentoring local technical staff across country teams.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor's Degree or Diploma in Network Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field
- At least 2 to 3 years of experience in maintaining high-availability enterprise LAN/WAN and VoIP/telephony systems.
- Demonstrated expertise in network redundancy, uptime optimization, and executing zero-downtime maintenance.
- Proven track record in Tier 2 technical escalation management, incident response, and root-cause analysis.
- Strong cross-functional coordination and communication skills to execute system upgrades across regional field offices without direct managerial authority.
- Working towards or holding relevant network certifications (e.g., CCNA or CompTIA Network+) is preferred.
- Fluency in English and Kinyarwanda is required.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Rubengera, Rwanda

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

## Application Deadline

03 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

Program Description (Background)

## ***The successful candidate can be based anywhere in the world where International Medical Corps has a program office. It is a remote position with significant travel to country programs as requested.***

## **Advisor, Global MHPSS Technical Unit**

## **About International Medical Corps**

International Medical Corps is a global, humanitarian, nonprofit organization dedicated to saving lives and relieving suffering through health care training and relief and development programs.

Established in 1984 by volunteer doctors and nurses, International Medical Corps is a private, voluntary, nonpolitical, nonsectarian organization. Its mission is to improve the quality of life through health interventions and related activities that build local capacity in underserved communities worldwide. By offering training and health care to local populations and medical assistance to people at highest risk, and with the flexibility to respond rapidly to emergency situations, International Medical Corps rehabilitates devastated health care systems and helps bring them back to self-reliance.

## **Job Summary**

## **As a member of the HQ TU MHPSS Team, provide technical quality oversight and programmatic guidance and support to global and country-level MHPSS activities and programming.**

## **Essential Duties & Responsibilities**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation

1. **Program support**: Support country teams and provide guidance and oversight in the development and running of culturally appropriate mental health and psychosocial activities, including MH PHC integration, MHPSS case management, Early Childhood Development, Psychological First Aid, designing holistic recreational, vocational and social activities for children and youth targeting refugees and vulnerable populations across the region, peer support programs for people with chronic or severe mental illness, mental health advocacy and other programs in line with global guidelines and IMCs approach.
2. **Proposal Development**: Assist country teams in developing further MHPSS programming as appropriate and in the development of project proposals
3. **Standards and principles**: Ensure that all MHPSS work is in keeping with IASC guidelines on MHPSS support in emergencies.
4. Promote global guidelines such as IASC MHPSS guidelines where appropriate opportunities arise
5. Ensure and promote complementary and holistic coordinated community based MHPSS programming compliance with IMC’s MHPSS approach and Technical Unit Guidance notes on minimum and comprehensive quality standards for MHPSS programs.
6. **Crosscutting integration**: Provide support to country teams based on identified needs and working to ensure IMC holistic and crosscutting approaches across MHPSS, Nutrition, Health, Child Protection and GBV program areas.
7. **Coordination**: Support country level coordination WG efforts, promoting IMC’s active participation and/or leadership, and contribution to WG advocacy, coordination and mapping activities.
8. Support country teams in coordinating activities with relevant Government Authorities, International and National Organizations, advocating for best practices, and partnerships in line with national strategies.
9. **M&E**: Develop and employ consistent, standardized tools for monitoring and evaluating processes and outcomes of IMC MHPSS programs across the region, with attention to record of lessons learned through evidence-based practice for the purpose of project replication or expansion.
10. **Representation and visibility**: Represent IMC and its MHPSS programmes in relevant national and international conferences and meetings.
11. **Travel**: Support teams remotely and in person through frequent field visits

**Reporting**

1. Regular reporting and updates to TU Senior Global MHPSS Advisor and regional Senior Director
2. Regular contact with Senior Global MHPSS Advisor about planning, methods and tools used, and progress.
3. Expected Outputs for each country technical assistance field visit will include:
    - Field trip report that includes a situational analysis, program(s) assisted, assistance provided, and recommendations for follow up/improvement.
    - Annexes that include all work products including any new or improved MHPSS tools or measures used during the assignment.

## **Skills & Qualifications**

1. The qualified candidate will be a mental health professional (psychologist, clinical social worker, psychiatrist, or psychiatric nurse) with professional practice experience in clinical mental health
2. At least 5+ years’ experience in setting up, establishing and running MHPSS programs in humanitarian and low-resource settings
3. In-depth knowledge of global guidelines (e.g. IASC Guidelines on MHPSS In Emergency Settings)
4. Training and capacity building experience
5. Very good ability to mentor, support and motivate others
6. Strong organizational and supervisory skills
7. Strong reporting and writing skills
8. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work within different cultural environments
9. Honest, hardworking and a self-motivated
10. Ability to work within a team structure or in isolation, flexible, and can cope with stressful workloads and working with limited resources
11. Ability to travel often and on short notice to project sites
12. An excellent command of verbal and written English and French

International Medical Corps is a ‘first-responder’ both to natural and men-made disasters and has a mandate of working in remote locations. The organization has a comprehensive security management policy and plan in place and committed to do everything possible within its remit to ensure safety and security. Notwithstanding, the mandate and programming choices of International Medical Corps require staff with high degree of resilience, extremely decisive quality and ability to move fast. International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

Job Description

**JOB SUMMARY:** As a member of the Headquarters (HQ) Technical Unit (TU) MHPSS Team, provide technical quality oversight and programmatic guidance and support to global and country-level MHPSS activities and programming

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

• Program support: Support country teams and provide guidance and oversight in the development and running of culturally appropriate mental health and psychosocial activities, including mental health (MH)/primary health care (PHC) integration, MHPSS case management, Early Childhood Development, Psychological First Aid, designing holistic recreational, vocational and social activities for children and youth targeting refugees and crisis-affected populations across the region, peer support programs for people with chronic or severe mental illness, mental health advocacy and other programs in line with global guidelines and International Medical Corps (IMC) approach.

• Proposal Development: Assist country teams in developing further MHPSS programming as appropriate and in the development of project proposals

• Standards and principles: Ensure that all MHPSS work is in keeping with Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) guidelines on MHPSS support in emergencies.

• Promote global guidelines such as IASC MHPSS guidelines where appropriate opportunities arise

• Ensure and promote complementary and holistic coordinated community based MHPSS programming compliance with IMC's MHPSS approach and Technical Unit Guidance notes on minimum and comprehensive quality standards for MHPSS programs.

• Crosscutting integration: Provide support to country teams based on identified needs and working to ensure IMC holistic and crosscutting approaches across MHPSS, Nutrition, Health, Child Protection and VAWG program areas.

• Coordination: Support country level coordination Working Group (WG) efforts, promoting IMC's active participation and/or leadership, and contribution to WG advocacy, coordination and mapping activities.

• Support country teams in coordinating activities with relevant Government Authorities, International and National Organizations, advocating for best practices, and partnerships in line with national strategies.

• M/E: Develop and employ consistent, standardized tools for monitoring and evaluating processes and outcomes of IMC MHPSS programs across the region, with attention to record of lessons learned through evidence-based practice for the purpose of project replication or expansion.

• Representation and visibility: Represent IMC and its MHPSS programs in relevant national and international conferences and meetings.

• Travel: Support teams remotely and in person through frequent field visits

• Reporting: Regular reporting and updates to TU Senior Global MHPSS Advisor and regional Senior Director

• Regular contact with Senior Global MHPSS Advisor about planning, methods and tools used, and progress.

**Expected Outputs for each country technical assistance field visit will include**

• Field trip report that includes a situational analysis, program(s) assisted, assistance provided, and recommendations for follow up/improvement.

• Annexes that include all work products including any new or improved MHPSS tools or measures used during the assignment

Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive.

Job Requirements

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

• Typically a 4-year University degree in related area. Equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

• The qualified candidate will be a mental health professional (psychologist, clinical social worker, psychiatrist, or psychiatric nurse) with professional practice experience in clinical mental health

• Typically, 10+ years of relevant and progressive experience working in a mental health-related field, including at least 5+ years' experience in setting up, establishing and running MHPSS programs in humanitarian and low-resource settings

• In-depth knowledge of global guidelines (e.g. IASC Guidelines on MHPSS In Emergency Settings)

• Training and capacity building experience

• Very good ability to mentor, support and motivate others

• Strong organizational and supervisory skills

• Strong reporting and writing skills

• Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work within different cultural environments

• Honest, hardworking and self-motivated

• Ability to work within a team structure or in isolation, flexible, and can cope with stressful workloads and working with limited resources

• Ability to travel often and on short notice to project sites

• An excellent command of verbal and written English

Additional Technical or Language Requirements

Fluency in French required

### **ETHICAL CONDUCT AT INTERNATIONAL MEDICAL CORPS**

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our Code of Conduct and Ethics and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our Code of Conduct and Ethics, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the Code of Conduct and Ethics, all staff are required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our Code of Conduct and Ethics and Whistleblower Policy prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

### **EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES**

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

### **MISCONDUCT DISCLOSURE SCHEME**

All offers of employment at International Medical Corps are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. International Medical Corps participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme from the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). In accordance with this, we will request information from an applicant’s previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

jobs.title: Head of Systems and Operations for Myanmar
jobs.body:
**Duty Station:** Yangon, Myanmar

**Line Manager:** Country Director

**Start Date:** November 2026

**People in Need (PIN)** is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 20 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad.

## **About the Myanmar Programme at People in Need**

People in Need (PIN People in Need (PIN) is an international, non-profit organization providing humanitarian and development assistance around the world. In Myanmar, People in Need started to work in 2002, when it launched financial assistance to civil society groups and provided humanitarian response to people affected by Cyclone Nargis in 2008. PIN supports local civil society partners with a focus on strengthening local civil society organizations and providing them with the necessary knowledge and funding. Through humanitarian response, development and education projects and community cohesion-building programmes tailored to local conditions, and by working closely with local actors, PIN helps local communities cope with both water-induced disasters and human-made crises.

## **Position Summary**

The Head of Systems & Operations (HoSO) is a core member of the Country Management Team (CMT) for People in Need’s Myanmar Country Programme (CP) and jointly ensures the effective, efficient and accountable management of the entire CP and shares responsibility for the effective and efficient delivery.

The HoSO is responsible for strategically leading and continuously improving all key support functions — **Procurement & Logistics**, **Finance**, **Human Resources**, and **Administration**. In performing this role, the Head of Systems & Operations will ensure an enabling environment for the implementation of the Country Programme, while maintaining operations and systems that meet the accountability requirements of People in Need and its donors.

HoSO also directly leads the process of development and staff capacity building across the departments in terms of systems and operations.

## **Duties & Responsibilities**

- Strategic leadership
- Ensuring External and Internal Compliance
- Management of Human Resources and capacity development
- Finance management
- Logistics and procurement management

**And fulfils any other tasks as required.**

### **Requirements:**

- Hands-on approach
- Background in finance, operations, or a combination of both
- Experienced in managing teams
- Ability to coordinate and communicate clearly with different groups of people and to respect different cultural backgrounds
- Ability to work independently and effectively
- Ability to deal with a complex compliance agenda
- Analytical skills and systematic approach
- Responsibility, ownership, proactive approach, flexibility
- Experience with project management is welcome
- English language proficiency

## **PIN Offers:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organisation in a challenging context;
- Salary and benefits according to PIN salary scale and HR policies; expected salary 3250-3500 EUR super gross (based on experience), plus monthly subsistence allowance of 1395 EUR;
- Housing Allowance or accommodation arranged by PIN;
- 25 days of holiday and 10 sick days per year;
